title: Use of artificial intelligence and other data-driven technologies for coastal management
abstract: Biogeochemical cycles occur naturally in coastal regions. Estuaries, wetlands, and tidal creeks assist these cycles. Since increased anthropogenic activities and naturally occurring events act as stressors, they impact physical, chemical, and biological processes in maritime spaces and hence these cycles. This makes existing ecosystems susceptible to trophic imbalance. abstract: Introduction Construction delays remain a challenge in projects, often resulting in cost overruns, disputes, productivity losses, and schedule inefficiencies. abstract: In high-altitude regions with complex surface cover, traditional remote sensing-based geological mapping struggles with lithological boundary delineation and fine classification due to severe topographic relief, intricate lithological assemblages, and imbalanced sample distributions. abstract: A clear assessment of rehabilitation exercise performance is important for safe and personal training. abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) can support climate mitigation through renewable-energy forecasting, demand-side management, and low-energy transport routing, but the climate value of these applications is frequently reported without deducting the emissions generated across the AI system life cycle. abstract: Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs), commonly known as submarine drones, provide a critical capability for modern naval operations requiring persistent presence in contested and GPS denied environments. This paper addresses autonomous positioning and area keeping of AUVs within predefined underwater zones using integrated inertial, acoustic, and velocity based navigation systems. abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly mediating how humans acquire knowledge, make decisions, and perform cognitive activities. In higher education, the delegation of cognitive activities to algorithmic systems has the potential to shift human judgment and responsibility. This study aims to examine Qur’anic anthropology as a foundation for reframing human agency under increasingly AI-mediated conditions. abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology that reshapes public sector accounting by improving financial management efficiency, transparency, and accountability. This study aims to examine the role of AI in the digital transformation of public sector accounting and its contribution to enhancing public financial governance. abstract: Shrimp is a popular seafood product, but it spoils quickly even when stored at low temperatures. This is mainly because of microbial growth, enzyme activity, and chemical changes that reduce its freshness and quality over time. Therefore, predicting the shelf life of shrimp is important for maintaining food quality, ensuring consumer safety, reducing food waste, and improving storage management. abstract: Groundwater scarcity and its declining situation in the semi-arid area of Jaipur district, Rajasthan make it imperative to adopt scientific solutions to locate suitable rainwater harvesting sites. abstract: Coral reefs play the main role in marine ecology, as home and shelter to many aquatic species, and quite importantly, supporting local economies. abstract: Abstract Accurate forecasting of caisson tilt during construction is important for ensuring structural stability and effective construction management. However, reliable prediction remains challenging when only limited early-stage observations are available. In this study, the caisson tilt forecasting problem was formulated as an early-stage limited observation forecasting task using time-series data generated from numerical simulations. abstract: This study examined public affairs communication in the era of climate change and artificial intelligence: strategies for policy and advocacy and governance in Nigeria. The technological determinism theory was anchored in this study. This study adopted a qualitative research method, utilising in-depth interviews to explore the role of artificial intelligence in public affairs communication for climate policy advocacy and governance in Nigeria. abstract: The growth of liquid energy pipeline networks has promoted economic development but also pose significant challenges for monitoring pipeline operating conditions. Conventional manual analysis, grounded in pipeline operating principles, is highly reliable but extremely labor-intensive and time-consuming. abstract: The complex terrain and increasing forest fire incidents in recent years make high-mountain environments vulnerable to forest fires, posing a threat to ecological and economic well-being. However, research related to forest fires remains limited in the mountain region. The study aimed to assess the forest fire risk by integrating eleven predictive layers (biophysical, topographical, climatic, and anthropogenic factors) and a Random Forest (RF) model in Rasuwa, a mountainous district of Nepal. abstract: Accurate energy consumption prediction for underwater gliders is critical for long-endurance ocean missions. abstract: Rainfall is a key factor in hydrological analysis, yet precipitation time series are often incomplete due to malfunctioning of instruments. abstract: This study presents a framework for municipal solid waste (MSW) forecasting using artificial neural networks (ANNs) and Monte Carlo (MC) simulations. abstract: The increasing complexity of suspicious financial activities has reduced the effectiveness of conventional rule-based monitoring for modern anti-money laundering (AML) applications. abstract: Abstract: Microalgae serve as a rich source of diverse secondary metabolites and macromolecules. abstract: Assessing contaminant-induced dysfunction in complex living systems is critical, but remains technically challenging. abstract: Hydrological modelling is essential for water-resources assessment and climate adaptation planning; however, its application in many African basins is constrained by sparse hydro-meteorological observations, limited monitoring networks, and high uncertainty in groundwater recharge and subsurface-flow processes. abstract: Coastal benthic ecosystems are shaped by the combined effects of climate change and anthropogenic pressures. Ocean warming, acidification, and deoxygenation interact with eutrophication, pollution, bottom trawling, and coastal development, altering biodiversity, habitat structure, and functioning from shallow coasts to continental margins. abstract: Spinal infections are a serious category of deep-seated infectious diseases that pose significant threats to human health. They are caused by a broad and complex spectrum of pathogens, including bacteria, fungi, and rare opportunistic organisms. abstract: Abstract Clay content is an important determinant of soil physical and chemical behaviour, influencing water retention, nutrient availability, and agricultural productivity. abstract: A growing number of studies in astrobiological research have utilized and shown the potential in applied machine learning. However, the number of these studies are still quite limited. abstract: Abstract Modern marine surveys generate tens of thousands of underwater images per expedition, yet many are unusable due to image quality deterioration. title: Real-Time AI-Based Detection of Fish and Humans in Underwater Environments
abstract: Underwater visual monitoring is difficult because light attenuation, turbidity, color distortion, occlusion, and changing backgrounds can reduce the reliability of conventional object detection. This work presents an underwater human and fish detection system that combines a waterproof camera, image preprocessing, YOLO-based real-time object detection, and convolutional neural network (CNN) classification. title: Monte Carlo and Neural Network-based Prediction of Base Shear Force in Airport Tunnels using the Pushover Method Considering Both Soil-Structure Interaction and Non-Interaction across Different Soil Types
abstract: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are powerful nonlinear function approximators that can learn complicated relationships from data. They offer increasing value in civil, seismic, and geotechnical engineering applications. Recent findings indicate that ANNs can also be applied to structural health monitoring, material behaviour prediction and the evaluation of deep buried structures, whereas their application to airport tunnels remains largely unexplored. title: Shallow-water Seafloor Topography Refinement Using Sentinel-2 and Multi-Source Gravity Data via a Depth-Stratified XGBoost Approach
abstract: Summary Shallow-water depth data serve as the essential foundation for marine spatial planning and coastal engineering projects. However, due to the attenuation of spectral signals, traditional retrieval of shallow-water seafloor topography struggles to maintain high accuracy in highly turbid waters and deeper areas. Furthermore, existing machine learning models incorporating spatial information are highly susceptible to spatial overfitting, which severely limits their generalization ability in complex waters. title: Inteligencia Artificial y Derechos Humanos: Riesgos, Desafíos y Perspectivas de Regulación Jurídica
abstract: This research analyzes the risks that the development and use of artificial intelligence (AI) may pose to the protection of human rights. It addresses privacy, algorithmic discrimination, transparency, accountability, information manipulation, and cybersecurity. It also examines regulatory responses developed in the United States, China, and Europe, with particular attention to the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act. abstract: Marine wharves, consisting of concrete or steel decks supported by pile foundations, operate in harsh marine environments involving waves, vessel impacts, and corrosive seawater. Even minor cracks or early-stage corrosion in piles can lead to sudden structural failure. Early detection is therefore essential. abstract: The global economy is heavily reliant on healthy ecosystems, which provide humanity’s foundation for prosperity, resilience, and well-being. This interdependence has driven growing international interest in developing frameworks to assess and account for the value of natural capital to humanity, society, and the economy. abstract: The detection of hydrothermal plumes is crucial for discovering active seafloor hydrothermal fields and exploring seafloor resources. To enable autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) to adapt their survey strategies in real time, this study proposes an integrated online identification algorithm that couples real-time anomaly detection with fluid-type classification using deep learning models trained on historical data from the Qianlong-II AUV. abstract: Hawksbill sea turtles (Eretmochelys imbricata) representing multiple regional stocks are known to reside in SE Florida, and play an important functional role in the health of coral reef ecosystems. title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND THE LAW
abstract: It is too early to definitively predict how generative artificial intelligence (‘AI’) will affect the law and the legal profession. How much of the hype will come to pass, or whether the effects of AI will be revolutionary or evolutionary is yet unknown. Although the extent of those effects may not be fully evident today, early glimpses show the potential for structural disruption is real, pervasive, and likely to be far-reaching. abstract: The encyclical Magnifica Humanitas of H. H. León XIV reflects on the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to human dignity, emphasizing that technological progress acquires meaning only when it serves the human person and the common good. The document warns about the risks of the technocratic paradigm, the dehumanization of relationships, information manipulation, educational inequalities, and the impact of automation on work. title: Modelling the financial viability of offshore aquaculture using a case study of a sea bass farm in the Bay of Lion, France
abstract: The extension of net pen aquaculture to open ocean sites provides many advantages to the industry including opportunity for expansion, utilization of high energy sites, and better resilience to certain near shore or surface-associated stressors. The industry has been slow to develop due to high perceived risks and a lack of operating farms to provide financial information for open ocean farm operations. title: A decision framework for selecting IMERG bias-correction methods in complex tropical watersheds
abstract: Accurate satellite precipitation estimates are critical for hydrological modelling and climate-risk management in the tropics, where sparse gauges and complex storm regimes increase uncertainty. This PRISMA-guided systematic review synthesizes advances in bias correction for GPM-IMERG across monsoonal, equatorial, orographic, and coastal basins. Evidence is organized into bias controls, classical and distribution-based corrections, machine-learning/hybrid methods, and hydrological impacts. title: Image-Based Visual Identification of Coral Health Signs Using UPT and ROI-Based ImageJ Annotation in a Thermal-Discharge Coastal System
abstract: Image-based visual assessment provides a practical approach for documenting coral health signs in coastal systems where laboratory diagnosis is not available. This study applied a quadrat-based Underwater Photo Transect (UPT) method combined with Regions of Interest (ROI)-based ImageJ annotation to identify visually observable coral health signs, rather than laboratory-confirmed coral diseases, in the thermal-discharge coastal waters surrounding the Paiton Power Plant (PLTU Paiton), East Java, Indonesia. abstract: Background and Aim: Bossavirus delphinidgamma1 is a dolphin-associated gammaherpesvirus for which genomic information from tropical Asian marine mammal populations remains scarce. This study aimed to detect and partially characterize Bossavirus delphinidgamma1 in captive common bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops truncatus) in Indonesia and evaluate an integrated Oxford Nanopore Flongle–Illumina sequencing workflow for viral surveillance using non-invasive, low-biomass samples. abstract: Fine-scale ocean dynamics strongly influence coastal mixing, sediment transport, and vertical exchange, yet remain difficult to observe at the spatial scales at which they occur. Here, we use total surface current vectors measured by the airborne Ocean Surface Current Airborne Radar (OSCAR) to investigate sub-kilometer divergence, vorticity, shear rate, and vertical velocities in the tidally dominated Iroise Sea around Ushant Island. abstract: The northern waters of Liaodong Bay (LDB) frequently exhibit low water quality due to the region's semi-enclosed hydrological conditions, high terrestrial pollutant inputs, and seasonal sea ice cover. Existing studies have not systematically elucidated the comprehensive regulatory mechanisms of sea ice on the marine environment. title: Machine Learning Classification and Adaptive Power Control for RGB Underwater Visible Light Communication
abstract: Underwater visible light communication (UVLC) offers high data rates over acoustic and radio-frequency links but is highly sensitive to bubble-induced scattering. This paper presents an RGB wavelength-division-multiplexed UVLC system simulated in OptiSystem across clear-water, intermediate, and bubble-induced turbidity conditions. Eye-diagram features are classified using XGBoost, achieving 98.75% test accuracy and 96.18% (±2.17%) repeated cross-validation accuracy, statistically validated against SVM and Random Forest. abstract: Abstract Despite recent progress in quantifying anthropogenic carbon (C anth ) in global oceans, coastal regions remain understudied due to methodological and observational challenges. Here, we develop and generalize a Regional rEgression–based Coastal Anthropogenic carbon estimation algorithm (RECA) designed specifically for coastal environments. abstract: This study explores the application of fluorescence hyperspectral imaging (FHSI) for marine ecosystem monitoring, combining laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) with hyperspectral imaging (HSI), an approach rarely applied in marine ecology. Photopigments such as chlorophylls, carotenoids, and phycobiliproteins emit distinct fluorescence signals when excited at specific wavelengths. abstract: The PISA 2025 results, released by the OECD in September 2026, place Chile below the OECD average in Science, Mathematics and Reading, with declines of 9 and 12 points in Mathematics and Reading respectively between 2022 and 2025. Some 59% of Chilean students fall below Level 2 in Mathematics, compared with 35% across the OECD. title: Study on mechanical, corrosion and fractured surface of n-Mn modified Al5052 alloy: an ANOVA and ANN prediction of wear rate
abstract: Aluminum (Al) 5052 alloys are extensively utilized in marine environments, pressure vessels, and automotive parts due to their better strength and low density. However, more investigation is required to comprehend how the nanoscale manganese (n-Mn) element affects their mechanical, tribological, corrosion, and machinability. The development of Al5052 alloy modified with n-Mn by increasing the weight percentage in 0.25% increments from 0 to 1% through stir casting is the main focus of this study. abstract: The study examines catastrophic safety incidents in icebreaker escort operations on the Northern Sea Route (NSR). It develops strategies to prevent future accidents by analysing the Baikal–Vladivostok accident in the Yenisey Gulf of the Kara Sea in 2024 as a case study using the Swiss Cheese Model (SCM). abstract: Accurate prediction of sea level change in the Mediterranean Sea is essential for coastal risk management; however, the nonstationary behavior of sea level makes this difficult. This study presents a hybrid framework that integrates variational mode decomposition (VMD) and dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) with long short-term memory (LSTM) and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) to forecast monthly sea level anomaly (SLA). abstract: The Internet of Underwater Things (IoUT) supports marine sensing, environmental monitoring, subsea inspection, and autonomous underwater operations. However, IoUT communication is constrained by limited bandwidth, long propagation delay, time-varying underwater channels, intermittent connectivity, and strict energy budgets. abstract: Accurate prediction of cumulative plastic strain (CPS) is essential for assessing the deformation stability of marine strata subjected to artificial ground freezing (AGF). This study aims to clarify how variations in clay content and pore-water salinity regulate cyclic responses after freeze–thaw (FT) disturbance. abstract: Rip currents pose significant threats to coastal safety and to autonomous marine vehicles operating nearshore. However, deploying high-precision monitoring models on resource-limited platforms remains challenging. This paper proposes a comprehensive framework that combines a novel architecture and compression methodology. abstract: The port and logistics electromechanical industry underpins port production and supply chain operation, and its level of intelligentization is directly related to the improvement of operational efficiency and industrial capacity. title: Stable isotopes from Earth science to bedside medicine: beyond tracers and toward mechanistic biomarkers in medical oncology
abstract: Stable isotopes are non-radioactive variants of the same element whose small mass differences produce predictable effects in chemical and biological systems. While medicine has mainly used the administration of enriched stable isotopes as tracers of physiological function, the natural sciences developed stable-isotope ratios into robust measures of source, transformation, and underlying mechanism across Earth and life history. abstract: The unprecedented expansion of human activity boundaries is turning spillover from a chance event into a foreseeable ecological and epidemiological certainty. title: Intelligent Visibility Estimation Under Sea Fog Conditions Based on Deep Learning
abstract: Accurate visibility information under sea fog or low-visibility conditions is essential for ensuring navigational safety in ports and nearshore waters. This study combines single-frame images extracted from nearshore sea fog observation videos with synchronized meteorological variables to investigate sea fog visibility estimation and develops the ConvNeXt-MS-WDFM model. abstract: Fault slip modeling, based on laboratory-derived friction laws, has significantly enhanced our understanding of fault mechanics. abstract: This study investigates the influence of bottom topography on the development of instabilities in Gulf-Stream-like jets using a two-layer quasi-geostrophic model. The approach combines a linear stability analysis with nonlinear numerical simulations to examine the formation of baroclinic instabilities and coherent structures such as eddies. title: Comparison of data-driven and numerical weather prediction models for rainfall nowcasting in major cities of Bangladesh
abstract: Flood-prone Bangladesh requires accurate short-term rainfall prediction, yet conventional numerical weather prediction (NWP) models remain computationally intensive and regionally limited in skill. This study evaluates and compares four deep learning (DL) architectures — Simple Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Stacked LSTM, Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) — against the physics-based Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model for one-hour-ahead rainfall forecasting across six climatologically diverse stations in Bangladesh. abstract: Abstract The Pitzer model is widely used in process models for determining the thermodynamic properties of concentrated aqueous electrolytes. The main drawback is the need for experimentally determined parameters for each ion pair in the system. The estimation of unknown Pitzer parameters of electrolytes is thus an attractive prospect. This paper investigates machine learning-based models for the task of predicting the Pitzer parameters of binary electrolytes based on the properties of the constituent ions. title: Seeing what students learn: assessing cognitive representations and academic outcomes via EEG image reconstruction
abstract: Abstract Understanding how humans process visual information during learning remains a central challenge in cognitive neuroscience. Traditional approaches typically rely on behavioral observations or indirect neural measures, which limits direct insight into learners' internal cognitive representations. title: Valuation Methods and Their Relevance in Achieving Marine Protected Areas Targets: A Systematic Review
abstract: The prolific human-induced pressures on marine ecosystems leading to negative externalities such as beach erosion, biodiversity loss, and climate change are matters of global concern. Marine protected areas (MPAs) have emerged as a tool to conserve marine biodiversity and support human livelihoods. abstract: Monocular Depth and Surface Normals Estimation (MDSNE) is crucial for tasks such as three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction, autonomous navigation, and underwater exploration. Current methods rely either on discriminative models, which struggle with transparent or reflective surfaces, or generative models, which, while accurate, are computationally expensive. abstract: Modeling and simulation (M&S) techniques have evolved from optional engineering tools to indispensable pillars of modern maritime practice. This article presents a comprehensive systematic review of the most important modeling and simulation methodologies applied to maritime industry processes, including workflows for ship design, shipyard fabrication and construction, port and terminal operations, vessel traffic management, maintenance scheduling, supply chain logistics, and risk management procedures. title: Improved performance of machine learning-based VIIRS night-time detection of lit fishing vessels through feature engineering
abstract: Reliable detection of lit fishing vessels from night-time satellite observations is essential not only for monitoring fishing activity but also for investigating the distribution of fishery resources when integrated with marine environmental information. However, false detections caused by anthropogenic coastal illumination remain a major challenge for vessel detection using observations from the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS). abstract: Weather prediction is crucial in agriculture, transportation, and disaster management. Accurate and timely forecasts are essential for making informed decisions and minimizing risks. This study proposes a hybrid machine learning approach for weather prediction, combining Ridge Regression for feature extraction and selection and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) for training and evaluation. title: Illuminating Streptomyces : Raman Spectroscopy for Antibiotic Detection and Monitoring
abstract: ABSTRACT The genus Streptomyces is well known as a prolific source of many bioactive compounds. This review outlines the principles of Raman spectroscopy and its application to bacterial systems, with particular emphasis on the secondary metabolites produced by Streptomyces . Streptomyces are unparalleled chemical factories, producing over two‐thirds of all naturally derived antibiotics and bioactive molecules. abstract: Abstract Austenitic stainless steels are widely used in coastal and marine infrastructure for its corrosion resistance, yet failures associated with chloride-induced stress corrosion cracking (SCC) continue to be reported. In this work, the SCC susceptibility of 316L austenitic stainless steel was investigated using test solutions designed to simulate Arabian gulf seawater and compared with a reference standard brine. title: Leveraging artificial intelligence for sustainable development and policy integration in the shipping industry
abstract: Shipping is a critical industry for global trade but is associated with environmental externalities like air, underwater noise, and light pollution. Transitioning to a sustainable future requires optimizing propulsion systems, which currently suffer from fossil fuel reliance and energy losses. This research develops an AI-assisted evidence-synthesis framework to examine sustainable shipping and propulsion technologies and support a policy framework for a sustainable maritime agenda. abstract: Bathymetric data are a fundamental component of ocean observing systems, supporting applications in ocean modelling, coastal hazard assessment, marine spatial planning, and navigational safety. However, these datasets remain highly fragmented due to the diversity of acquisition platforms, including hydrographic surveys, autonomous vehicles, satellite-derived bathymetry, and legacy chart products, which often differ in spatial reference systems, vertical datums, resolution scales, and metadata quality. abstract: Coral reefs support marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of coastal communities, yet their condition in Indonesia, including Bali, continues to decline due to coral bleaching. abstract: Smart nanocomposite packaging has emerged as a promising approach for enhancing food preservation by improving barrier performance, enabling active functionality, and supporting intelligent quality monitoring. Its integration with non-thermal preservation technologies, including pulsed electric fields, cold plasma, ultraviolet irradiation, and high-pressure processing, offers new opportunities to extend shelf life while minimizing thermal damage to food products. title: Recurrent implantation failure: a registry-corroborated, age-stratified definition and pragmatic five-tiered management algorithm
abstract: Recurrent implantation failure (RIF) remains a significant challenge in reproductive medicine, imposing substantial emotional, clinical, and financial burden on affected couples. RIF is generally defined as failure to achieve pregnancy after multiple transfers of good-quality embryos, yet progress in the field has been constrained by the absence of a universally accepted definition and by the inherent complexity of investigating the embryo–endometrial interface. title: The one-Layer Antarctic model for Dynamical Downscaling of Ice–ocean Exchanges (LADDIE) version 2.0
abstract: Abstract. Projections of Antarctic mass loss and its contribution to sea-level rise are highly sensitive to the applied ocean-driven melting. As fully coupled continental-scale ocean–ice sheet models are scarce, ice sheet models are typically run in standalone configurations, forced with parameterised sub-shelf melting. To provide a physically more detailed alternative to melt parameterisations, we here present version 2.0 of the one-Layer Antarctic model for Dynamical Downscaling of Ice–ocean Exchanges (LADDIE). title: Where freshwater meets the sea: satellite–model insights into salinity dynamics in the Venice Lagoon
abstract: Salinity is a key descriptor of transitional water bodies at the land–sea interface, and resolving its spatiotemporal dynamics is essential for understanding water-mass exchange, habitat distribution, and ecosystem functioning. However, available observations remain limited in their ability to resolve dynamic freshwater–marine interactions at relevant spatial scales. The Venice Lagoon, a complex transitional system exposed to interacting natural and anthropogenic pressures, offers a valuable setting for investigating these dynamics. title: Computational Model for Exploration of Microbial Chemotaxis Dynamics on Casson-Maxwell Reactive Fluid in Off-Centered Stagnation Point Flow: A New Frontier in Computational~Intelligence
abstract: Comprehending bioconvection facilitates the modelling of natural processes in aquatic environments and improves the efficacy of systems incorporating microorganism suspensions. It connects biology with fluid dynamics, providing insights into the impact of living creatures on fluid flow behaviour. The current study offers insights into the mechanisms of heat, microorganism and mass transfer in complex fluids, with potential applications in biomedical devices, chemical engineering and industrial processes involving non-Newtonian fluids under the influence of electromagnetic and thermal effects.

abstract: Accurate stratigraphic characterization is essential for offshore geotechnical engineering, where nearshore marine sediments commonly exhibit strong spatial variability and complex stratigraphic transitions. Although machine learning (ML) methods have shown promise for CPTU-based stratigraphic identification, random sample-based validation may overlook spatial dependence among CPTU measurements and consequently overestimate model generalization. abstract: Study Region Jeju Island, South Korea, is a groundwater-dependent volcanic island with steep orography, coastal exposure, and sparse high-elevation gauges, where precipitation variability strongly influences drought diagnostics. title: SIAVASH: A solver-free, cloud-native EO–ML framework for weak-line screening and flood hazard mapping in data-scarce regions
abstract: • Solver-free EO–ML generates 30 m design-event flood-depth and hazard maps. • XGBoost and SHAP reveal strong but basin-specific depth relationships. • Fold ensembles show stable depths, with uncertainty concentrated near boundaries. • Weak-line/WSE-PF screening finds local changes but modest basin-scale effects. • FOEN and ADR7 provide complementary probability–intensity hazard screening. title: Comparative analysis and optimization of multi-model artificial intelligence for microscopic detection of fungal structures in superficial fungal infections
abstract: Background Superficial fungal infections present a growing threat to global public health. Traditional diagnostic techniques, including microscopy and culture, are time-consuming and subjective, often limiting diagnostic accuracy. Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diagnostic tools offer a promising adjunct to improve efficiency and standardization of microscopic fungal detection. Methods We systematically compared six deep learning models, including the You Only Look Once (YOLO) series, the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) series and the Detection Transformer (DETR). title: Inter-strain diversity among coastal picocyanobacteria across salinity gradients
abstract: Strains of the picocyanobacteria genera Synechococcus and Cyanobium occur in cold-temperate zones, from coastal waters to the open ocean, spanning a range of salinities and water depths. To thrive across different salinities, picocyanobacteria strains acclimate internal turgor by expending metabolic energy to accumulate compatible solutes and extrude inorganic ions. We grew five picocyanobacterial strains, derived from a range of source habitat salinities, under a matrix of light and salinity levels. title: Inteligencia artificial y blockchain en el notariado ecuatoriano
abstract: [Purpose] This article analyzes the institutional barriers constraining the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and blockchain in Ecuador's notarial system, understood as components of the digital transformation of public services dependent on telecommunications infrastructure. It aims to identify and characterize such barriers, assess their comparative severity against the Brazilian case, and formulate analytical propositions on the viability conditions for notarial digital transformation. title: Rethinking Potential Flood Damage Assessment: A Data‐Driven Alternative to Varnes‐Based Models
abstract: ABSTRACT Reducing flood damage is a key challenge for both administrators and communities, particularly in the face of increasing climate‐related impacts. A fundamental prerequisite for effective damage reduction is a detailed understanding of the spatial distribution of territorial susceptibility to flood damage. title: Spectral index and machine learning-based evaluation of coastal urban thermal dynamics using google earth engine
abstract: Abstract This present study introduces a cloud-based geospatial and machine learning framework for assessing coastal urban heat island (UHI) dynamics in Thoothukudi coastal region, Southern India, using 12 seasonal Landsat composites (2010–2025) processed through Google Earth Engine (GEE). Seasonal classification followed Indian Meteorological Department definitions: Summer (March-June), Northeast Monsoon (October-November) and Winter (December-February). title: A Lightweight Channel–Frequency Joint Attention Network for Underwater Ship-Radiated Noise Separation
abstract: Underwater acoustic signals (UAS) in marine environments are often contaminated by noise from biological activity, ocean waves, and equipment. Under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions, target ship-radiated components and background noise are strongly mixed, making reliable underwater detection, recognition, and communication challenging. To address this problem, this paper proposes Multi-Scale TCN, DPRNN, and Attention TasNet (MSDA-TasNet), a lightweight end-to-end source separation network for underwater ship-radiated noise. title: F-MNet: flux-modulated network for radial power prediction of space reactors
abstract: Rapid and accurate prediction of radial power distribution is crucial for the design and operation of space nuclear reactors. However, traditional Monte Carlo methods incur prohibitively high computational costs, while conventional data-driven surrogate models face severe overfitting and insufficient generalization capabilities under small-sample and data distribution shift conditions. Addressing the problem of radial power prediction for rod-controlled space reactors, this paper proposes F-MNet (Flux-Modulated Network), a physics-informed neural network architecture. title: Detecting Trachinotus Blochii with a YOLOv8 Model and Video Dataset: A Deep Learning Approach for Fisheries Monitoring
abstract: This study develops a deep learning-based object detection model using YOLOv8 to detect Bawal Bintang/Star Pomfret fish (Trachinotus Blochii) in real time and with high accuracy from a video dataset captured in a 3x3x3 m3 Floating Net Cage (KJA) off the Karimunjawa coast. The video was taken using an Underwater Camera placed at a position 1.5 meters deep at KJA. This study aims to develop an automated fish monitoring system to detect Star Pomfret fish and improve efficiency and accuracy in fisheries resource management. title: Advancing Sustainable Development in OECD Countries: Carbon Emission Efficiency, Growth–Emission Decoupling, and Digital–Structural Transformation
abstract: ABSTRACT Advancing sustainable development requires reconciling economic growth with carbon reduction. This study investigates carbon emission efficiency (CEE), growth–emission decoupling, and digital–structural transformation in 35 early OECD member countries from 1995 to 2023. It combines the IGT decoupling model, a three‐stage DEA framework using the Super‐EBM model, the GML index, and truncated regression to evaluate decoupling patterns, static and dynamic CEE, and the drivers of low‐carbon transition. title: Noninvasive diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease: a review of emerging biomarkers and multimodal approaches
abstract: Noninvasive biomarkers are expanding access to biological assessment of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). This review evaluates blood-based, neuroimaging, retinal, electrophysiological, digital, and behavioral measures alongside structured cognitive and functional assessment, and examines multimodal and machine-learning approaches for detection, differential diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring. title: A mutual information-driven hybrid deep learning framework for SDN intrusion identification
abstract: Software-Defined Networking (SDN) enhances network programmability and manageability through decoupling the control and data plane, though the same has resulted in the controller being an attractive assault target. To date, no flexible Intrusion Identification System (IDS) developed for SDN is only capable of efficient intrusion identification with a low FPR (False Positive Rate), So restricting its applicability. title: Artificial intelligence driven framework for enhancing sustainability and resilience in communal cattle insurance in Lupane District Zimbabwe
abstract: Communal cattle farming in Sub-Saharan Africa continues to face destabilization from non-linear climate variability, yet insurance penetration remains negligible. In Lupane District, Zimbabwe, uptake is exceptionally low at approximately 0.01%, despite recurrent droughts that threaten household livelihoods. This study aimed to develop an AI-driven framework to enhance sustainability and resilience in communal cattle insurance within the district. title: Approaches and disputes regarding Artificial Intelligence regulation
abstract: El artículo examina los enfoques y disputas en torno a la regulación de la inteligencia artificial, a partir de episodios recientes que intensificaron la preocupación por la pérdida de control humano sobre los modelos, como la fuga de sistemas de OpenAI de su entorno de pruebas en julio de 2026 y la carta abierta Pacing the Frontier. Se analizan las alternativas de regulación externa, autorregulación e internacional, junto con sus obstáculos técnicos, institucionales y de cumplimiento. title: Autonomous Underwater Vehicle Hull Design: Design Principles, Hydrodynamic Evaluation and Optimization
abstract: Autonomous Underwater Vehicles have become essential platforms for ocean exploration, environmental monitoring, offshore engineering, and military applications. As the primary hydrodynamic component of an AUV, the hull significantly influences drag, endurance, maneuverability, and payload capacity. With advances in computational fluid dynamics (CFD), parametric modeling, optimization algorithms, and artificial intelligence, AUV hull design has evolved from empirical approaches to simulation-driven and intelligent optimization frameworks. title: Regulatory language limits satellite-based enforcement in marine protected areas
abstract: Abstract The international community has committed to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, and satellite monitoring can now detect industrial fishing inside marine protected areas (MPAs) at near-global scale. Yet remote detection establishes only a vessel’s identity, position, time, and movement; whether those facts can support enforcement action depends on how the law is written. We analysed the regulatory text of 9740 MPA zones and 119 national legal instruments across 15 countries. title: Enhancing urban flood risk assessment: A PCA-integrated deep learning surrogate for hazard and damage prediction
abstract: This study proposes an integrated deep-learning framework for rapid urban flood hazard mapping and damage prediction from compact rainfall descriptors. A simulation-based reference database linked synthetic rainfall scenarios with grid-based flood-depth maps generated by a validated rainfall-runoff and inundation model and category-specific damage indicators derived from damage assessment. title: Explainable Deep Learning Reveals Future Changes in East Asian Extreme Winter Predictability
abstract: Deep learning-based approaches have emerged as powerful tools for seasonal prediction, yet their skill remains limited for extreme anomalies, and warming climates may alter predictability sources. Here we present a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based framework to assess how seasonal predictability changes in a future climate, focusing on East Asian extreme winters. Our CNN, trained on CESM2-LENS simulations for historical and SSP3-7.0 scenarios and optimized with Amplitude Focal Loss, reliably captures seasonal mean and extreme temperatures. title: Determining the Principal Directions of a Point Set in the Plane and in Space
abstract: Introduction . The problem of determining the principal directions of a point set in the plane or in space is solved numerically. The task is to determine the orientation of an extremal line passing through the centroid of the set and minimizing or maximizing the functional defined as the sum of the squared distances from all points of the set to the line. title: An Interpretable Deep Learning Framework for Spatial Prediction of Soil Salinity Using Multi-Source Remote Sensing and Environmental Data: A Case Study of Cangzhou, Hebei Province, China
abstract: Soil salinity poses a significant challenge to agricultural productivity and sustainable land management in coastal and semi-arid regions. Soil salinity in coastal agricultural regions is controlled by complex interactions among surface conditions, groundwater processes, soil properties, and terrain characteristics. Accurate spatial prediction requires integrating remote sensing observations with environmental information that represents these processes. title: Shifts in spawning patterns in three species of reef-building corals in the Mexican Caribbean
abstract: Most Caribbean reef-building corals reproduce by broadcast spawning numerous egg-and-sperm bundles simultaneously into the water column prior to external fertilization. This is a pivotal bottleneck in the lifecycle of broadcast-spawning organisms because it relies on the synchronization of gamete release to precise species-specific nights and times. However, changes in spawning patterns have been documented in a wide variety of species from different oceans. title: Ensemble machine learning-based scaling up of wetland carbon dynamics across the Southeastern U.S.
abstract: Abstract Background Although the Southeastern United States (SE US) has been identified as a major terrestrial carbon sink, the balance of CO 2 and CH 4 fluxes from its wetlands remains poorly constrained due to strong environmental heterogeneity and limited regional-scale assessments. In this study, we used observations from 24 wetland sites located in the SE US, including freshwater and salt marshes, to train machine learning models (Random Forest, XGBoost, Support Vector Machine, Artificial Neural Network, and Partial Least Squares Regression) to predict monthly mean gross primary productiv

title: Hybrid machine learning framework for drought forecasting: integration of LSBoost, RQNN, CNN-RNN, CNN-LSTM and advanced data decomposition
abstract: Drought is a natural disaster with serious impacts on agriculture, water resources management and ecosystem balance. Ongoing global warming and climate change exacerbate drought cases. Therefore, proper tools are essential for long-term drought monitoring and efficient drought forecasts. The Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI) is a reliable indicator developed to monitor long-term drought trends and is widely used to define agricultural and hydrological droughts. title: High‐Resolution Satellite Imagery Reveals Landscape‐Scale Benthic Habitat Changes in a Turbid Coral Reef
abstract: ABSTRACT Coral reefs are under increasing threat from local and global stressors, resulting in changes to the composition and spatial structure of benthic habitats. This study uses high‐spatial resolution satellite imagery and landscape metrics to analyse changes to the shallow, turbid reef at Sebastião Gomes on the Abrolhos Bank in the Southwestern Atlantic Ocean between 2010 and 2024. title: Machine learning prediction of chloride convection-zone depth in marine tidal concrete with model explainability and experimental validation
abstract: Reliable prediction of chloride convection-zone depth is important for service-life assessment of tidal-zone concrete, but most data-driven chloride studies focus on surface concentration or diffusion-related indicators. This study proposes a data-driven prediction and explainability framework for chloride convection-zone depth. A database of 624 experimental measurements with 25 material, curing, exposure, and loading features was compiled from published studies. title: The atoll gap: area, governance, and the under-recognition of a major coral reef system
abstract: Global assessments project widespread coral reef degradation under continued ocean warming and acidification, underscoring the urgent need to identify and account for the full diversity of coral reef systems within conservation planning. Atolls are dynamic reef-ocean-land systems whose persistence depends on coral reef sediment production, land-sea connectivity, and cross-ecosystem nutrient subsidies. title: Spatial Diversity of Marine Protists Along the Northern Norway Fjords During the Sub‐Arctic Summer
abstract: Polar coastal waters are highly complex and productive ecosystems that experience increasingly higher average water temperatures, shallower and stronger stratification, and higher glacier-melting rates. Yet, the environmental complexity and high microbial diversity within fjords pose challenges to understanding the impacts of these changes and the ecological processes driving them. abstract: Each year, hundreds of thousands of tons of derelict fishing gear become entangled in ship propellers, and resolving such incidents currently requires divers to manually cut the entangled material underwater, exposing them to the risk of secondary accidents. To address this problem, we developed a radial quadruped underwater robot that walks along the hull of a ship using electromagnetic feet and swims freely using propellers mounted on the distal link of each leg. abstract: This paper presents a virtual boundary integral neural network (VBINN) for three-dimensional exterior acoustic problems. The method introduces a virtual boundary within the scatterer or vibrating body and represents the associated source density using a neural network. abstract: Accurate classification and localization of Cloud-to-Ground (CG) lightning are essential for the development of reliable early warning systems in tropical regions and the improvement of thunderstorm monitoring. This study proposes a multimodal machine learning framework for CG lightning classification and polarity-based localization with synchronized atmospheric and electromagnetic measurements collected in Melaka, Malaysia, in 2024. abstract: A new species is described from Thailand, Collotheca laddae sp. nov ., and a pictorial key to all Collotheca species and subspecies recorded in Southeast Asia is provided. The new species was discovered during a freshwater zooplankton identification workshop. This species is characterized by a five-lobed infundibulum with very small lateral lobes and short vibratile setae. abstract: ABSTRACT Ocean currents represent a stable source of blue energy. Flag‐type triboelectric nanogenerators (F‐TENGs), which have been widely investigated for harvesting energy from low‐velocity ocean currents, generally rely on bluff body to induce vortex. abstract: Mesoscale eddies play a crucial role in the ocean, and accurate detection of their three-dimensional (3D) structures is essential for understanding marine dynamics. However, 3D eddy reconstruction remains challenging: traditional methods provide limited pixel-level boundary delineation, while existing deep learning approaches suffer from insufficient physical constraints and unrealistic eddy geometries. title: Attention-Guided Deep Learning Framework for Ovarian Cancer Subtype Classification
abstract: Ovarian cancer histotype classification is challenging because of substantial morphological heterogeneity and subtle subtype-specific features. This work presents a controlled evaluation of high-resolution pathology representations and slide-level aggregation methods for automated classification of five ovarian cancer subtypes from whole-slide histopathology images. Precomputed CONCH patch embeddings were aggregated using mean pooling, max pooling, gated attention-based multiple-instance learning, and a max-pooling cascade. title: A study on the evolutionary patterns of the acoustic environment of large-scale truss-type deep-sea aquaculture platforms
abstract: To investigate the impact of large-scale offshore aquaculture platform operations on the acoustic environment of local waters, this study analyzed the observed evolution of the acoustic environment around a large truss-type platform and its surrounding waters based on a continuous 46-hour synchronous multi-channel observation dataset acquired under typical calm sea conditions. abstract: This study develops a hybrid analytical and computational framework for the (2+1)-dimensional Boussinesq equation, which models weakly nonlinear, weakly dispersive shallow-water gravity waves relevant to wave resonance and oblique interactions in coastal and ocean engineering. title: GIS-based Deep Learning for Identifying and Characterizing Small Community Lagoon Wastewater Treatment Systems
abstract: Wastewater lagoon systems remain a dominant form of secondary treatment for small communities in the United States due to their low energy requirements, operational simplicity, and affordability. Despite their widespread use, national inventories of lagoon systems are fragmented, inconsistently reported, and often outdated, with non-discharging systems particularly underrepresented. These data gaps limit effective infrastructure planning, environmental assessment, and equitable allocation of resources. title: Explainable machine learning for predicting microplastic burden in commercially important freshwater fish and assessing dietary exposure
abstract: Microplastic (MP) contamination in commercially important freshwater fish represents an emerging concern for aquatic ecosystem integrity and human food safety. This study presents an interpretable machine learning framework for predicting and assessing MP accumulation in European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax), Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus), bighead carp (Hypophthalmichthys nobilis) and crucian carp (Carassius auratus) collected from four retail markets in Yichang City, Hubei Province, China. title: A Caribbean bright spot coral reef exceeds thermal limits during the fourth global coral bleaching event
abstract: Marine heatwaves are increasing in both frequency and intensity, exposing coral reefs to prolonged periods of thermal stress and driving recurrent mass coral bleaching. Nevertheless, coral decline remains heterogeneous, with some reefs maintaining unexpectedly high coral cover despite exposure to thermal and other environmental disturbances. This study analysed benthic community change across Banco Capiro in Tela Bay and the south-side reefs of Utila, Honduras, from 2013 to 2025, spanning the 3rd and 4th Global Coral Bleaching Events. title: Linking marine benthic biodiversity and ecosystem functions related to carbon cycling in a continental mud depocenter
abstract: Abstract. The importance of carbon storage in continental seafloor sediments is increasingly recognized, yet the role of benthic macrofaunal biodiversity in the regulation of these processes remains poorly understood. Benthic macrofauna contributes to organic carbon cycling through respiration and secondary production, while the sediment reworking (bioturbation) and ventilation (bioirrigation) of infauna promote the redistribution and remineralization of organic matter in sediments. abstract: This study proposes a method to enhance neural network performance when training data and application data are not very similar, e.g., out of distribution problems, as well as pattern and regime shifts. In contrast to previous approaches to out of distribution problems, which alter the inputs and outputs of an operator, our approach alters the operator itself. title: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation for treatment-resistant depression in Singapore: a retrospective, naturalistic study
abstract: Introduction Naturalistic repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) outcome data for treatment-resistant depression remain limited in Southeast Asia. This retrospective study describes such outcomes from a general hospital in Singapore. Method 28 outpatients received rTMS (10Hz high-frequency or intermittent theta-burst) targeting the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (F3 scalp position) between May 2022 and May 2025. title: An attention-enhanced residual network framework for structural damage detection based on structural health monitoring data
abstract: Local damage in steel structures often produces only subtle differences in vibration responses, and measurement noise can further reduce identification robustness. To address these challenges, this study proposes a structural damage identification method that combines Markov transition field (MTF) encoding with a coordinate-attention-enhanced residual network. title: Multiscale pH fluctuations on a stable algal reef community (SE Sardinia, Tyrrhenian Sea)
abstract: The Mediterranean Sea is threatened by ocean acidification and warming, in combination with habitat loss, pollution, invasive species, and overexploitation. Assessing local high-frequency pH variability in the context of relevant basin-scale time series data is essential to understand ecosystem vulnerability. We report the results of the Italian national pH monitoring based on the Marine Strategy Framework Directive, and the pH dynamics observed at Capo Carbonara. title: Projected intensification of summer upwelling along the Southeastern Coast of China
abstract: Coastal upwelling is a key dynamical process along the southeastern coast of China, regulating regional circulation, biogeochemical cycling, and marine ecosystem dynamics. While previous studies have provided valuable insights into the mechanisms and variability of this coastal upwelling, its future evolution and underlying physical drivers under climate change remain unclear. title: El poder infraestructural en Inteligencia Artificial
abstract: Os estudos de comunicação e mídia frequentemente analisam as dinâmicas de poder na inteligência artificial (classificatória, preditiva, generativa, agentiva, etc.). No entanto, escassos estudos abordam o poder emergente do desenvolvimento infraestrutural da IA. Primeiro, a composição da pilha de tecnologia da IA e a plataformização de microsserviços distribuídos (I). Segundo, a integração e reconfiguração das práticas cotidianas (II). title: Spatiotemporal Precipitation Trends and Hybrid Machine Learning Prediction in the Humid Rainforest Climatic Zone of Nigeria
abstract: This study investigated the spatiotemporal trends and hybrid machine learning prediction of precipitation in Nigeria’s humid rainforest climatic zone using 45 years (1981–2025) of monthly rainfall data from Calabar, Yenagoa, Benin City, and Ikeja. Data obtained from the NASA POWER database were analyzed using statistical, spatial, and machine learning techniques. title: Integrating Remote Sensing, Geographic Information Systems, and Machine Learning for Environmental Monitoring and Sustainable Resource Management
abstract: Environmentally sensitive coastal areas are rapidly becoming urbanised, increasing pressure on vegetation, wetlands, surface-water resources and the natural resource base. The current study combines remote sensing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and machine learning to evaluate changes in Land Use/Land Cover (LULC) and environmental conditions in the Lekki–Ajah axis of Lagos State, Nigeria. Built-up areas, vegetation, wetlands, surface water and bare/exposed land were mapped using multitemporal satellite imagery and spatial datasets. title: A Hybrid Quantum Optimization Framework for Oil Spill Detection Using Marine Radar
abstract: Oil spills at sea pose a serious threat to marine ecosystems and coastal economic development. Therefore, rapid and accurate detection of oil spills is crucial for emergency response and environmental protection. Marine radar offers unique advantages in short-range, continuous, and all-weather monitoring, making it an important supplementary tool for oil spill detection. title: Deep learning–assisted coral morphology cover across 742 sites on the Great Barrier Reef (2022–2025): A Great Reef Census citizen science dataset
abstract: Abstract Citizen science can expand the spatial extent of coral reef surveys, but its value is often limited by inconsistent data quality and slow manual analysis. Here we combine volunteer‐collected imagery with deep learning to overcome these constraints, delivering validated coral cover data at scale. We present 46,879 benthic seascape images from 742 sites across 267 reefs on the Great Barrier Reef, collected by Great Reef Census volunteers between September 2022 and February 2025. title: The burden of inflammatory bowel disease in Asia (1990–2023) and projections to 2050: A comprehensive analysis of the 2023 global burden of disease study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn's disease (CD), is becoming an increasingly important public health concern in Asia, with rising incidence and prevalence reported across the region. Despite progress in global burden studies, data gaps remain in Asia due to variations in healthcare and socio-demographic factors. This study aims to address these gaps by assessing the burden of IBD across Asia from 1990 to 2023, focusing on regional trends in UC and CD. title: Propagation-physics-guided channel augmentation and temporal–spectral fusion for domain-robust underwater acoustic target recognition
abstract: Underwater acoustic target recognition (UATR) is essential for ocean-intelligence sensing, but deep learning-based models often suffer from performance degradation under ocean acoustic domain shift. This problem arises because ship-radiated noise recorded under different propagation channels, vessel operating states, background noise levels, and recording configurations may exhibit substantial distribution discrepancies. title: Cohort-level growth modeling of ethical engagement with artificial intelligence in education
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in higher education, yet limited evidence explains how students’ ethical engagement develops over time. Existing research is largely cross-sectional and often treats ethical awareness, reflection, and responsible use as a unified competence. This study examined cohort-level changes in AI Ethics Awareness (AEAw), Responsible AI Use (RAIU), and AI-Driven Reflection on Decision-Making (AIRD), including relationships among their initial levels and growth rates. title: Hip Fracture Registry and Audit Readiness in Southeast Asia: A Scoping Review and Public-Evidence Implementation Gap Map
abstract: Hip-fracture registries and audit systems support feedback, benchmarking, and quality improvement, but the public visibility of this infrastructure across Southeast Asia is unclear.This review mapped publicly identifiable registry readiness, audit, care quality, and secondary prevention evidence for hip-fracture care across Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) countries.We conducted a scoping review and public-evidence implementation gap map across the 10 ASEAN member states.Searches covered PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL)

title: Environment-conditioned deep learning for severe convection nowcasting
abstract: Severe convection produces localized hazards that often require warnings before radar echoes fully reveal storm development. Convective initiation and the maintenance of intense convection remain challenging for radar-only nowcasting because pre-convective signals may be absent from recent radar observations, and strong echoes often decay rapidly in forecasts. title: Exploring pre-service teachers’ STEM readiness in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand: Comparative insights from teacher education programs
abstract: STEM education has become a central agenda for enhancing human resource quality and global competitiveness. This study explored pre-service teachers’ readiness to implement STEM teaching in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand, with particular attention to their conceptual understanding, implementation ability and experience, perceived barriers and institutional support, and attitudes toward STEM education. title: How heterogeneous environmental regulations shape marine sustainable development: evidence from coastal China
abstract: Marine sustainable development requires reconciling economic growth with environmental protection, making the design and selection of effective environmental regulatory instruments increasingly important under tightening marine ecological constraints. In this study, marine sustainable development is measured by marine green total factor productivity (MGTFP). title: Predicting long-term degradation of prestressed bridge girders using a hybrid finite element and deep learning approach
abstract: Prestressed concrete girders are widely used in bridge and railway infrastructure. However, their long-term performance is highly vulnerable to environmental effects, particularly corrosion, which significantly compromises structural serviceability and durability. Accurately quantifying corrosion-induced deterioration over extended periods remains challenging due to the substantial time and computational demands of conventional finite element analyses. title: Asymmetric bloom lengthening drives high-latitude ocean chlorophyll accumulation imbalance
abstract: Terrestrial ecosystems maintain a stable time-allocation budget between growth and senescence, but whether this applies to the ocean remains unclear. Using fused satellite LiDAR and ocean-color data (2007–2022), we show that marine phenology is variable and asymmetric. In high latitudes ( > 50°N), the bloom growth-to-decline ratio (RGD) is declining by ~5.3% per decade. title: Tornado damage prediction using machine learning
abstract: Tornadoes are the most violent of all atmospheric windstorms. Although they occur throughout the world, the highest frequency is observed in the US, where over 1,700 tornadoes were recorded in 2024 alone. Intensity measures that characterize tornado damage, such as the Enhanced Fujita (EF) scale, are derived from post-event assessment on the ground. This somewhat circular aspect of damage characterization and EF scale determination remains a major limitation for long-term prediction of damage. title: APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON MARKETING PERFORMANCE, GUEST SATISFACTION AND LOYALTY: IMPLICATIONS FOR SUSTAINABLE INTERNATIONAL HOTEL BUSINESS IN ABUJA, NIGERIA
abstract: The growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping hotel marketing and guest-service delivery, yet empirical evidence on its implications for guest satisfaction and loyalty in developing hospitality markets remains limited. This study examined AI applications in selected international hotels in Abuja, Nigeria, focusing on their perceived contribution to marketing performance, guest satisfaction and loyalty, as well as barriers to adoption. abstract: Estudios críticos, administrativos y técnicos de comunicación y de ciencias sociales suelen diagnosticar vínculos estrechos entre los gigantes tecnológicos (Big Tech) y el nuevo verano de la inteligencia artificial (IA). abstract: Flood susceptibility mapping (FSM) is dominated by studies of upland catchments. At the same time, near-sea-level coastal and backwater floodplains, where inundation is shaped by reclamation, land use, tidal influence and constrained drainage rather than relief, remain comparatively under-explored. title: From track to impact: a review of multi-hazard typhoon forecasting and resilience
abstract: While recent advancements in tropical cyclone prediction have been extensively documented, existing review literature remains heavily fragmented into isolated academic domains, such as artificial intelligence, data assimilation, or coastal hydrodynamics. This fragmentation obscures the operational reality of disaster risk reduction. To address this critical gap, this paper presents a transdisciplinary systematic review of the entire end-to-end climate service value chain. title: A review of the effectiveness of solutions to achieve the good environmental status of the marine environment
abstract: Europe’s seas are at the nexus of a “triple crisis” of biodiversity and habitat loss, climate change, and pollution, increasingly eroding the ecosystems’ resilience and capacity to provide ecosystem services. Although essential, existing European Union policies, especially the Marine Strategy Framework Directive (MSFD), proved insufficient. abstract: Desde sus primeros tiempos, la inteligencia artificial ha encontrado un campo fértil de aplicación en el dominio médico; quizá por la forma en que se modelan y abordan eventos, y por la apertura del personal sanitario. Lo importante es que ha ayudado a resolver de manera práctica problemas de interés; según la época, se han aplicado algoritmos de tendencia. abstract: Abstract The relatively short modern observational record limits our understanding of the relationship between global tropical cyclone (TC) frequency and sea surface temperature (SST), resulting in uncertain future TC projections. Using novel deep-learning-based past-millennium simulations with the Ai2 Climate Emulator version 2 (ACE2), we provide insight into the connections between SSTs and TCs. abstract: Abstract Ring foundations efficiently support axisymmetric structures like silos, storage tanks, chimneys, and cooling towers with reduced concrete volume compared to solid circular foundations. Their ultimate bearing capacity is strongly affected by asymmetric loading and spatial variability in soil properties. This study presents a hybrid machine learning framework to predict normalized bearing capacity factors and safety factors for ring foundations in spatially variable cohesive-frictional (c-φ) soils. title: FPGA-Based Neural Network Accelerators for Space Missions: A Survey
abstract: Space missions are growing ever more ambitious, placing greater demands on onboard computing. Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) have garnered interest due to their reconfigurability and cost-effectiveness. At the same time, neural network (NN)-based methods are proving invaluable for critical spacecraft tasks such as autonomous operations, remote sensing, selective downlink, and data compression. title: An Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Sentinel-1 SAR Wave-Mode Significant Wave Height Retrieval via Spotter-Buoy-Corrected ERA5 Reanalysis
abstract: Significant wave height (SWH) is a fundamental parameter for ocean engineering, maritime safety, and climate studies. Although spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) wave mode observations provide global, all-weather coverage, accurate SWH retrieval remains challenging due to the complex ocean-to-SAR imaging mechanism. This paper presents an explainable machine learning algorithm for retrieving SWH from Sentinel-1 SAR wave mode data. title: Machine learning-aided groundwater level and CO2 emission estimations in Indonesian tropical peatland
abstract: ABSTRACT Tropical peatlands store a large fraction of global soil carbon and emit large amounts of CO 2 from peat decomposition and root respiration. Accurate quantification of peatland carbon emissions requires a prediction that is sensitive to environmental gradients. This study estimated biweekly total and heterotrophic peat CO 2 emissions (Rs and Rh, respectively) in the peatland hydrological unit (PHU), which represents the whole peatland ecosystem on Rupat Island, Indonesia. abstract: Subsea pipeline systems constantly face harsh marine environments, where complex fluid-structure interactions and nonlinear seabed responses cause severe mechanical vibrations threatening long-term structural integrity. Consequently, continuous real-time monitoring is vital. Traditional high-fidelity numerical models remain highly computationally expensive for remote edge devices, while purely data-driven machine learning models lack physical interpretability and struggle generalizing in dynamic underwater conditions. title: Multi-objective optimized signal decomposition with explainable and reliable hybrid models for multistep significant wave height forecasting in ocean wave energy applications
abstract: Accurate forecasting of significant wave height (Hs) is vital for marine safety, coastal engineering, and renewable energy production. This study presents an effective integrated model system to forecast Hs for two distinct sites in Australia, Gladstone and Palm Beach, over various time horizons from 30-min to 24-h ahead during the period of 2018 to 2022. abstract: Abstract Short-range rainfall forecasting in tropical coastal megacities is a formidable challenge owing to the nonlinear dynamics, strong seasonality, and pronounced interannual variability that characterise monsoon precipitation regimes. This study develops and evaluates deep learning frameworks for multi-lead-time (D+1 to D+4) daily rainfall forecasting over Mumbai (72.88°E, 19.07°N), India, a densely populated coastal metropolis where accurate precipitation prediction is directly consequential for flood early warning. abstract: Precipitation nowcasting plays a critical role in early hazard warning, especially for rapidly evolving convective systems. This study proposes a radar-based deep learning model that combines convolutional neural networks (CNN) for spatial feature extraction, a recurrent spatiotemporal module (ConvLSTM) for image sequences, and axial attention to capture spatiotemporal context. title: Regime shifts in South Florida groundwater: distinguishing upstream recharge from coastal sea level influences (1997–2022)
abstract: Groundwater dynamics in South Florida play an important role in shaping the hydrologic balance of the region. This study investigated long-term trends in groundwater elevation, surface water stages, and their interactions across Water Conservation Areas 3A and 3B, Everglades National Park, coastal watersheds, and Florida Bay. abstract: Trigonium zonatulatum (Greville) A. Mann, originally described as Triceratium zonatulatum Greville, was previously known solely from the Indo-Pacific, Indian Ocean, and Bering Sea. Here, we report the first record of this diatom species from the Atlantic Ocean (Caribbean Sea), based on material collected at Boca Chica Beach, Dominican Republic. title: Optimized machine learning models for identification of autism spectrum disorder
abstract: Early and accurate diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) relies heavily on identifying critical behavioral and clinical markers within high-dimensional datasets. However, standard feature selection methods frequently struggle with premature convergence and suboptimal feature identification. abstract: Cross-border artificial intelligence (AI) cooperation is expanding, but evidence on its effect on domestic technological capability in recipient economies is scarce. Drawing on absorptive capacity theory, we create a composite AI absorptive capacity index for 10 Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) economies, encompassing innovation foundations, application foundations and industrial support. abstract: Abstract The Himantura species complex consists of large demersal whiprays vulnerable to coastal fisheries, yet unresolved taxonomy within the genus hinders conservation efforts, making molecular assessments crucial for effective fishery management. This study clarified genetic relationships among Himantura species in the Western Indian Ocean (WIO) using species delimitation techniques. abstract: Rapid urbanization and the replacement of vegetated surfaces by impervious materials can substantially alter urban thermal environments, while water bodies, topography, and coastal setting may further modify these patterns. Understanding how these factors contribute to land surface temperature (LST), particularly across large and geographically heterogeneous cities, is important for spatially targeted heat mitigation. abstract: Agricultural irrigation systems can bear the heavy losses of water through runoff, evaporation, and deep percolation. Crop water requirements vary with crop species, growth stage, soil properties, evapotranspiration, weather, and plant water status; therefore, irrigation scheduling based on a single parameter is insufficient. abstract: The current trend involving the use of paper-based medical prescriptions and the exchange of such by the social media is a major problem in automated and accurate text extraction in healthcare processes. This paper suggests a complete smart pipeline to digitize the images of medical prescriptions with lightweight deep learning-based classification, specialized Optical Character Recognition (OCR) engines, and comparative benchmarking of results using a large language model (LLM). abstract: Deep-sea mining tracked vehicles are subject to substantial parametric uncertainty from hydrodynamic effects, soft-seabed interaction, suspension nonlinearities, and actuator degradation. This paper proposes a coupled adaptive neural network (CANN) strategy for an 8-DOF six-wheel half-vehicle active suspension. abstract: Gastric cancer still has rather high rates of incidences around the globe and the amount of tumor infiltrating lymphocytes in the tumor tissues has proved to be a reliable predictor of prognosis in patients suffering from this type of disease. abstract: Exploration and reflection on problem-based learning building critical thinking. Media are needed to stimulate the ability to analyze real-world problems, express logical opinions, and implement solutions as critical thinking skills that foster an attitude of environmental concern. abstract: Accurate urban land-use classification is essential for hydrological modeling, yet most studies evaluate classification schemes solely by pixel-level accuracy rather than their hydrological consequences. abstract: Research in marine ecosystem ecology increasingly integrates biodiversity status and trends, ecosystem functioning, and human pressures. Understanding how marine biodiversity supports ecosystem functioning remains central to the field, while growing concern over ecosystem condition has shifted attention towards relationships between human pressures and ecological responses. abstract: Molecular imprinted polymers (MIPs) have various applications such as chemical sensing and drug delivery systems because they can selectively attach molecules that fit the template. abstract: Accurately identifying whether a field of view of satellite hyperspectral infrared sounders is clear or cloudy is critical for geophysical parameter retrieval and meteorological applications. abstract: Understanding the relationships between fruit morphological traits and biochemical characteristics is essential for the efficient utilization of plum (Prunus domestica L.) genetic resources in breeding programs. abstract: Climate transition has increased investors' concerns about carbon risk, yet evidence remains limited on how firms' technological capabilities shape market responses, particularly in emerging markets. abstract: Understanding historical coastal change over multi‐decadal timescales is fundamental for coastal hazard assessment and adaptation planning. In Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ), national‐scale coastal change information has historically been fragmented, limited in spatial resolution or constrained to relatively short timeframes. abstract: En publicación científica se han probado distintos incentivos para optimizar el proceso de revisión por pares (RPP), sin lograr un impacto significativo en los tiempos y calidad de las revisiones. title: Jornalismo de dados e Inteligência Artificial: Estudo de casos para compreender alcances e limitaçõesda automatização na América Latina
abstract: This paper analyzes ten cases of AI integration in data journalism (two global, eight Latin American). AI expands operational capacity (volume and speed) but does not replace epistemic decisions, which remain under editorial control. The automation gradient —signaling, predictive scoring, large‑scale classification, total output validation— is proposed as an alternative to the automatic/semiautomatic binary. In Latin America, the main constraint is data governance: the lack of public information in processable formats limits the reach of AI, regardless of the models’ capabilities.

abstract: The corrosion behavior of weathering steels in marine atmospheric environments emerges from the synergistic interactions among alloy chemistry, exposure duration, and environmental loading, exhibiting strong nonlinearity and multiscale coupled responses. abstract: The integration of coding and Artificial Intelligence (AI) into vocational education is essential for equipping students with 21st-century digital competencies, yet implementation in remote and island regions like Bangka Belitung archipelago province remains fragmented and unsustainable. abstract: Introduction Coastal social-ecological systems face climate change, resource exploitation, and fragmented governance. abstract: This article examines the scientific and conceptual foundations for developing an artificial intelligence-based adaptive digital twin method aimed at early fault detection and the reduction of associated energy losses in solar photovoltaic systems.
