abstract: Abstract Airborne microplastic (MP) particles are transported through the atmosphere, yet direct measurements at altitude remain scarce. abstract: Introduction Seaweed aquaculture production is expanding globally but threatened by increasing climate stressors, including extreme events. Ocean-based aquaculture is especially vulnerable to marine heatwaves, which can rapidly raise temperatures above the physiological limits of organisms, including macroalgae. abstract: In the Southern Ryukyu Islands (Okinawa, Japan), the most important and well-known site with Neolithic pottery is the Shimotabaru shell-mound, located on the south coast of Hateruma Island, approximately 200 km east of Taiwan. abstract: Agriculture in SE Asian coastal lowlands is vulnerable to inundation and associated crop production loss. abstract: Abstract Video auditing can provide vital insights into complex industrial operations where quality, safety, and compliance are critical. abstract: Sargassum blooms in the tropical North Atlantic have surged to unprecedented levels, causing massive algal tides that severely impact coastal ecosystems. abstract: Accurate integrated water vapor (IWV) estimates are essential for atmospheric monitoring, yet reanalyses can retain systematic discrepancies relative to in situ observations. abstract: INTRODUCTION: Reef restoration practitioners aim to preserve coral genetic diversity by protecting reefs and cultivating diverse genotypes in coral nurseries. abstract: Marine litter (ML) has attracted attention from international and national regulatory bodies because of its impact on biodiversity, water quality and the blue economy. abstract: Carbon emission prediction of coastal port-industrial zones integrates industrial production, maritime logistics and spatial environmental governance. title: Computational identification of candidate biomarkers and compounds associated with skeletal muscle insulin sensitivity improvement mediated by physical activity: an integrative multi-omics and computational chemistry study
abstract: Background Insulin resistance (IR) underlies many chronic diseases. While physical activity improves skeletal muscle insulin sensitivity (IS), the underlying molecular mechanisms and targeted drug strategies remain elusive. This hypothesis-generating study integrates bioinformatics and computational chemistry using public datasets; all findings are computational predictions requiring experimental validation. Methods Using a skeletal muscle dataset (GSE24215, n = 10) of bed rest-induced IR and exercise-reversed IR, candidate genes were identified via WGCNA and differential expression analysis.

abstract: Abstract Stock price time series exhibit inherent nonlinearity, nonstationarity, and volatility, which limit the predictive capacity of classical econometric models and conventional machine learning approaches. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel hybrid framework, LSTM-ARO-VMD, that integrates Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and the Artificial Rabbits Optimization (ARO) algorithm within a unified, simultaneously optimized architecture. title: Environmental preferences and jurisdictional distribution of juvenile loggerheads in the eastern North Pacific
abstract: Abstract While the basin-scale movements of North Pacific loggerheads are well documented, habitat use remains poorly understood for juveniles in the eastern North Pacific (ENP), including the exclusive economic zones (EEZs) of Mexico and the United States (U.S.). These areas represent developmental habitats where turtles encounter dynamic environmental conditions, fisheries threats, and management frameworks. abstract: This work focuses on the 3D tracking control issue for underactuated underwater vehicles (UUVs) subject to model uncertainties, external disturbances, and actuator mechanical degradation by mechanical wear. abstract: The demand for energy sustainability has driven interest in biomass-derived carbon electrode materials for electrochemical energy storage. abstract: The Red Sea and Gulf of Aden are strategically vital maritime corridors connecting Africa, Asia, and Europe, and are increasingly affected by geopolitical rivalry, maritime insecurity, hybrid threats, and military competition. These developments carry significant implications for Egypt's national security, economic interests, and the security of the Suez Canal. abstract: Marine steel structures endure cyclic loading throughout their service life. Acoustic emission (AE) is an effective passive non-destructive testing technique. It captures transient elastic waves released during damage evolution in real time and supports online damage monitoring. AE waveforms are complex, and the structural conditions to be recognized are diverse. Deep learning has therefore become essential for automated structural condition recognition. abstract: Abstract High-temperature thermal energy storage in subsurface reservoirs (HT-RTES) can help balance seasonal heat demand and supply by storing excess thermal energy in subsurface reservoirs. Mature hydrocarbon fields are promising storage targets because their reservoir properties are relatively well constrained; however, many legacy fields lack modern petrophysical data. abstract: ABSTRACT Seawater is an abundant and cost‐free electrolyte source for Zn‐ion batteries, but its high chloride ions (Cl − ) content severely corrodes zinc (Zn) metal anodes. abstract: Aquaculture facilities in marine ranches continuously fragment and release microplastics, which accumulate in filter-feeding shellfish and enter residents’ diets. abstract: Estuaries are subject to frequent stressors, including elevated nutrient loading and extreme hydrologic events, which impact water quality and disrupt ecosystem stability and function. The capacity of an estuary to resist changes in function in response to precipitation events is an important descriptor of ecosystem response dynamics, especially when interpreted within the context of baseline system condition and ecological state. This study focuses on modifying agricultural waste using a quick, simple, and easy solid-phase extraction approach. abstract: The high-dimensional Fokas model can describe a wide range of complex nonlinear wave phenomena; however, traditional analytical methods struggle to obtain a diverse set of exact analytical solutions, which limits the theoretical analysis and engineering applications of such models. title: The Navier–Stokes Equations: A Critical Review of Theory, Computation, Turbulence, and Data-Driven Frontiers
abstract: The Navier–Stokes equations describe the motion of viscous fluids and stand at the center of modern fluid mechanics. They also define one of the hardest open problems in mathematics, for the question of whether smooth three-dimensional solutions can develop singularities in finite time remains unresolved. This review provides a critical, evidence-based synthesis of the subject from its foundations in the work of Leray and Hopf through the mathematical, computational, and data-driven landscape of 2026. title: Integrative taxonomy reveals a new species, Anadara adiastola sp. nov. (Bivalvia, Arcidae) from the northern Arabian/Persian Gulf, north-western Indian Ocean
abstract: A new species of the arcid genus Anadara is described from intertidal and shallow subtidal habitats in Kuwait, northern Arabian/Persian Gulf. Anadara adiastola sp. nov . is diagnosed using shell morphology and soft-part anatomy and further assessed through COI sequence data. The new species is characterised by an oblong to subtrapezoidal shell, 31–35 radial ribs, weak cross bars mainly on the anterior ribs, and a thick periostracum forming long bristles, especially on the posterior slope. abstract: Background Nitrogen availability strongly regulates growth and biochemical accumulation in marine diatoms, but the magnitude and direction of these responses are strain-specific. Optimizing nitrate supply may therefore provide a practical approach for improving biomass production and the accumulation of high-value metabolites in diatoms. abstract: This paper proposes a unified framework for understanding the universe as a single continuous process of increasing complexity, operating through successive layers of organisation each built on the last. abstract: Katablepharids (or kathablepharids) are plastid-less, biflagellate protists widely distributed in marine and freshwater environments. Here, we report a new katablepharid species, Katablepharis ulleungensis sp. nov., isolated from a black sandy beach in Ulleung-do, South Korea. title: Integrating climate adaptation initiatives for coastal resilience: governance lessons from the Catalan coast
abstract: Mediterranean coastal regions face increasingly interconnected climate risks that require adaptation across sectors and governance levels. Despite growing policy commitments and a widening portfolio of adaptation initiatives, implementation often remains fragmented. This study examines the governance conditions under which diverse climate adaptation initiatives can be integrated to support coordinated regional and local resilience. abstract: Silk fibroin, a natural textile material spun by silkworms over millennia, is emerging as a transformative platform for integrating human intelligence with artificial intelligence. Its core innovation lies in the meso-functionalization strategy, which precisely programs protein refolding and hierarchical assembly. abstract: Abstract. In the Namib Desert, fog is an essential water source and occurs when and where advected marine stratus clouds intersect with the land surface. title: The History and Labor of Web Scraping
abstract: Abstract Both the free labor of generating data online and the importance of data work which cleans, labels, and verifies these data are required for producing artificial intelligence (AI) systems. Between these two essential moments in AI production, we identify web scraping as the intercalary process of extracting data from the internet at scale. abstract: Abstract The environmental crisis and the advancement of generative artificial intelligence pose new challenges and opportunities for education. The objective of this study was to describe the level of development of environmental action competence in secondary school students during their interaction with a Narrative Conversational Agent based on generative artificial intelligence. abstract: Marine governance should be understood as a form of global governance because of the systemic nature of marine challenges. abstract: Tidal flooding has become an increasingly significant environmental hazard in coastal areas. abstract: The tropical Pacific plays a pivotal role in global climate, and changes in its mean state and in the El Niño Southern Oscillation can substantially alter regional hydroclimates with major economic and societal impacts. abstract: Tourism in Goa is concentrated along the coastal belt, generating congestion, environmental stress, and uneven spatial development. This study develops a spatial decision-support framework to identify areas where tourism pressure should be contained and areas where diversification is more feasible. The analysis uses a 1 × 1 km grid across Goa and integrates tourism amenity indicators, environmental conditions, accessibility measures, and regulatory constraints. title: A new species of sole (Pleuronectiformes, Soleidae), Soleichthys labyrinthus, from the China Sea
abstract: The genus Soleichthys (Soleidae) suffers from taxonomic confusion due to morphological similarities. In this study, a new sole species, Soleichthys labyrinthus sp. nov ., is described based on the holotype and 24 paratypes collected from the northern South China Sea and the East China Sea. This new species is readily distinguished from its congeners by a unique combination of characters: 78–86 dorsal-fin rays and 65–73 anal-fin rays; the ocular side is tawny brown, featuring a labyrinth-shaped reticulated pattern and lacking the typical transverse bands found in most congeners. title: Transformer-Based Bias Correction of ERA5 Winds over the East China Sea and Wind Resource Trend During 2016–2025
abstract: Accurate wind information is essential for offshore wind-resource assessment in the East China Sea, yet global reanalyses remain poorly constrained in this region. Using one year of multi-height (20–200 m) floating-lidar observations from the Shanghai Far-Sea Wind Demonstration Site, this study evaluates ERA5 wind performance, develops a machine-learning bias-correction model, and reconstructs a bias-corrected decadal (2016–2025) hub-height wind resource. ERA5 reproduces observed wind variability with moderate fidelity (Pearson R = 0.71) but systematically underestimates wind speed above ~50 m

title: Thermally Recoverable Fracto‐Mechanoluminescence in Manganese‐Based Hybrid Halides for Fatigue‐Resistant Structural Health Monitoring
abstract: ABSTRACT Fracto‐mechanoluminescence (FML) materials have recently demonstrated great potential as next‐generation interactive optoelectronic systems, while they generally suffer from irreversible fatigue degradation under long‐term cyclic stress, severely limiting their practical applications. Here we design the flexible FML composite films based on the manganese‐based hybrid halide EPB 2 MnBr 4 (EPB = ethyltriphenylphosphonium), exhibiting intense green emission under mechanical stimuli. title: An Immobilized Marine Glycosyltransferase Acts as a Stabilized Biocatalyst for the Synthesis of Mannosylated Phosphoisoprenoids
abstract: Glycosylated phosphoisoprenoids constitute valuable bioactive molecules and starting materials for complex glycosylation cascades. Herein we report the identification and the functional characterization of a newly identified polyprenyl phosphomannose synthase from the marine microorganism Rhodococcus erythropolis PR4. This enzyme, normally unstable in its free form, is significantly stabilized by immobilization and can be reused up to four times for sustainable phosphoisoprenoid derivatization.
institutions: Universidad de la República de Uruguay

title: Zero-label cross-region solar radiation forecasting using domain adaptation-based transfer learning
abstract: Accurate solar radiation prediction is essential for integrating photovoltaic (PV) systems into power systems and supporting supply–demand management. However, many regions lack on-site irradiance measurements due to limited sensor deployment. To address this, this study investigates domain adaptation (DA)-based transfer learning for solar radiation prediction under zero-label conditions, where solar radiation measurements are unavailable in the target region. Three representative DA methods: Domain Adversarial Neural Network (DANN); Deep Correlation Alignment (Deep CORAL); and Deep Adaptation

title: Coupled thermo-fluid-structural dynamics and stability of rotating pipes conveying fluid flow
abstract: In this work, we introduce a new thermo-fluid-structure interaction formulation for the first time to study in a systematic manner the influence of thermal stress, gyroscopic force, and fluid dynamics inside the structure on the stability of rotating pipes. The governing equations of motion are formulated based on thermoelasticity theory and the Hamilton principle that considers flow-structure interaction and thermal expansion effects. title: Atomic-level design and device modeling of lead-free Cs2AgSbCl6 double perovskite solar cells through DFT, SCAPS-1D, and predictive algorithms
abstract: Lead-free double perovskite solar cells (DPSCs) have emerged as attractive alternatives to conventional lead-based perovskites because of their superior environmental compatibility, enhanced chemical stability, and reduced toxicity. In this research study, the performance of a solar cell architecture FTO/IGZO/Cs 2 AgSbCl 6 /Cu 2 O are systematically studied by the simulation software known as SCAPS-1D. DFT calculations were performed using WIEN2k package to investigate structural and optoelectronic properties of Cs 2 AgSbCl 6 material to determine its suitability for photovoltaic applications.

title: Toward real-time wave forecasting via data-driven reduced-order modeling with data assimilation
abstract: Reliable wave forecasts are a cornerstone of coastal risk management and offshore operations, yet operational products remain expensive to generate at high resolution and can be insufficiently calibrated for decision-making under uncertainty. We present a hybrid forecasting framework that couples data-driven reduced-order modeling with sequential data assimilation to produce flow-dependent, spatially coherent ensembles of significant wave height over the North Sea. title: Evaluation of risk scenarios in Ecuador using Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite remote sensing, ERA5-Land climate data, and XGBoost

title: Decoupled operational transfer path analysis for vibration source identification in marine steam turbine generator sets
abstract: To address strong multi-source coupling, complex transmission paths, and reference-channel crosstalk in operational transfer path analysis (OTPA) of marine steam turbine generator sets, this study proposes a decoupled OTPA method based on vibration source coupling separation. title: Uso de inteligencia artificial en la educación: Beneficio o perjuicio en los estudiantes
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been progressively integrated into educational processes through smart tutors, adaptive learning platforms, virtual assistants, and generative AI tools, such as ChatGPT. These technologies can personalize instruction, provide immediate feedback, facilitate access to information, and support students with different learning paces and needs. However, their use also poses risks related to technological dependence, misinformation, data privacy, unequal access, plagiarism, and a decline in critical thinking. title: Comparative Evaluation of Deep Object Detection Architectures for Automatic Target Recognition in Real-World AUV-Acquired Side-Scan Sonar Imagery
abstract: Reliable detection of underwater objects is important for mine countermeasures, unexploded-ordnance surveys, navigational-hazard assessment, and subsea infrastructure inspection. Interpretation of side-scan sonar (SSS) imagery is still largely performed by trained human operators, making post-mission analysis time-consuming when large volumes of data are collected. title: A SwiGLU enhanced ConvNeXt framework for multispectral Sentinel-2 land use and land cover classification
abstract: Land use and land cover (LCLU) classification from multispectral satellite imagery is important for applications such as urban planning, environmental monitoring, agriculture, and disaster management. Existing deep learning based approaches have improved LCLU; however, most of them utilize only the red, green, and blue (RGB) bands of multispectral sentinel-2 imagery, thereby underutilizing the complementary spectral information available in the near-infrared (NIR), short-wave infrared (SWIR), and derived spectral indices such as normalized difference built-up Index (NDBI), Normalized Differenc

title: The impact of the Montreux convention on NATO regarding the security of the black sea region
abstract: This study examines how the Montreux Convention shapes NATO’s defense posture on the Eastern Flank within the Black Sea security environment. Building on international relations theory, maritime law, and geopolitical analysis, it evaluates regional security and international cooperation under Montreux’s legal regime. Using literature review, comparative analysis, and case studies, the research finds that Montreux remains pivotal to regional stability and international security dynamics, constraining naval movements while providing predictability that reduces escalation risks. title: The mediating role of technology innovation in order to strengthen the South China Sea trade
abstract: Purpose: This study aims to develop a strategic management model to strengthen Indonesia’s maritime trade competitiveness in the South China Sea (SCS) by integrating good and clean governance, interagency synergy, government policy, and technological innovation. Design/methodology/approach: This study employs a quantitative explanatory approach using Structural Equation Modeling based on Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) to examine the relationships among governance, interagency synergy, government policy, technological innovation, and trade strengthening. title: Loss of foundation species from nearshore hardbottom communities in the Florida Keys
abstract: Nearshore hardbottom (NSHB) habitats occur in shallow coastal waters throughout the Florida Keys and support sessile benthic invertebrate communities dominated by sponges and octocorals. In turn, these sessile benthic invertebrates provide unique structural habitats, supporting motile invertebrate and fish communities. We examined changes to NSHB faunal communities in the Florida Keys under two different hydrological regimes (bayside and oceanside) in 2006 and 2023. title: Inferential dominance of global hierarchical neural architectures for multi-horizon univariate environmental forecasting
abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate multi-horizon forecasting of atmospheric pollutants is essential for environmental decision-support systems, particularly under spatially heterogeneous and temporally dependent conditions. This study evaluates the inferential dominance of global hierarchical neural architectures for univariate forecasting of PM 2.5 , PM 10 , O 3 , and NO 2 concentrations over Paraná, southern Brazil, using CAMS-EAC4 reanalysis data from 2010 to 2024. title: Lake sediments uncover glacier change on the Kerguelen Islands during the past 1500 years
abstract: Climate change is driving the rapid retreat of glaciers across the sub-Antarctic zone. Using continuous lake sediment-based records of past glacier changes, the recent trends can be evaluated in a long-term context. Here, we analyse sediments from two glacier-fed lakes: Lake Athéna II and Lake Héra, located downstream the Chamonix Glacier on the sub-Antarctic Kerguelen Islands in the Indian Southern Ocean. title: Forecasting compound sea level extremes: the 29–30 October 2018 Adriatic storm surge and meteotsunami extreme
abstract: On 29-30 October 2018, an extreme sea level occurred in the Adriatic Sea, driven by a combination of long-period (storm surge) and short-period (meteotsunami) oscillations. Storm surges were strongest in the northern Adriatic, while shorter-period oscillations dominated in the middle Adriatic, where a meteotsunami was observed and recorded in Vela Luka Bay (Korčula Island). This type of extreme sea level event, arising from the combination of a storm surge and a meteotsunami, is termed a compound extreme and poses both a major threat and a forecasting challenge. abstract: Introduction The population of Bolboschoenoplectus mariqueter has substantially declined because of habitat modification and competition. Therefore, this study aimed to characterize the photosynthetic and stoichiometric traits of B. mariqueter and their environmental regulation in a natural tidal-flat population to facilitate successful conservation. title: Robust Peanut Size Grading via Scale-Augmented Ordinal Classification and Morphological Feature Fusion
abstract: Deep learning models classify peanut size accurately under fixed imaging conditions, but accuracy drops when apparent object scale changes, for example with camera-to-object distance. Ordinal losses and feature-level fusion are rarely compared under a leakage-controlled protocol. To address both gaps, this study evaluates a single pipeline that pairs scale-aware training with morphological feature fusion. abstract: ABSTRACT Basalt fiber‐reinforced polymer (BFRP) composites have emerged as a promising, environmentally responsible alternative to conventional glass fiber (GF) and carbon fiber (CF) composite systems. Produced from natural volcanic basalt rock without chemical additives or toxic by‐products, basalt fiber combines good mechanical properties, strong chemical resistance, and a wide thermal service range with a substantially lower environmental production footprint than conventional synthetic reinforcement fibers. title: Mycelium of science diplomacy: Cultivating Gulf biodiversity data sharing in complex trust environments
abstract: In the Persian-Arabian Gulf, conservation is uniquely complicated by transboundary ecosystems, migratory species, and anthropogenic pressures in the world’s hottest sea. Additionally, inadequate infrastructure, inconsistent data standards, and limited data interoperability complicate cross-border collaboration for science where geopolitical sensitivities, institutional fragmentation, and uneven capacities create a complex trust environment that can constrain cross-border collaboration. title: Early warning models for rainfall-triggered clustered landslides: Advances, challenges and future perspectives
abstract: Against the backdrop of global climate change and the increasing frequency of extreme rainfall events, rainfall-triggered clustered landslides have become a major concern in mountainous disaster risk management due to their sudden occurrence, regional clustering, and high destructive potential. This paper systematically reviews the current development and technological advances in early warning models for rainfall-triggered clustered landslides. title: Flow-dependent effect of sub-yield elastic loading on the corrosion behavior of B10 CuNi alloy
abstract: B10 Cu Ni alloy is commonly subjected to both flow and external loading during marine service, but the influence of sub-yield elastic strain on its corrosion behavior and its dependence on flow velocity remain unclear. Here, B10 Cu Ni alloy was exposed for 168 h to simulated seawater at flow velocities of 0–4 m/s under loading conditions of 0 and 200 MPa. Weight-loss measurements, electrochemical measurements, and surface analyses were combined to investigate its corrosion behavior. title: Predicting regional gray swans via translocation: AI weather models and Dubai’s unprecedented 2024 rainfall
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) models have transformed weather forecasting, but their skill for unprecedented weather extremes is unclear. Here, we analyze GraphCast, AIFS, and FuXi forecasts of the unprecedented 2024 Dubai storm, which had twice the training set's highest rainfall in that region. GraphCast and AIFS accurately forecast this event up to 8 days ahead. FuXi forecasts the event but underestimates the rainfall. title: Intelligent wind ear: traffic surveillance audio-based wind speed level recognition for crosswind hazard monitoring
abstract: Strong winds and associated crosswind risks are frequent hazards that threaten vehicle stability, necessitating high-resolution wind monitoring and early warning. This study repurposes traffic surveillance cameras as the Intelligent Wind Ear (IWE), an audio-based framework for wind speed level (WSL) recognition that provides wind intensity information to support crosswind risk assessment. title: On the effectiveness of two universal metabarcoding primer pairs in amplifying Arctic gelatinous zooplankton DNA from tissue and environmental samples
abstract: Gelatinous zooplankton (GZP) comprise a highly diverse group of marine taxa that play key ecological roles throughout the world’s oceans. However, their fragile bodies make them difficult to effectively study using traditional sampling methods such as net and optical surveys. While the recent advancements of non-invasive DNA metabarcoding techniques have become valuable tools in GZP biodiversity research, the performance of commonly used metabarcoding markers for these taxa remains poorly understood. title: Penguins maintain effort, despite reduced dive efficiency, with limited physiological response under increased swimming workload
abstract: In highly variable marine habitat, it is key to understand how free-ranging animals cope with variation in the energy cost of locomotion. Here, we experimentally tested how an apex marine predator, the king penguins (Aptenodytes patagonicus) adjusted to an increase cost of locomotion when foraging at sea. title: Feeding ecology and conservation implications for the critically endangered guitarfish Glaucostegus granulatus in northern Sri Lanka: Feeding ecology and conservation for guitarfish
abstract: Elasmobranchs play important ecological roles in coastal marine ecosystems, functioning as predators, mesopredators, and occasional scavengers. Guitarfishes (order Rhinopristiformes) are key benthic components but are increasingly threatened by fishing pressure, particularly bycatch in small-scale fisheries. This study examines the feeding ecology and ontogenetic dietary variation of the Sharpnose Guitarfish Glaucostegus granulatus in northern Sri Lanka. abstract: The coastal road infrastructure system in Kien Giang Province is affected by extreme weather, limited data, shortcomings in organizational-financial-policy arrangements, and the need to improve maintenance quality under climate change. title: Population dynamics and stock assessment of the white anglerfish, Lophius piscatorius (Actinopterygii, Lophiiformes, Lophiidae), in the central Mediterranean Sea (GSA 12)
abstract: The white anglerfish, Lophius piscatorius Linnaeus, 1758, is a demersal species of great ecological and commercial importance in Tunisian waters. This study uses data-limited assessment methods to evaluate the population dynamics and stock status of this species in northern Tunisia (GSA 12). title: Digital twins for energy wells through multiscale physics-data fusion: Review, challenges, and a conceptual framework
abstract: Energy wells underpin critical technologies in the global energy transition, including geothermal energy extraction, carbon capture and storage, and underground hydrogen storage. In recent years, digital twin (DT) concepts have been increasingly explored to support well design, monitoring, and integrity management. However, most existing DT implementations for energy wells remain limited in scope and maturity, with incomplete integration of multiscale physics, evolving field data, and adaptive operational decision support. title: Hybrid transformer and CNN for hyperspectral image classification with spectral band selection
abstract: Abstract Hyperspectral images (HSI) play a vital role in remote sensing applications such as surveillance and precision agriculture, yet they face challenges including limited labeled samples and class imbalance. This paper presents a new method for HSI classification by integrating spectral band selection with advanced deep learning techniques. First, we propose an optimized band selection method alongside data augmentation using crop-and-resize transformations to enhance feature diversity. title: Unsupervised probing critical transitions in complex systems using generative diffusion models
abstract: Critical transitions can irreversibly change complex systems, making anticipation a fundamental challenge. Machine learning is increasingly used for early warning, but many approaches require transition labels or control information. Probabilistic time-series forecasting models naturally produce predictive uncertainty by generating future trajectories from observations. title: Promoting Agricultural Green Productivity Through Geographical Indication Certification: Mechanisms and Spatial Heterogeneity
abstract: Agricultural green transformation is important for achieving economic growth and environmental sustainability. Geographical indication agricultural products (GIAPs) have become a useful tool for improving agricultural green total factor productivity (AGTFP). However, the mechanisms through which GIAPs affect AGTFP and their spatial differences are not yet fully understood. title: A Knowledge Graph-Based Question Answering System for Marine Diesel Engine Fault Diagnosis Integrating Intent Recognition and Named Entity Recognition
abstract: Abstract To address the challenges of knowledge acquisition and low information utilization efficiency in marine diesel engine fault diagnosis, this paper proposes a question answering system integrating intent recognition and named entity recognition. First, a domain-specific knowledge graph for marine diesel engine faults is constructed to achieve the structured representation of multi-source fault knowledge. title: GGFA-SwinIR: A gradient-guided and frequency-aware joint multi-scale framework for bathymetric DEM super-resolution
abstract: High-resolution bathymetric digital elevation models (DEMs) support marine geoscience, but global grids can smooth fine-scale terrain where observations are sparse. We present GGFA-SwinIR (Gradient-Guided Frequency-Aware SwinIR), a shared-backbone discrete multi-scale framework for × 2 , × 4 , and × 8 reference-grid reconstruction. The framework integrates gradient-magnitude guidance, bicubic-base residual prediction, and pixel, gradient, and complex-spectrum supervision. abstract: Abstract In near-shore shallow-water environments, continuous autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) motion causes substantial acoustic target scale variations, while seabed sediments, rocks, and clutter severely degrade sonar image quality. These factors collectively increase the difficulty of underwater small-target detection and recognition. abstract: Water Quality Management is an essential competency in Brackish and Marine Fisheries Agribusiness because it requires students to integrate scientific knowledge, technology, quantitative analysis, and problem-solving skills in authentic aquaculture contexts. However, learning activities are still predominantly supported by conventional materials, while the use of digital learning resources remains limited. title: Mapping the Mangrove Suitability Area in the Coast of Indonesia Using a Random Forest Model
abstract: Mangrove ecosystems play a crucial role in climate change mitigation through their exceptional capacity for carbon storage, yet their distribution in Indonesia—the country with the second-longest coastline in the world—remains underutilized for large-scale restoration and management. Despite being home to around 25% of the world’s mangrove forests, many coastal areas have lost their mangrove cover due to massive degradation and conversion. title: Left to cope alone: how pregnant and postpartum women and their newborns manage extreme heat in coastal Kilifi, Kenya
abstract: Background In coastal Kenya, high seasonal temperatures compound structural challenges that include intermittent water access, resulting in health burdens from extreme heat. Women can experience limitations in the coping strategies available to them for protecting their health and wellbeing from high indoor and outdoor temperatures. This paper, drawing on the Climate Heat and Maternal Neonatal Health Africa (CHAMNHA) study, aims to describe how mothers and their newborns in rural Kilifi cope with extreme heat in their daily routines. abstract: Sweeping gas membrane distillation (SGMD) is a thermally driven desalination process that uses a membrane to remove salts from seawater, achieving high salt-rejection rates at relatively low operating temperatures. abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and Language Modeling (LLM) have taken on a significant role in software engineering, acting as a universal translator between natural language and technical specifications. These tools help optimize processes such as requirements engineering, test automation, and code generation, among others, allowing for valuable time savings in agile production environments. abstract: The environmental footprint of maritime transport, combined with growing social and regulatory pressure to tackle pollution, has brought the shipping industry to the forefront of the sustainability agenda. abstract: This study evaluated whether a global modeled soil product adds predictive value to locally calibrated digital soil mapping of topsoil soil organic carbon (SOC; 0–30 cm) in an irrigated Peruvian coastal valley. abstract: Vibrio parahaemolyticus is a halophilic Gram-negative bacterium widely distributed in marine and estuarine ecosystems, and a leading cause of seafood-borne gastroenteritis worldwide. abstract: The research endeavor at hand is basically meant to trace the most prominent regulatory, operational, fuel-related, and technological approaches employed for maritime emission reduction. abstract: Neurodevelopmental impairments like cerebral palsy are prevalent infant developmental problems in clinical infant healthcare. abstract: Abstract Analyzing the behavior and body patterns of octopuses in nature is challenging due to their camouflage capabilities, changes in skin texture and color, body deformations, and frequent occlusions. title: Physics-informed cross-domain image synthesis for microalgae growth phase classification in turbid media
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based classification of microalgae growth phases in Palm Oil Mill Effluent (POME) requires representative training images. However, the available public data originate from a water medium with characteristics that differ from those of the POME. Existing methods apply uniform weighting to each channel and are inconsistent with light absorption in turbid media, leading to the collapse of the chromatic margin between the growth phases. Thus, these methods can only meet the global distribution (C1) but fail to simultaneously maintain inter-phase discriminability (C2).

abstract: Abstract A rapid transition toward sustainable and clean energy is necessary for a secure energy future in today's dynamic world. Biohydrogen produced from waste biomass is gaining momentum; however, raw biohydrogen comprises tracer impurities, and its commercial use further requires extensive downstream technologies. abstract: The massive emergence of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has introduced a structural transformation in the contemporary communication ecosystem. This article proposes analyzing this scenario as the rise of a "synthetic communication ecosystem," in which mediation is no longer limited to the selection or distribution of human content but incorporates the automated generation of plausible discourse. title: Beyond historical catch: developing a climate-adaptive fisheries allocation framework for transboundary fish stocks under international law
abstract: Climate change is rapidly altering the geographical distribution of transboundary fish stocks, challenging the legal and institutional assumptions upon which international fisheries governance has traditionally been based. Existing allocation systems, largely founded on historical catch records and relatively stable stock distributions, are becoming increasingly inconsistent with ecological realities, generating disputes among coastal States and undermining the effectiveness of Regional Fisheries Management Organisations (RFMOs). Because autophagy control has two context-dependent roles in the development of cancer, it is a prospective therapeutic target. abstract: The polymer composites with enhanced mechanical, thermal, and tribological properties are increasingly important for advanced structural applications. In this study, hybrid composites based on an epoxy-benzoxazine matrix reinforced with basalt fibers (BF), waste cotton textile fibers (WCTF), and graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) were developed. title: Future of edge AI in biodiversity monitoring
abstract: Abstract Many ecological decisions are slowed by the gap between collecting and analysing biodiversity information. Edge computing moves data processing closer to the sensor, with edge artificial intelligence (AI) using AI models for data processing and selective data transfer. edge AI extends the scope of biodiversity monitoring by complementing retrospective ecological analysis with real‐time sensing, enabling responsive and adaptive decision‐making. However, the adoption of edge AI systems in ecological research remains fragmented because deploying efficient and reliable systems is complex.

abstract: This study analyzes the impact of integrating artificial intelligence (AI) on students’ academic performance and motivational perceptions. A total of 114 first-year Tourism degree students from Complutense University of Madrid (Spain) participated. The assessed skill was oral production in English for specific purposes (ESP) in the tourism field, through two promotional videos: one created conventionally and another supported by AI. abstract: The logistics conditions in a country play a crucial role in ensuring the smooth flow of trade, which in turn leads to increased revenue and trust from other nations. A robust logistics environment must address several key factors, such as infrastructure, customs procedures, timeliness, and others. As a member of ASEAN, Indonesia has a favorable geographic advantage from an economic perspective, which represents a potential that must be fully exploited. abstract: Abstract. Data-driven artificial intelligence (AI) weather models are increasingly positioned as alternatives or complements to physics-based numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems, yet systematic model evaluation studies that compare both paradigms under controlled experimental conditions remain limited. abstract: Many regions of India face floods and droughts in the same year, sometimes within a few hundred kilometres of each other. During a heavy monsoon spell, reservoirs in one basin release large volumes of water to protect their dams, and much of this water flows to the sea, while districts in a neighbouring basin run short of drinking and irrigation water a few months later. title: Flow partitioning modulates salt intrusion response to river discharge in a river-network estuary
abstract: Salt intrusion in river-network estuaries is commonly related to upstream freshwater discharge, but the relationship may vary among channels due to flow redistribution within the estuarine network. In the Modaomen Estuary of the Pearl River Delta, salt intrusion poses a serious threat to freshwater security during the dry season. title: The Impact of AI on STEM Education and Workforce Readiness in Nigeria
abstract: This study explores the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in enhancing STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) education and workforce readiness in Nigeria. Amid rapid global technological change, Nigeria faces critical challenges in aligning its education system and labour market with AI-driven demands, including outdated curricula, infrastructural deficits, limited digital literacy, and underinvestment in teacher training. title: Quantifying SMART drumline catches in an Australian bather protection program
abstract: The global incidence of shark bites on humans has increased over time, driving the development of shark mitigation strategies to reduce the frequency of human-shark interactions. Traditional lethal shark control programs have used fishing gear aimed at reducing local shark populations. There has, however, been a shift towards more ecologically sustainable, non-lethal approaches. One such method is the SMART (Shark Management Alert in Real Time) drumline, which is designed to capture, tag and relocate target sharks. abstract: Late Triassic was not only a key episode for the evolution of the Qiangtang Basin but also a critical interval marking the final closure of the Paleo-Tethys Ocean on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. title: Metal-organic frameworks for separation of organic compounds in liquid phase
abstract: Abstract Liquid-phase separation underpins numerous sectors of modern chemical industry, yet achieving high selectivity for separation of mixtures of organic compounds remains a persistent challenge. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), showing exceptional tunability in composition, topology and pore environment, hold unique promise to address this challenge. This review surveys recent progress in studies of MOFs for the selective extraction and purification of organic substrates in liquid phase, with a focus on elucidating the mechanism of selectivity. title: Image of the City in the Age of Large Language Models: ChatGPT as a New Urban Observer
abstract: This research examines how city images of Istanbul’s Historic Peninsula are evolving with artificial intelligence and expanding user-generated content. City image refers to a mental representation of urban structure, and imageability to the ease of forming it. abstract: This article analyzes the intersection between Buddhism and artificial intelligence through a reading of Redimeidu bosang (2004) by Park Seonghwan, a Korean science fiction story in which a robot attains enlightenment in a Buddhist temple. title: Fine‐Tuning a Machine‐Learned 3D Cloud Climatology Reveals Aspects of Cloud Cover Trends
abstract: Abstract The Chalmers Cloud Ice Climatology (CCIC) is unique among long‐term cloud records: using retrievals from merged geostationary 11 μm observations, it provides continuous 3D estimates of both frozen hydrometeor mass and cloud probability. Here, we present a key update to CCIC: enhanced detection of thin clouds through tuning of its neural network cloud probability outputs. abstract: Integrated Internet of Things (IoT), blockchain, and Big Data Analytics (BDA) offer substantial potential to improve visibility, trust, coordination, and decision-making in maritime logistics. However, their combined adoption remains constrained by interdependent technological, organisational, and environmental barriers, particularly in emerging economies. abstract: The Ogasawara Islands of Japan are oceanic islands that are home to two endemic genera of lace bugs (Hemiptera, Heteroptera, Tingidae), namely, Acanthomoplax Souma & Kamitani, 2021 (Tinginae, Tingini) and Omoplax Horváth, 1912 (Tinginae, Tingini). abstract: Introduction: Academic work in higher education increasingly relies on digital tools and Artificial Intelligence (AI). For medical and nursing students, making safe, critical, and responsible use of these technologies is essential to develop self-regulated learning in the face of changing practice scenarios. title: Human-validated LLM-assisted assessment of a large-scale online precision medicine course in diabetes
abstract: Precision medicine increasingly relies on multimodal data and artificial intelligence, creating a need for scalable education and assessment. We developed an online diabetes precision medicine course and conducted an observational single-group pre–post evaluation of knowledge, confidence, and rubric-scored open-ended responses among 435 learners who completed the course. title: High-resolution mangrove mapping in Guatemala using PlanetScope imagery and a SWIR-free moisture index
abstract: Mangrove forests are ecologically and socioeconomically important ecosystems that require accurate and timely monitoring. This study presents a high-resolution mangrove mapping approach along the Pacific coast of Guatemala using PlanetScope imagery integrated with a machine-learning framework. Sentinel-2 and Landsat data were used to derive the Modular Mangrove Recognition Index (MMRI), which depends on shortwave infrared (SWIR) bands. abstract: This study aimed to analyze the evolution of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven marketing within the Ecuadorian entrepreneurial ecosystem since the COVID-19 pandemic. A systematic literature review was conducted using a qualitative approach, with a descriptive scope and a non-experimental design. title: Salt marsh porewater alkalinity varies with plant species identity and growth stage
abstract: Salt marshes are increasingly recognized as important sources of total alkalinity (TA), contributing to coastal carbon sequestration. While hydrological drivers are well studied, plant-mediated effects on TA export remain poorly constrained. Here, we assess how plant species identity and diversity influence TA production in a marsh mesocosm experiment including eight species and two- and five-species mixtures. title: Metabolic adaptation of a methanogen to a ferruginous environment associated with intracellular Fe- and S-rich nanoparticles
abstract: Across the great oxidation event (GOE) period, the oceans experienced a major transition from ferruginous (Fe 2+ -rich) to localized euxinic (HS − -rich) conditions. abstract: ABSTRACT 3 H ‐Pyrrolo[2,3‐ c ]quinoline is a typical tricyclic heterocyclic scaffold with a fused 6‐6‐5 ring system. This class of compounds exhibits outstanding medicinal and biological activities and possesses excellent metal‐ion detection performance, making it a research hotspot in medicinal and materials chemistry. abstract: ABSTRACT As digital innovation becomes increasingly organized through intercity networks, cities’ access to external knowledge, technologies, and market opportunities depends not only on local conditions but also on their positions within broader innovation networks. abstract: Background Enterococcus faecalis ( E. faecalis ) is frequently associated with persistent root canal infections and treatment failure, and effective strategies for its elimination remain limited. Plant-derived compounds may provide alternative antimicrobial strategies for endodontic treatment. abstract: Abstract Deep learning has been widely adopted in the field of bioacoustics, enabling behavioral and ecological research into many sound producing animals through the use of specially designed and trained models. So-called foundational models can generalize to novel species or tasks, but require larger and more diverse training datasets. abstract: Abstract Accurate river water level estimation is crucial for flood prevention, disaster mitigation, water resource management, and river-network regulation. However, water level variations in complex river-network regions are characterized by strong non-stationarity and nonlinearity, posing significant challenges to accurate estimation. title: Codon-aware multi-scale feature fusion for metagenomic sequence classification
abstract: Microorganisms exert profound influences on both natural ecosystems and human society. As the cornerstone of microbial research, metagenomics relies on the precise analysis of large-scale, multi-source genomic data. However, discriminating among diverse sequence types remains a formidable challenge. title: Global Long-wavelength Body-wave Catalog (GLoBoCat) for Lower Mantle P and S Wave Travel Times
abstract: Long period seismic body wave travel times are a foundational source of information regarding the Earth's interior. Manual methods provide travel time catalogs with high internal consistency, but have not kept pace with the rapid growth in teleseismic waveforms. Here we use attention-based machine learning trained on prior manual datasets to develop a catalog spanning 2010-2023 which is consistent with previous catalogs and easy to update. abstract: Information on heat-related health risks that is based on meteorological data and forecasts is important for outdoor workers, farm managers, and many other stakeholders, but visualization and interpretation of climate data in a user-friendly way remains a challenge. This proof-of-concept research developed Sol, an artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot to conveniently interpret and communicate heat stress risks through smartphones and other devices. abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate monitoring of rainfall intensity is essential for forecasting and managing floods. The surveillance video-based rainfall measurement method has potential for high spatial and temporal resolution rainfall monitoring. Existing video-based rainfall estimation models have incorporated temporal information; however, challenges remain in improving accuracy and robustness under different environmental conditions. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents a comprehensive review of live‐line work on high‐voltage transmission overhead lines, with a focus on insulation performance, air‐gap breakdown and discharge physics under realistic operating conditions. This review primarily covers journal publications from approximately 2014 to 2026, with emphasis on recent developments in the field. title: An AI-Enabled Multi-Level Governance Framework for Consulting and Research Institutes in Saudi Public Universities
abstract: This study examines the governance of institutes of studies and consulting services in Saudi public universities, which operate as hybrid entities combining academic and contract-based consulting functions. Despite their strategic role, these institutes face governance challenges, including overlapping authorities, unclear roles, and inconsistent levels of transparency and accountability. title: Reinforcement Learning‐Based Sliding Variable Optimal Control for Canonical Nonlinear Systems With Unknown Control Direction
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents a sliding variable‐based optimal control (SVBOC) framework for canonical nonlinear systems with unknown control direction. The approach integrates reinforcement learning (RL) with neural network (NN) approximation to address the challenge of solving the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) equation in systems with unknown dynamics. By constructing a sliding variable from tracking errors, the method avoids recursive backstepping steps. title: Adoption of Digitalization in Construction Safety: A TCCM-based Literature Synthesis and Development of the DSRAO Framework
abstract: Digitalization has been increasingly portrayed as a game-changing approach to enhancing construction safety through the adoption of technologies like Building Information Modelling (BIM), sensors, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and data analytics-based safety tools. abstract: Precipitation isotopes integrate the cumulative effects of moisture transport, rainout, and land–atmosphere interactions, making them valuable tracers of monsoon hydrological processes. However, the dominant controls on isotope variability differ across the Indian Summer Monsoon region. title: Exploring learning in classic African board games: a review of recent literature
abstract: Abstract A growing body of research on board games demonstrates that these games can function as learning environments and provide opportunities for learning across diverse contexts. Although learning is often conceptualized contextually within this literature, studies increasingly demonstrate that meaningful learning can occur through participation in board game environments. abstract: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) enables continuous monitoring of dynamic strain along tens of kilometres of optical fibre, generating massive datasets whose interpretation and automated analysis remain challenging. DAS data can be understood as a time-distance image array. However, the absence of standardised representation methods limits both the physical interpretability and the development of automated image-based analysis pipelines. abstract: Hardness testing is one of the most widely applied methods for evaluating the mechanical properties of metallic materials in manufacturing and quality control. Among standardized techniques, Brinell, Vickers, and Rockwell are most commonly used, all relying on precise measurement of indentation geometry. Although several recent works have used hyperspectral imaging combined with predictive models to estimate algal biomass and valuable pigments, utilizing the advantages of hyperspectral sensing to reveal key physiological spectral indices remains far less definitive in microalgae. abstract: Satellite image classification plays an important role in various applications like monitoring, surveillance, land cover planning, etc. Deep learning models with many learnable parameters face overfitting as model depth increases and have struggled to extract both fine details and broader patterns simultaneously. Parametric Model Embedding (PME) addresses this issue by constructing reduced variables from geometric information while preserving an explicit backmapping to the original design parameters. abstract: Abstract Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is being investigated for renewable-energy forecasting, optimisation, predictive maintenance, synthetic-data generation, and infrastructure planning. This study reviews global advances and critically assesses their implications for Africa's sustainable energy transition. abstract: Abstract Mixotrophs, phytoplankton capable of both phototrophy and heterotrophy, serve crucial yet complex roles in ocean food webs and carbon cycling. title: Evaluation and bias correction of reanalysis wind data for resource assessment and long-term power prediction
abstract: Reliable long-term wind-power prediction requires linking short-term mast measurements with long-term reanalysis data. This study developed integrated methodology using measurements from five coastal and near-coastal sites, four reanalysis datasets, seven Power Law exponent methods, and seven bias-correction techniques. The proposed Day–Hour Lookup-Table Power Law produced lowest average mean absolute error, root mean square error (RMSE) and standard deviation of error of 0.23, 0.35 and 0.33 m/s, respectively, and maintained relative RMSE of 4.31–6.30% during chronological hold-out validation.

title: Joule-heated regenerable carbon dioxide capture filter for demand-controlled ventilation in indoor applications
abstract: Carbon dioxide (CO2) plays a key role in indoor air quality and is traditionally managed through ventilation, which often increases energy consumption. This work proposes a demand-controlled ventilation system integrated with a CO2 filter to reduce both indoor CO2 levels and ventilation-related energy use. The modular CO2 capture filter was manufactured by spray-coating an amine-functionalized solid sorbent onto a carbon fiber substrate, enabling rapid thermal regeneration via Joule heating within 15 min at 100 °C. title: A reproducible baseline framework for Landsat satellite-based water quality modeling
abstract: Remote sensing can monitor water quality at a large scale and low cost, but many existing models are narrowly tuned and hard to generalize. To the best of our knowledge, this study introduces a reproducible, end-to-end evaluation framework for Landsat-based water quality modeling. It compares machine learning algorithms, water quality indicators, cloud-cover thresholds, temporal matching windows, and water body types using a single standardized dataset. title: Deciphering the anticorrosion performance of Arnica montana extract for mild steel in 1.5 M HCl using experimental and computational insights
abstract: The increasing demand for environmentally benign alternatives to conventional corrosion inhibitors has stimulated interest in plant-derived materials. This study explores Arnica montana extract (AME) as a sustainable corrosion inhibitor for mild steel (MS) exposed to 1.5 M HCl, employing an integrated experimental and computational strategy. The novelty of the work lies in coupling a renewable botanical inhibitor with advanced soft-computing and molecular simulation approaches to simultaneously optimise, predict, and explain corrosion inhibition behaviour. title: Geologically-inspired and mutation-aware driven well log density reconstruction method for complex heterogeneous formations
abstract: To address the issue of data distortion in traditional well log density reconstruction methods caused by harsh borehole environments in complex heterogeneous formations, and the challenge for general machine learning models to capture high-frequency abrupt change features due to the lack of geophysical constraints, this paper proposes a density curve reconstruction framework integrating geologically-inspired feature engineering and a mutation-aware mechanism. title: Training the Next Generation of Future Surgical Residents: A Scoping Review and Proposal for an Undergraduate Curriculum From the Italian Polispecialistic Society of Young Surgeons
abstract: AIM: The transition from medical school to surgical residency is marked by a persistent gap between theoretical instruction and clinical readiness. In Italy, variability in training programs across centers creates persistent gaps in residents’ medical education. Scientific societies are asked to identify current training gaps and define the core competencies required for effective surgical training. title: Understanding cell fate decisions with temporal attention
abstract: Understanding non-genetic determinants of cell fate is critical for developing and improving cancer therapies, as genetically identical cells can exhibit divergent outcomes under the same treatment conditions. In this work, we present a deep learning approach for cell fate prediction from raw long-term live-cell recordings of cancer cell populations under chemotherapeutic treatment. Our Transformer model is trained to predict cell fate directly from raw image sequences, without relying on predefined morphological or molecular features. title: Assessing Climate Change Risk Perception and Adaptation Intentions Using the Theory of Planned Behavior: Insights From a Study of Small‐Scale Fishers in Ningbo, China
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate change increasingly threatens coastal fisheries and the livelihoods of small‐scale fishers. Although the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) has been widely used to explain pro‐environmental intentions, its application to climate adaptation in fisheries remains limited, and the role of risk perception as an antecedent to the TPB constructs requires further examination. This study applies an extended TPB model in which climate change risk perception (RP) is specified as an antecedent, while political trust (PT) and environmental responsibility (ER) are examined as moderators. title: Unraveling the spatial heterogeneity of pre-summer extreme rainfall regimes in South China using multi-dimensional joint clustering
abstract: Abstract The temporal evolutions of extreme rainfall (ER) events are highly dynamic. In addition, the destructive potential of ERs is fundamentally governed by multi-dimensional metrics, including rainfall accumulation, event duration, and intra-event rain-rate evolution. However, classical ER clustering methods are based on one-dimensional metrics, therefore suffering from critical limitations and one-sidedness in characterizing ER behaviors. title: One Health Perspective of Antimicrobial Resistance: Interconnections between Humans, Animals, Food and the Environment
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is one of the most pressing global public-health threats, associated with approximately 5 million deaths in 2019 and projected to cause up to 8.22 million deaths annually by 2050 if unaddressed, with the burden falling disproportionately on low- and middle-income countries. title: Entrepreneurial Opportunity Landscape in Wealth Management – Technology-Driven Entrepreneurship
abstract: With the rapid advancement of digital technologies, such as artificial intelligence, big data, blockchain, and cloud computing, the traditional wealth management industry is undergoing profound transformation. While technology-driven innovation is reshaping wealth management service models, it has also given rise to a multitude of entrepreneurial opportunities. From a technology-driven entrepreneurship perspective, this paper integrates entrepreneurial opportunity theory to construct a three-dimensional analytical framework encompassing "Technology – Value Chain – Customer Base." title: Fully automatic trace gas plume detection
abstract: Abstract Future imaging spectrometers will expand contemporary data volumes by orders of magnitude, requiring automated methods to upscale labor-intensive detection of trace gas point sources. Here we present a fully-automated approach that achieves operational performance for plume detection and labelling without human participation. Our method combines machine learning (ML)-based morphological analysis with physics-based spectroscopic model fitting. We deploy it on data from the EMIT imaging spectrometer, operating in two modes. title: An overview of discrete element modeling for slope stability
abstract: Abstract Slope failures are among the most damaging geohazards worldwide, causing not only loss of life and infrastructure but also severe and often irreversible environmental consequences: destruction of vegetation cover and arable soil, blockage and contamination of watercourses, increased downstream sedimentation, and long-term disturbance of mountain and coastal ecosystems. Reliable stability assessment is therefore both an engineering and an environmental priority. title: From mushroom metabolome to prioritized anti-diabetic metabolite candidates: LC-MS/MS and AIDDISON™-assisted screening of Pleurotus citrinopileatus
abstract: The decline in pharmaceutical R&D productivity necessitates innovative strategies to explore nature's vast chemical diversity. Traditional natural product discovery is hampered by slow, resource-intensive methods where novel therapeutics may reside. This study introduces a high-throughput workflow integrating untargeted metabolomics with an artificial intelligence (AI) drug discovery platform to rapidly identify anti-diabetic candidates from the mushroom Pleurotus citrinopileatus . title: Meter-scale pedestrian PET and cooling-lever attribution with an ai surrogate: a microclimate digital twin for a heat-resilient Barcelona superblock
abstract: Pedestrian heat stress, expressed as physiologically equivalent temperature (PET), swings across dangerous thresholds within meters as sun, tree shade, and building shadow change, yet weather and satellite data are too coarse to resolve it, and city heat indicators do not map to what a pedestrian feels. title: A Flexible Thin‐Film Tactile Sensor for Robust Force and Position Sensing Under Extensive Deformations
abstract: ABSTRACT Electronic skins capable of precise tactile perception under large mechanical deformations are critical for the advancement of soft robotics and wearable interfaces. However, achieving force and position perception in ultrathin flexible sensors while maintaining stable performance under mechanical deformation remains challenging. Here, we present a thin‐film flexible tactile sensor that can sense normal contact force and two‐dimensional in‐plane positional information, with stable performance across a range of bent states. title: Uncertainty-Aware Mineral Prospectivity Mapping with Positive-Unlabeled Learning and Conformal Calibration: Ni Mineralization in the Yilgarn Craton
abstract: Abstract Mineral prospectivity mapping (MPM) supports exploration targeting, yet most machine learning approaches emphasize point probabilities with limited uncertainty quantification or coverage guarantees. Regional MPM faces incomplete deposit labels from biased exploration, spatial autocorrelation invalidating random cross-validation, and limited decision-relevant guidance linking probability surfaces to exploration priorities. title: Accounting for metallogenic heterogeneity in ensemble learning-based mineral prospectivity mapping: A case study of copper mineralization in eastern Junggar, Xinjiang, China
abstract: While machine learning has greatly advanced data-driven mineral exploration, its effectiveness is often limited by geological heterogeneity arising from the coexistence of multiple mineralization types within the same area. For example, in eastern Junggar, Xinjiang, China, copper deposits occur within a broadly shared regional metallogenic framework and exhibit similar surface expressions, yet different deposit types vary significantly in ore-controlling factors and geochemical signatures. title: Design and implementation of an IoT-based multimodal stress monitoring architecture using edge AI and physiological sensors
abstract: Abstract With the escalating increase in the number of stressful disorders, there is a need to design smart, intelligent, non-intrusive, and scalable solutions to support the monitoring of stress conditions in Internet of Thing (IoT) scenario. Here in this paper, an IoT-based multimodal stress sensing framework is presented with an embedded facial emotion recognition mechanism. The architecture of the proposed system can be recognized as a typical layer architecture for an IoT system: perception layer, edge intelligence layer, and application layer. title: Development of an Explainable GeoAI Wildfire Risk Analysis Model Using Multi-Source Geospatial Data
abstract: Accounting for approximately 31% of the global land surface, forests play a critical and indispensable role in sustaining ecological balance. Among the various pressures affecting forests, forest fires constitute a major environmental problem, posing significant threats to natural ecosystems while disrupting forestry activities and leading to substantial economic losses. In Türkiye, forest fires are predominantly observed in the Aegean, Mediterranean, and Marmara regions. title: Triboelectric‐Electromagnetic‐Piezoelectric System for Self‐Powered Aeolian‐Vibration Sensing and Suppression on Overhead Lines
abstract: ABSTRACT This study develops a hybrid triboelectric‐electromagnetic‐piezoelectric generator for overhead‐line applications. Integrating a multilayer spring‐mass TENG (MS‐TENG), a vertical‐reciprocating EMG (VR‐EMG), and an anti‐vibration PEG (AV‐PEG), the device unifies energy collection, vibration sensing, and adaptive damping within one platform. Operating effectively in the 5–40 Hz aeolian‐vibration band, the three modules deliver peak outputs of 272.8 V/31.2 µA/3.3 mW, 16.2 V/26.1 mA/59.7 mW, and 61.7 V/0.83 mA/9.8 mW, respectively. title: Incorporating multiple bands and land cover improves cross-sensor normalization
abstract: The Landsat archive and the Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) 2.0 virtual constellations enable monitoring of long-term and rapid environmental change with optical imagery, but differences in sensor design and atmospheric correction algorithms require cross-sensor normalization to ensure consistent observations. This study evaluates methods for such normalization using two global datasets: Landsat ETM+/OLI and HLS 2.0. title: Development of Syair-Based AI Animation Media for Suluk Hamzah Fansuri Expert Session as a Student Spiritual Education Media
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into Islamic Religious Education (PAI) offers opportunities to develop innovative learning media that support students' spiritual education. This study aims to develop AI-based animation media adapted from Hamzah Fansuri's Syair Sidang Ahli Suluk and examine students' responses to its use as a medium for spiritual education. title: Metal‐Polyphenol Network‐Based Biomaterials for Infected Bone Defects: Microenvironment Regulation and Stage‐Oriented Regenerative Strategies
abstract: Infected bone defects are not simply bone defects complicated by bacterial infection; they are dynamic pathological niches in which biofilms, intracellular bacterial persistence, oxidative stress, dysregulated immunity, vascular failure, and pathological bone remodeling are mutually reinforcing. This coupling explains why bacterial killing alone rarely restores functional bone. Metal-polyphenol networks (MPNs), assembled through reversible coordination between metal ions and polyphenols, can translate these pathological stimuli into programmable therapy. title: Temporal Trends, Inequality and Forecasting of ISP Latency in Nigeria, 2020–2023
abstract: Internet Service Providers (ISPs) experience variability and inequality in network latency, affecting service quality and user experience. This study addresses assessment of latency performance by quantifying trends, inequality, regime changes, and forecasting behaviour across ISPs. Monthly latency measurements collected from January 2020 to December 2023 were cleaned by removing zero and negative observations and summarised using descriptive statistics. title: Spatiotemporal evolution and influencing factors of regional resilience in China: evidence from provincial panel data using Spearman-CRITIC and XGBoost-CatBoost-SHAP
abstract: Regional resilience is closely related to sustainable development because it reflects the capacity of a region to maintain stable economic, social, ecological, and infrastructural functions under long-term transformation. Based on provincial panel data for China from 2007 to 2024, this study constructs a regional resilience evaluation system covering economic resilience, social development resilience, ecological and environmental resilience, and infrastructure resilience. title: ETSAM: effectively segmenting cell membranes in cryo-electron tomograms
abstract: Cryogenic Electron Tomography (cryo-ET) is an emerging experimental technique used to visualize cell structures and macromolecules in their native cellular environment. Accurate segmentation of cell structures in cryo-ET tomograms, such as cell membranes, supports the study of cellular organization and function. However, several inherent limitations in cryo-ET, including the very low signal-to-noise ratio, missing wedge artifacts from limited tilt angles, and other noise artifacts, collectively hinder the reliable identification and delineation of these structures. abstract: Introduction Traditional ascent of Mount Everest (8,848 m) typically requires 40–50 days of on-mountain acclimatization. title: Wildfire Dynamics on the Kinburn Peninsula, Ukraine, Using Sentinel-1 SAR and Optical Data (2022–2025)
abstract: Since 2022, the Kinburn Peninsula, Ukraine, has been located within an active war zone, where frequent and recurrent wildfires have affected heterogeneous coastal sandy ecosystems. Burned-area mapping in this landscape is complicated by wetlands, salt flats, exposed sands, reedbeds, artificial pine plantations, cloud cover, smoke and restricted field access. title: Sensitivity analysis of the simulation of tropical cyclone Amphan using the WRF model
abstract: The sensitivity of twenty-four physics option combinations in the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model is investigated through simulations of the track, intensity, and landfall of tropical Cyclone Amphan. Simulation accuracy is evaluated using data from an international best track archive. Track performance is assessed using root mean square error (RMSE), while intensity is evaluated by comparing the minimum sea level pressure (MSLP) and the maximum wind speed measured at a height of 10 m above sea level. title: Development and Evaluation of An Integrated AI-Based Technology for Pipelines Integrity Assessment
abstract: In this study, an integrated framework of Artificial Intelligence (AI) based Digital Twin for predictive integrity assessment, corrosion monitoring, pipeline maintenance optimization and disruption reduction was developed and evaluated for both piggable and unpiggable pipeline system under Nigeria environmental conditions. The challenges faced with pipeline corrosion, poor operational condition, vandalism, inadequate cathodic protection system and environmental hazards in shallow water, deep offshore, Niger Delta swamp and land terrain environment were the focus of the study. title: Uncertainty-aware estimation of compressive strength for fly ash concrete with enhanced probabilistic prediction performance by incorporating the associated mortar strength
abstract: Machine learning (ML) has been widely utilized to estimate the compressive strength ( f c ) of fly ash (FA) concrete due to its high efficiency and accuracy. However, the inherent variability in concrete materials introduces significant uncertainty in f c value, which traditional deterministic ML models cannot quantify. To address this engineering problem, this study proposes to adopt natural gradient boosting (NGBoost), a renowned probabilistic ML model, to estimate f c for FA concrete. title: Remote Sensing and Geospatial Approach for Land Degradation Risk Assessment in the Costa Verde Bay Southeast of Brazil
abstract: This study evaluates land degradation risk in Brazil’s Costa Verde by adapting the United Nations Environment Program, Priority Actions Program Regional Activity Centre (PAP/RAC) methodology for the first time to a humid tropical coastal environment. Unlike previous applications confined to semi-arid and Mediterranean contexts, this research integrates the PAP/RAC framework with 40 years of multi-source remote sensing data (Landsat 5/8/9; 1985–2025), land use/land cover change detection, and Mann–Kendall trend analysis, a hybrid approach that has not previously been applied in this biome. title: Land Use and Land Cover Dynamics in Dinajpur District: Spatio-Temporal Trends and Future Scenario Using Google Earth Engine and CA–Markov Modeling
abstract: Investigation on the detection and prediction of changes in land use and land cover (LULC) is essential for reinforcing sustainable management and planning. As a result, the purpose of this research was to discover LULC changes in the Dinajpur area of Bangladesh between 2000 and 2020, as well as anticipate future changes for 2040. Landsat-5, 7, 8, and 9 pictures, as well as vegetation indices and topographic parameters, were used to classify LULCs in 2000, 2005, 2010, and 2020. title: Factorized-gating mixture of experts enables cross-regime turbulence modeling
abstract: Predicting turbulent flows is vital for advancing aerospace, energy, and environmental technologies, yet remains critically limited by the accuracy of turbulence models. While machine learning has led to the widespread development of data-driven turbulence models, existing approaches predominantly rely on monolithic dense networks that struggle to generalize across diverse flow regimes. To address this challenge, we introduce the factorized-gating mixture of experts (FG-MoE) framework, where regime-specific experts are trained and blended via spatially varying probabilities. title: Twenty years of Kilimanjaro observations across 5000 m reveal tropical elevation-dependent warming under clear-sky conditions
abstract: Abstract Mountain regions are experiencing rapid climate change. However, temperature trends along elevation gradients remain poorly understood in the tropics, where long-term high-elevation air temperature ( T air ) observations are sparse. Here, we examine elevation-dependent warming (EDW) on Mount Kilimanjaro by combining a unique long-term in situ T air transect with Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) land-surface temperature (LST), surface and topographic datasets. Using machine learning, we map clear-sky T air at four MODIS overpasses at 1 km resolution for 2004–2024.

title: Does public attention effectively reduce climate risk vulnerability? Evidence from 30 Chinese Provinces from 2012 to 2022
abstract: Purpose In the context of intensifying global climate risks and increasingly frequent extreme weather events, enhancing climate adaptation capacity and strengthening risk management have become urgent tasks for governments and the public. The purpose of this study is to examine the effect of public climate attention on provincial climate vulnerability across Chinese provinces.
