title: Hydrodynamic Modeling of Maximum Tidal Levels at the Tondano River Estuary
abstract: The Tondano River Estuary is an area affected by the interaction of tides, currents, winds, and bathymetric conditions that affect sea level and hydrodynamic conditions of the coastal area. This study aims to analyze the maximum tidal height at the Tondano River Estuary using the MIKE 21 Flow Model (FM). The study was conducted using a quantitative approach, employing numerical hydrodynamic modeling that integrated bathymetry, coastline, tides, and wind data into a flexible mesh domain. title: Sea-level contribution from Thwaites Glacier doubles in an observation-constrained ice-sheet model
abstract: Thwaites Glacier is a major contributor to Antarctic mass loss and a key source of uncertainty in future sea-level rise. Ocean-driven melting at its grounding line drives rapid retreat, yet most models treat the transition between grounded and floating ice as a sharp boundary, neglecting kilometer-scale seawater intrusions that develop as the grounding line migrates and forms a grounding zone. title: Differential Impacts of Proxy Archives on Paleoclimate Reconstruction Performance
abstract: Abstract Reconstructing past climates is challenging because pre‐instrumental observations are geographically sparse and proxy records are noisy; data assimilation offers one approach to address these limitations. Although such reconstructions are now widespread, the extent to which different proxy archives determine their accuracy remains unclear. title: Impact of grid resolution on the abyssal ocean representation in numerical models
abstract: Abstract. Accurately representing abyssal water masses and their inter-basin pathways remains a challenge for global ocean models and reanalyses. In this study, we investigate how horizontal and vertical resolution influence the simulation of abyssal waters by first evaluating three ocean reanalyses and one forward ocean model, focusing on Antarctic Bottom Water pathways from the Weddell Sea to the Argentine and Brazil basins and through the Vema Channel. title: Benchmarking time-series foundation models for multitask predictive maintenance in digital twins
abstract: Digital twins provide a comprehensive virtual representation of physical assets, distinguishing themselves from traditional control systems through long-term diagnostic and prognostic capabilities. However, current digital twin architectures face a critical scalability barrier: they rely on dedicated, single-purpose models for every distinct query, task, physical scale, and operating context, resulting in unsustainable engineering overhead. title: Digital twins across the ship lifecycle: Implementation patterns, MBSE integration, and contributions to ship maintenance
abstract: This study aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the current technological landscape regarding Digital Twins (DT) in the shipbuilding industry, including their integration with Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) and their effects on maintenance. The maritime industry is characterized by high levels of asset complexity and long lifecycles, which often result in information gaps and a heavy reliance on reactive maintenance practices. title: Improving large-scale river routing models with ESA long-term CCI discharge data assimilation: advancing accuracy for climate studies
abstract: Abstract. Large scale hydrological models like CTRIP and MGB are essential for simulating river dynamics and supporting large-scale climate studies. Their accuracy can be significantly improved through satellite data assimilation. This study leverages 20 years of high-resolution discharge data (2000–2020) from the ESA Climate Change Initiative (CCI) to enhance CTRIP and MGB models via ensemble Kalman Filter frameworks (HyDAS and HYFAA). title: Reassessing Methanesulfonic Acid as a Sea Ice Proxy: An Example From the Weddell Sea Sector
abstract: Abstract Antarctic sea ice has declined since 2015, but placing this trend in a longer‐term context remains challenging. Ice core methanesulfonic acid (MSA) offers a potential record of sea ice variability beyond the instrumental period, yet its applicability in sectors including the Weddell Sea remains unclear. We present an MSA record from the Gomez ice core on the southwest Antarctic Peninsula and combine air mass back‐trajectories and satellite observations to reassess the MSA‐sea ice relationship. title: Biomarkers and diatoms as tracers of phytoplankton communities and past sea ice conditions in the southwestern Ross Sea, Antarctica: drivers and variability over the last 200 years
abstract: Abstract. The Ross Sea, Antarctica, is among the most seasonally productive areas globally, where different classes of phytoplankton, such as diatoms and haptophytes (Phaeocystis antarctica), play key roles in marine ecosystems and the carbon cycle. Sea ice dynamics strongly influence Ross Sea phytoplankton blooms, yet the effects of recent sea ice changes on bloom composition and productivity remain poorly constrained. title: Antarctic sea ice over the past 130 000 years – Part 2: A review of its role in the Earth system
abstract: Abstract. Antarctic sea-ice cover reached historically low levels in 2023, consistent with the simulated decrease in sea-ice extent in response to anthropogenic warming. Antarctic sea ice is closely linked to multiple components of the Earth system, thus its demise could precipitate widespread, cascading changes across the cryosphere, atmosphere, and ocean. title: Digital Twin-Based Environmental and Safety Management Framework for Sustainable Oil & Gas Facilities and Construction Projects in Saudi Arabia
abstract: Digital twins are increasingly used as operational interfaces that connect physical assets, engineering models, and instantaneous data. However, their environmental and safety benefits remain fragmented in oil and gas and construction research. This review develops an integrative framework for Saudi Arabian facilities and projects, where rapid infrastructure delivery, challenging climate, and high-risk operations require proactive risk management. title: Seasonal and Interannual Variability of Coastal Black Sea Waters off Bulgaria (2022–2025): A Copernicus Marine Reanalysis Assessment
abstract: This study assessed spatial, seasonal, and interannual variability in physical and biogeochemical indicators in surface waters along the Bulgarian Black Sea coast during 2022–2025 to provide an integrated characterization of coastal marine conditions. Copernicus Marine Level 4 multiyear reanalysis products at 0.025° × 0.025° resolution were aggregated into four climatological seasons and summarized for a 25 km coastal strip divided at Cape Emine into northern and southern sectors. title: Quantifying Deep Ocean Methane Along the Central Chilean Margin
abstract: Abstract Cold seeps are dynamic seafloor environments that provide conduits for methane (CH 4 ) to be transferred from marine sediments to the global ocean and, in shallow settings, the atmosphere. These seeps are ubiquitous along continental margins yet their spatial extent and impact on the marine carbon cycle are poorly constrained. During a research expedition to the underexplored Chilean Margin, we utilized an ROV‐mounted in situ CH 4 sensor and multibeam sonar to map seep fields. title: Steric‐Setup Effects on US East Coast Sea‐Level Change
abstract: Abstract The extent to which coastal sea levels co‐vary with open‐ocean variability is explored through evaluation of a balanced dynamics framework relating sea level with pressure, density, and velocity along the continental shelf and slope seafloor. Using high‐resolution regional ocean model output, we develop and evaluate this relationship at 34 stations along the US East Coast. title: Recent warming and stratification changes in the southern Tyrrhenian Sea
abstract: Warming of the upper ocean is expected to strengthen stratification and reduce the efficiency of wind-driven mixing, affecting water-column stability, nutrient supply, biological productivity, and oxygen ventilation. Despite its importance in the climate system and its rapid change, long-term observations of water column stratification remain limited in the Mediterranean Sea. abstract: As Earth system science moves toward global-domain and multi-sphere coupling, traditional two-dimensional spatial information frameworks can no longer fully meet the integrated spatial computing demands of deep space, deep Earth, and deep ocean applications. Building on research in Discrete Global Grid Systems (DGGS), this paper provides a comprehensive review of Earth System Spatial Grid (ESSG) for three-dimensional Earth system modeling. title: Impact of Assimilating Remote Sensing Observations on Wind and Wave Analysis Offshore of the Contiguous United States
abstract: This study assesses the impact of assimilating remote sensing observations of significant wave height (SWH) and 10 m wind speed (WSPD) into the analysis using a weakly coupled data assimilation (WCDA) framework to improve ocean surface monitoring offshore of the Contiguous US (CONUS). title: Impact resistance of an enhanced auxetic steel system under high-velocity impact loading
abstract: Abstract Vehicle-borne improvised devices (VBIDs) represent a severe threat in terrorist attacks due to their combined impact and explosive effects. Protection systems may lose effectiveness when first subjected to high-impact forces from VBIDs or high-velocity projectiles before subsequent blasts. title: The Influence of Sea‐Land Breeze on the Circulation and Air‐Sea Thermodynamics of the Mississippi Sound and Bight

abstract: Introduction . abstract: Coral reefs are one of the most biologically diverse ecosystems in the ocean, but are now under increasing threat from climate related ocean warming. While numerous studies have focused on the impact of sea surface temperature (SST) on coral reef condition, those that specifically looked into whether long-term background SST variability had an impact on reef stability have had conflicting results, with some analyses showing negligible association and others showing significant associations. abstract: Nature-based Solutions are increasingly considered for protecting eroding coasts, yet the conversion of wave attenuation by submerged vegetation into a measurable reduction of nearshore erosion remains only partly quantified. title: Chlorophyll extremes during a surface marine heatwave in a seasonally stratified shelf sea
abstract: Abstract Marine heatwaves are increasing in frequency and intensity globally against a background of long-term climate warming, yet their impacts on subsurface biogeochemistry in temperate shelf seas remain poorly constrained. Here, we present high-resolution in situ observations of chlorophyll during a Category IV marine heatwave in June 2023, collected using an autonomous ocean glider in a seasonally stratified shelf sea. abstract: High-resolution marine environmental fields are essential for ocean monitoring, forecasting, and coastal applications, but the spatial resolution of reanalysis products may be insufficient for representing localized gradients and fine-scale structures. title: Interpreting Air Temperature Trends Across the Antarctic Peninsula Between 1979 and 2025
abstract: Abstract The near‐surface temperature of the Antarctic Peninsula is marked by strong spatio‐temporal variability. In situ observations are scarce and therefore have limited spatial coverage. Furthermore, ERA‐5 reanalysis does not have a sufficient spatial resolution to capture the steep topography and other climate gradients of the peninsula. abstract: Frequent tropical cyclones in the North Indian Ocean significantly disrupt coastal and marine environments. This study integrates multi-platform datasets – including satellites, Argo floats, moored buoys, and tide gauges – to analyze the ocean‒atmosphere response to four 2024 cyclones: Remal, Asna, Dana, and Fengal. abstract: Global climate change and intensifying marine heatwaves contribute to abrupt fishery collapses. abstract: Recent observations in the eastern Arabian Sea reveal the persistent presence of surface-floating tarballs along India's west coast from May to December. title: Integrated retrieval of ocean surface wind and current fields from single-geometry SAR observations through a physically constrained Bayesian framework
abstract: Ocean surface winds and currents are coupled through air–sea interaction but are commonly retrieved independently from spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR). abstract: Abstract. abstract: Estimating eruption source parameters is critical for volcanic hazard assessments and understanding eruptive dynamics. title: The development and persistence of doldrums over the Great Barrier Reef
abstract: Abstract. Marine heatwaves and coral bleaching pose significant threats to the Great Barrier Reef (GBR), particularly during austral summer when atmospheric conditions can significantly enhance ocean surface warming. One such condition is the development of doldrums, characterised by weak winds and reduced cloud cover, which promote increased solar heating of the ocean surface. abstract: Marine and terrestrial ecosystems are usually treated as separate components of the global carbon cycle, and whether variability in ocean biology reaches plant growth on land has remained unclear. title: Contribution of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation to Global Mean Sea Level Trends: Revisited
abstract: Abstract Three decades of satellite altimeter observations reveal a continued rise in global mean sea level (GMSL), with the rate of rise reflecting the combined effects of decadal variability and long‐term warming. abstract: The biological pump (BP) constitutes a key component of the global carbon cycle by mediating the export of organic carbon from the surface ocean to the deep sea. abstract: Abstract Microplastics (MPs) are an emerging environmental concern owing to their widespread presence and ecological impacts. abstract: Abstract. This paper introduces EnviFlux, which is a software tool (written in C++) to study the inverse problem of estimating the distribution of fluxes of a trace gas at the Earth's surface. This is done using a four-dimensional variational technique, which combines information from (i) synthetic observations of the trace gas spanning a defined time window, (ii) a transport model linking the initial concentration and surface fluxes to predictions of the observations, and (iii) a-priori information. abstract: The performance of a full-scale top-hinged flap-type wave energy converter in the open sea is analyzed numerically in this study. title: Land-atmosphere feedback amplifies circulation-dominant fire weather risk over eastern Siberia
abstract: Wildfires in eastern Siberia have intensified significantly in recent decades. abstract: Karenia brevis, a harmful algal bloom (HAB) organism behind Florida’s red tide, persists in the Gulf of Mexico year-round at low concentrations. title: Constrained optimal control and hydrodynamic scaling of the RM3 two-body point absorber
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive hydrodynamic and multiscale optimization framework for the Reference Model 3 wave energy converter deployed at the La Serena site, Chile. abstract: Groundwater flow modeling in urban areas is of great importance in the context of water level depletion due to the high population, unplanned urbanization and industrial growth. In N’Djamena, groundwater is the main source of drinking water. Under these conditions, groundwater flow modeling is essential to better understand the dynamics and behavior of the urban groundwater system of the city. abstract: Abstract. This study investigates the structure-acoustic coupling characteristics of a novel deepwater pressure hull, idealized as a triple spherical shell. abstract: The East Asian summer front (EASF) plays a key role in regional precipitation and heat stress, yet its long-term positional changes remain poorly understood. abstract: Near-inertial currents (NICs) play a key role in surface material redistribution and ocean mixing, yet their long-term variability remains poorly known. abstract: Abstract The El Niño‐Southern Oscillation is a dominant driver of Pacific‐North American (PNA) variability on seasonal‐to‐interannual timescales through its influence on tropical Pacific convection. abstract: Maritime transportation in the western part of the Black Sea is strongly affected by meteorological conditions such as wind, waves, and visibility. title: Integrated Structural Assessment of an Industrial Port Jetty under Vessel Upgrading in Gresik
abstract: Increasing the vessel class at an existing jetty can be governed by structural resistance, lateral pile response, marine equipment, or water depth. This study evaluates a 10,000 DWT pile-supported precast dry-bulk jetty at Industrial Port, Gresik, for 20,000, 30,000, and 40,000 DWT vessels. The assessment used project drawings, vessel particulars, bathymetry, borehole and SPT records, metocean data, finite element modelling, reinforced-concrete capacity checks, pile axial and lateral evaluation, fender and bollard screening, and a finite element method model. title: Numerical investigation on the hydrodynamic behaviour of a wind-solar-aquaculture integrated floating structure
abstract: To address the challenges of spatial competition, high construction costs, and cumulative environmental impacts associated with traditional single-function offshore resource development, this study proposes an innovative wind-solar-aquaculture integrated structure named “AquaEnergy”. The system integrates floating offshore wind turbines, aquaculture cages, and floating photovoltaic panels within the same marine area, enabling the synergistic development of renewable energy and aquaculture while promoting green and low-carbon utilisation of ocean resources. title: Sea Cucumber‐Inspired Double‐Network Biopolymer Hydrogels for Programmable Soft Machines
abstract: Engineering biopolymer-based hydrogels with robust load-bearing capacity, reversible mechanical programmability, and adaptive actuation remains difficult due to weak physical crosslinking and porous structure. Inspired by the mutable dermis of sea cucumbers, a collagen-alginate double-network elastomeric (CoDE) hydrogel integrates a covalently crosslinked collagen cryogel scaffold with an ionically crosslinked alginate sacrificial network. title: Hybrid Multi‐Gateway Authentication Protocol for 6LoWPAN‐Based Marine Wireless Sensor Networks
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper proposes a secure and efficient three‐factor authentication scheme to address the security issues in the integration scenario of multi‐gateway wireless sensor networks (WSNs) and 6LoWPAN in marine Internet of Things (IoT). Existing approaches exhibit vulnerabilities to cryptographic breaches, single‐point failures, high computational costs, and inefficient long‐distance transmission in maritime settings. To mitigate these limitations, we integrate blockchain technology, elliptic curve cryptography (ECC), the Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT), and a dynamic credential update m

title: Characteristics and Ambient Conditions of Mesoscale Convective Systems Moving Offshore in the Yangtze‐Huai River Basin, East China
abstract: Abstract This work for the first time studies the characteristics and environment conditions of mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) that move offshore (i.e., land to sea, LS) in the Yangtze‐Huai River Basin (YHRB), East China. In the warm season (April–September), LS MCSs account for 25.5% of the total MCSs, exhibiting a decreasing trend from spring (April–May) to later summer (August–September). LS MCSs most frequently occur from late morning to early evening. title: Modeling the dynamic responses of a 2 × 2 gravity-type fish cage group under combined wave-current conditions
abstract: The hydrodynamic response of gravity-type cage groups under harsh open-ocean sea states is closely linked to long-term production safety. However, severe wave-current forcing may produce response transitions and internal load-path changes that remain insufficiently resolved for interconnected cage groups. This study develops a numerical model of a 2 × 2 cage group using the lumped-mass method and examines how wave height (H), wave period (T), and angle of attack (α) govern its motion responses, volume loss rate, and mooring tensions. The model is validated against published experiments for net

title: Rockfall hazard assessment at Baia Castle cliff (Phlegrean Fields, Italy): implications for cultural heritage sites in a seismically active volcanic area
abstract: Coastal cliffs developed in volcanic tuffs are highly susceptible to instability due to the combined effects of structural discontinuities, marine erosion, and seismic activity. This study presents a multi-method assessment of rockfall hazard at the Baia Castle cliff (Phlegrean Fields, southern Italy), an area affected by ongoing bradyseism and with a significant cultural heritage exposure. UAV-based photogrammetry, field structural surveys, and geomechanical characterisation were integrated to reconstruct the geometry and discontinuity network of the cliff. title: Catching fire – On cremations in Late Iron Age Åland Islands, Baltic sea
abstract: The cremation was an important part of the mortuary rituals in Late Iron Age Åland Islands, c.550–1050 CE. More than 10 000 burial mounds with cremations found in c.440 farmstead cemeteries are known from the Åland Islands. The burial practice is characteristic of those common in Eastern Sweden. We here analyse how the cremation was carried out, considering detailed macroscopic analyses of the level of calcination of the cremated remains of humans and included animals. title: Regional Trends in Northern Hemisphere Summer Extratropical Cyclone Activity and Their Link to Precipitation and Temperature Trends
abstract: Abstract In recent years a robust weakening of the storm tracks has been identified in reanalysis data. This trend has been linked to coinciding changes in surface temperature extremes and precipitation over land. Here we use a surface‐based metric to quantify regional trends in the boreal summertime low‐level extratropical cyclone activity (ECA) and link this to surface impacts. We compare trends over the satellite‐era across a single model large ensemble (SPEAR‐MED Large Ensemble) and the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) simulations, including full and single forcing sim
institutions: NSF National Center for Atmospheric Research

title: Predicting environmental health-related search patterns using freely available digital and reanalysis data: A critical evaluation of Google Trends and global datasets for Morocco
abstract: Climate change and environmental degradation increasingly threaten urban public health, yet monitoring infrastructure is often unavailable in resource-constrained settings. This study develops and critically evaluates a machine learning framework that predicts environmental health-related search behavior , used as a low-cost digital proxy rather than a measure of clinical burden, in Morocco using exclusively open-access global datasets. We integrated five years of weekly data (April 2020 to April 2025) from ERA5 meteorological reanalysis, Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service products, and

title: TREND AND ANOMALY OF TEMPERATURE SERIES IN WEST AFRICAN COASTAL URBAN AREAS: THE CASE OF ABIDJAN, CÔTE D'IVOIRE (1985-2024)
abstract: Climate change is accompanied by a growing intensification of temperatures at the local scale, as observed in several cities of the sub-region, yet their evolution and trends remain insufficiently quantified. This study aims to examine the trends and anomalies of temperatures in the city of Abidjan over the period 1985-2024. Daily maximum (TX), minimum (TN), and mean (TM) temperature data, provided by SODEXAM, were analyzed using the Mann-Kendall trend test combined with Sen's slope, as well as an anomaly index calculated relative to the 1985-2024 climatological normal. journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: Revisiting how the euphotic depth is computed
abstract: The method of computing the euphotic depth, the depth horizon in the ocean above which light is sufficient for net primary production, has lacked consensus in the literature. Although many still use a % light level as a definition, a practice which dominates textbooks in oceanography, the modeling community uses a constant basal respiration to set the threshold. Following Banse (2004), we remind the readers that phytoplankton only sense absolute irradiance level, and recommend the use of a fixed value, named the ’compensation irradiance’, to define this layer. title: Investigation of Flow Structures in an Aquaculture Tank Under Rolling Excitation Using Statistical Analysis and Proper Orthogonal Decomposition
abstract: Large-scale offshore aquaculture vessels provide an effective approach for expanding marine aquaculture; however, the complex flow characteristics induced by water circulation systems and vessel motion remain insufficiently understood. In this study, a numerical model based on the volume of fluid (VOF) method and the k-ω SST-DES turbulence model was developed to investigate the vortex flow characteristics. The developed numerical model accurately captured the vortex flow characteristics and free-surface fluctuations in the aquaculture tank, and the dominant coherent structures were identified

title: Effects of wind-wave misalignment on motion responses of a floating wind turbine with a shared-anchor mooring system
abstract: Wind-wave misalignment significantly affects the dynamic responses of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs). A fully coupled aero-hydro-mooring numerical model was established in OrcaFlex for a FOWT with a three-line shared-anchor mooring system. The numerical analysis evaluated three representative sea states (LC1, LC2, and LC3) alongside multiple wind-wave heading combinations. title: Nonlinear dynamics of time-variable slope circulation
abstract: Abstract. Bottom topography strongly constrains ocean circulation in the Arctic, and both theory and numerical modeling suggest that nonlinear flow–topography interactions influence slope-following currents. Yet, how such interactions modify the circulation response to time-variable surface forcing remains poorly understood. Using idealized shallow-water simulations of flow over a corrugated slope in a re-entrant channel, we investigate how nonlinear features arise and evolve under oscillatory forcing. title: Long-term spatio-temporal assessment of thermal comfort in Antalya (Türkiye) using the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI)
abstract: Climate change and the increasing frequency of extreme heat events have intensified thermal stress, particularly in Mediterranean regions, posing significant challenges to human health, quality of life, and sustainable urban development. Therefore, accurate assessment of outdoor thermal comfort has become increasingly important for supporting climate adaptation and planning strategies. This study aims to investigate the long-term (2000–2025) spatio-temporal changes of thermal comfort in Antalya (Türkiye) using the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI). title: Thermal–Fluid–Solid Coupling Analysis of Enhanced Heat Transfer and Thermal Stress in Shark Skin Micro-Rib Tubes
abstract: A multi-field coupled numerical model integrating fluid flow, convective heat transfer, and thermal stress is established for a shark-skin-inspired V-shaped micro-rib heat exchange tube. Using the shear stress transport (SST) k-ω model, its thermal–hydraulic performance is compared with a smooth tube, revealing the mechanism of vortex-induced thermal boundary layer disturbance. Based on an L32 orthogonal array and range analysis, the sensitivity of seven geometric parameters to pressure drop and heat transfer power is quantified. title: Turbulence and mixing along a microtidal and stratified estuary-shelf transition
abstract: Abstract. This study investigates the hydrodynamic and mixing processes at the estuary–shelf transition of a microtidal system, and the buoyant plume generated at the Patos Lagoon mouth (Brazil). Using measurements of turbulent kinetic energy (TKE) dissipation (ϵ), current velocities, salinity, and temperature collected during a high-discharge period (∼9,400 m³ s-1), we characterize the spatial evolution of turbulence and mixing along the channel, from the source to the buoyancy-driven plume region. title: A numerical study on scaling relations for field-scale scour development at pile foundations
abstract: Local erosion around foundation elements, generally referred to as ’scour’, is of major concern when designing hydraulic structures. When placed in natural open water systems, these structures influence the local dynamics of the flow and bed, which could result in lowering of the embedment level, with potentially severe consequences. The majority of knowledge on scour originates from laboratory experiments, which are inevitably associated with scaling conflicts. The absence of full-scale scour development data might be complemented with results from numerical modelling on typical field scale d

title: Record-setting heavy precipitation occurrence in 2024
abstract: Precipitation extremes have increased globally in recent decades, consistent with a warming climate. We find that 2024 experienced a record-high frequency of heavy (≥99th percentile; F P≥99 ) precipitation events globally based on MSWEP (Multi-Source Weighted-Ensemble Precipitation) observations from 1979 to 2025. This extends a long-term trend of ∼0.03%/decade in F P≥99 , with similar but more uncertain increases for the 99.9th percentile. title: Effect of hydrostatic pressure on transport-reaction processes of cement paste under sulfate attack
abstract: Cementitious materials in deep-sea environments may be simultaneously subjected to hydrostatic pressure and sulfate exposure, leading to coupled transport–reaction processes that differ from those under conventional sulfate attack. In this study, laboratory exposure experiments and numerical simulations were combined to investigate the effects of hydrostatic pressure on sulfate transport and AFt formation in cement paste. The results show that increasing hydrostatic pressure markedly enhances sulfate ingress, resulting in greater penetration depths and higher sulfate contents within the cement

title: A numerical forecast for birch and grasses pollen concentration in Germany
abstract: Prevention of pollen exposure is a way to assist allergic individuals to better cope with their disease. To enable this prevention, a prediction of next day(s) pollen flight is needed. The most accurate predictions are from numerical models which calculate the expected airborne pollen concentrations using simulation of emission combined with atmospheric dispersal processes (as in the SILAM model). However, current numerical models are based on historical averages and make predictions for the whole of Europe, which is not always optimal for a specific location. title: Beyond Linear Regression: A Non-Linear Hygroscopic Growth Correction for Satellite-Derived PM2.5 Estimation in Tropical Environments
abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) estimation from satellite-derived Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) is often biased in humid tropical environments because aerosol water uptake enhances optical extinction without a corresponding increase in dry particulate mass. This study develops a physics-informed, non-linear AOD-to-PM2.5 conversion framework that explicitly accounts for hygroscopic growth. Four years (2020–2023; N = 1.456 daily observations) of AOD, PM2.5, and relative humidity (RH) data from the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) global reanalysis over Jakarta, Indonesia, were used
journal: Indonesian Journal of Environmental Management and Sustainability

title: Cyber-Physical Testing of Wind-Assisted Ships: Recent Developments and Open Data Set for the SOBC-1 Bulk Carrier
abstract: Abstract This paper presents recent improvements in the cyber-physical test method for wind-assisted ships at SINTEF Ocean. In particular, a dynamic lifting line method, that interacts in real-time with the physical ship model, enables now modelling transient aerodynamic effects, sail-hull interaction, and sail-sail interactions. The behaviour of a free-running wind-assisted ship can therefore accurately be documented also during sudden changes in wind velocity or other transient conditions. title: Drivers governing the seasonality of new particle formation in the Arctic
abstract: Abstract. New particle formation (NPF) is the phenomenon wherein gaseous precursors form critical clusters of barely a few nanometres in diameter, after which, under favourable conditions these particles can grow to climate-relevant sizes. Here we present measurements from 2022 to 2024 of particle and ion number size distributions from the Zeppelin Observatory (ZEP), an Arctic research station situated on the western edge of Svalbard. title: Three-dimensional kinematic open boundaries for multi-directional wave simulations in SPH
abstract: Mesh-free Lagrangian methods including smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) are ideal for complex ocean engineering involving large free-surface deformations, yet their high computational cost in 3D large-scale domains remains a barrier. Hybrid coupling strategies combine mesh-based far-field solvers with near-field SPH to offer a solution; however, a core challenge has been maintaining consistent free-surface tracking along 3D interfaces under multi-directional waves. title: A VFIFE-based non-contact monitoring approach for mooring line tension in floating offshore wind turbines
abstract: The safety of mooring systems is critical for Floating Offshore Wind Turbines (FOWTs), yet contact-based tension monitoring suffers from difficult installation, susceptibility to damage and limited long-term reliability. This study proposes a non-contact monitoring method based on the Vector Form Intrinsic Finite Element (VFIFE), which determines mooring tension from the measured motion of the floating platform. institutions: State Key Laboratory of Coastal and Offshore Engineering

title: Predicting winter cold surge scenarios using ensemble forecasting and clustering techniques
abstract: East Asian cold surges develop through several distinct spatiotemporal evolution patterns, each characterized by a different intensity and duration. Beyond forecasting whether a cold surge will occur, anticipating which type will develop would allow the likely evolution scenario to be foreseen in advance, providing valuable lead time for disaster preparedness. title: A Bayesian MCMC approach for snow density estimation from SMOS over the Northern Hemisphere
abstract: Snow density is a key parameter for calculating snow water equivalent, snow albedo, snow emissivity, and snow mechanical properties. It is therefore essential in water resource management, snow-air energy exchange computation, cold regions engineering design, and avalanche prevention. In a warming climate, snow density is undergoing rapid changes, which pose challenges for static snow density evolution equations in predicting spatiotemporal variability. journal: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

title: Vízi és víz alatti járművek csatolt vibroakusztikai modellezése
abstract: A víz alatti kisugárzott zaj (underwater radiated noise, URN) predikciója a haditechnikai alkalmazásokban és a tengeri környezet védelmében egyaránt stratégiai jelentőségű. A szakirodalom és a szabványosítási gyakorlat alapján az URN nem értelmezhető pusztán hidrodinamikai jelenségként: a gerjesztések, a szerkezeti rezgések és a vízterhelés csatolt vibroakusztikai multifizikai (multiphysics) rendszerként határozzák meg a távoli térben mérhető hangnyomásszintet. title: Downside-risk pre-positioning for resilient scheduling of an off-grid deep-offshore electricity-hydrogen integrated energy system under extreme weather
abstract: An off-grid deep-offshore electricity-hydrogen integrated energy system (DOEH-IES) provides a practical carrier for onsite offshore wind utilization and multi-energy coordination. However, under typhoon conditions, coupled wind-wave effects and platform motion reduce the available power of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs), introducing a time-varying downside risk that conventional scheduling methods often fail to mitigate proactively. title: Secular polar motion from non-surface-loading processes estimated using satellite gravimetry
abstract: SUMMARY Polar motion (PM) provides an independent, observation-based constraint on global mass redistribution, but interpretation of its long-term variability is primarily limited by uncertainty in the glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA) contribution, for which conventional model-based estimates exhibit substantial differences. Here we develop a refined approach that uses primarily GRACE and GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO) observations to estimate the secular PM associated with non-surface-loading processes, predominantly GIA. title: Methodology for a human-centric CIM: Translating non-geocoded citizen perceptions into spatial indicators
abstract: To address the growing complexity between the built environment and urban life, modern urban planning has increasingly relied on digital technologies for decision-making, including City Information Modeling (CIM). While CIM has matured from standards and data integration to real-time analytics and digital twins, most initiatives optimize physical systems while struggling to incorporate “intangible” citizen-generated data. title: Contrast in the Boundary Layer Convergence Lines at Desert−Oasis Border With Different Vegetation Gradient
abstract: Abstract Motivated by an observed asymmetry in boundary layer convergence lines (BLCLs) between the Kubuqi and Ulan Buh desert borders of the Hetao Oasis in northern China, this work aims to document the differences in BLCL frequency and convective initiation and their potential drivers. Using radar, surface Automatic Weather Station, and reanalysis data in June–August from 2012 to 2022, we found that the Kubuqi border had more frequent, earlier‐forming, and more convective BLCLs, whereas the Ulan Buh border had fewer, shorter‐lived, and more tortuous ones. title: A Generation Mechanism of Thorpe‐Detected Turbulence: A Case Study Using WRF Model Simulation
abstract: Abstract Turbulence in the free atmosphere has been widely estimated using the Thorpe method, which identifies vertical inversions in potential temperature profiles as evidence of overturning. However, the mechanisms driving Thorpe‐detected turbulence remain poorly understood, due largely to limitations in spatial and temporal resolution of observational and reanalysis datasets. This study presents the first real‐case numerical simulation of Thorpe‐detected turbulence using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model. title: Contrasting Effects of Turbulence on Tropical Cyclones During Landfall
abstract: Abstract Planetary boundary layer (PBL) turbulence modulates tropical cyclone (TC) intensity through competing mechanisms: (a) frictional dissipation that weakens TCs and (b) frictional convergence that drives stronger low‐level inflow and intensifies TCs. Three landfalling TCs (Beryl, Francine, and Milton) were simulated to examine how enhanced PBL turbulence affects TC intensity during landfall. title: Materials and architected structures for underbody blast mitigation in armoured fighting vehicles: From conventional protection systems to additively manufactured metallic lattices
abstract: Armoured Fighting Vehicles (AFVs) must survive distinct but interacting threat classes, including kinetic-energy and armour-piercing projectiles, shaped-charge jets, high-velocity fragments, top-attack munitions, and buried mine/IED blast. This review therefore positions underbody energy absorbers within the wider layered protection architecture, while deliberately focusing its detailed assessment on mine/IED blast mitigation. title: Modeling and optimization of battery-based energy storage systems for UAVs
abstract: The paper presents the improvement of the energy efficiency of drones used in different missions. In this paper, a model for Li-ion batteries is created, made through equivalent electrical circuits. This method facilitates the examination of the relationship between the required energy consumption and the electrical response of the battery to demands. title: Observations of Gravity Wave Packets Using a Multiple Balloon, Multiple Linear Regression Technique
abstract: Abstract Typical climate model resolutions preclude the explicit simulation of most of the spectrum of atmospheric gravity waves (GWs). Climate models must therefore rely on GW parameterizations, which observations help constrain. Between 2011 and 2021, Loon LLC launched thousands of balloons, some of which flew close enough together to be affected by the same GW packet. These groups provide sufficient information to estimate the wavenumbers of GW packets. We identify 23 distinct GW packets seen by groups of four or more balloons using Wavelet analysis. Contrasting drivers of summer extreme hourly precipitation over the southeastern and northeastern Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Abstract Extreme hourly precipitation (EHP) across the Tibetan Plateau (TP) often triggers flash floods and landslides due to the region's complex and steep terrain, yet its inter-station covariations and formation mechanisms remain inadequately understood. Using climate network analysis of hourly station data and dynamic diagnostics, this study examines EHP synchronicity across the southeastern and northeastern TP and elucidates the underlying mechanisms from a perspective of sea surface temperature (SST)-forced circulation evolution. title: Sources of skillful seasonal forecasts of springtime CONUS tornado activity
abstract: Despite progress in continental United States (CONUS) tornado forecasting, operational seasonal outlooks remain challenging due to intrinsic predictability limits. While previous studies link the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) to spring tornado frequency, relying on single tropical indices misses crucial regional variability. Here, we present a novel hybrid dynamical-statistical framework that introduces a paradigm for long-lead predictability. title: Wetland restoration enhances ecological quality in urbanizing regions
abstract: Abstract Introduction Rapid urbanization and climate change drive widespread wetland degradation, yet it remains unclear whether wetland restoration improves ecological quality (EQ), a composite indicator reflecting vegetation, thermal, hydrological, environmental, and soil conditions at regional scales in highly urbanized landscapes. Objectives This study aimed to quantify the spatiotemporal dynamics of wetland extent and EQ in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region, assess the contribution of wetland restoration to EQ improvement, and disentangle its effects from climatic, edaphic, topographic, an

title: Dust Loading Increases During Topsoil Flash Droughts Under Rapid Surface Drying and Vegetation Stress
abstract: Abstract Using satellite‐derived dust optical depth (DOD), reanalysis meteorology, and a global topsoil flash drought (TSFD) inventory for 2003–2022, we find that TSFD events are associated with increased dust loading at the global scale. During TSFD events, 44.7% of land pixels exhibited positive DOD anomalies. The net global DOD anomaly increased significantly over the study period; however, this trend cannot be attributed solely to TSFD‐related effects, as changes in background environmental conditions may also have contributed. title: Historical climate extremes in Europe and the connection between spring precipitation and summer heat
abstract: Abstract. Hot European summers are often preceded by dry springs such as in 2022, but also in 1473 or 1540, two well-known summers of catastrophic heat. Spring precipitation deficits deplete soil moisture levels, which can amplify extreme summer temperature anomalies in Europe through land-atmosphere feedback mechanisms and altered atmospheric circulation. However, the link is not particularly strong, and hence long time series might help to better elucidate the mechanisms. title: Tornado environments derived from ERA5 over Indonesia
abstract: Abstract Tropical maritime regions, such as Indonesia, experience tornadoes. However, the tornado environment in Indonesia remains poorly understood. In this study, we analyzed convective and kinematic parameters associated with 119 tornado cases from 2010 to 2024. Prior to examining tornado environments, the performance of ERA5 reanalysis was evaluated against sounding observations. ERA5 tends to underestimate some parameters in tropical maritime regions, particularly low-level parameters (0–1 km) compared to mid- and deep-level parameters (0–3 km and 0–6 km). title: How Can the MJO's Planetary Scale Kelvin Wave and Synoptic Kelvin Waves Move at Different Phase Speeds in the Same Large‐Scale Environment?
abstract: Abstract Equatorially trapped Kelvin waves can occur through the depth of the troposphere and beyond. Previous works have demonstrated that these waves respond profoundly to the background flows through which they propagate, leading to variation in phase speed and dispersion characteristics. Vertical variation in the background flow might allow for the waves to move at different phase speeds through the same geographical regions. institutions: University at Albany, State University of New York

title: Characteristics of Energy Dissipation Rate at the Standard Weather Observatory Under Various Atmospheric Conditions and Its Application to Aviation Turbulence Intensity
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of low‐level turbulence (LLT) is critical for aviation safety, particularly for the emerging urban air mobility industry and aircraft takeoffs and landings. To better understand and predict these hazards, the characteristics of the energy dissipation rate (EDR) in the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) were investigated using 8‐year high‐frequency sonic anemometer observations collected at multiple altitudes of the 307‐m meteorological tower in the Boseong Standard Weather Observatory (BSWO), South Korea. title: Wind conditions shape co-migration fidelity in trans-Saharan birds at a Mediterranean stopover site
abstract: Weather is a key driver of bird migration, particularly near ecological barriers, where migratory species often converge before crossing. While its effects on individual timing are well documented, how weather reshapes the temporal assemblage of migratory bird communities remains unexplored. title: Spatiotemporal Covariability of Extreme Precipitation and Integrated Vapour Transport Over the Tibetan Plateau During 1979–2015
abstract: ABSTRACT Extreme precipitation and atmospheric moisture transport are closely linked components of the Tibetan Plateau (TP) hydroclimate, but statistical covariability should be distinguished from causal control. We analyse extreme‐precipitation and integrated vapour transport (IVT) indices over 1979–2015 using APHRODITE precipitation and ERA5 reanalysis. title: Milder winters alleviate seasonal challenges for a migratory goose facing Arctic warming
abstract: Many migratory birds now reach their Arctic breeding grounds earlier in response to advancing springs and shifting nutrient peaks, either by departing earlier from non-breeding grounds or by travelling faster. For dark-bellied brent geese, there is limited potential to travel faster, as their spring migration is already among the fastest of Arctic geese and swans. Earlier departure would require reaching departure body mass earlier, either through a faster accumulation of energy stores during spring staging in the Wadden Sea or via adjustments earlier in the annual cycle. title: The influence of vapor pressure deficit changes on global terrestrial evapotranspiration
abstract: Abstract. Vapor pressure deficit (VPD) is increasingly recognized as the primary driver of uncertainty in future global evapotranspiration (E) trends. Accurately characterizing the spatiotemporal dynamics of VPD and clarifying its mechanisms of influence on terrestrial E are crucial for improving water-use efficiency, optimizing ecosystem structure and function, and addressing the challenges of global climate change. title: Development and evaluation of the ECHAM6-iMAPLE v1.0 coupled atmosphere–ecosystem model
abstract: Abstract. Land-atmosphere interactions play a fundamental role in regulating climate variability, ecosystem productivity, and air quality through coupled exchanges of energy, water, carbon, and reactive trace gases. However, many Earth system models adopt simplified representations of vegetation physiological processes, leading to biases in terrestrial carbon and water fluxes and increased uncertainties in climate simulations. title: Extreme wave height estimation using a hybrid distribution approach
abstract: Accurate estimation of design wave heights is paramount for the safety and resilience of coastal infrastructure. However, extreme value analysis with limited samples faces two critical challenges: spurious identification of bounded EV-III distributions due to statistical fluctuations, and severe underestimation risks stemming from uncertain finite upper limits. title: Intensification of East Asian summer extreme precipitation under a net-zero anthropogenic CO 2 emission scenario
abstract: Global warming has intensified extreme precipitation, a trend projected to continue as warming persists. However, how extreme precipitation characteristics respond to global warming mitigation strategies remains poorly understood. This study examines East Asian summer extreme precipitation responses under a net-zero anthropogenic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emission scenario. Despite substantial cooling over East Asia following atmospheric CO 2 concentration decline, the intensity of extreme precipitation events continues to increase for about 30 years and does not subsequently weaken. title: The impact of along-strike variations in overriding plate thickness on subduction dynamics and mantle flow
abstract: Subduction zones are inherently three-dimensional systems and exhibit pronounced trench-parallel variability in key observables, including the deformation style of the overriding plate, trench migration rates, slab geometry, and mantle flow patterns. Geodynamic models typically invoke external mantle flow and/or along-strike variations in the properties of the subducting slab to explain this variability, often neglecting the influence of the overriding plate, despite growing evidence of its strong control on subduction dynamics. title: Assessing mangrove sensitivity to thermal variations through a satellite-based analysis on the southern São Paulo coast, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Mangroves near subtropical range limits may benefit from fewer cold constraints, yet warmer conditions can also increase atmospheric water demand. These competing possibilities were examined in the Cananéia-Iguape Coastal System, southeastern Brazil, by combining ERA5 2 m air temperature with MODIS normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), enhanced vegetation index (EVI), and leaf area index (LAI). abstract: Since the beginning of modern satellite monitoring around 1980, near-surface and tropospheric temperatures in the northern Canadian-Greenland Arctic have substantially warmed, with magnitudes comparable to those in the pan-Arctic. However, the main causes of this marked regional warming and its magnitude in future projections remain debated because of large inter-model spread across historical and future periods. title: Cloud vertical structure across China from a national Ka-band cloud radar network: thermodynamic, dynamical, and land-surface controls
abstract: Abstract. Cloud vertical structure plays a central role in regulating Earth’s radiation balance and hydrological cycle, yet it remains poorly represented in weather and climate models due to limited high-resolution observations. Using a newly established national network of 80 Ka-band cloud radars, we provide the first high-spatiotemporal-resolution characterization of cloud vertical structure across China for 2024 and quantify its thermodynamic, dynamical, and land-surface controls. title: Optical Distortion Induced by Cavitating Flow over Submerged Hydrofoils: A Coupled Computational Fluid Dynamics and Ray Tracing Study
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) increasingly rely on optical sensors for navigation, reconnaissance, and environmental monitoring; however, high-speed operation near the air-water interface generates free-surface waves and cavitation that create strongly non-uniform density and refractive-index fields, causing image distortion beyond the scope of conventional ray-tracing models. title: Tracing the Journey of Microplastics from Aquatic Ecosystems to Seafood
abstract: Microplastic pollution has become an important environmental issue due to the widespread occurrence, persistence, and biological accessibility of small plastic particles in aquatic ecosystems. Fish and other seafood organisms are of particular concern because they may come into contact with microplastics at different stages of their life cycle. These particles can be taken up directly from contaminated water and sediments or indirectly through the consumption of contaminated food. title: Numerical Investigations of the Thermofluid Performance of a Solar Collector Tube used in Maritime Applications
abstract: The increasing demand for reducing fuel consumption and improving energy efficiency in maritime industry has intensified interest in solar thermal systems for auxiliary energy supply. In this study, a numerical model of a solar collector tube is developed in COMSOL Multiphysics. The main objective of this paper is to evaluate the thermal performance of a solar collector tube from the thermofluid behavior perspective. title: RHITA: a web tool for real-time detection of extreme weather events
abstract: Abstract. Extreme weather hazards are increasing and stakeholders need rapid, transparent information during unfolding events. We present RHITA (Real-time Hazard Identification and Tracking Algorithm), an open-source framework and web tool for near real-time detection and tracking of weather-related hazards over Europe. RHITA identifies grid cells exceeding local quantile thresholds, groups them into spatial clusters, and links clusters through time to reconstruct three-dimensional events in longitude, latitude, and time. title: Bio-inspired trailing edge optimization for a double-suction pump impeller: a hybrid NSGA-II and CFD approach
abstract: Energy consumption reduction in pump systems has attracted increasing attention. Improving the efficiency of double-suction pumps can contribute to reducing energy consumption due to their extensive applications. This paper aims to optimize the double-suction pump by introducing the bionic structure inspired by the pectoral fin structure of humpback whales. In particular, this paper targeted the design improvement of the trailing edge of the double-suction pump impeller based on the tubercle structure on the pectoral fin. title: Climatology of large-scale atmospheric conditions favorable to clear-air turbulence over Europe (1950–2025): the role of quasi-biennial solar modulation
abstract: Abstract Turbulence represents a primary hazard for aviation, with Clear-Air Turbulence (CAT) posing a unique threat due to its visually undetectable nature. This study evaluates the 75-year temporal evolution of the macro-environmental atmospheric conditions favorable to CAT over Europe and North Africa from 1950 to 2025. Using monthly ERA5 reanalysis data at 200 and 225 hPa, seven synoptic-scale diagnostic indices were analyzed: Horizontal Divergence (HDG), Richardson Number (Ri), NCSU1, Brown Index (BRI), Ellrod Index (EI1, EI2), and Potential Vorticity (PV). title: The OpenSat4Weather dataset: Ku-band satellite link data for precipitation monitoring
abstract: Abstract. The TV-SAT signals received by the ground antennas of Satellite Microwave Links (SMLs) can be opportunistically used for identifying and quantifying precipitation. Hence, SMLs can serve as low-cost rainfall sensors complementary to conventional instruments. However, a significant challenge for opportunistic sensors, such as SMLs and their terrestrial counterpart, i.e., commercial microwave links (CMLs), stems from potential ownership issues, possibly hindering progress in the development of processing tools and validation studies. title: Intrinsic transition mechanism of shallow convection in the wintertime extratropics
abstract: Abstract We examined the evolution of shallow convective structures in the atmospheric boundary layer in response to changes in the basic state. Idealized numerical experiments were designed to reflect a typical winter monsoonal environment with prescribed sea surface temperatures (SSTs) varying from 273 to 287 K. title: Structural integrity and ultimate strength of tubular joints in naval architecture
abstract: Tubular joints are fundamental components in the design of offshore platforms, naval vessels, and marine superstructures, offering high strength-to-weight ratios and favourable hydrodynamic behaviour. Because their welded intersections concentrate multiaxial loads, they are among the most vulnerable regions of any marine tubular framework. title: Warm-sector heavy rainfall over the eastern China plains: identification, characteristics, and precursor dynamic signals
abstract: Abstract. Warm-sector heavy rainfall (WSHR) features small spatial scales, posing critical forecast challenges, while its fractional contribution to regional heavy rainfall and its short-term precursors remain poorly quantified. Drawing on 2021–2025 warm-season (June–September) observations from 493 surface rain gauges, ERA5 reanalysis, and a radar wind profiler (RWP) mesonet across the eastern China plains, we build an objective identification framework integrating automated front detection, warm-sector mask, and station-specific 99th-percentile hourly rainfall thresholds to separate WSHR fro

title: Spatial distribution, transport patterns, and dynamic processes of microplastics in global rivers: A review
abstract: : Rivers serve as the principal pathway for transporting microplastics from land to the ocean, thereby playing an indispensable role in their global transport. This study conducted a bibliometric review based on 176 field-observation datasets and 323 mechanism-related publications spanning 2004-2026 to synthesise the spatial distribution, transport patterns and dynamic processes of microplastics in global river systems. title: Atmospheric fingerprints of urbanization: Satellite-based detection of nitrogen dioxide, sulfur dioxide and carbon monoxide dynamics in a tropical highland city

title: Hysteresis of western North Pacific tropical cyclone activity under multiple CO 2 removal scenarios
abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclone (TC) activity is expected to change under future climate mitigation pathways, yet its response to carbon dioxide removal (CDR) remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the hysteretic response of the genesis potential index (GPI) over the western North Pacific (WNP) using an Earth system model under four idealized CDR scenarios with different peak CO 2 concentrations. title: Feasibility analysis of evacuation routes under metro flooding based on 3D modeling of flood inundation dynamics
abstract: Metro stations, characterized by enclosed spatial configurations, are highly vulnerable to extreme flooding, posing severe threats to human life and property. Understanding the hydrodynamic processes of flood intrusion and their implications for evacuation routes is therefore essential for urban flood risk reduction. title: Assessing power system vulnerability to climate-related stressors and shocks: The case of Indonesia
abstract: Climate change and extreme weather are increasing the vulnerability of power systems globally, particularly in emerging economies such as Indonesia. Yet, existing studies often assess these impacts in isolation, focusing on individual components or specific hazards, leaving system-level effects—at provincial and national scales—under-examined. To address this gap, we develop an integrated, spatially explicit approach to assess an energy system's climate-related vulnerabilities and their impacts, and apply the approach to Indonesia. title: A Synthesis of Research on the Rollover Stability of Prestressed Concrete Girders Supported on Elastomeric Bearings
abstract: Rollover stability is a critical concern for prestressed concrete bridge girders, particularly during handling, transportation, and erection when lateral restraint is limited. The growing use of long-span, slender sections has increased their susceptibility to rollover instability, especially under the combined influence of geometric imperfections, thermal gradients, eccentric loading, and inclination and deformation of bearing surfaces. title: Interannual and seasonal evolution of supraglacial drainage systems on Nivlisen Ice Shelf, East Antarctica
abstract: Abstract. Supraglacial channel networks (SCNs) represent critical components of the surface drainage system on Antarctic ice shelves, facilitating the redistribution of meltwater, including into and out of supraglacial lakes, potentially influencing ice-shelf stability. However, the seasonal and interannual variability in their spatial extent, structural evolution, and climatic sensitivity remain poorly quantified, particularly compared to observations of supraglacial lakes. title: Changes in precipitation seasonality over the Indochina Peninsula during 1981–2020: observational evidence and attribution of anthropogenic forcing
abstract: Precipitation seasonality is a fundamental characteristic of monsoon climates, with direct implications for regional water resources and ecosystem stability. Here, we investigate changes in precipitation seasonality over the Indochina Peninsula and assess the responses to different external forcings. We use multiple observation-based precipitation datasets and CMIP6 single-forcing simulations. Precipitation seasonality is quantified as the difference between precipitation accumulated during the consecutive wettest and driest 6-month periods identified using a moving-window approach. abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the variability and evolution of precipitation extremes associated with climate change is essential to support adaptation strategies, risk management, and civil protection. In this context, this study investigates the climatology, observed trends, and future projections of precipitation extremes in the Southeast Atlantic Hydrographic Basin (SAHB), a region of great socioeconomic relevance in Brazil. title: Population-resolved single-emitter spectroscopy
abstract: The heterogeneity in optically active nanomaterials often hinders efforts to understand their basic photophysics and can limit their use in practical applications. Existing methods have difficulty characterizing single-emitter spectra and optical heterogeneity with accuracy and ease-of-use. Here, we introduce SPICEE (SPectrally Imbalanced Correlations from Ensemble Emission), a photon-correlation technique that automatically samples an ensemble to recover statistical trends in the single-particle spectra. title: Technical note: A physically based correction of WRF temperature using atmospheric lapse rates for high-resolution hydrological simulations in a glacierized catchment
abstract: Abstract. High-elevation alpine catchments are particularly affected by the global rise in temperature. Understanding the drivers of climate-induced changes in the hydrological response of these catchments in the past is relevant for developing future adaptation strategies for water resources and risk management. However, the study of long-term changes since the last Little Ice Age (around 1850) is strongly limited by the availability of hydrometeorological observation data. title: Estimating Twomey forcing sensitivity to aerosol plume spreading rates
abstract: Abstract. The amount of sunlight that reaches Earth's surface can be reduced by increasing cloud droplet number and decreasing droplet size (i.e., Twomey forcing), a central idea underpinning the Marine Cloud Brightening strategy. Cloud albedo depends nonlinearly on cloud droplet concentration, meaning the spatial extent of aerosol plumes could be an important constraint on the brightening potential. title: Dynamical and thermodynamic mechanisms driving the April 2025 severe thunderstorm over eastern India
abstract: On 10 April 2025, a severe thunderstorm impacted eastern India, causing disastrous impacts across 19 of Bihar's 38 districts. Survey-estimated peak surface winds of 120 km/h (based on structural damage assessment) contributed to 63 deaths—40 from wind-related hazards and 23 from lightning strikes—with the district of Nalanda experiencing the most extensive devastation. title: A design wave method for the prediction of extreme combined wind-wave loads on floating wind turbines
abstract: The design wave approach has been used in the past to evaluate short-term extreme wave loads on offshore structures, effectively reducing the required test duration compared to the irregular wave Monte Carlo approach. The method uses short-duration wave episodes specifically designed to excite extreme loads. Also known as response-conditioned waves (RCW), they are used in a multi-fidelity framework, where the load statistics are first estimated using an efficient low-fidelity surrogate response model. title: Decadal predictions of wind, solar and compound power indicators to support the European renewable energy sector
abstract: Abstract. Renewable energy production is strongly influenced by climate variability and change, making the energy sector sensitive to fluctuations on decadal timescales. Decadal climate predictions, which aim to forecast climate variability over the next few years, therefore offer potential value for anticipating near-term changes in wind and solar resources and supporting climate-informed energy planning. abstract: Denitrification is the primary pathway for fixed nitrogen (N) removal from aquatic systems. abstract: The stability of airport infrastructure is critical to preventing structural cracks, preserving high-precision equipment, and maintaining air traffic under heavy, repetitive loads. In this context, an in-situ geotechnical characterization and shallow foundation design study was conducted for a building at Cotonou Airport. The geotechnical investigations were based on three piezocone tests (CPTu) carried out to refusal depths of 8.0 to 9.0 meters. title: Identification of optimal ERA5 model level for wind resource assessments in mountainous terrain
abstract: Abstract. Accurate estimation of hub-height wind speed is crucial for wind resources assessment at prospective sites. Traditionally, long-term wind speed series are derived from short-term site observations combined with reanalysis products, most commonly the ERA5 single-level data at 10 m and 100 m heights. However, the coarse spatial resolution of ERA5 limits their reliability in complex mountainous regions, leading to weak correlations with local wind measurements due to not adequately resolved near-surface flow. title: CFD-Based Numerical Optimization of the Thermal Performance of PCM-Integrated Hollow Bricks: Combined Effects of Cavity Geometry and Phase-Change Temperature under Hot-Climate Conditions
abstract: Abstract This study presents a two-dimensional transient CFD investigation of the thermal performance of hollow bricks incorporating air, glass wool, and phase change materials under the hot-climate conditions of Kairouan, Tunisia. Five brick geometries and three PCMs-RT26, RT30, and RT34 were evaluated over a 24-h thermal cycle using ANSYS Fluent R19. title: Spontaneous zonal symmetry breaking of tropical rain belt
abstract: Abstract The intertropical convergence zone (ITCZ) is a central component of tropical climate, yet the conditions under which a tropical rain belt remains zonally extended or becomes unstable to zonal organization remain poorly understood. Here we investigate this problem using idealized non‐rotating kilometer‐scale simulations forced by a prescribed sea surface temperature (SST) distribution that varies only in the meridional direction. abstract: The Tampa Bay estuary is a vital ecological and economic hub, whose productive, shallow-water habitats are highly vulnerable to both chronic anthropogenic stress and acute environmental disturbance events (e.g., extreme weather, human incidents). Historically, the bay's health was monitored primarily through low-frequency, monthly field sampling that has provided a foundational baseline of water quality for the last fifty years. title: Quantifying the microclimatic feedback of citywide rooftop photovoltaic deployment in Sendai, Japan
abstract: Rooftop photovoltaic (PV) deployment supports urban decarbonization, but its local microclimatic effects and interactions with urban morphology remain underexplored, particularly in coastal cities such as Sendai, Japan. The current study uses the weather research and forecasting (WRF) model with PV parameterization scheme and local climate zone (LCZ) data at 400 m resolution to conduct five experiments (exp_ctrl, exp_25, exp_50, exp_75, and exp_100) representing 0–100% citywide PV roof coverage during the hottest week of 2025. title: Multipoint plasmonic–MOF fiber sensor for CO2 monitoring in humid environments
abstract: Optical sensing using metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have the potential to revolutionize environmental gas monitoring but remains constrained by single-point architectures and the lack of quantitative analysis of critical interferents such as humidity. Here, we overcome these limitations by fabricating a multi-point, multifunctional plasmonic–MOF sensor on a single optical fiber. Mechanical and numerical evaluation of expansive soils for flexible road pavement stabilization using sugarcane bagasse ash and lime
abstract: Abstract The expansive, highly swelling clay soils, which have low bearing capacity, result in damage to flexible pavements. Utilizing locally available waste materials to develop low-cost, sustainable stabilizers improves the engineering properties of the subgrade. Laboratory-strength enhancement, establishing links between material-level stabilization and structural response via numerical modeling, has become a landmark. This study aims to assess the combination of sugarcane bagasse ash (SCBA) with lime as a remedial measure for expansive soil and its effect on flexible pavement performance.

title: How much ash to sink a vessel? Development of vulnerability functions for modelling capsizing risk under volcanic ashfall
abstract: Volcanic ashfall has only recently been recognized as a destabilizing hazard for small craft, as evidenced by vessel capsizing during the 2011–2012 Cordón Caulle eruption in Argentine Patagonia. However, the ash loads required to compromise vessel stability remain poorly constrained. This study presents the first operational methodology to quantify capsizing risk under volcanic ash loading through an analytical vulnerability framework. abstract: This study examines a section of a centralized district heating network for which the optimal pipe diameter and flow velocity must be determined. Unlike traditional approaches that focus only on hydraulic or thermal aspects, the proposed method considers the full life cycle of the network and the associated greenhouse gas emissions. This includes not only pump electricity consumption and heat losses, but also the carbon footprint of steel pipe production and transportation. abstract: Rising need for clean and reliable energy has raised tidal power system interest. The large tidal range in the Gulf of Khambhat has good potential for the extraction of tidal energy. abstract: Industrial and port areas require integrated air quality assessment methods combining monitoring observations, meteorological conditions and atmospheric dispersion modeling. In this study, we have investigated the pollution behavior and industrial source contributions in the Sohar Port and Freezone industrial area of Oman for a multi-year period of ambient air quality monitoring data and meteorological observations and AERMOD dispersion modeling results for PM 10 , NO 2 , SO 2 and CO. abstract: Evaluating the vertical sealing capacity of faulted mudstone caprocks is critical for assessing fluid preservation and trap integrity. However, common quantitative indices, such as hydrocarbon fault-connection thickness (Hfc) and Shale Smear Factor (SSF), often fail to provide reliable sealing thresholds within the brittle–ductile transition zone. abstract: Abnormal vibration is one of the primary causes of high-pressure fuel pipe failure. To investigate the vibration characteristics of a high-pressure fuel pipe under combined diesel engine excitation and fuel pressure pulsation, a two-way fluid–structure interaction (FSI) model was established. abstract: Abstract On 2 May 2025, an Mw 7.4 earthquake occurred ∼120 km off the southern tip of Tierra del Fuego, at the transition of the Shackleton Fracture Zone and the Chile Trench. title: Analysis of amplifying effect of antecedent drought on rainfall-induced shallow landslides
abstract: Abstract Rainfall-induced shallow landslides are typically attributed to short-term meteorological triggers such as rainfall intensity and duration. However, the influence of antecedent hydrological conditions, particularly prolonged dry spells, has received limited attention despite their potential to alter soil behavior significantly. This study investigates the role of antecedent dry spells on landslide occurrence in the clay-rich terrains of the eastern Black Sea region of Türkiye. title: Studying and investigating the feasibility of utilizing buried condensers in steam power plants
abstract: Conventional steam power plants reject a substantial fraction of their thermal energy through condenser systems, while this low-grade waste heat remains largely unutilized. This study proposes and evaluates a novel integrated concept in which buried condenser pipelines simultaneously function as a condenser cooling system and a seasonal thermal energy storage (STES) medium by storing rejected heat within the surrounding soil for subsequent winter recovery. title: Beyond the slip paradigm: Distributed inelastic deformation as a missing tsunami source class
abstract: Tsunami source models generally assume that tsunami-generating deformation is localized on fault surfaces and is therefore represented entirely by fault slip. However, observations from major tsunamigenic earthquakes together with recent dynamic rupture simulations suggest that distributed inelastic deformation can contribute substantially to tsunami generation without requiring correspondingly large shallow fault slip. title: Ground-based spectral irradiance for intra-hour photovoltaic power forecasting
abstract: Electricity markets worldwide are shortening their settlement intervals, with Australia adopting 5-minute settlement in 2021 and the European Union now mandating a 15-minute imbalance settlement period across Member States. Shorter intervals sharpen the value of accurate intra-hour photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting at the timescale of cloud-induced ramp events, which broadband irradiance cannot fully resolve. title: Stress and Free Span Analysis of an Offshore Pipeline in the Gulf of Guinea
abstract: Offshore pipelines are critical infrastructure for hydrocarbon transportation from subsea production facilities to processing systems. However, seabed irregularities and hydrodynamic forces often lead to unsupported free spans that threaten pipeline structural integrity through excessive bending stresses and vortex-induced vibration (VIV). This study assesses the stress and free span behaviour of an 18-inch API 5L X70 offshore pipeline in the Gulf of Guinea to determine the maximum allowable free span length under combined static and dynamic loading conditions. journal: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science Engineering and Technology

title: Seasonal predictability of spring solar resources and wind-solar variability across the United States
abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of solar and wind energy across the United States is increasing the demand for reliable seasonal forecasts to guide energy planning and grid operations. Here we show high seasonal prediction skill for springtime solar energy resources over the southwestern United States using a state-of-the-art seasonal forecast system. title: Comparison of carbon and nitrogen turnover in normally grown and deformed foraminifera
abstract: Abstract In this study, we investigated the feeding behavior of deformed and normal benthic foraminifera (Protista, Rhizaria) of the species Ammonia veneta . The degree of deformation was visualized by scanning electron and light microscopy. Food uptake and assimilation were quantified in undeformed, slight deformed (1–3 abnormal chambers), and heavy deformed (irregular coiling) individuals using isotopic labeling and confocal microscopy. title: Short-lived halogen sources and chemistry in the Community Earth System Model v2 (CESM2-SLH)
abstract: Abstract. The implementation of short-lived halogen (SLH) sources and atmospheric chemistry in the Community Earth System Model v1 (CESM1), has extended the capabilities of this state-of-the-art model to study how SLH chemistry alters the oxidative capacity of the atmosphere and, consequently, the Earth’s climate. In this manuscript, we summarize 15 years of research and developments of SLH chemistry in CESM1 and present a complete revision of the porting of the original SLH implementation into the latest released version of CESM (v2), hereafter CESM2-SLH. title: Triggered Shallow Megathrust Slip following the 2020 Mw7.6 Sand Point (Alaska) Strike-Slip Earthquake Explains its Tsunami
abstract: On October 19, 2020, the Mw7.6 Sand Point earthquake occurred near the Shumagin Islands in Alaska. Moment tensor solutions suggest oblique strike-slip faulting, but the earthquake was accompanied by an uncharacteristically large tsunami. Prior models explain this with co-seismic megathrust slip release, or shallow very slow thrust slip in the overriding plate. Here, we analyze the most complete land-based data set available for this earthquake including teleseismic and high-rate GNSS waveforms, static GNSS and InSAR deformation, and relocated aftershock distributions.
