title: Contribution of chemical components to cloud condensation nuclei prediction across multiple continental sites
abstract: Aerosol–cloud interactions represent a major uncertainty in climate projections. Cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) are particles upon which cloud droplets form, yet in situ CCN measurements remain scarce. Aerosol chemical component exerts important control over CCN activity. It remains unclear how reliably aerosol chemical composition predicts CCN number concentration (N CCN ). This study compiled a dataset of N CCN (supersaturation of 0.1 to 1%) collocated with aerosol chemical components at 20 global continental sites, spanning from remote natural to heavily polluted regions. title: A survey of actuarial climate indices: a new index for France and its insurance applications
abstract: Abstract Climate change is often defined as the long-term fluctuations in climate patterns affecting the planet. Among its observed effects are: increased average temperatures and higher frequency/severity of extreme weather events, such as heat waves, droughts, floods, or windstorms. These new climate risks produce an incremental effect on the frequency/severity of claims in several insurance branches. title: Astronomical forcing and coal accumulation model of the Middle Jurassic Xishanyao Formation in the Turpan–Hami Basin, Northwestern China
abstract: The Xishanyao Formation in the Taibei Depression of the Turpan–Hami Basin consists predominantly of coal-bearing fluvial and lacustrine deposits characterized by frequent interbedding and systematic vertical facies transitions. These strata exhibit repetitive stacking patterns and thickness variations, suggesting the presence of sedimentary cycles. The cyclic architecture corresponds closely to astronomical forcing signals. title: Wetland loss amplifies regional heat exposure: insights from the 2023 Southeast Asia heatwave
abstract: Wetlands play a crucial role in regulating regional climate through their effects on surface energy balance and evapotranspiration. However, rapid wetland loss in Southeast Asia has raised concerns about its potential to intensify extreme heat exposure during heatwaves. This study investigates the impact of wetland loss on regional temperature and human heat stress during the 2023 heatwave in the Cambodia Lower Mekong Delta (CLMD). title: High-performance geodynamics on GPUs using the PETSc CUDA backend (GAUZZ v1.0.0)
abstract: Abstract. The GPU is a computing architecture designed for parallelism in vector and matrix operations. To solve the Stokes equations in geodynamics, we apply a preconditioned conjugate-gradient (PCG) method to the pressure Schur complement system. The algorithm is dominated by sparse matrix-vector products, vector inner products, vector updates, and repeated velocity subproblem solves, all of which map onto GPU architectures. title: Strong latitudinal contrasts in global wet/dry patterns since the Last Glacial Maximum and under future warming
abstract: Understanding regional wetting and drying under global warming remains challenging. Here we show, using global climate simulations and 191 records of past climate, that terrestrial moisture changes over the past 21,000 years follow a pronounced latitudinal pattern. Our reconstruction shows progressive wetting at high northern latitudes from the Last Glacial Maximum to the pre-industrial period. By contrast, many regions dominated by mid-latitude westerly winds are wetter during cold periods, whereas low-latitude monsoon regions are generally wetter during warm periods. title: Environmental conditions associated with active lightning events in April around the Nansei Islands
abstract: Abstract A lot of cloud-to-ground lightning strikes sometimes occur around the Nansei Islands in April, while those April lightning bursts (ALBs) have not been investigated. This work aims at elucidating the environment contributing to ALBs through a case study and composite analysis. Two-thirds of the ALBs cases are characterized by a carrot-shaped clouds, indicating a mesoscale convective system known as the back-and-side building. title: Late Cenozoic Sediment Provenance in the Northern Canterbury Basin, Aotearoa New Zealand
abstract: Late Cenozoic strata of the northern Canterbury Basin record uplift and erosion of mountain ranges adjacent to the transition from oblique subduction to strike‐slip on the Australian–Pacific plate boundary. Using the provenance of conglomerate clasts and sandstone samples, we reconstruct sediment transport pathways and, by inference, exhumation and reverse faulting during plate boundary development in the northeastern South Island. journal: New Zealand Journal of Geology and Geophysics

title: Effects of rectified sinusoidal bar-type Bragg breakwater on harbor resonance mitigation under regular wave excitation
abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of Bragg breakwaters in the form of periodic rectified sinusoidal bars (RSB)—retaining only the crest portion of complete sinusoidal topography—in mitigating harbor resonance induced by regular waves. A series of numerical experiments are conducted using the fully nonlinear Boussinesq model FUNWAVE 2.0, in which the breakwater is deployed at varying distances from the harbor entrance and the effects of bar amplitude, bar number, bar width, and spacing are systematically examined. title: New operational perspective to identify aerosols and hydrometeors in real-time with a pioneering algorithm (CONIOPOL) based on single-wavelength polarization lidar (CL61)
abstract: Abstract. Air quality monitoring and climate studies require continuous, vertically resolved observations to characterize aerosols and their impact on radiation, cloud microphysics, and atmospheric composition. In this study, we present CONIOPOL (CONIOlogy + POLarization), an automated depolarization-based classification algorithm developed with the polarized Automatic Lidar Ceilometer (ALC), CL61 (Vaisala Oyi, FIN) installed at Uccle, Belgium. title: Real-time and online fatigue assessment of metallic structures: A review and transferability assessment for mobile working machines
abstract: Fatigue damage limits the service life of metallic structures, including mobile working machines. Fatigue information available during operation can support monitoring, maintenance, and control. Deployment of fatigue monitoring is challenging under complex loading, limited sensing, and harsh environments. To the authors’ knowledge, this is the first scoping review of real-time and online fatigue-assessment approaches for metallic structures that examines their transferability to mobile working machines. title: Extreme Atmospheric Moistening and Drying Events at Ny‐Ålesund and Their Relation to Weather Systems
abstract: Abstract Understanding the role of water vapor in Arctic amplification requires a detailed evaluation of its spatio‐temporal variability. In this work, we use an integrated water vapor (IWV) data set from a ground‐based microwave radiometer at Ny‐Ålesund, Svalbard, covering 2012–2024, to characterize temporal IWV variability. We also identify extreme atmospheric moistening and drying events based on a new detection method and relate them to large‐scale circulation patterns and airmass pathways. title: Role of monsoon intraseasonal oscillations in modulating extreme rainfall and aerosols over central India
abstract: This observational study diagnoses the influence of the monsoon intraseasonal oscillation (MISO) on aerosols and extreme rainfall events (EREs) in Central India, using the satellite datasets from CERES and GPM-IMERG, from 2003 to 2019. The research examines explicitly how MISO phases modulate aerosol optical depth (AOD) and the occurrence of EREs during the summer monsoon. We found that high AOD phases correspond to reduced ERE frequency, while low AOD phases see increased ERE occurrences, showing negative correlation. title: Resolution Dependence of the Climate Feedback Parameter in Km‐Scale Climate Models
abstract: Abstract Global storm‐resolving models (GSRMs) provide new opportunities to investigate the climate response to warming with explicitly resolved deep convection. However, the limited number of existing studies has so far precluded the systematic assessment of similarities and differences across GSRMs. Here, we compare the Cess sensitivity (the climate sensitivity estimated from the response of atmospheric radiation budget to uniform surface warming) of the ICOsahedral Nonhydrostatic (ICON) model with three other GSRMs and CMIP5/6 models, using AMIP and aquaplanet model experiments under unifor

title: Iberulite fall and formation mechanism during a Sahara dust event in Switzerland in February 2021
abstract: Abstract. Sahara dust events can promote the formation of micrometer‑sized spherical mineral aggregates known as iberulites as they are usually found on the Iberian Peninsula. Iberulites have not, to our knowledge, been reported from Central Europe. Two formation mechanisms – in- and below scavenging – have been given. Strong iberulite fall (IFs) were observed in Western Switzerland in February 2021 when large amounts of dust were transported from the Moroccan-Algerian border towards Central Europe during a Saharan Dust Event (SDE). title: Hydrodynamic Analysis of Aquaculture Net Cages Under Coupled Netting-Fish-Sediment Interactions
abstract: To address the limitations of existing studies that neglect sediment feedback and thus underestimate the complexity of the flow field, this study develops a three-dimensional hydrodynamic model for aquaculture cages that couples a porous-media representation of netting with a two-way discrete-phase model for sediment transport. title: Automated mapping and multi-decadal changes in glacial lakes in the Upper Indus Sub-Basin, Western Himalaya, using Google Earth Engine
abstract: The Western Himalayan Glacial lakes are undergoing rapid transformation as a result of intensified glacier retreat driven by changing climatic conditions, increasing the likelihood of glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs). This study conducts an automated, multi-decadal analysis of glacial lakes in the Upper Indus Sub-Basin using Landsat imagery spanning 1990 and 2025, processed within the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform. title: Evaluating Statistical Downscaling Techniques for Regional Hydroclimatic Change Projections Over CONUS
abstract: Abstract Projecting the impacts of future climate change is critical for water managers planning infrastructure resilience strategies. Global earth system model output is generally too coarse to provide the detailed, localized information needed for impact assessment, and the computational cost of running higher‐resolution global simulations over sufficiently long periods is prohibitive. Downscaling methods span a wide range of computational cost, and statistical approaches in particular offer a relatively inexpensive way to refine climate model output into a more actionable form. title: Synchronized heat extremes over Western Europe and the Yangtze-Huai river basin during summer 2025
abstract: Abstract Western Europe and the Yangtze–Huai River Basin experienced two exceptional synchronized extreme heat events during the summer of 2025, providing a unique opportunity to investigate the mechanisms linking geographically distant heat extremes. Because the two events exhibit similar large-scale dynamical evolution, the first event is examined in detail to illustrate the underlying processes. title: Microphysics and Kinematics of a High Flash Rate Storm With a Bottom‐Heavy Charge Structure
abstract: Abstract An atypical thunderstorm with unusual lightning and charge structure characteristics propagated through Cordoba province, Argentina, during the austral warm season in late 2018. This storm exhibited echo tops near 10.5 km, with high lightning activity concentrated at low altitudes. Storm total flash rate surpassed 120 min −1 , with peak initiation altitude at 6 km, the inferred altitude interface between a lower positive charge region and an overlying negative region. title: Water quality monitoring challenges during the war in Ukraine: new contaminants and approaches to their detection
abstract: ABSTRACT Graphical overview of water pollution and monitoring under conflict conditions. Water pollutants are grouped into conflict-related contaminants, including explosive compounds, ammunition additives, uranium and heavy metals; conventional pollutants, including nutrients, heavy metals and organic matter; and hazardous pollutants also occurring in civilian activities, including petroleum hydrocarbons, pesticides, phenols, pharmaceuticals, personal care products and microplastics. title: Near-field source formation in current-forced dredged-sediment releases: two-phase morphology, slip and modal diagnostics
abstract: Abstract Open-water disposal of dredged sediment generates a dense near-field cloud that descends through the water column, deforms under ambient-current forcing and reorganizes into a near-bed source for subsequent transport. Within the present two-dimensional numerical framework, this source-formation stage determines the early suspended-sediment footprint and provides a compact description of the near-bed state that may later be supplied to transport and deposition models. title: From Static Biomimetics to Programmable and Adaptive Systems: Advances in Milli-structures in Directed Fluid Transport
abstract: Abstract Directed fluid transport is critical to diverse applications spanning water purification, atmospheric water harvesting, point-of-care diagnostics, thermal management, and energy conversion, yet conventional microfluidic systems often require external pumps and complex infrastructure, severely limiting their scalability and adaptability. Directed fluid transport enabled by milli-structured surfaces has rapidly evolved from static, one‑way capillary designs to dynamic, reconfigurable and programmable systems. title: Improving the CLASSIC (v1.8) snow model to better simulate Arctic snowpacks
abstract: Abstract. This study enhances the snow model of the Canadian Land Surface Scheme including Biogeochemical Cycles (CLASSIC), with a particular focus on Arctic environments. Key snow model physics improvements include adjustments to the thermal conductivity at the top of the first soil layer, a revised computation of the temperature at the snow–soil interface (hereafter, bottom snow temperature), and the addition of a windless exchange coefficient in sensible heat flux calculations. title: INTEGRATION OF RISK-BASED RESILIENCE STRATEGIES INTO INTELLIGENT SAFETY MANAGEMENT OF SHIP-PORT CYBER-PHYSICAL SYSTEMS
abstract: The article presents an integrated scientific and methodological concept of navigation safety management based on risk-oriented and resilience strategies in the context of cyber-physical interaction between ship and port systems. The aim of the study is to develop a conceptual model of risk-oriented planning for maritime transport networks that ensures increased reliability of mooring operations under operational uncertainty. title: Summertime ozone sensitivity to temperature in China: observational evidence and mechanistic attribution in urban and rural areas in the Yangtze River Delta region
abstract: Abstract. As climate change increases frequency and intensity of hot extremes, understanding how elevated temperatures influence surface ozone (O3) across different chemical regimes is critical. We combine observations from summer 2022 in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) with targeted United Kingdom Chemistry and Aerosols (UKCA) Box experiments to quantify and attribute the temperature sensitivity of ground-level O3 in a VOC-limited urban megacity (Shanghai) and a predominantly NOx-limited rural region (Lishui). title: Flow dynamics of cryolava or impact melt on Titan’s surface
abstract: Titan, a unique body in the solar system, resembles a life-size Miller–Urey experiment where pockets of liquid water might interact with abundant organic matter. Its young surface (less than a billion years) shows signs of material exchange with the interior, and an isotopic signature is detected in the atmosphere. Cryovolcanism and meteor impacts represent potential high energy mechanism for these exchanges. title: Projected temperature extremes variability assessment using CMIP5 multi-model ensembles over Gujarat, India
abstract: The regional impacts of extreme climate events have been worsening over the last two decades and have intensified over the years. It has a major effect on health, agriculture and the hydrological cycle on a large scale therefore, it’s very important to determine and quantify the future duration and intensity of such events. title: Role of atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic forcing in the extreme 2025 European summer heatwave
abstract: Abstract In summer 2025, an extreme heatwave propagated northeastward across Europe, sequentially affecting Southwestern (SWEU) and Northern (NEU) Europe with record-breaking durations in the 1979-2025 record. However, the roles of atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic forcing in the 2025 European high-temperature conditions remain unclear. title: A Fermatean fuzzy fault tree and Bayesian network hybrid for collision and grounding risk in a congested strait
abstract: Collision and grounding remain the dominant accident categories in congested straits, where dense crossing traffic, sharp bends and strong currents act together with human and technical failures. Quantitative risk assessment in such waters is hampered by scarce failure data and by the vagueness of expert judgement. This study proposes a hybrid model that couples Fermatean fuzzy fault tree analysis with a Bayesian network for the assessment of collision and grounding risk during the transit of a congested strait. title: Drainage of Kronshtadskiy subglacial lake in Antarctica observed by double-differential SAR interferometry
abstract: Hundreds of subglacial lakes in Antarctica have been reported by using radio-echo sounding and satellite altimetry, but the detection of small and short-lived hydrological events has remained challenging due to limited spatial and temporal resolution. In this study, we applied the Double-Differential Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (DDInSAR) technique to analyze surface-elevation changes associated with the Kronshtadskiy subglacial lake near the Amery Ice Shelf, East Antarctica. title: Extensive glacier loss in the coterminous United States
abstract: Glaciers populate the mountain ranges of the western conterminous United States and despite their importance to alpine hydrology, their area and volume change have never been comprehensively evaluated. Our study shows that since the mid-twentieth century about one-quarter of the glaciers have disappeared and the overall area and volume are reduced by one-third. The pattern of glacier shrinkage suggests most glaciers in the conterminous United States are largely maintained by local topographic influences due to their small size. title: Precipitation nowcasting model based on multi-source data fusion and efficient additive attention
abstract: Short-term precipitation nowcasting serves as an indispensable technical support for the early warning and risk management of meteorological hazards. To improve the nowcasting accuracy by leveraging complementary information from multi-source data, this study proposes a precipitation nowcasting model based on multi-source data fusion and efficient additive attention (EAA-MNFP). title: New constraints on the postglacial evolution of Lago Maggiore, Northern Italy
abstract: ABSTRACT Lago Maggiore is situated in an overdeepened valley reach at the southern margin of the European Alps, and its thick sediment infill allows the reconstruction of the postglacial valley and lake evolution. We study here the sedimentary succession in the lower Ossola Valley, which is infilled by ~500 m of deposits. title: Research Proposal for Investigation and Assessment of the Fishing Ban Effect on Songjiang Perch in the Fuyang Section of the Qiantang River Based on Broadband Acoustic Technology
abstract: Songjiang perch (Trachidermus fasciatus) is a catadromous fish with important ecological and conservation value in the Qiantang River, and it is also a national Class II protected wild animal. To evaluate the protection effect of the fishing ban period on Songjiang perch in the Fuyang section of the Qiantang River, this study intends to use a broadband scientific echosounder to measure the acoustic characteristics of Songjiang perch by the controlled method and the modeling method, and to conduct two acoustic surveys at night in May and July in the Fuyang section of the Qiantang River. title: Anthropogenic aerosol reduction contributes to faster flash drought onset in a changing climate
abstract: Flash droughts have emerged as severe hazards, posing growing challenges to natural and socioeconomic systems, yet the influence of recent aerosol reductions on their onset remains unclear. Here, we investigate the impacts of aerosols and their underlying mechanisms using multi-source observations and large-ensemble climate simulations. Lower aerosol levels are increasingly linked to severe soil moisture deficits, with aerosol effects on onset-speed variability intensifying across 69.2% of regions. title: Rossby wave diversion as a source of subseasonal predictability for extreme Meiyu-Baiu events
abstract: Meiyu-Baiu, the distinct rainy season in subtropical East Asia, is characterized by a quasi-stationary Meiyu-Baiu Front (MBF) along which excessive rainfall and mega floods often occur. This study shows that the spatial stationarity of MBF, and thus its potential to generate catastrophic flooding is inherently modulated by synoptic-scale disturbances over northeastern East Asia. title: Simulating jökulhlaups from an ice-marginal lake within a 2D model of subglacial drainage and basal sliding
abstract: Abstract. Ice-marginal lakes are an increasingly common feature of glacierised landscapes, and their sudden drainage beneath glaciers (a jökulhlaup) can threaten downstream communities and infrastructure. Numerous efforts to model jökulhlaups have been made, however, because these models are 1D representations of a single channel connected to a lake, they cannot simulate lateral jökulhlaup propagation through the subglacial system. title: Spaceborne multi-sensor tracking reveals hydrologic decoupling during the record-breaking Sahara flood
abstract: Satellite remote sensing enables large-scale quantification of extreme hydrologic events in data-scarce regions, yet the integration of multi-sensor observations to resolve hydrologic responses remains limited. The record-breaking 2024 Sahara flood presents a unique opportunity to evaluate satellite-based characterisation of hydrologic extremes in hyper-arid environments. title: Global Assessment and Error Budget of EarthCARE Column Aerosol Optical Depth: Physical Limits and Quantitative Mitigation
abstract: Abstract The Earth Cloud Aerosol and Radiation Explorer (EarthCARE) provides critical spaceborne high spectral resolution LiDAR observations for global aerosol profiling. However, integrating these vertically resolved aerosol extinction coefficient profiles into column Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) introduces systematic biases from physical observation boundaries, which currently lack global validation and quantitative attribution. title: From concept to action: Driving impact through responsible research practices in the International Polar Year 2032–2033 An early career perspective
abstract: Regions at the poles are warming at rates two to four times higher than the global average, driving profound environmental, societal, and geopolitical changes. As Polar Early Career Researchers with careers extending into and beyond the 5th International Polar Year in 2032–2033, we have a responsibility to shape research practices that are impactful, ethical, and sustainable. title: Implementation of a New Paradigm for Hydrometeorological Support for Enterprise Leaders and the Public for Adaptation Purposes
abstract: The aim of the article is to increase the efficiency of hydrometeorological support users for the population and enterprises leaders by implementing a new paradigm. The failure of enterprises to account for all climate and change-related risks, combined with the absence of systematized and formalized impact forecasts and recommendations for preventive actions, leads to increased losses. To establish a modern hydrometeorological support system, the paper proposes an implementation integrated approach of an end-to-end data processing scheme ‒ spanning from observation to decision support. title: Distilling complexity: stylized facts as explicit, auditable foundation for ecological theory and modeling
abstract: Ecological models routinely rely on broad empirical regularities to constrain theory and validate predictions, yet these regularities are typically applied implicitly under alternative labels such as "patterns", "laws", or "benchmarks." Such implicit applications obscure a model's empirical commitments, hide unverified assumptions, mask scale dependencies, and hinder transfer across systems. abstract: The influence of aerosols on climate is determined not only by their global distribution but also by their composition. However, so far, a large fraction of the development efforts for satellite-based aerosol retrievals has focused on inverting from different single instruments the total column aerosol optical depth (AOD), as measure of the total abundance of atmospheric aerosols. title: Impact-based flood-damage assessment in Japan under longitudinal typhoon-track perturbations and levee-height variations during Hagibis (2019)
abstract: Abstract Impact-based flood-damage assessment integrates hydrometeorological information with vulnerability and exposure data to generate comprehensive evaluation of flood damage. This study uses the Integrated Land Simulator to assemble an impact-based flood-damage assessment framework for Typhoon Hagibis (2019), one of the most powerful typhoons to strike Japan in recent years. To systematically evaluate how typhoon-track position and levee height influence flood damage, we conduct longitudinal typhoon-track perturbation experiments and levee-height variation scenario analyses. abstract: This study investigates how submerged vegetation influences breaker bar development using the process based IH2VOF-SED model, which couples a two-dimensional vertical Reynolds averaged Navier–Stokes solver with sediment transport and bed evolution. The model is evaluated against laboratory measurements for bare and vegetated beach profiles under regular erosive waves. title: Towards Integrated Adaptive Environmental Management of Cultural Heritage Sites: A Thematic Review and Conceptual Framework
abstract: In recent years environmental management has been raised to a new level in the context of cultural heritage sites. Climate change, urbanization, mass tourism, and limited institutional resources and management capacities are the most pressing challenges facing cultural heritage today. These issues clearly demonstrate that fragmented, segmented approaches are insufficient and unable to adapt effectively or safeguard the cultural values inherited by future generations. title: The Growing Role of Evaporative Demand in Driving Record‐Breaking Droughts in the Amazon Basin
abstract: Abstract Amazon droughts have historically been driven by precipitation deficits, but recent escalating drought events highlight a regime shift toward “hot droughts.” By decomposing historical drought drivers (1979–2024), we show that rising evaporative demand (represented by potential evapotranspiration, PET) now acts as a primary driver of drought intensification. While rainfall deficits remain the dominant contributor to the record‐breaking 2024 drought, escalating atmospheric thirst almost doubled its severity. title: Long-term climatology of vertical profiles of polarimetric variables and ice-microphysical retrievals at X-band – Part 1: Radar calibration
abstract: Abstract. In a two-part series of papers, a climatology of quasi-vertical profiles (QVPs) of polarimetric variables and ice-microphysical retrievals such as ice water content, total number concentration and mean volume diameter is presented. QVPs are generated from plan position indicator scans at 18° elevation angle measured with the X-band radar located in the city of Bonn in western Germany between 2013 and 2023. title: Global climate impact of land-surface change driven by radiative effects
abstract: Abstract A robust proportionality between radiative forcing and global-mean temperature has been established for most climate drivers. However, land-surface changes are considered an exception due to their potential to alter surface hydrology, introducing non-radiative effects that may rival those from surface albedo changes. title: Hysteresis of extreme precipitation in East Asia under various CO2 removal pathways
abstract: Extreme precipitation poses severe societal and economic risks under elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2), yet current understanding of how it will respond to various future CO2 removal scenarios remains limited. Focusing on East Asia, a region highly vulnerable to monsoonal dynamics and anthropogenic influences, here we assess the hysteresis of extreme precipitation responses under four CO2 concentration thresholds and two emission reduction rates using climate model simulations. title: Surface Nucleation‐Mode Particles Increase During Intense Vertical Exchange Between the Atmospheric Boundary Layer and the Free Troposphere
abstract: Abstract Vertical exchange between the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) and the free troposphere (FT) is a key pathway for aerosol transport and can substantially influence surface air quality. In this study, an intense ABL‐FT exchange event over Shanghai on 29 March 2024 was captured and analyzed using ground‐based Doppler wind LiDAR, microwave radiometer, particle‐size spectrometer measurements, and numerical diagnostics. abstract: Abstract. Substantial efforts and improvements in air quality across Europe lowered levels of air pollutants including particulate matter (PM) in the last decades. However, significant proportion of the European population still lives in areas exceeding WHO recommendations, especially in Northern Italy, Balkans and Eastern Europe, including Serbia. Targeted PM mitigation strategies require extensive air quality monitoring and modelling including source apportionment (SA) studies. title: Invited perspective: Uncertainties in natural systems may be uncomfortable, but ignoring them would be absurd
abstract: Abstract. Uncertainties in natural systems are pervasive, varied, and unavoidable due to inherent open system complexity and limited knowledge. Therefore, the evolution of a natural system cannot be predicted deterministically and probabilistic forecasts are commonly used to account for these uncertainties. As the Voltaire-inspired title suggests, representing and quantifying all uncertainties in hazard and risk forecasting is difficult yet essential for an effective risk-cycle management and for a meaningful scientific evaluation of forecasting models. title: Diverse coupling between climate change, socio-economic factors and climate potential productivity in Africa
abstract: Africa’s accelerating climate warming has rendered its climate potential productivity (CPP) increasingly vulnerable, raising global concerns over biodiversity, water resources, and food security. Understanding the long‑term evolution of CPP and its driving mechanisms has therefore become an urgent research priority. This study analyses the spatiotemporal patterns and correlates of CPP across Africa, using the Thornthwaite Memorial model in combination with trend detection, correlation, and econometric analyses. title: Macroscopic and mesoscopic mechanical behavior of the interface between piles and unsaturated sand under vertical cyclic loading
abstract: Understanding the degradation of pile bearing capacity under vertical cyclic loading requires an in-depth investigation of the pile–unsaturated sand interface. This study employs a multi-scale approach—combining visualized cyclic loading tests, particle image velocimetry (PIV), and discrete element method (DEM) simulations—to elucidate the underlying macro–meso evolutionary mechanisms. title: H2CHAIN: Integrated web platform for energy-balance-constrained planning of green hydrogen value chains
abstract: Planning a green hydrogen project couples siting, generation, electrolysis, storage, conversion and cost decisions that are usually assessed in separate tools. This paper presents an integrated web-based decision-support platform for the planning and analysis of green hydrogen value chains. The platform combines geospatial analysis, techno-economic modeling, and system-level scenario assessment within a modular architecture that is accessible through a standard web browser. title: Investigation of glacier mass balance based on multi-source observation in the Karakoram over the past 25 years
abstract: The "Karakoram Anomaly" - the atypical stability of glaciers in a warming climate-has introduced considerable uncertainty into projections of regional water resources. However, the resilience of this anomaly under sustained climate forcing remains poorly quantified. In this study, multi-source geodetic data (ASTER, NASA DEM, ICESat‑2) were integrated to reassess glacier mass balance across the Karakoram and its sub‑regions between 2000 and 2024. abstract: The simulation fidelity of Fluid–Structure Interaction (FSI) is critical for predicting multi-phase (solid-liquid-gas) interactions that involve large deformations and failure evolution. While the Material Point Method (MPM) offers a robust numerical procedure for those problems, the choice of the Equation of State (EOS) for weakly compressible fluids remains a subject of compromise between computational accuracy and efficiency. abstract: Abstract. In 2019, Brazil experienced an intensive fire season, despite the absence of major climate anomalies to enhance fire activity. Existing carbon monoxide (CO) emission estimates from state-of-the-art fire emission inventories differ by a factor two for the period and region. We provide a top-down estimate on CO emissions from these fires using the new CarbonTracker Europe – Long/Short Window (CTE-LW/SW) inverse modelling framework driven by column-averaged dry air CO mole fractions (XCO) from the MOPITT and TROPOMI satellite instruments. title: Gas Turbine Propulsion Systems for Naval Vessels: Energy Flow Calculation Methodology and HighPressure Rotor CFD Simulation
abstract: This paper addresses the modernization of naval propulsion systems through the adoption of gas turbine technology, with emphasis on thermodynamic calculation methodology and rotor flow simulation. The study is centred on the Rolls Royce gas turbine, employed in naval propulsion applications and covers all thermodynamic states from atmospheric air intake through the two-stage compression process, combustion chamber, high-pressure and lowpressure turbine stages, to the power turbine exhaust. abstract: Abstract. We study the suitability of an initial condition ensemble to form the conceptual basis of defining climate. title: The Effectiveness of Primary and Secondary Radar in the Malaysian Air Defence Mechanism
abstract: Radar surveillance constitutes a critical component of modern air-defence systems, enabling states to detect, identify, track and respond to aerial activities. This capability is particularly important for Malaysia due to its geographical separation, extensive maritime approaches, large airspace and increasing exposure to foreign military aircraft, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and unidentified aerial activities. title: A 256-year daily rainfall record reveals multiscale rainy-season variability and emerging hydroclimatic hazard over northern East Asia
abstract: Monsoon rainy seasons shape water supply and flood hazard across northern East Asia, but their long-term variability remains poorly understood because few daily rainfall records extend beyond the instrumental era. Here, we reconstruct rainy-season onset, retreat, and duration from a 256-year daily precipitation record for Seoul (1770-2025), providing an unusually long view of seasonal monsoon behavior. title: A revisited Cartesian-diver experiment: metastable sinking and comparison between experiments and a nonlinear model
abstract: Abstract We present a revisited Cartesian-diver experiment in which a small air-filled balloon, loaded with a metal sphere and plasticine, undergoes a metastable sinking motion in a water column. The experiment illustrates how hydrostatic pressure compresses the trapped air, reduces the buoyant force, and eventually drives an accelerated descent. title: Hydrodynamic and ecological modeling for water quality assessment in Lake Qaroun, Egypt
abstract: Abstract Qaroun Lake, a closed salty lake in the Fayoum depression of Egypt, is an important natural resource that supports fishing, wildlife, and local communities. It mainly receives water from a dense drainage network, with some possible small contribution from groundwater. Since it has no outlet and loses water only through evaporation, its salinity keeps increasing. Any change in the amount or quality of incoming water strongly affects the lake’s environment. title: Hazard hexagons: the influence of anthropogenic climate change on extremes in regions globally
abstract: Abstract The sixth assessment report (AR6) of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) presented regional summaries of the scientific knowledge of changing weather extremes and the human influence upon this. The hexagon figures, found in the Summary for Policymakers (SPM), were a key part of this presentation. abstract: The hydrodynamic study of multiple arrays of point-absorber wave energy converters is carried out. The aim is to determine the optimum interfloat spacing between wave energy converters to maximize the array's performance. Multiple factors are examined at different wave heights and different spacing ratios: Response Amplitude Operator (RAO), Harmonic Ratio (HR), phase difference, interaction factor (q-factor), absorbed power, and Capture Width Ratio (CWR). title: Effect of corrosion damage on cyclic tensile mechanical behavior of grouted sleeve connections
abstract: ABSTRACT Grouted sleeve connections are essential load-bearing components of precast concrete bridges, whose mechanical performance deteriorates under corrosive conditions. Existing research mainly focuses on their monotonic tensile performance, whereas cyclic tensile responses and corrosion-affected constitutive models remain insufficiently studied. This study conducted cyclic tensile tests on twenty-four sleeve specimens after electrochemical accelerated corrosion. abstract: Abstract Atmospheric non‐methane hydrocarbons (NMHCs) are important trace species with anthropogenic and natural sources including fugitive emissions from fossil fuel mining and distribution, biomass burning, biofuel combustion, and biogenic emissions from microbes and plants. abstract: Abstract. Accurately representing polar stratospheric clouds (PSCs) in global Chemistry-Climate Models and Earth System Models is important as they play a key role in springtime ozone depletion in polar regions by activating both chlorine and bromine species through heterogeneous reactions and denitrifying the stratosphere. Here, we present and evaluate an updated PSC parameterisation scheme implemented in the UK Earth System Model (UKESM1.1). title: Dipole‐Like Responses in Near‐Surface Ozone Induced by Mid‐Latitude Cut‐Off Lows Over East Asia: A 40‐Year Simulated Climatology
abstract: Abstract Midlatitude cut‐off lows (COLs) strongly influence weather, climate, and regional ozone (O 3 ) variability, yet their seasonal impacts on near‐surface O 3 and underlying mechanisms remain inadequately understood. title: Developing a Risk-Based Environmental Management Framework for Large-Scale Infrastructure Projects in Saudi Arabia
abstract: Saudi Arabia’s infrastructure transformation under Vision 2030 is creating an exceptional need for environmental management systems that can operate at the scale, speed, complexity and ecological sensitivity of giga- and mega-project delivery. Conventional environmental management plans often catalogue impacts and controls but do not always provide a transparent method for prioritising uncertain, cumulative and high-consequence environmental risks across the project life cycle. abstract: To address the engineering drawbacks of sealing walls in connecting roadways, including low construction efficiency, high risk of structural instability and poor long-term airtightness, this paper proposes a novel dual-wall sealing structure. Based on site investigation, numerical simulation and field engineering practice, systematic refinement analyses were carried out on the geometric dimensions and material properties of the sealing wall. abstract: ABSTRACT Attributing regional evapotranspiration (ET) and assessing its impacts are critical for understanding land‐atmosphere interactions in climate‐sensitive regions such as northern China. This study fuses six gridded ET products with in situ measurements using Random Forest after excluding poorly representative flux sites. abstract: Abstract We conducted a 220‐m mesh simulation over the global domain with realistic topography. This can be called a first “global large‐eddy simulation” (GLES) for deep convection. The resolution dependence across km‐ to sub‐km scales and sensitivity to turbulence schemes are investigated. title: Observed sub-surface warming in the Northern Eurasia (1963-2022)
abstract: Abstract Long-term soil temperature changes in high-latitude regions have been reported mainly focusing on the near-surface air and sub-surface soil temperature because of limited observational data. This gap still obscures spatiotemporal changes and associated processes of vertical thermal changes at multiple soil layers over such climate-sensitive regions. abstract: Abstract Satellite remote sensing of ozone has progressed from daily global observations by polar‐orbiting platforms to hourly regional monitoring by geostationary platforms. However, retrieving detailed vertical profiles remains challenging because satellite measurements have inherently limited vertical sensitivity. abstract: ABSTRACT Internal pressure and localized external loads place competing demands on the structural design of tubular composites. Three‐dimensional angle‐interlock tubular woven composites (3DATWCs) with different warp lining yarn ratios and warp column counts were fabricated from carbon fiber and epoxy resin and evaluated through quasi‐static internal pressure, low‐cycle internal pressure fatigue, lateral compression, and low‐energy multiple and high‐energy single drop‐weight impact tests. title: Climate risk, uneven development, and threshold-dependent tourism resilience in selected cities of western China
abstract: Abstract Climate risk and socioeconomic development are increasingly reshaping tourism resilience, particularly in climate-sensitive and unevenly developed regions. Yet how climate risk and economic development jointly influence tourism, and how these effects vary across regions, remains insufficiently understood. title: Urban Heat Island Monitoring Using Thermal Infrared Satellite Data in Italian cities
abstract: Climate change is driving a sustained increase in global temperatures and an intensification of extreme events, including heatwaves. Urban areas are typically warmer than the surrounding suburban and rural environments, a phenomenon known as the Urban Heat Island (UHI) due to the presence of buildings and inhomogeneous surfaces, which affects surface energy and water exchanges as well as the local meteorology. title: Operational-Response-Aware Two-Stage Stochastic Scheduling of Renewable Port Microgrids under Arrival-Driven Congestion and Demand Amplification
abstract: Electrified container ports are coupled logistics–energy systems in which uncertain vessel arrivals determine berth occupancy, shore-power activation, cargo-handling intensity, and the residual demand balanced by renewable generation, battery storage, and the utility grid. This study develops a scenario-based stochastic framework linking a non-homogeneous vessel-arrival process to queue-consistent berth occupancy, congestion-responsive demand, photovoltaic and wind uncertainty, battery dispatch, and grid exchange. title: Lifestyle-Driven Phenotypes in Sensitive Skin: A Cross-Sectional, Multicenter Study Across Urbanization Tiers
abstract: Sensitive skin is shaped by intrinsic physiology and environmental exposures, yet how concurrent lifestyle factors modulate its expression remains poorly characterized. This study examined how differing environmental and lifestyle conditions influence sensitive skin phenotypes through clinical evaluation, biophysical measurements, and biomarker profiling. title: Collective effects of synoptic processes and equatorial waves on the genesis of a strong westerly wind burst event in late 2023
abstract: Abstract A strong westerly wind burst (WWB) event that occurred from 6–16 November 2023 has been suggested to have substantially influenced the development of the strong 2023/24 El Niño, yet the mechanisms governing its genesis remain poorly understood. Our analysis indicates that the Madden–Julian Oscillation and equatorial convective Rossby waves jointly initiated the event, with the latter playing the dominant role. abstract: ABSTRACT The lateral response of partially embedded single piles, referred to as extended pile shafts, subjected to combined vertical and lateral loads is investigated using a novel analytical method that explicitly accounts for the P ‐Δ effect caused by axial pile force and the layering of foundation soils. abstract: Abstract We investigate the role of the elasticity and density of the forearc mantle wedge corner on the stress distribution in the forearc region of subduction zones, using numerical quasi‐2D lithospheric deformation models for the Cascadia, Nankai, NE Japan, and Costa Rica subduction zones. title: Improved detection of methanogenic archaea by validating 16S rRNA gene primers using defined archaeal–bacterial mock communities
abstract: Abstract Archaea play essential roles in global biogeochemical cycles, yet their diversity in environmental samples remains understudied. Limited coverage of universal primers towards archaea, their very low abundance relative to bacteria in the studied samples, inefficient cell lysis and the incompleteness of reference databases complicate archaeal 16S rRNA gene sequencing. abstract: The seafood processing industry faces critical operational challenges in maintaining mass-balance integrity because manual, paper-based recording causes data lag and human input errors. This study aims to optimize PT XYZ's seafood production system by developing an integrated Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) architecture and evaluating its economic feasibility for real-time operational transparency. title: Inter-station measurements redundancy and bias structure for optimising closely spaced radiosonde thermodynamic profiling networks
abstract: Accurate and internally consistent radiosonde temperature and relative humidity profiles are fundamental to numerical weather prediction (NWP), boundary-layer studies, climate monitoring, and satellite data validation. title: Discrepancies in Extreme Daily and Monthly Precipitation Trends Between Observations and Earth System Models
abstract: Abstract While extreme precipitation is expected to intensify globally in a warming climate, changes in extreme precipitation on regional scales remain uncertain. To understand how well Earth system models (ESMs) capture recent changes in regional extreme precipitation, we compare trends in daily and monthly extreme precipitation across multiple observational data sets and three ESM ensembles. title: Declining terrestrial water storage is associated with changes in effective hydrological memory and drought buffering
abstract: Abstract Drought impacts in large river basins depend not only on precipitation deficits but also on how terrestrial water storage (TWS) buffers climate anomalies through hydrological memory, which is the persistence of past storage conditions. In this study, we quantify this as the “effective hydrological memory,” measured as the e-folding decay time of the low-frequency TWS (periods over 12 months) autocorrelation function, since it integrates climate signals and basin physical properties. title: Linearised metamodel for two-dimensional sloshing effects in partially-filled rectangular tanks under horizontal excitation
abstract: Sloshing dynamics in partially-filled rectangular tanks remains a computationally demanding phenomenon in applications such as tuned liquid dampers, largely due to high computational costs of using high-fidelity sloshing models. Additionally, the effective damping of coupled dynamic systems is challenging to describe with existent equivalent or reduced-order sloshing models. This article introduces a linearised force-based modelling strategy by using time-domain approach, that constructs equivalent mass and damping derivatives for the sloshing effect under horizontal excitation. title: Modulation of Slow Slip Event Characteristics Throughout the Costa Rica Subduction Zone Earthquake Cycle
abstract: Abstract Slow slip events (SSEs) represent an aseismic transient slip mode that repeats quasi‐periodically, near or partially overlapping with the megathrust earthquake zone. However, the process of stress interaction between SSEs and earthquake zones is not clearly understood. Here, we apply an earthquake and SSE sequence model to simulate the interseismic variability of SSE characteristics, and compare to observations pre‐ and post‐2012 M w 7.6 Nicoya earthquake in the Costa Rica subduction zone, including six SSEs from 2003 to 2012 and four from 2014 to 2019. title: A novel spatiotemporal-enhanced aerosol retrieval model based on GNSS-derived PWV
abstract: Aerosol optical depth (AOD) is a core indicator for quantifying atmospheric pollution, and its spatiotemporal variation is strongly influenced by meteorological factors, including water vapor, a critical driver of atmospheric moisture transport and energy balance. To investigate the role of water vapor in AOD modeling, this study integrates global navigation satellite system (GNSS), precipitable water vapor (PWV), and ERA5 meteorological data to develop a high-resolution spatiotemporal AOD model over Europe, at 0.25° spatial and 1-hour temporal resolution. title: Salt Cavern Hydrogen Storage for Renewable‐Dominated Smart Energy Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT Power systems with high shares of variable renewable energy increasingly face balancing challenges that extend beyond intraday variability to multiday shortages, seasonal mismatch, resource adequacy and system resilience. Salt cavern hydrogen storage (SCHS) has emerged as a promising underground hydrogen storage option for renewable‐dominated smart energy systems. It can act as the large‐scale storage component that connects renewable hydrogen production with downstream hydrogen use and power‐to‐hydrogen‐to‐power pathways. abstract: This article examines the applicability of the mesh-free Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) method for numerical simulation of surfable solitary waves propagating over an artificial seabed in a wave pool. The simulations were performed using DualSPHysics, with particular attention given to the accurate reproduction of the free-surface profile. The wave crest overturning, which is highly sensitive to the accuracy of the numerical method, was considered separately. title: Uncertainties in recent tropical stratospheric and tropospheric ozone changes limit the use of observational constraints for assessing future ozone change
abstract: A variety of chemical and dynamical processes in the troposphere and stratosphere affect tropical total column ozone (TCO), the net effect of which may cause changes in surface UV radiation and impact human and ecosystem health. We use dynamical linear modeling to estimate changes in tropical TCO and partial column ozone (PCO) in the troposphere and three stratospheric layers to assess agreement between satellite composites and chemistry-climate model simulations from two multi-model experiments (CCMI-1 and CCMI-2022). title: Research on the reliability assessment method for Gas Insulated Switchgear based on composite risk assessment model
abstract: Fault diagnosis in safety–critical industrial infrastructure is often hindered by the data scarcity of catastrophic failures and subjective uncertainty inherent in domain knowledge. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel Hybrid Knowledge-Data Fusion method via a HW-TOPSIS-FTA-FBN model. This method proposes a “Human-Cyber-Physical” fusion loop that transforms qualitative cognition into quantitative reasoning. title: Morphological Characteristics of Tropical Precipitation Features Producing Extreme Instantaneous Rain Rates in GPM and DYAMOND Global Storm Resolving Models
abstract: Abstract The influence of the spatial organization of tropical convection on the production of extreme instantaneous localized tropical rain rates remains poorly constrained, both in observations and in models. Using retrievals from the Ku‐band radar onboard the GPM satellite, we identify tropical precipitation features (PFs) and quantify their morphological characteristics. We find that PFs that produce extreme instantaneous rain rates are on average larger and have a higher convective area fraction than the average PF. title: A long-term dataset of tropical cyclone radius of maximum wind in the Western North Pacific Based on a Bayesian consensus of multiple estimates
abstract: Abstract The radius of maximum wind (RMW) is one of the key parameters for characterizing the structure of tropical cyclones (TCs). Although multiple methods have been developed to estimate the RMW, their estimates can sometimes differ substantially and are not always available, making it difficult to construct a comprehensive long-term RMW dataset. This study develops a Bayesian consensus method to derive a single RMW estimate from multiple RMW estimates. title: Lifetime Estimation of Blade Erosion Using Rain Erosion Test Data With Different Analysis Methods
abstract: ABSTRACT Lifetime estimation regarding leading‐edge erosion of wind turbine blades involves a series of mathematical and statistical procedures, including regression fitting, tolerance interval formulation, and weathering modeling approaches. This work investigates the intermediate steps in the fatigue assessment process and the associated sources of variability, using data from a whirling arm rain erosion test (RET) machine, time‐series liquid precipitation and wind data from two sites, and the IEA reference 15 MW wind turbine. title: Ecosystem complexity and climate adaptation in Oman: Climate-water-ecosystem nexus
abstract: This study examines the relationships among climate variability, water-related variables, and vegetation dynamics across the Sultanate of Oman. Using six decades of climatic and hydrological data, the study evaluates long-term climate variability patterns, identifies the main climatic and ecohydrological factors associated with native vegetation dynamics, and proposes a Climate–Water–Ecosystem framework to explore interactions, trade-offs, and synergies within arid environments. title: Influence of atmospheric circulation on temperature extremes in mountainous regions of Central Europe during 1961–2025
abstract: Abstract Recent climate change is most clearly manifested in rising global temperatures, with regionally amplified warming observed in Central Europe, including its mountainous areas. This study analyses trends in mean annual and seasonal air temperatures and evaluates the influence of atmospheric circulation on temperature extremes in Central European mountains during 1961–2025, comparing the periods 1961–1990 and 1991–2025. title: Mid-mantle discontinuities beneath subduction zones linked to depth-dependent deformation of bridgmanite
abstract: Bridgmanite, the main mineralogical phase in the Earth's lower mantle, is intrinsically anisotropic and may therefore generate seismic anisotropy in actively-deforming regions, particularly subduction zones. The bulk of the lower mantle is widely regarded as well-mixed but recent seismic observations suggest structures at mid-mantle depths whose origin remains unclear. Here, we propose a mechanism that could generate seismic discontinuities beneath subduction zones with depth distributions consistent with some of the observed mid-mantle reflectors. title: Positive-unlabeled graph ranking for assembly-center-oriented resilience-green sustainability evaluation of China Railway Express node cities
abstract: China Railway Express (CR Express) has become an important rail-based logistics corridor for improving Eurasian connectivity, regional openness, and sustainable freight organization. However, evaluating its node cities remains challenging because assembly-center labels are incomplete, city performance is network-dependent, and logistics development is increasingly shaped by resilience and green-sustainability requirements. title: Biofilm‐Mediated Persistence of Salmonella in Poultry Processing: A Comprehensive Review of Isolate Heterogeneity, Stress Adaptation, and Antimicrobial Resistance
abstract: Salmonella enterica remains a major foodborne pathogen in poultry-processing environments, where its persistence is largely attributed to biofilm formation on food-contact and non-food-contact surfaces. Despite extensive research on Salmonella control, persistent contamination continues to challenge food safety due to the complex interplay among isolate-specific traits, stress adaptation, and antimicrobial resistance (AMR). title: Forecasting European temperature-related mortality in Summer 2024: data-driven vs. physics-based forecast approaches
abstract: Abstract. Heat has emerged as a major public health concern. Over 62,000 heat-related deaths were estimated to have occurred during the European summer of 2024, exemplifying the pressing need to develop effective early warning systems. Such systems depend critically on the quality of the underlying forecasts, and recent work has focused on developing impact-based forecasts for heat-related mortality, which provide impact-oriented information. title: Urban accidents and safety governance in China (2015–2024): evolution, achievements, and future pathways
abstract: Urban safety governance is critical for China’s sustainable urbanization. This study evaluates the evolution of urban safety governance in China (2015–2024) through a five-dimensional analytical framework—resilience, risk governance, collaborative governance, spatial justice, and system modeling. abstract: Smart system and participatory process become buzz words in disaster risk management highlighting the importance of those concepts in reducing the impact of disasters effectively. Surabaya, like other cities, put a lot of effort to implement them in their administrative process especially in flood risk management. title: Recurrent hotspot zones of projected heat and dry-spell persistence across MENA
abstract: Persistent heat and dryness increasingly shape climate risk by extending exposure time, yet future projections are often communicated as pixel-wise changes that obscure recurrent spatial organisation. Here we identify recurrent hotspot zones of projected heat and dry-spell persistence across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). title: Path planning for logistics UAVs considering energy consumption and safety under wind field uncertainty
abstract: Wind disturbances at low altitudes increase energy consumption and safety risks for multirotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in densely built urban environments. High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is too expensive for online path planning, while threshold methods represent hazardous regions as binary no-fly zones. This study proposes a path planning framework that combines a Fourier neural operator (FNO) surrogate with a multiplicative cost model incorporating predictive uncertainty. title: Revealing hydrochemical regimes and health risks in an urban karst spring system
abstract: Groundwater in urban karst spring systems is increasingly impacted by coupled natural processes and anthropogenic nitrogen loading, yet the linkage between hydrochemical evolution, nitrate-related health risk, and contaminant transport remains insufficiently resolved. This study develops an integrated framework for the Baiquan spring system by combining hydrochemical analysis, entropy-weighted water quality index (EWQI), probabilistic health-risk assessment, numerical transport modelling, and multivariate clustering. title: Adaptive multi-agent optimization in intelligent-connected vehicles based on deep reinforcement learning
abstract: In order to provide offloading services for computationally demanding and time-sensitive operations on vehicles, multi-access edge computing has emerged as a successful paradigm. However, there are typically spatiotemporal load mismatches across edge servers due to significant vehicle mobility. As a result, task migration is used to transfer excessive tasks from overloaded to underloaded servers in order to maintain dynamic workload balance. title: Path dependency in multistage direct shear tests on a dense mixed-grained soil: a DEM-based micromechanical interpretation
abstract: Multistage direct shear testing reduces material demand and specimen-to-specimen variability compared with conventional testing, but later stages may become path-dependent because the specimen is not fully reset between loading steps. This study investigates this path dependency for a dense mixed-grained gravel–sand with plastic fines (GKB1) by combining laboratory tests with a DEM-based micromechanical interpretation. title: Spatiotemporal characteristics of vegetation responses to compound drought and heatwave events in Central Asia
abstract: With climate warming intensifying, compound drought and heatwave (CDHW) events have become more frequent and intense in arid Central Asia, severely affecting vegetation growth. However, systematic quantitative assessments of vegetation responses and their drivers under such compound extremes remain limited. Using meteorological and remote sensing data, we identified growing-season CDHW events across Central Asia from 1982 to 2023. title: U.S. oil and gas methane emission intensity declined 2019–2024 with little indication of federal policy impact
abstract: The U.S. federal government undertook a historic legislative effort to regulate methane emissions from the oil and gas sectors beginning in 2021 through the Inflation Reduction Act and Waste Emissions Charge. Despite a substantial rollback of these regulations in subsequent years, U.S. oil and gas methane emissions during this policy window are largely uncharacterized. title: Brief communication: Rise of the Guadalupe River – a multifaceted post event analysis of 4 July 2025, flood in Central Texas
abstract: Abstract. The flash flooding across Central Texas on July 4th, 2025, caused more than 130 fatalities and property losses exceeding 20 billion dollars. The objective of this study is to diagnose the drivers of this catastrophic event and to analyze the temporal variability in forecasting flood inundation dynamics in the hours leading up to and during the event. abstract: Abstract. The rapid development of Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) has established new computational paradigms for enhancing air quality modeling efficiency. title: Integrated assessment of meteorological drought impacts on terrestrial water storage and vegetation dynamics in East Africa
abstract: Abstract Water is essential for life, and effective hydrological management is crucial for economic stability and quality of life. Poor water resource governance can lead to scarcity, displacement, or even fatal consequences. Hydrological conditions in East Africa are influenced by drivers such as demographic expansion, industrialization, droughts, and vegetation dynamics. This study explores how total water storage in the region responds to drought intensity and vegetation variability. title: Evaluating the EPICC-Model for regional air quality simulation: a comparative study with CAMx and CMAQ
abstract: Abstract. This study presents a systematic evaluation of China’s independently developed EPICC-Model for regional PM2.5 and MDA8 O3 simulations against established international models, using WRF meteorological fields and a multi-source integrated emission inventory. Results highlight the strengths of the EPICC-Model in several aspects: it achieves relatively high spatial consistency with measurements for PM2.5, with an annual ​​index of agreement (IOA) of 0.80, and accurately captures pollution patterns in heavily polluted North China. title: Structural diagnosis and evolution of urban resilience in dryland oasis urban agglomerations from an eco-immunological perspective
abstract: Dryland oasis urban agglomerations face increasing drought risk, but gains in long-term adaptive capacity may not translate into stronger structural resilience because additive indices allow strong dimensions to offset weak ones. title: Evaluation of the Spatial Distribution of Some Thermal Comfort Indices in Iraq Using the RayMan Model
abstract: Lack of comprehensive evaluations of spatial thermal comfort parameters across Iraq remains a concern as the risks of excessive heat and climate change increase. This study analyzes the spatial distribution of outdoor human thermal comfort in Iraq using the Physiologically Equivalent Temperature (PET) and Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI). Monthly meteorological data from 38 stations (1981–2024) were obtained from the NASA POWER database and used in the RayMan model to calculate PET and UTCI. title: Analysis of Snow Cover Dynamics in the Beas River Basin during 2019-2021
abstract: Snow is a key component of the Himalayan cryosphere and plays a significant role in water resource availability and hydrological processes. This study examines the characteristics of snow cover in the Beas River Basin using MODIS satellite imagery for the period 2019-2021, with particular emphasis on temporal variations in snow cover and its potential influence on the hydrological cycle. abstract: The weld efficiency, fracture position and microstructure of dissimilar friction stir welded joints between Al-Mg and pure Fe, produced at rotational speeds of 300-1100 rpm and a constant welding speed of 100mm/min, were investigated using finite-element simulation, tensile tests, microhardness tests, scanning electron microscopy, transmission electron microscopy and electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) techniques. title: Does higher-resolution climate forcing improve impact model performance?
abstract: Abstract Climate-impact assessments increasingly use high-resolution climate forcing, often assuming that finer spatial detail improves impact projections. Yet this assumption has rarely been tested systematically across impact sectors, regions, and forcing variables. Here we use coordinated simulations from 16 impact models participating in the Inter-Sectoral Impact Model Intercomparison Project (ISIMIP) to evaluate how increasing forcing resolution from 60 km to 10 km, 3 km, and 1 km affects both climate-input accuracy and impact-model performance. title: Agricultural drainage networks as non-point phosphorus pollution control systems: Scale-dependent retention and primary drivers
abstract: Agricultural drainage networks increasingly function as distributed pollution control systems for mitigating non-point source phosphorus (P) export to aquatic ecosystems. However, the spatial heterogeneity of P retention and its specific drivers across varying ditch orders remain poorly understood, as most studies focus on isolated, single-order segments. title: Assessing Probable Maximum Precipitation in the Soummam Basin (Algeria) Using Bias‐Corrected Climate Projections
abstract: ABSTRACT Probable Maximum Precipitation (PMP) represents a major hydro‐meteorological hazard in Algeria, with its frequency and intensity increasing under the effects of climate change, thereby heightening threats to populations, infrastructure, and ecosystems. Yet existing PMP projections rarely employ multi‐variable bias correction or systematically compare correction methods, which is a critical gap given PMP's dependence on multiple correlated variables. title: Sensitivity of the summertime diurnal precipitation cycle over three representative regions of China to convective trigger and closure treatments in a single-column model
abstract: Abstract. Using a single‑column model, we investigate how trigger and closure treatments in ZM, TDK, and UNICON convection schemes affect DCP over China. abstract: Abstract The six-equation, single-velocity, two-phase flow model based on the diffuse-interface method (DIM) with stiff pressure relaxation has recently gained attention for its ability to handle metastable fluids, ensure robust positivity of volume fractions, and yield effective sound speeds consistent with Wood’s law. title: Hydrological response to climate change across semi-arid sub-basins of the Tensift watershed, Morocco
abstract: The hydrological systems of watersheds are increasingly affected by climate change, resulting in altered rainfall patterns, more intense droughts, and disrupted runoff. This study analyzes the impacts of these changes on streamflow across eight sub-basins of the Tensift Basin. To achieve this objective, the GR2M hydrological model was applied using bias-corrected climate data from five RCM–GCM modelling chains (CNRM, CMCC, IPSL, GUF, and ICTP) from the Med-CORDEX initiative. title: Long-term trends of carbon monoxide over the North Pacific upper troposphere from in-situ airplane measurements 1991–2018
abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) is not a greenhouse gas, but as the dominant sink of the hydroxyl radical it governs the oxidising capacity of the troposphere and so indirectly forces climate. Its trends in the North Pacific upper troposphere matter disproportionately: this is the principal outflow corridor for Asian anthropogenic emissions, the fastest-growing combustion source of the past half-century, yet it has almost no routine ground-based monitoring and satellite retrievals resolve it poorly. title: Satellite altimetry reveals heterogeneity in global flood peak timing and its shifts
abstract: Flood peak timing (FloPT) is a key indicator of hydrological responses to climate change. Yet global FloPT assessments is limited by sparse and uneven in-situ discharge observations. Here, we demonstrated the capability of satellite altimetry to estimate FloPT worldwide and presented the global map of observed FloPT, with a dramatic improvement in spatial coverage, especially in Global South countries. title: Climate Change Projections for Mexico in the 21st Century
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate change projections for Mexico remain subject to substantial regional and inter‐model uncertainty, particularly for precipitation. Here, we assess 21st‐century changes in temperature and precipitation over Mexico using 36 CMIP6 models under four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1‐2.6, SSP2‐4.5, SSP3‐7.0 and SSP5‐8.5). abstract: The increasing need for renewable energy has resulted in the swift proliferation of wind power, both onshore and offshore. In order for the adequate development of off shore wind industry, it is necessary to resolve some uncertainties with regards to foundation employed for these structures. With wind turbines becoming larger and more powerful, the need for strong, stable, and efficient foundation systems is more critical than ever. abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) geological modeling is an essential tool for assessing digital mine safety and detecting underground cavities. abstract: Abstract Recent observational studies have demonstrated that supersaturation fluctuations (SS’) in clouds induced by turbulence at scales smaller than 100 m can significantly affect microphysical processes such as aerosol activation and droplet condensation. title: Online capacitance-integrated development of a hybrid bioprocess model for industrial fungal fermentations
abstract: The growing demand for fermentation-based products has increased interest in bioprocess modelling approaches compatible with routinely available industrial process data. Capacitance probes are promising because they provide online data related to viable biomass, but their use in filamentous fungal fermentations remains challenging, as state-of-the-art cell-count-based calibration methods of capacitance data are not applicable to hyphal organisms under industrial settings. title: Future Northeastward Shift of Extratropical Transition of Tropical Cyclones Over the North Atlantic in Downscaling Projections
abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclones (TCs) often undergo extratropical transition (ET) at the midlatitudes, becoming post‐tropical cyclones (PTCs). We combine a logistic regression PTC identification model with synthetic TC tracks and intensities from the Columbia HAZard model (CHAZ) to project future ET completion over the North Atlantic (NA). Projections are based on downscaled outputs from 12 Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) models under three shared socioeconomic pathways (SSPs): SSP2‐4.5, SSP3‐7.0, and SSP5‐8.5. title: Modelling of 3D Fatigue Crack Growth in Tubular Joints: An Automated Framework for CFRP‐Strengthened T‐Joints Under Out‐of‐Plane Bending
abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents an automated computational framework for simulating three‐dimensional (3D) fatigue crack growth and adhesive delamination in carbon fiber‐reinforced polymer (CFRP)‐strengthened steel tubular T‐joints. The model integrates continuum damage mechanics with the extended finite element method (CDM‐XFEM) to concurrently simulate progressive damage in the steel substrate and failure at the bonded interfaces. title: Investigation of the effect of albatross bill impact on CFRP and GFRP wind turbine blades using Diomedea exulans collision scenarios
abstract: Wind turbine blades are highly vulnerable to damage from transverse loads such as bird collisions, which can compromise structural integrity, reduce aerodynamic efficiency, and raise ecological concerns. This study employed finite element simulations in Abaqus Explicit to examine the collision of a Diomedea exulans (wandering albatross) bill with Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer (CFRP) and Glass Fiber Reinforced Polymer (GFRP) blades. title: A quantitative model for embedding quantum-secure communications and evaluating communication autonomy in industrial control systems
abstract: Industrial control systems would increasingly depend on remote operation, online monitoring, and potentially autonomous control. This creates new requirements for secure, low-latency communications, and introduces new operational constraints on secret key availability, communication autonomy, and resilience under normal and abnormal conditions. We present a time-dependent quantitative model for embedding quantum-secure communications in an industrial control system and demonstrate its implementation on Purdue’s fully-digital 10-kWth research reactor (PUR-1). abstract: Abstract This study evaluates the capability of the MLUCM BEP + BEM to reproduce intra-urban variability of air temperature and relative humidity in Lecce (Italy) during summer 2025. A network of six measurement sites representing contrasting urban morphology, vegetation cover, and land-use conditions was used to characterize the thermo-hygrometric structure of the city and evaluate model performance. title: UAV integrated IoT sensing platform for sustainable air quality monitoring and real time AQI estimation
abstract: Monitoring modern air pollution requires flexible but portable systems that can be used to gather real-time data in various settings. This paper describes a drone-based air quality monitoring platform with IoT-enabled sensors integrated into it. The system carries multiple gas sensors CO, NO 2 , O 3 , SO 2 , and PM 2.5 , all managed by a Raspberry Pi 4 (Model B). The platform operates at a 1 Hz sampling rate performing onboard data filtering, dynamic caching and wireless synchronization with a cloud platform (ThingSpeak®) for real-time visualization. title: Accessibility and surface area drive desert toad presence at artificial water sites in the Great Basin and Mojave Deserts
abstract: Artificial Water Sites (AWS) are human-made or modified water sources constructed or maintained for livestock, select wildlife game species, or other management purposes in arid environments. However, non-target species such as desert toads have been documented utilizing AWS. Because the reproductive ecology of desert toads relies on water, understanding factors explaining their presence at AWS can inform conservation practices. title: Performance assessment and parametric analysis of CFST columns with various concrete infills
abstract: This study investigated the structural behaviour of Concrete Filled Steel Tubular (CFST) columns under axial compression using two infill materials: Lightweight Concrete (LWC) and Hybrid Fibre-Reinforced Concrete (HFRC). In Phase I, the LWC mix was developed by partially replacing the fine aggregate with perlite and the coarse aggregate with pumice stone, and incorporating PVA fibres. title: Planetary Boundaries and construction: pressures on water, air, and soil in Jordan
abstract: Background The Planetary Boundaries (PB) framework defines a finite safe operating space for humanity. In semi‑arid Jordan—one of the world’s most water‑stressed countries—urban construction is an important driver of pressures on scarce blue water resources, local air quality, and soil function. Objective This study (i) assesses how current construction practices in Jordan’s main urban centers translate into local Earth‑system pressures and (ii) proposes an Earth‑system governance model that links these pressures to enforceable project‑ and sector‑level controls. title: Information-preserving maximum likelihood noise analysis of GNSS coordinate time series with missing values in the first-differenced domain
abstract: Abstract Global Navigation Satellite System‌ (GNSS) coordinate time series often exhibit temporally correlated colored noise and missing values. When non-stationary noise component is present, first-order differencing can be used to transform the noise into a stationary process. However, the standard first-differenced Maximum Likelihood Estimate (MLE) discards all differenced observations involving missing epochs, resulting in an additional loss of valid differenced information.
