abstract: Individuals may understand environmental regulations yet fail to act on that knowledge, reflecting a persistent knowledge-action gap that conventional classroom instruction rarely addresses. To examine one potential remedy, we conducted a comparative field study in which 150 university students completed paper-based tasks on wetland protection laws either in a natural wetland park or in a classroom setting. abstract: Background The coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic demonstrates the importance of organizational sustainability across all sectors, and universities are no exception. It revealed deep-seated fragilities in institutional supply chains, revealing that the ability to sustain core educational and research missions is inherently connected to the robustness of supply chain capabilities, thus underscoring the need to shift from a reactive to a proactive stance in university operations. title: Adaptive observation weighting in TCKF1D-Var for ground-based multi-sensor thermodynamic retrievals prior to nocturnal heavy precipitation over China
abstract: Abstract. Ground-based microwave radiometers (GMWRs) and Mie–Raman lidars (MRLs) provide valuable thermodynamic observations for atmospheric profiling, but conventional variational retrieval frameworks typically rely on static observation weighting assumptions that may not adequately represent varying observation quality under precipitation conditions. To address this limitation, an adaptive observation weighting framework based on the Thermodynamic-Constrained Kalman Filter 1D-Var framework (TCKF1D-Var) is developed and evaluated using 107 nocturnal heavy-precipitation cases. title: Safety and Resilience in Slope Engineering Design for New Buildings under Extreme Rainstorm Climates
abstract: The safety of construction slopes holds significant importance in engineering and architecture, with the lack of resilience against extreme weather conditions being particularly critical. This paper systematically examines the fundamental flaws in traditional design theories regarding the limitations of compression-shear stress paths and the assumption of constant soil parameters. title: Modelling sediment transport and the relative dominance of sediment sources in agricultural catchments with the SWAT+ model
abstract: Abstract Purpose Greater understanding of the contributions from different sediment sources and their linkages to the downstream suspended sediment load (SSL) is essential to advancing knowledge of catchment sediment transport dynamics and informing sediment management. Implementation and uncertainty-based analysis of integrated catchment hydrologic and sediment models can provide valuable insights into sediment sources and their relative dominance at the catchment scale. title: Assessing long-term rainfall trends using non-parametric approach in Warangal district, Telangana, India
abstract: Assessing long-term rainfall variability is crucial for understanding regional hydroclimatic dynamics and informing water resource management; however, studies integrating rainfall trend detection with homogeneity assessment are scarce in the Warangal district of Telangana, India. This study presents a comprehensive spatio-statistical analysis of long-term rainfall variability in the Warangal district of Telangana, using the Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Station data (CHIRPS) dataset. abstract: Abstract. Stratosphere-troposphere exchange (STE) plays a fundamental role in the global atmospheric budget of chemical constituents. The troposphere-to-stratosphere transport (TST), as a part of STE, can inject anthropogenic pollutants from the Earth’s surface into the stratosphere, changing its chemical composition and influencing radiative processes. title: Research on engineering measures to mitigate the intensity of blast wave reflection in confined spaces
abstract: When explosions occur in confined spaces, the reflected waves generated by their interaction with confining surfaces can threaten the structural safety of nearby installations. To address this engineering challenge, this paper investigates the potential of column-shaped obstacle (CO), slope-shaped obstacle (SO), and forward-positioned slope-shaped obstacle (FSO) to mitigate the intensity of reflected waves through wave-obstacle interactions. title: Balancing theory and computational tools in undergraduate engineering education
abstract: The growing use of computational tools in engineering education creates opportunities for applied learning but also raises concerns that software proficiency may be prioritized over theoretical understanding. This qualitative descriptive study examined how undergraduate students in water resources and hydraulic engineering courses demonstrated theoretical understanding, theory-tool integration, and engineering judgment across laboratory assignments. abstract: In previous years, water is abundant in the Padsan River Watershed, even in tropical climates. However, with increasing variability due to global warming, the watershed faces disruption of water resources. This requires thorough study, yet with fragmented data management, it becomes challenging. abstract: This study aimed to develop a framework for mitigating cost and schedule overruns through the integration of Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) and the Analytic Network Process (ANP). Data were obtained from project documentation and questionnaires administered to five experts who assessed six factors and 23 internal subfactors contributing to cost and schedule deviations. abstract: Fuel Cell Electric Vehicles (FCEVs) provide zero-emission operation and high energy density, enabling their use as mobile clean energy for standalone DC grid support and vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) charging. The proposed framework aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goal 7, Affordable and Clean Energy. The proposed system experimentally evaluated an air-cooled Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFC) system under controlled DC load conditions and EVs battery charging. title: ENGLISH SLANG IN THE DIGITAL AGE: LEXICAL INNOVATION, PRAGMATIC CHANGE AND CROSS-PLATFORM VARIATION
abstract: This article examines contemporary English slang as a dynamic form of lexical innovation shaped by digital communication. Rather than treating social media as a neutral channel through which pre-existing slang is simply transmitted, the study approaches platforms as linguistic environments that influence the formation, circulation, reinterpretation, and partial normalization of slang units. abstract: Abstract This study evaluates drought-resilient maize production strategies under arid conditions using a Smart Adaptive Balanced Ranking Yoke (SABRY), a transparent sequential workflow that combines conventional statistical inference, entropy-weighted TOPSIS ranking, robustness assessment, and a separately reported conditional scenario analysis. Five treatments were assessed over two growing seasons in Nubaria, Egypt, using three independent field plots per treatment in each season. title: Bioclimatic optimization for medium density housing in Jakarta transit oriented developments through microclimate simulation
abstract: Rapid urbanization and the expansion of Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) in tropical megacities often overlook the microclimatic experience of pedestrians, leading to severe Urban Heat Island (UHI) effects and thermal discomfort. This study introduces and computationally evaluates the Bioclimatic Transit-Infill Housing (BTIH) concept, a medium-density housing model with minimum parking, located at the Blok A Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) station in Jakarta, Indonesia. title: Deformation-enhanced fluid evolution and skarn–IOCG transition in the Paleoproterozoic Elaine Dorothy Cu–Au system, Mount Isa Inlier, Australia
abstract: Abstract The Elaine Dorothy Cu-Au deposit, located in the Mary Kathleen Domain of the Mount Isa Inlier, Australia, records the interaction of Paleoproterozoic skarn metasomatism, fluid evolution, and deformation. The deposit is hosted by carbonate- and calc-silicate-rich rocks of the Corella Formation and comprises diopside–garnet–scapolite–wollastonite ± amphibole assemblages associated with pyrrhotite–chalcopyrite–pyrite mineralisation. title: Improved estimation of net ecosystem CO 2 exchange over North America using LSTM-based flux upscaling (2001–2021)
abstract: Abstract. Accurate estimation of regional-scale terrestrial carbon budgets is of great importance but remains challenging. With particular advantages, the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks method shows potential in improving regional carbon budget upscaling estimations. Here, based on LSTM, we upscale regional net ecosystem carbon exchange (NEE) with available flux tower measurements and satellite land surface observations in North America. title: From manual classification to transformer-based language models: assessing the quality and consistency of historical convective event records
abstract: Abstract. Historical text sources represent a central, yet methodologically challenging basis for the reconstruction of convective weather events. This study examines the extent to which historical reports on thunderstorms and hailstorms contain reliable climatological information, despite heterogeneous sources, varying degrees of detail and linguistic diversity. title: Using climate models in climate assessments: a Bayesian perspective
abstract: Outputs from complex Earth system models (ESMs) participating in the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP) are a major source of information for policy-relevant assessments of climate change. The way we view and interpret the CMIP archive shapes our understanding of the real world, yet many assessments present analysis choices only implicitly. abstract: Abstract. Lightning is one of the main sources of NOₓ in the Earth’s atmosphere, yet there is considerable variability in NOₓ production during thunderstorms. title: Non-monotonic response of net dust deposition kinetics to low wind speeds
abstract: Abstract. Dry deposition is a major sink for mineral dust, yet its behavior under weak winds remains poorly constrained and is often parameterized monotonically with wind speed. Here we quantify size-resolved dust deposition kinetics in a large closed-circuit recirculating wind tunnel using a two-stage protocol (brief high-wind loading followed by low-wind deposition at 0, 2, 4, and 6 m s⁻¹). title: Surface solar radiation and day-to-day temperature variability in China during 1961–2022: evidence from the dimming–brightening transition
abstract: Abstract Climate change affects natural and human systems not only through changes in mean temperature but also through rapid temperature fluctuations between consecutive days. Using homogenized daily mean and maximum temperature observations and reconstructed surface solar radiation at 1759 matched stations in China during 1961–2022, we evaluated the seasonal cycles, probability distributions, and long-term trends of day-to-day temperature variability (DTD and DTDMAX). title: Comparative analysis of rainfall erosivity estimation approaches and temporal resolution effects: A critical review supported by an observational case study
abstract: Accurate estimation of the rainfall erosivity factor (R-factor) is fundamental for soil erosion prediction and informed land conservation. This study provides a comprehensive review of the historical evolution and current status of R-factor estimation, ranging from simplified empirical equations to complex process-based models. Special emphasis is placed on data requirements, model assumptions, and method transferability. title: Advancing satellite-driven monitoring of phenological responses to extreme climatic events in the Alpine space
abstract: Climate extremes driven by climate change, such as heatwaves and severe droughts, have significantly impacted the ecosystem of the European Alps. Climate projections indicate that the frequency and intensity of such extreme events in this region will continue to rise. However, it remains unclear how heatwaves and extreme droughts affect the long-term evolution of local vegetation. Long-term time-series of satellite-based vegetation indices and climate records were analyzed to catch effects of climate extremes on spatiotemporal trends of plant phenology. title: An interpretable deep reinforcement learning framework for dynamic wind farm maintenance scheduling with enhanced power generation and stability
abstract: Wind farm maintenance scheduling is a challenging sequential decision-making problem due to the dynamic operational environment, multi-objective optimization requirements, and complex dependencies among turbine states, maintenance resources, and future power generation dynamics. Existing optimization and deep reinforcement learning methods often suffer from limited interpretability and insufficient capability in proactively balancing energy production efficiency and output stability. title: Integrating MaxEnt and MaxNet for climate-resilient habitat restoration: Predicting the ecological niche of Eucalyptus tereticornis in semi-arid landscapes
abstract: Accurate modeling of species distribution is essential for effective biodiversity conservation, afforestation planning, and land-use management. This study presents a comparative analysis of two prominent presence-only species distribution models Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) and MaxNet to evaluate their efficacy in predicting the ecological niche of Eucalyptus tereticornis in a semi-arid agro-climatic region. abstract: This study presents a synthetic proof-of-concept surrogate-assisted simulation–optimisation framework for identifying potentially mineralised locations using groundwater copper-isotope observations. The methodology adapts established groundwater contaminant-source characterisation principles, in which unknown source release histories are reconstructed from down gradient concentration measurements, to the investigation of concealed copper mineralisation. title: Mission-level H2 consumption modeling of a retrofitted Cessna 208B using ADS-B derived flight profiles
abstract: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the feasibility and operational efficiency of retrofitting a Cessna 208B aircraft with a hydrogen-electric propulsion system for short-haul cargo operations. Unlike conventional studies relying on idealized flight profiles, this research leverages real-world Automatic Dependent Surveillance–Broadcast (ADS-B) data sourced from Flightradar24 to simulate five actual flight missions. title: Non-stationary time series attribution for heatwaves over Europe
abstract: The increasing occurrence of extreme weather events since the beginning of the 21st century has led to the development of new methods to attribute extreme events to anthropogenic climate change. The way in which the extreme event is defined has a major influence on the attribution result. A frequently overlooked aspect concerns the temporal dependence of extremes. This study presents an approach for attributing complete time series during extreme events to anthropogenic forcing. title: Tracing Mantle Upwellings Beneath Changbaishan/Mount Paektu: New Insights From Transition Zone Discontinuity Structure
abstract: Abstract Intraplate volcanism in Northeast Asia, located in a distant back‐arc setting, challenges conventional models of mantle convection and volatile cycling. Using receiver function data from over 300 broadband stations, we image the mantle transition zone (MTZ) beneath the Changbaishan/Paektu volcano. title: A fuzzy c-means based dual-layer flux-blending framework for high-resolution dam-break simulations
abstract: Dam-break flow modelling involves a trade-off as resolving steep gradients requires high-order discretisations, yet these tend to generate spurious oscillations near discontinuities. Moreover, classical limiters used to suppress such oscillations rely largely on single-parameter algebraic indicator rules. This study replaces the procedure with a fuzzy c-means flux-blending framework for the finite-volume solution of the shallow water equations. title: Investigating the high seismic velocities and buoyancy of cratonic roots – the possibility of diamond
abstract: Abstract High seismic velocity keels extending to depths greater than 200 km underlie the oldest parts of continents, the Precambrian cratons. These keels have probably been formed early in Earth’s history, and the preservation of these deep, cold, and highly viscous roots in a convective mantle remains enigmatic. A classical view is that the excess density due to colder temperatures is compensated for by a light composition. Here, we map the magnesium number (Mg#, a proxi for mantle depletion) within cratonic keels, based on the thermochemical interpretation of a global shear velocity model.

title: Updating thermal head of RECoverable Autonomous Sonde (RECAS) for better drilling performance in Qilin Subglacial Lake exploration
abstract: Abstract. There are numerous subglacial lakes in Antarctica, typically covered by thick ice sheets. Qilin subglacial lake is one of the largest subglacial lakes in Antarctica, lying beneath approximately 3600 m of ice. The exploration of this unique environment is of considerable scientific importance. Recoverable Autonomous Sonde (RECAS) has been proposed for exploring Qilin subglacial lake. title: Melt Production and Volatile Release From Thermochemical Mantle Plumes
abstract: Abstract Mantle plumes are thought to generate Large Igneous Provinces (LIPs), the largest outpourings of lava in the geologic record, which are associated with long‐lasting climatic warming events and mass extinctions. However, the controls on mantle degassing by plumes remain poorly constrained. Here we use thermochemical plume models to compute the melt production and carbon release from compositionally heterogeneous plumes that sample peridotite and eclogite. title: A prototype multi-hazard early warning system integrating flood and landslide forecasting: application in the upper Garonne River Basin
abstract: Multi-Hazard Early Warning Systems (MHEWS) are essential for disaster risk management, yet operational implementation remains limited by challenges in hazard integration, forecast uncertainty, and computational requirements. This study develops and evaluates a fast and lightweight prototype MHEWS integrating fluvial flooding and shallow landslide forecasting. title: A sensorless and explainable decision-support framework for risk-aware photovoltaic cleaning prioritization in desert environments using public environmental datasets
abstract: Abstract Photovoltaic (PV) systems in desert environments experience substantial soiling losses, while dedicated soiling sensors can increase monitoring cost and maintenance burden. This study develops a sensorless, risk-aware decision-support framework for PV cleaning prioritization using daily NASA POWER meteorological data, with PVGIS-SARAH3 used as an independent solar-resource consistency check at the target coordinate. title: Designing expandable digital learning ecosystems through student-generated immersive learning environments
abstract: Introduction Immersive technologies and student participation have transformed digital education by enabling learners to contribute not only to learning activities but also to the development of digital learning environments. However, existing studies primarily focus on individual gamified applications or immersive learning experiences, while the long-term evolution, reuse, and institutional integration of student-generated environments remain insufficiently explored. title: Circular Economy and Construction Waste Management in Saudi Mega-Projects: Pathways Towards Vision 2030 Sustainability Targets
abstract: Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 is accelerating the delivery of large-scale urban, tourism, transport, industrial and infrastructure projects while simultaneously strengthening national ambitions for environmental protection, resource efficiency and waste diversion. The scale of this development creates a strategic challenge: construction and demolition waste cannot be managed only as an end-of-pipe disposal problem. abstract: Abstract The impact of long-term snow cover variability on winter tourism in the mountainous areas of Poland is an increasingly important research topic, particularly in light of the anticipated effects of climate change. abstract: Abstract Despite extensive research on the Nile River Basin, few studies represent the entire basin as a connected hydrology–infrastructure–demand system. Existing basin-wide models are either dated, not openly accessible, or limited in their integration of hydrological processes, infrastructure operations, and spatially distributed water demand. abstract: Accurate assessment of lake water balance is vital for sustainable management in data-scarce regions. abstract: Introduction Urban expansion in arid regions drives vital socio-economic development but places significant pressure on urban systems through land competition and infrastructure strain. abstract: Precipitable water vapor (PWV) is critical for severe weather forecasting, yet existing GNSS Precise Point Positioning (PPP) retrieval methods are limited by neglecting tropospheric horizontal gradients and lacking regional coverage. abstract: Aceh is at the edge of Indonesia, with a high level of disaster vulnerability and difficulties in managing its humanitarian logistics system. abstract: Abstract The Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets exhibit high variability in flow speed, over multiple orders of magnitude. abstract: Abstract The diversification of herbivorous dinosaurs and the rise of angiosperms in the Late Cretaceous are each well established, but the link between them is debated. Broad-scale diversity patterns in the two groups appear not to closely align, and there is no direct evidence of dinosaur adaptation to angiosperm-based diets. abstract: Abstract The growing global demand for clean and sustainable energy has increased interest in hydrogen as an alternative fuel that is both affordable and widely accessible. While substantial research has focused on hydrogen generation through serpentinization, the potential of organic-rich systems remains largely unexplored. title: Tracking hydrological drought propagation in river networks: an event-based framework
abstract: Hydrological droughts are dynamic phenomena that evolve across space and time, propagating through river networks under the influence of climatic forcing, catchment properties, and human regulation. Despite substantial progress in drought research, most existing approaches rely on aggregated indicators or statistical relationships, limiting their ability to explicitly characterise how individual drought events propagate within connected river systems. abstract: Flood early warning in data-scarce regions is constrained by sparse gauging and limited modelling capacity. abstract: ABSTRACT Colloidal photonic crystals (CPCs) serve as versatile optical platforms for healthcare sensing and real‐time physiological monitoring. Recent developments have focused on scalable assembly techniques and the integration of CPCs with stimuli‐responsive hydrogels. abstract: Giant ficrons are a rare but recurrent sub-type of Acheulean handaxe, that in Britain are predominantly found in assemblages dating to the MIS 9 interglacial. abstract: Groundwater decline in irrigated semi-arid alluvial plains reflects interacting land-surface, climatic, pumping, and hydrogeological controls. This study evaluates spatial associations among urbanization, Curve Number-based event-runoff potential, regional climate variability, and groundwater-depth change in Multan, Pakistan. abstract: Abstract Glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) pose a growing risk in high mountain regions as climate-driven glacier retreat accelerates lake expansion and new lake formation. abstract: Abstract This study investigates the broadband vibration attenuation and energy-dissipation mechanisms of obstacle grid particle dampers attached to cantilever plates through sweep-frequency experiments and discrete element method (DEM) simulations. Damper locations were selected based on the principal modal antinode regions, and the responses of bare-plate, added-mass, grid-free, and obstacle-grid configurations were compared for vertical and horizontal arrangements. title: Aerodynamic Characteristics and Wind Load Partitioning in Double-deck Girders: Effects of Inter-deck Clearance Height
abstract: The inter-deck clearance height (IDH), defined as the vertical distance between decks, is a key parameter in the aerodynamic design of double-deck bridges. abstract: Abstract This study investigates the crashworthiness performance of thin-walled columns equipped with functionally graded, multi-level spherical crush initiators. The proposed concept extends previous solutions by introducing a sequence of embossments with varying diameters and depths along the column height, enabling controlled variation in local structural deformation resistance and progressive folding under impact loading. abstract: Net primary productivity (NPP) varies with climate and soil resources, but whether species-level plant traits provide information beyond these environmental controls remains unclear. abstract: Abstract Offshore blast walls are critical safety barriers designed to protect personnel and equipment from hydrocarbon explosions. Traditional designs often struggle to simultaneously satisfy code requirements for deflection limits and weld integrity under high-intensity blasts. abstract: This research addresses the need for sustainable manufacturing and quality assurance of high-load components in the oil and gas sector within the frameworks of Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0. abstract: Background Dyslipidemia is an important modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, and growing evidence suggests that long-term ambient air pollution exposure may adversely affect lipid metabolism. abstract: Abstract Bladeless resonant wind turbines are an alternative technology for small-scale wind energy harvesting because they convert vortex-induced structural oscillations into electrical power without rotating blades. abstract: Abstract Generated by differential surface heating within the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL), thermals are essential for sustaining flight in non-motorized aviation such as paragliding, hang gliding, and gliding. title: Stochastic thermodynamics and predictability of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes: an application to the Madden-Julian Oscillation
abstract: Climate oscillations are intrinsically out-of-equilibrium phenomena, yet the connection between their predictability and nonequilibrium thermodynamic properties remains unexplored. We develop a coarse-grained stochastic thermodynamic framework for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) processes and apply this framework to climate data via linear inverse models (LIMs), linking predictability, entropy production, dynamical activity, and path action. title: Similar evapotranspiration responses mask contrasting modes of water access during drought in California
abstract: Atmospheric warming raises evaporative demand, but actual evapotranspiration (ETa) may track demand or decouple under water limitation. Here, we quantified demand-tracking ability from regression slopes relating deseasonalized ETa and reference evapotranspiration (ETo) anomalies across California during 2008-2024. Forests and croplands retained similar positive tracking under severe drought, whereas grasslands and shrublands showed weak or negative responses. title: A Two-Element Capsule Antenna for Near-Field Polarization MIMO in Wireless Capsule Endoscopy
abstract: Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MIMO) technology is considered to be a viable method for spectral efficiency and data rate enhancement in wireless communications. This article presents a two-element capsule antenna with orthogonal current distributions for polarization multiplexing in a wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) application at 915 MHz. The proposed antenna was evaluated in a MIMO link where it served as the transmitter and an existing on-body antenna was the receiver. The performance was assessed in two distinct environments: an anatomically accurate human body model using full-wave (FW

title: Solitons in the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with the pseudo-Raman term, anti-diffusion gain and nonlinear loss
abstract: We introduce a nonconservative nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE) which includes additional nonlinear terms accounting for the pseudo-stimulated-Raman-scattering (pseudo-SRS) effect and cubic loss. An essentially novel feature of the model is the linear anti-diffusion gain, which leads to the obvious blow-up in the infinite or spatially periodic system. We consider the absorptive boundary conditions, which suppress the blow-up driven by effective convective instability in the setup. institutions: National Research University Higher School of Economics

title: Energy conserving compatible space--time FEM for deterministic and stochastic rotating shallow water
abstract: We present a fully discrete energy conserving discretisation of the rotating shallow water equations with arbitrary order in space and time. A space time finite element discretisation is used, built from compatible finite element methods in space and continuous Petrov-Galerkin schemes in time. Projected auxiliary variables for Hamiltonian derivatives are necessary for exact energy conservation. We provide an iterative solver approach based on monolithic patch smoothers, which allows us to efficiently converge a Newton method sufficiently that energy errors due to the solver are very small. title: Polarforming for MIMO Covert Communications
abstract: Covert communication conceals wireless transmission activity, but conventional multi-antenna designs rely mainly on spatial beamforming and can be constrained by limited spatial degrees of freedom. This paper investigates polarization-reconfigurable antenna (PRA)-aided multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) covert communication, where Alice and Bob perform transmit and receive polarforming, respectively, and Willie uses a vertically polarized antenna for radiometric detection. We jointly optimize the transmit covariance matrix and the transmit and receive phase shift vectors to maximize Bob's a

Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: Interplay between Excitability and Noise in Analog Spiking Neurons
abstract: A spiking neuron is a dynamical system exhibiting a limit cycle (a spike) when subject to sufficiently excitatory input. Famous neuroscience experiments by Bryant and Segundo as well as Mainen and Sejnowski revealed that the spike times of some biological neurons are more reliable when subject to time-varying stimuli compared to constant ones. Provided with an industrial physics-based transient noise SPICE simulation framework compatible with foundry transistor compact models, we have demonstrated similar behaviours for a CMOS analog spiking neuron designed for neuromorphic computing hardware

title: Molecular Structure Effects in Low-Lying $P$-wave Bottom-Strange Meson Spectrum
abstract: Recently, the LHCb Collaboration reported a new narrow bottom-strange meson, $B_{s0}^*(5700)$ with mass $M= (5698.9 \pm 1.5 \pm 0.6)$~MeV, width $Γ<9.8$~MeV, and spin-parity $J^P=0^+$ in the $B_s^0π^0$ invariant-mass spectrum. Motivated by this observation, we study the low-lying $P$-wave $B_s$ mesons in a two-stage refined constituent quark model. The one-loop radiative corrections to the confinement--one-gluon exchange potential ($α_s^2$) lower the whole multiplet by $25$--$50$~MeV and improve the level ordering; however, the scalar $B_{s0}^*$ mass still exceeds the LHCb data by $\sim120$~Me

title: WEEVIL: design and commissioning of an ice-sublimation chamber and a cryogenic submillimeter radiometer for studying rarefied gas plumes
abstract: We present WEEVIL (WatEr Emission of Vapor from Ice in the Laboratory), an experimental facility developed to study ice sublimation under laboratory conditions to support observations of comets and icy moons. The setup combines a submillimeter heterodyne radiometer and a high-vacuum cryogenic chamber, enabling spatially and temporally resolved monitoring of gas plumes formed during ice sublimation under controlled laboratory conditions. This paper describes the facility's design and implementation. Furthermore, we present the commissioning of the experimental setup, including the first water-v

title: Entropy-Stable and Well-Balanced Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for the Compressible Euler Equations in Vector-Invariant Form
abstract: We develop structure-preserving methods for the compressible Euler equations with gravity in vector-invariant form and potential temperature as a prognostic variable within the flux-differencing discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method (DGSEM) framework. By discretizing the nonconservative terms as symmetric and antisymmetric products, we derive two-point numerical fluxes that conserve both the thermodynamic entropy and the total energy. title: Accessing electronic entanglement via photo-assisted two-electron tomography
abstract: Witnessing entanglement between electrons propagating in quantum circuits requires accessing their two-electron coherences, which encode the two-particle quantum correlations generated by Coulomb interactions. Yet, experimental reconstruction of two-electron coherence remains a major challenge. We introduce photo-assisted two-electron tomography, a quantum coherence reconstruction protocol from dc-currents and time-averaged current correlations, routinely measured in electron quantum optics experiments. title: DNA-based monitoring uncovers contrasting salinity-driven diversity patterns of bacterial and protist plankton in the Baltic Sea area
abstract: Salinity has been identified as a primary factor structuring community composition in global diversity assessments of free-living bacteria in non-extreme environments. It remains unknown whether the same is true for protists. Moreover, changes in alpha diversity of both bacteria and protists across the brackish salinity gradient remain elusive. Here, we analyzed protist and bacterial diversity using DNA metabarcoding across 398 surface water samples synchronized with national monitoring of the Baltic Sea and the Kattegat-Skagerrak. title: Patterns and environmental drivers of marine annelid distribution in the Arctic Ocean
abstract: The Arctic Ocean (AO) is experiencing declining sea ice extent and thickness and increasing sea surface temperatures, with cascading consequences for the entire ecosystem. Here, we compiled all available occurrence records of marine Annelida from the Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS) and the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GIF) and analyzed the number of records, the number of species, and expected species richness (ES15 and ES50) in relation to depth, ecoregion, ca. 12,500 km 2 hexagonal cell and associated them with environmental drivers. title: Multiple strategies and cues define baleen whale migration
abstract: Migration is a do-or-die life-history strategy, yet factors shaping it remain poorly studied in many marine taxa, as direct observations are difficult. Building on animal migration theory, we used satellite tracking data from 21 southern right whales tagged in Aotearoa New Zealand to investigate migratory cues, timing and routes. Whales followed either a direct westward route or a longer, indirect route via higher latitudes when migrating from their wintering grounds to summer feeding grounds. journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
institutions: Istituto di Scienze Marine del Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche

title: Hidden subsurface suspended sediment export from Greenland's marine‐terminating glaciers
abstract: Abstract Runoff and calved ice volumes from the Greenland Ice Sheet are well constrained, but quantifying the associated suspended sediment flux remains challenging. Here we present near‐terminus observations from three glacierized fjords in southeast Greenland, combining full‐depth turbidity profiles and current velocity from summer 2024 to evaluate sediment export. We identify extensive subsurface sediment plumes from marine‐terminating glaciers which are undetectable using remote sensing approaches and underrepresented in fjord sediment‐core reconstructions. Southern University of Science and Technology

title: Ancient terrestrial forests reborn as modern marine ecosystems under shifting sea levels
abstract: Abstract Sea-level rise and coastal erosion can submerge terrestrial carbon-rich landscapes, yet the ecological fate and climate significance of such relict coastal carbon deposits remain largely unknown. We report the discovery of submerged tropical peat reefs in the shallow coastal waters of the Bazaruto Archipelago, Mozambique; a legacy of ancient coastal forests now transformed into benthic marine habitats. title: Mathematical Modelling of the Black Sea Coastline Considering its Fractal Structure and Grid Generation
abstract: Introduction . The coastline of a reservoir is a complex natural object, which geometry has irregularity and signs of selfsimilarity, and the length depends on the scale of measurement. Despite the widespread study of its fractal properties, the transition to a digital representation of the coastline is a complex procedure and is a current topic of research. title: Ocean acidification pushes Mediterranean marine calcifiers toward a tipping point
abstract: Abstract The increasing emission of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) is altering seawater chemistry, lowering ocean pH and threatening marine biodiversity. Predicting how marine biota will be adversely affected by ocean acidification (OA) remains a key challenge. Here, we document that functional morphological traits offer a more robust metric of calcifier sensitivity to OA than taxonomic diversity alone. Using benthic foraminifera from a Mediterranean CO 2 vent system, we identify an empirically derived pH threshold beyond which community structure and function shift markedly. institutions: Centre for Arctic Gas Hydrate, Environment and Climate

title: Documented technology adoption in environmental impact assessment: a mixed-methods study of adoption–perception gaps in Korea
abstract: Despite rapid advances in AI, big data analytics, GIS, real-time monitoring, and predictive modeling, their integration into environmental impact assessment (EIA) practice remains poorly documented. This study employs a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design to examine documented technology adoption in Korean EIA and Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA). title: Where Should E-Commerce Fulfillment Hubs Be Located?A GIS–MCDM Framework for Supporting SMEs in Libya
abstract: E-commerce in emerging and fragile markets often develops faster than the physical logistics systems required to support reliable and efficient order fulfillment. This study develops an integrated geographic information system (GIS) and multi-criteria decision-making framework for evaluating candidate cities for e-commerce fulfillment hubs in Libya. title: Integrating Strategic Environmental Assessment into Regional Development Planning for Sustainable Development in Bireuen Regency
abstract: Regional planning in Bireuen has to respond to basic-service needs while also dealing with pressure on watersheds, forested land, and areas exposed to hydro-meteorological hazards. This paper examines how far the 2025-2029 Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is carried into the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (Indonesian term: Rencana Pembangunan Jangka Menengah Daerah/RPJMD), rather than remaining a separate compliance document. title: UGRAS: A GIS-based integrated flight safety risk analysis system using a multi-criteria and data-driven approach
SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT FOR ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION IN BANGLADESH: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES
abstract: Bangladesh exemplifies a central paradox of sustainable development: how to maintain rapid economic and social progress without undermining the ecological systems upon which development depends. This paper critically examines Bangladesh's environmental governance architecture, the major barriers to its effective implementation, and opportunities for achieving a just green transition. It adopts a qualitative, desk-based methodology combining doctrinal legal analysis with critical examination of national policies and plans, international commitments, judicial decisions, and institutional reports
journal: Journal of Asian and African Social Science and Humanities

title: Ziviler Katastrophenschutz: Einbindung von Bürgerinnen und Bürgern in Hochwasserszenarien und Sturmfluten mit mobilen Anwendungen
abstract: Zusammenfassung Der Klimawandel erhöht das Risiko von Sturmfluten und Hochwasserereignissen und stellt bestehende Warn- und Krisenkommunikationssysteme vor wachsende Herausforderungen. title: Comparing Strava and survey-based data for coastal recreation accounting
abstract: Coastal zones provide recreational ecosystem services across land and sea, yet spatial data for ecosystem accounting is limited. We compared Strava activity data with survey-based public participation GIS (PPGIS) data across the Oslofjord, Norway, to assess spatial and sociodemographic biases in crowdsourced recreation accounting. Strava over-represented activities along the coastal belt and across marine areas, while under-representing island visitation and leisure-oriented activities. title: An Ecosystem-Based Marine Spatial Planning Approach for Sustainable Natural Resources Management in the Bangladesh Delta
abstract: Despite the establishment of maritime boundaries with Myanmar (2012) and India (2014), which secured sovereign rights over approximately 118,813 km² of the Bay of Bengal, marine space is still managed on a sector-by-sector basis, and no marine spatial plan has been prepared. This study identifies significant ecological, economic, and cultural areas within Bangladesh's maritime zone, and proposes a framework for the blue economy and develops an ecosystem-based model of marine spatial planning (MSP). title: Cardiac responses to underwater sound playback in juvenile green and loggerhead sea turtles: an exploratory biologging study
abstract: Anthropogenic underwater noise is an increasing concern in marine environments, yet physiological responses of sea turtles remain poorly understood. We examined cardiac responses to underwater sound playback in three juvenile green turtles (Chelonia mydas) and four juvenile loggerhead turtles (Caretta caretta) maintained after incidental capture. Electrocardiogram, acceleration, depth, and turtle-borne acoustic data were recorded during 44 trials. title: Multilocus phylogeny and historical biogeography of the pill millipede genus Rhopalomeris (Diplopoda, Glomerida) in Thailand
abstract: Abstract Southeast Asia is widely recognized as a global biodiversity hotspot with a complex geological history and high species richness across multiple taxa. The pill millipede genus Rhopalomeris Verhoeff, 1906 has received increasing taxonomic attention in recent years, with several new species described, particularly from western Southeast Asia, including Thailand and Myanmar. However, its historical biogeography has remained insufficiently understood. title: Measurements of the Size and Physical Properties of Marine Particles Using Atomic Force Microscopy: Implications for Marine Biogeochemical Cycles
abstract: Abstract Particle size and physical properties such as stiffness and adhesiveness affect sinking velocity and flux in the ocean, yet conventional two‐dimensional measurements lack accuracy and mechanical information. In this study, we applied atomic force microscopy (AFM) to quantify three‐dimensional size and physical properties of marine particles. Three hundred and sixty‐eight particles were collected using a marine snow catcher from the pycnocline and benthic boundary layer at three coastal‐to‐offshore stations in the northwestern Pacific. title: Spatial disparities in surf-resource sustainability: Implications for coastal policy and marine education in Taiwan
abstract: This study situates global surf sustainability within the Taiwanese context, where recreational surfing has developed since the 1980s and expanded internationally after 2010, yet region-wide assessments of surf-resource sustainability remain limited. Little is known about how sustainability conditions vary across Taiwan’s coastal regions, which sustainability dimensions contribute most strongly to these disparities, and what implications such patterns have for coastal governance and marine education policy. title: Temperate marine macrophytes are highly variable sources of Biogenic Volatile Organic Compounds – a comparative study from the Baltic Sea and NE Atlantic
abstract: Abstract. Biogenic Volatile Organic Compounds (BVOC), emitted by Earth’s ecosystems, affect several chemical processes in the atmosphere that have profound climate impacts. Despite their climate relevance, global BVOC budget estimations are still highly uncertain, with ocean-derived emissions being particularly poorly constrained. Marine macrophytes (i.e. macroalgae and seagrass) are a large and widespread organismal group whose BVOC emission rates are particularly poorly quantified. title: Combined effects of elevated temperature and fluoxetine exposure on early development of the sea urchin Paracentrotus lividus
abstract: Temperature rise associated with climate change increases the vulnerability of coastal species, which are also exposed to pharmaceuticals. We investigated the effects of thermal stress and fluoxetine (FLX), alone and in combination, on early developmental stages of the sea urchin Paracentrotus lividus, a key coastal species. Gametes, zygotes and embryos were exposed to ambient (18°C) and near-future projections (21°C, 24°C) to identify the most sensitive developmental stage to warming. In parallel, environmentally relevant FLX concentrations were tested under near-future temperature scenarios.

title: ANOVATS: a subsampling-based test to detect differences among short time series in marine studies
abstract: Assessing marine ecosystems is important for understanding the impacts of climate change and human activity, as well as for maintaining healthy oceans and ecosystems. In marine science, it is common for biologists and geologists to identify regional differences based on expert knowledge, frequently through data visualization. However, time series data collected through surveys in marine studies typically span only a few decades, limiting the applicability of classical time series methods. title: A source-to-sea decision-support framework for wet-weather wastewater load management: evidence from Jiaozhou Bay
abstract: Coastal concentration compliance can overlook increased wastewater throughput during wet weather. We developed a source-to-sea decision-support framework using 2019–2022 wastewater, river, and marine observations from Jiaozhou Bay, China. The analysis combined source-record auditing, hydraulic and concentration decomposition, benchmark comparison, and source–receptor chronology. At Loushan wastewater treatment plant, throughput increased by 87.5% from the second to the third quarter of 2020 while total phosphorus remained low at 0.06–0.07 mg L −1 . title: 4-MBC in Australian sunscreens as an unmonitored discharge pathway into Great Barrier Reef coastal waters
abstract: Abstract 4-Methylbenzylidene camphor (4-MBC, also known as enzacamene), a chemical UV filter prohibited or never permitted across the EU, UK, China, ASEAN, US, and Japan, remains legal in Australian therapeutic sunscreens at concentrations up to 4% w/w. The European Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety concluded in 2022 that no safe concentration could be established, and the UK Scientific Advisory Group on Chemical Safety confirmed this in 2025. title: Tracing Groundwater–Seawater exchanges using geochemical tracers (radon, radium, stable isotopes of water) in a seasonally frozen beach
abstract: Groundwater–seawater exchanges remain poorly documented in subarctic and arctic regions, particularly during winter, when coastal ice alters hydrogeology conditions and limits sampling opportunities. This study investigates winter groundwater dynamics at a seasonally frozen beach by combining the use of various geochemical tracers. Stable water isotopes (δ 2 H and δ 18 O) were used to identify the origin of the water, whereas short-lived radioisotope tracers ( 222 Rn, 223 Ra, 224 Ra) were used to trace subsurface geochemical processes along the groundwater flow path, from the upper beach to th

title: FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT AND EXPORT SOPHISTICATION IN ASEAN-5 DURING THE ASEAN PLUS THREE COOPERATION PERIOD
abstract: Export sophistication is widely regarded as a channel through which trade contributes to sustained growth, yet evidence on its relationship with foreign direct investment (FDI) in Southeast Asia during the period of deepening ASEAN Plus Three (ASEAN+3) cooperation remains limited. This study examines trade with China, Japan, and the Republic of Korea (South Korea) and the relationship between FDI inflows and export sophistication in five ASEAN economies (Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand) over the period of the ASEAN Plus Three Cooperation Work Plan 2007-2017. title: Marine habitat use and movement of sympatric anadromous Dolly Varden and Arctic Char in the Canadian Arctic
abstract: Abstract Objective Inuit subsistence fishers in Kugluktuk, Nunavut, Canada, have noticed changes in the timing and locations of their catches of Arctic Char Salvelinus alpinus and northern form Dolly Varden S. malma malma (collectively referred to by the community as “char”) in the past ∼20 years. In response, an ongoing research program was formed to study char in partnership with the Kugluktuk Hunters and Trappers Organization. title: Mathematics anxiety and problem-solving ability in numerical methods courses: A repeated cross-sectional study across two Southeast Asian universities
abstract: Mathematics anxiety (MA) impedes mathematical learning by taxing cognitive resources, negatively affecting problem-solving ability (PSA). Some evidence suggests that the strength and nature of this negative association may vary across educational and cultural contexts. However, cross-cultural studies on MA and PSA, especially in Southeast Asia, remain limited. This study investigated cohort-level patterns of MA and PSA in a transnational Numerical Methods course at Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia (UTHM) and Universitas Pahlawan (UP), Indonesia. title: Experimental snowball earth viscosity drives the evolution of motile multicellularity
abstract: Abstract During the 70-million-year span of the Cryogenian Snowball Earth glaciations, low ocean temperatures beneath global sea ice increased water viscosity up to fourfold. In the absence of adaptation, unicellular organisms living in this viscous environment were limited in their ability to move and acquire nutrients. We experimentally test the hypothesis that multicellularity evolved in order to overcome this viscosity-induced metabolic deficit. title: Baltic Sea sediment bacterial communities show asymmetric and incomplete recovery after reciprocal temperature change translocation
abstract: Abstract Marine coastal systems are important for global biogeochemical cycling and are particularly sensitive to climate change effects due to their shallow depths, which results in rapid heat transfer to the sediments. Here we used one-year reciprocal in situ translocations of sediments between a Baltic Sea long-term (>50 years) warming-influenced bay and a nearby unaffected control bay to predict how the sediments and their associated bacterial communities may respond to future climate change and whether those changes were reversible. title: Assessment of Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion Potential in Cenderawasih Bay, Papua, Indonesia: Energy Performance, Techno-Economic Feasibility, and Environmental Considerations
abstract: This study evaluated the potential of Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion as a renewable electricity source in Cenderawasih Bay, Papua, Indonesia. Ocean temperature data from the World Ocean Atlas for 1955-2018 at station 21576 were analyzed to characterize the surface and deep-water thermal conditions and to assess the performance of an open-cycle Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion system. The assessment covered thermodynamic efficiency, electrical power generation, production cost, freshwater production, and potential environmental impacts. title: Remobilized volcanogenic sediments boost photophysiological activity in three symbiotic reef-building coral species
abstract: Abstract Coral reefs that surround volcanic islands are continually influenced by run-off carrying remobilized volcanogenic sediments. Although unaltered volcanic ash is known to supply trace metals that enhance coral holobiont productivity, the impacts of long-term exposure to weathered tephra, a far more likely scenario in island settings, are less understood. title: Particle-tracking assessment of potential groundwater pathways for radionuclide transport across the Futaba Fault, coastal Fukushima, Japan
abstract: Radiocesium deposited after the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant accident remains a long-term environmental concern, but its groundwater pathways toward inhabited coastal lowlands are poorly constrained. This study evaluates conservative groundwater pathways potentially relevant to radionuclide transport near the Futaba Fault in coastal Fukushima by coupling a steady-state MODFLOW-2005 model with MODPATH 7. title: From shark hunters to sea guardians: Environmental literacy transformation and socio-ecological transformation of the Bajo people in Sapeken Islands, East Java-Indonesia
abstract: The Bajo people are known for their closeness to and dependence on the sea. Over the past few decades, the Bajo people have undergone significant changes that are worth examining. This study aims to analyze the socio-ecological transformation of the Bajo people who inhabit Sadulang Besar Island, Sapeken Archipelago, East Java, with particular attention to how environmental literacy, intergenerational learning, and shifting livelihood strategies have contributed to changes in marine practices and ecological identity. title: A Modular, Cloud-Based GIS Platform for Automated Wildfire Risk Index Mapping
abstract: Wildfires are a growing environmental and socio-economic threat driven by climate change and land abandonment. As fire frequency and intensity increase, suppression alone is no longer sufficient, making prevention and preparedness essential. Earth Observation and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) enable the integration of environmental and socio-economic factors into decision-support tools for wildfire risk assessment. title: Hydrodynamics of bio-mimetic sponge arrays with non-uniform triangular arrangement under wave actions
abstract: Bio-inspired marine structures have attracted increasing attention as nature-based solutions for modifying coastal hydrodynamics and enhancing momentum exchange. Previous studies on isolated and dual sponge-inspired elements have shown limited hydrodynamic effectiveness under relatively low-height waves, where velocity redistribution and turbulence generation remain weak. To address this limitation, the present study proposes and experimentally fabricates a bio-mimetic pillar coral composed of non-uniform triangular sponge elements arranged in a progressive three-line configuration. title: Ocean predators as indicators of nano- and microplastic prevalence in pelagic food webs
abstract: Abstract Quantifying nano- and microplastics (NMPs) in ocean predators is fundamental to understanding the prevalence of these contaminants and potential impacts on ecosystem health. Pyrolysis gas chromatography tandem mass spectrometry with lipid correction was used to determine NMP concentrations and polymer composition in the muscle tissue of two pelagic predators (dolphinfish [ Coryphaena hippurus ], yellowfin tuna [ Thunnus albacares ]) across the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans. title: Unraveling the roles of shallow coastal habitats and salinity in shaping aquatic microeukaryotic communities using experimental and field approaches
abstract: Abstract Microeukaryotic communities in brackish coastal ecosystems are structured by complex interactions between environmental conditions and habitat heterogeneity. This study examines how moderate salinity levels (ranging from freshwater to salinity 6) and habitat type (water column, sediment, and biofilm) influence microeukaryotic diversity and community composition in shallow coastal waters of the Gulf of Finland, the Baltic Sea. title: Marine holobionts: a model arena for host–microbe biology, from ecosystem function to biotechnology
abstract: Abstract Microbial symbioses are the operating system of marine biology. Nearly every macroscopic organism in the ocean exists as a holobiont, the consortium composed of a eukaryotic host and its bacterial, archaeal, microeukaryotic and viral partners. Marine holobionts span a broader range of the metazoan tree of life than likely any other ecological setting on the planet. This breadth makes the marine realm a uniquely informative system to investigate how host-microbe partnerships shape organisms and ecosystems. title: Advanced Assessment of the Agro-Silvo-Pastoral Coherence in Transboundary Transitional Water Regions
abstract: Transitional waters play a vital role in the ecological health and sustainability of coastal areas. According to European Union legislation, transitional waters are coastal water bodies influenced by freshwater flows but are partly saline due to their proximity to the sea. This study focuses on agricultural and forestry regions adjacent to transboundary transitional waters—i.e., areas where two or more countries share an estuary, tidal inlet, delta, or lagoon and have a contiguous border in their territorial waters. title: Environmental Security of the Gulf During Armed Conflict: Marine Pollution Risks, GCC Preparedness, and a Regional Emergency-Response Framework
abstract: The Gulf is a strategically crucial and environmentally vulnerable semi-enclosed marine system supporting petroleum industries, international shipping, desalination facilities, coastal ecosystems, and urban centers. Alongside chronic industrial and maritime pressures, armed conflict introduces severe risks via direct military operations, targeting of energy infrastructure, drone and missile strikes, hazardous material releases, and disruption of monitoring networks. This review evaluates the potential marine pollution consequences of armed conflict in the region, examining historical precedent
journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities

title: Seascape genomics reveals high genetic diversity and apparent panmixia in endemic Southern Ocean phytoplankton
abstract: Abstract The adaptive potential and resilience of cold‐adapted phytoplankton to climate change have the potential to impact polar marine food webs and global biogeochemical cycles. Two central but poorly constrained facets of adaptive potential in polar phytoplankton are standing genetic diversity and its spatial structure. Here, we partially sequenced 30 field isolate genomes of a commonly‐occurring endemic Southern Ocean (SO) phytoplankton, the diatom Actinocyclus actinochilus , and analyzed patterns in standing genetic diversity and geographic structure. title: Small-scale fishers’ perceptions and behavioural responses to marine protected areas implementation
abstract: Marine protected area (MPA) implementation can lead to fishers’ displacement and opposition to conservation efforts. Yet, evidence on how MPAs affect fishing operations is limited, especially for the small-scale sector. Surveys and participatory mapping exercises (n=93) were carried out with small-scale fishers in four Mediterranean and one Black Sea MPA to investigate fishers’ behavioural responses and perceptions to MPA implementation. title: Industry-led mitigation of seal bycatch in North Sea pelagic trawl fisheries: Evaluating excluder device effectiveness and policy implications
abstract: Bycatch of marine mammals in commercial fisheries presents conservation, operational, and regulatory challenges, particularly in the Greater North Sea where trawl fisheries targeting forage fish overlap with seal foraging habitats. This study evaluates the effectiveness of two seal excluder devices—the DPPO’s excluder tube and the PFA’s excluder grid—designed to reduce incidental seal captures in sandeel and herring fisheries, respectively. title: Public perceptions and (lack of) support for mitigation of artificial light at night in coastal cities
abstract: Artificial light at night (ALAN) is an expanding environmental pressure in urban areas, yet effective mitigation depends on public support. We investigated how residents of two Chilean coastal cities perceive ALAN, its impacts and potential mitigation measures. Respondents demonstrated asymmetric environmental literacy, recognising the societal benefits of lighting while showing limited awareness of its ecological consequences, particularly for coastal-marine ecosystems. title: Intra-annual dynamics of larval fish assemblages and their environmental associations in the central Southern Black Sea
abstract: Larval fish assemblages are crucial indicators for monitoring marine ecosystem dynamics and the recruitment potential of fishery stocks. This study investigates the spatiotemporal dynamics of larval fish assemblages in the central Southern Black Sea (Sinop) and the environmental parameters shaping these patterns. An intra-annual monthly sampling survey identified 35 species across 20 families; the assemblage structure was dominated by Engraulis encrasicolus, Gobius niger, Sprattus sprattus, Mullus barbatus and Trachurus mediterraneus. title: No effect of short‐term exposure to ocean acidification on individual‐level variation in behaviour and susceptibility to predation in a Great Barrier Reef damselfish
abstract: Abstract Ocean acidification, caused by rising carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) in the atmosphere, has been reported to negatively impact a wide variety of behaviours in fishes, including activity, exploration, and predator avoidance. These effects have been documented at the population level, but many animal species naturally show large and repeatable individual‐level differences in behaviour. title: Cumulative impact of climate change and adaptation measures on Venice and its lagoon
abstract: Abstract Adaptation measures to climate change can generate unintended environmental consequences, particularly in vulnerable coastal systems. In the Venice Lagoon, the Mose mobile barrier system was designed to protect the city from sea-level rise and storm surges, still ensuring the lagoon-sea exchange. However, under climate change the frequency and duration of Mose closures will increase and this might modify lagoon water renewal and affect ecosystem properties. title: Effects of the summer season and religious holiday periods on tropospheric NO₂ levels in Türkiye’s coastal tourism destinations: A Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI and GIS-based analysis (2023–2025)
abstract: This study investigates tropospheric NO2 variations observed in the Mediterranean and Aegean regions—Türkiye’s prominent coastal tourism hubs—during the 2023–2025 period, within the context of seasonal summer intensity and short-term mobility during Eid al-Fitr (Ramadan Feast) and Eid al-Adha (Feast of Sacrifice). The study utilizes Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI tropospheric NO2 data to generate daily regional median values for selected coastal tourism districts. title: Microphytobenthos Primary Production and Organic Matter Mineralization Along the Sea Level Gradient in a Tropical Mudflat
abstract: Tropical tidal flats represent more than half of the global tidal flat area, however information on the ecological and biogeochemical role of microphytobenthos (MPB) in tropical environments remains scarce. The objective of this study was to analyze the changes in sediment biogeochemistry, MPB, community composition and net metabolism along the sea level (SL) gradient in a tropical tidal flat (Punta Morales, Gulf of Nicoya, Costa Rica). title: Offshore wind farm impacts on marine fauna across taxa and ecological levels: A global review
abstract: The expansion of offshore wind farms (OWFs) is central to global decarbonization strategies, yet their effects on marine biodiversity are only partially understood. This systematic review synthesizes 221 publications up to June 2025 to assess the ecological impacts of OWFs on marine fauna living below the sea surface. The evidence base is uneven, heavily focused on North European waters, fish, and invertebrates, while expanding OWF regions and marine mammals remain underrepresented. title: Fin whale movement patterns from the Mediterranean sea reveal summer habitat use in the North Atlantic and potential feeding behavior
abstract: Abstract Understanding the movements of highly mobile marine species is essential for identifying critical habitats and developing effective conservation measures. Although occasional movements of fin whales ( Balaenoptera physalus ) between the Mediterranean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean have been reported, the extent to which these movements represent a recurrent component of Mediterranean fin whale ecology remains unclear. title: GIS-based assessment of population and dwelling exposure to landslide-prone areas in the Valencian Community (Spain)
abstract: The spatial identification of population exposure to landslide-prone areas is essential for risk-informed territorial planning, particularly where impacts affect peri-urban and dispersed residential areas rather than consolidated urban centres. This study presents a GIS-based, multi-scale methodology to quantify and locate population and dwelling exposure beyond administrative boundaries by integrating landslide susceptibility mapping, residential cadastral data, and high-resolution population information from the 2021 census grid. title: Self-reporting alkalinity-responsive hydrogel for visual monitoring and microenvironment remodeling of seawater-immersed infected wounds
abstract: Seawater-associated infected wounds involve alkaline and hyperosmotic stress, polymicrobial contamination, biofilms, and persistent inflammation, collectively delaying healing. Herein, we developed QCB-Au@SPG, a pH-responsive hydrogel integrating fluorescent antibacterial QCB-Au, an alkali-sensitive SA-PBA network, and photocrosslinkable GelMA. title: Distinct drivers control trace metal distributions through the Atlantic Ocean
abstract: Trace metals (TMs) including iron, manganese, cobalt, nickel, copper, zinc, cadmium, and lead have important biogeochemical roles in the ocean. However, the controlling factors of TM distributions have not yet been quantified and investigated on an ocean scale. Here we take a holistic approach to demonstrate that transport through water masses formed in high latitudes can explain 60–90% of dissolved TM distributions and >75% of TM inventories in the interior Atlantic. title: Measuring Dry Deposition of Sea Spray Aerosol and Height of Aerosol Plume Using a Controlled Wave Pool
abstract: Abstract Deposition of sea spray aerosols facilitates atmospheric corrosion of materials, requiring maintenance and replacement over time. However, the dimensions of sea spray aerosol plumes produced from breaking waves have not been well‐characterized, limiting useful prediction of particle transport downwind and atmospheric corrosion. Therefore, this project aimed to measure sea spray aerosol production from breaking waves in a controlled environment at several elevations to obtain the height profile of an aerosol plume. title: Episodic High‐Latitude Occurrence of Walleye Pollock ( Gadus chalcogrammus ) in the Central Arctic Ocean Associated With Warm Subsurface Conditions: Multi‐Year Environmental DNA and Larval Evidence
abstract: ABSTRACT Episodic high‐latitude occurrences of subarctic fish due to Arctic warming present significant challenges for managing high‐latitude ecosystems. In this study, we present four consecutive years (2021–2024) of integrated environmental DNA (eDNA) monitoring and larval surveys for walleye pollock ( Gadus chalcogrammus ) conducted aboard the Korean icebreaker IBR/V Araon in the Chukchi Sea (CS) and Central Arctic Ocean (CAO). title: Carbon fluxes within an Arctica islandica habitat in the German Baltic Sea
abstract: Ongoing climate change and rising CO 2 emissions highlight the need to understand ecosystem carbon cycling to guide the conservation of carbon-rich, biodiverse habitats. We investigated organic carbon cycling and storage associated with the long-lived bivalve Arctica islandica in the German Baltic Sea. Through filtration and bioturbation, A. islandica may enhance the burial of organic carbon in deeper sediment layers. title: Visualizing the penetration behavior of tapered thread piles via transparent soil: Effects of thread design
abstract: With superior construction efficiency and load-bearing performance, precast tapered thread piles hold significant potential for offshore and coastal infrastructure. However, their installation mechanics remain poorly understood, and visual experimental investigations are scarce. title: Comparative Evaluation of Seawater-Based and Conventional Fixatives on Histological Quality in Broiler Chicken Tissues
abstract: Lung, liver, brain, heart, kidney, and spleen tissues obtained from 60 broiler chickens at a commercial abattoir in Afyon Province were fixed using six fixation solutions consisting of 10% neutral buffered formalin (NBF) or 70% ethanol, each prepared with distilled water, seawater (salinity approximately 38‰), or a distilled water–seawater mixture. title: PREFERENCES OF DIGITAL NOMADS: ANALYZING POPULAR DESTINATIONS AND DECISION-MAKING FACTORS THROUGH INTERACTIVE DATA VISUALIZATIONS USING PUBLIC ACCESS DATABASES
abstract: Digital nomadism is a rapidly spreading form of location-independent work that is fundamentally transforming the global labour market, economy, and tourism. The aim of this study is to quantitatively explore and model the destination preferences of digital nomads and to present an innovative, interactive data visualization framework. Our research analyses the structural changes of the period 2021-2024 following the logic of the PEST model (Political, Economical, Social, Technological). title: Eco-phenotypic characterization of Candida palmioleophila from poultry litter and marine environments: implications for One Health
abstract: Candida palmioleophila is an emerging opportunistic yeast frequently misidentified within the Meyerozyma guilliermondii complex, potentially obscuring its clinical and ecological relevance. Although its clinical significance is increasingly recognized, the phenotypic characteristics of environmental isolates remain poorly explored. title: Transformación Digital de la Gestión Financiera Universitaria: Implementación del Sistema SCVRP con Inteligencia de Negocio y Dashboards Interactivos
abstract: La dependencia de procesos manuales para validar pagos universitarios suele provocar errores administrativos y retrasos que afectan a los estudiantes. Para resolver esta situación, se implementó el Sistema de Control de Verificación de Recibos de Pago (SCVRP) en el Tecnológico Nacional de México, Campus Lerdo. Este trabajo no se limitó a digitalizar documentos físicos, sino que buscó transformar los datos financieros en herramientas de gestión útiles. abstract: Seagrasses have gathered increasing attention due to their multifaceted ecological roles. Apart from their ecological significance, seagrasses have exhibited potent antifungal properties, indicating potential for diverse applications. The antifungal efficacy of methanolic extracts derived from five seagrass species ( Cymodocea serrulata , Cymodocea rotundata , Halodule pinifolia , Halophila ovalis , and Syringodium isoetifolium ) was assessed against pathogenic fungal strains using the agar well diffusion method. title: GIS-based spatial prioritization of natural-hazard exposure and recorded COVID-19 case counts in Lemery, Batangas, Philippines
abstract: Local governments often maintain separate natural-hazard maps and health-surveillance records but lack a transparent method for identifying areas where these concerns overlap. This study applied a Geographic Information System (GIS) sieve-mapping approach to prioritize the 46 barangays of Lemery, Batangas, Philippines using 2,505 confirmed COVID-19 cases and ten natural-hazard layers covering seismic, landslide, coastal, flood, and volcanic hazards. title: Epistemic justice and deep-sea mining: UNCLOS’s facilitation of epistemic diversity the International Seabed Authority’s decision-making process
abstract: The paper discusses epistemic justice as a central justice framework to be considered in the regulatory process of exploitative deep sea mining, with the aim of bringing attention to the relevance of epistemic justice and diversity to deep sea mining scholarship. Epistemic justice is here understood as deeply connected to a broader social equity, and entails the fair treatment of different ’knowers’ and a creation, sharing, and validation of knowledge that is fundamentally diverse rather than based on one dominant knowledge-tradition. title: Advancing Micro-Ecotone Mapping Using UAV Photogrammetry and GIS
abstract: Ecotones are transitional boundaries between ecosystems and essential to regulating biodiversity and ecological processes. Although ecotones are often wider transition zones like aquatic-terrestrial boundaries, they can happen at fine spatial scales (micro-ecotones) and occur over only a few meters or even centimeters. In the past, ecotones have been examined using one-dimensional transects or coarsely resolved remote sensing data for analysis. abstract: Abstract Sparisoma cretense is undergoing a range expansion across the Mediterranean Sea, yet its establishment at northern latitudes of the westernmost Mediterranean remains uncertain. During July 2025, patterns consistent with the establishment of S. cretense in Cabrera National Park (39º 09’ N; 2º 57’ E) were assessed, and habitat features associated with its occurrence were identified. title: Best Practices in Open and Reproducible Antarctic Marine Sediment Core Research
abstract: Abstract Marine sediment cores from Antarctica are archived by national programs for reuse and resampling by future researchers, creating a resourceful way to conduct Antarctic science. With reduced budgets to conduct Antarctic field work and to collect new sediment cores offshore of the icy continent, the accessibility of these archived cores and availability of core data are in high demand. title: Phased ecological assembly of Triassic marine reptile faunas following the Permian–Triassic mass extinction: ecospace dynamics in South China
abstract: The Permian-Triassic mass extinction triggered a fundamental reorganization of marine ecosystems, yet the community-level functional dynamics of early marine reptile radiations remain understudied. Here we quantify ecospace dynamics of Triassic marine reptile faunas across an approximately 20-million-year sequence in South China, integrating 10 functional traits of fossil taxa and modern ecological analogues. abstract: Purpose – This study aims to implement Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) for analyzing election logistics distribution monitoring reports at Bawaslu RI and to develop an interactive dashboard to support topic exploration. The study addresses the difficulty of manually interpreting large collections of institutional reports containing operational, administrative, geographical, procurement, and legal information related to election logistics distribution. title: Interactive Effects of Episodic Warming and Phosphorus Pulses on Plankton Food-Web Rewiring In Freshwater Mesocosms
abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are increasingly exposed to short-duration heatwaves and episodic phosphorus inputs, both of which can substantially alter aquatic community structure and ecosystem functioning. However, the combined effects of these environmental stressors on plankton food-web organization and trophic interaction dynamics remain insufficiently understood. abstract: The shear strength of coral sand-pile interface affects the bearing capacity of pile foundation in island and reef engineering. However, there is still a lack of interface shear strength prediction model that can comprehensively consider the influence of multiple factors. title: A coupled water-quality–Ecopath with Ecosim model incorporating sand-lance aestivation dynamics in the Harima-Nada Sea
abstract: Sand lance ( Ammodytes japonicus ) is an important forage fish in the Harima-Nada Sea, Japan, but its stock has declined markedly in recent decades under concurrent changes in nutrient availability and water temperature. To clarify the mechanisms underlying these changes, we developed a region-specific coupled water-quality–Ecopath with Ecosim (EwE) model that explicitly incorporates sand-lance aestivation dynamics. title: SPATIAL STRATEGIES AND IMPLEMENTATION PATHWAYS FOR THE ALL-AGE FRIENDLY RENEWAL OF OLD COMMUNITIES IN ZHUHAI UNDER THE ORIENTATION OF MODERN MARINE CITIES
abstract: Coastal cities have shifted from outward expansion to reworking the housing stock they already hold, and renewing aging communities has become harder to manage as a result. Three pressures overlap in these neighborhoods: a resident profile that no longer matches the original design brief, almost no slack in the public space budget, and marine-climate risks that accumulate rather than arrive one at a time. title: Modulation of ETCCDI-based extreme rainfall indices by ENSO and the Indian Ocean Dipole over topographically complex North Sumatra, Indonesia
abstract: This study examines the characteristics of extreme rainfall in North Sumatra Province, Indonesia, and its teleconnections with the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD). The analysis uses a blended daily rainfall dataset from 1990 to 2024, combining station observations from the Indonesian Agency for Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics (BMKG) with the Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Station (CHIRPS) satellite data. title: Integrating AHP–GIS with Geophysical Validation for Groundwater Recharge Zonation in Samaru, Zaria, Nigeria
abstract: Groundwater plays a critical role in meeting domestic, agricultural, and industrial water demands, particularly in regions where surface water resources are limited or unreliable. Effective identification of groundwater recharge zones is therefore essential for sustainable planning and management. This study delineates groundwater recharge potential zones in Samaru, Zaria, Nigeria, by integrating the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) with Geographic Information System (GIS) techniques, supported by geophysical validation.
