title: Spatial organization and coordinated development of offshore wind industrial chains under governance decentralization: evidence from China's coastal provinces
abstract: Offshore wind industrial chains, encompassing upstream component manufacturing, midstream project development and operation, and downstream grid integration, underpin large-scale utilization, yet their spatial organization, structural linkages, and coordinated development remain underexamined. title: Reviewing the climate change landscape in South Africa’s marine fisheries: progress, gaps, and future directions
abstract: Climate change is reshaping South Africa’s marine ecosystems and fisheries with consequences for ecological productivity, livelihoods and governance. Although research on climate impacts on fisheries has expanded, the overall climate-risk landscape for South African fisheries has not been reviewed using the risk framing proposed in the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Fifth Assessment Report (AR5). title: Fluid–substrate coupled controls on mineral‑phase selection in the Kunlun hydrothermal system
abstract: Abstract Mineral precipitation at submarine hydrothermal vents transfers redox‑sensitive elements from the lithosphere to the ocean. However, conventional plume and sediment‑trap sampling poorly preserves particle‑scale signatures generated at reactive interfaces, hindering robust interpretation of near‑vent mineralization. title: Design and Implementation of an AIS Vessel Trajectory Visualization System Based on AMap
abstract: To address the challenges posed by the large volume and dense spatial distribution of AIS position data, as well as the limited support for interactive queries in conventional static displays, this paper designs and implements an AIS vessel trajectory visualization system based on AMap. title: Captive-raised juvenile hawksbill ( Eretmochelys imbricata ) turtles display naturalistic behaviours upon ocean release
abstract: Some conservation programs keep turtles temporarily under human care with the intention of releasing them later to strengthen wild populations. Historically, researchers have questioned whether key survival behaviours might be lost during captive-raising, potentially reducing post-release survivability. Yet no published studies have examined the in-water behaviour of captive-raised turtles in a way that allows comparison with wild conspecifics – an important gap for the critically endangered hawksbill turtle (Eretmochelys imbricata). abstract: Coastal habitats are characterized by steep and spatially heterogeneous environmental gradients that can influence plant population structure, growth and reproductive performance.Peucedanum japonicum is a coastal perennial plant distributed across diverse habitats, but differences in population characteristics and individual performance among populations under different local environmental conditions remain poorly understood.We compared vegetation, environmental conditions, structural characteristics, and individual growth and reproductive traits of P. japonicum across three habitat types in K

abstract: Abstract Although snakes of the genus Oxyrhopus are generally regarded as opportunistic predators, the relative roles of interspecific dietary differentiation, ontogenetic variation, and predator morphology in their feeding ecology remain poorly understood. We analyzed the diet of 253 preserved specimens representing four Oxyrhopus species from Bahia, Brazil. abstract: Abstract The Gulf of Suez is a geologically significant rift basin, characterized by Miocene-age formations that formed through extensional tectonics during the Tertiary period, ultimately facilitating the divergence of the Arabian Peninsula from the African continent. This region has considerable geothermal potential, making it a strategically valuable asset for developing clean, sustainable energy infrastructure. title: Growth, physiological responses, and water quality in juvenile Malabar grouper reared in a low-salinity RAS: An 84-day operational trial
abstract: Recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) are expanding globally as a sustainable aquaculture technology. Although RAS enable intensive production of marine fish, their high capital and operating costs necessitate strategies that improve growth efficiency while maintaining stable water quality. Low-salinity seawater promotes growth in many marine fish species; however, concerns remain that reduced salinity may impair biofiltration. abstract: This study aims to determine the effectiveness of freestyle swimming learning using a visualization model on the development of students' basic movements at SDN Mekargalih 4. The background of the study stems from the problem of low understanding of freestyle swimming techniques in students, especially related to the coordination of hand, foot, breathing, and body position movements. title: Spatial Assessment of Heat Health Risk in Brussels Through GIS and Local Climate Zone Analysis
abstract: Climate change and rapid urbanization are increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme heat events, posing significant risks to public health in cities. Although numerous studies have investigated urban heat islands and heat vulnerability, spatially explicit assessments integrating environmental, demographic, and urban morphological characteristics remain limited, particularly in European cities. abstract: Flooding remains a major environmental challenge in Ilorin Metropolis, Kwara State, Nigeria. abstract: ABSTRACT In Coastal Bangladesh, community-based water management groups (WMGs) and water management associations (WMAs) have been central to participatory water governance, yet their postproject sustainability remains uncertain. abstract: Green hydrogen is central to global decarbonization, yet its rapid expansion exposes a severe spatial contradiction: the regions possessing optimal renewable energy potential are overwhelmingly the planet’s most water-stressed and ecologically fragile landscapes. abstract: Crop rotation analysis is fundamental to understanding agricultural landscape dynamics, yet the complexity of multi-annual, spatially explicit agricultural data presents significant analytical challenges. abstract: Abstract Biodiversity loss threatens ecosystem services on which humanity depends, yet the strength, form and context-dependency of biodiversity–ecosystem service and biodiversity–ecosystem function relationships remain poorly quantified. abstract: ABSTRACT Open‐pit coal mining severely degrades soil and ecosystem functions, constraining regional sustainability. abstract: Ascetosporea is a group of parasitic protists within Endomyxa that primarily infect marine invertebrates and can cause serious damage to fishery resources such as oysters and prawns. Although approximately 50 species have been formally described, environmental DNA (eDNA) studies suggest that their diversity remains largely underestimated, with many lineages yet to be discovered. title: Have You Done Your Duty? Impact of Direct Mailing Campaign on Septic System Owners' Maintenance Knowledge and Behaviors in Coastal Texas Watersheds
abstract: As part of a watershed protection plan, the Texas Water Resources Institute and AgriLife Extension Service developed and distributed an educational postcard (``mailer'') about septic system maintenance to mailing addresses outside of public sewer service areas. The mailer was distributed four times within 1 year. The impact of this mailer was evaluated with a retrospective pre/post-test within a mailed survey. abstract: The article addresses air stability effects on whitecap coverage at sea. This is achieved by using the logarithmic mean wind speed profile including a stability function as well as adopting two sea surface roughness formulas. title: Exact traveling wave and soliton solutions for an extended (2+1)-dimensional shallow water wave equation
abstract: This paper investigates a nonlinear partial differential equation that models shallow water waves in the ocean. By applying the extended Wang’s direct mapping method and the extended hyperbolic function method, a variety of soliton solutions are obtained, including both bright and dark solitons. The study examines the behavior and physical properties of these solitons, with particular emphasis on the influence of temporal parameters on their propagation. abstract: Rapid coastal urbanization increases exposure to multiple hazards while intensifying competition for land essential for safe emergency refuge. This paper proposes a reproducible decision-support framework for planning Disaster Prevention and Relief Accessible Green Spaces (DPRAGS). title: Spatiotemporal Differentiation and Influencing Factors of Overseas Chinese Architectural Heritage: A Case Study of Minnan, China
abstract: The Minnan region in southern Fujian, China, comprising Quanzhou, Xiamen, and Zhangzhou, is one of China’s major traditional qiaoxiang (overseas Chinese hometown) regions. This study develops a spatial database of 682 Minnan Overseas Chinese Architectural Heritage (MOCAH) sites, divides their formation into four historical periods—Qing Dynasty (pre-1912), Early Republican Period (1912–1936), Wartime Republican Period (1937–1948), and Early PRC Period (1949–late 1970s)—and applies GIS-based spatial and statistical methods to examine their spatiotemporal differentiation and influencing factors.

abstract: This study develops a web-based digital marketing platform for tourism-sector micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Rua Village to improve access to business information, product promotion, ordering, and transaction management. The research applies a software engineering approach through system analysis, system design, Agile Scrum development, and system testing. abstract: Metal halide single crystals exhibit superior optoelectronic properties, promising for applications in optics and energy. title: Inventorization of spatial patterns and reassessment of benthic foraminiferal assemblages from mangrove ecosystems of Bay of Bengal
abstract: Mangrove ecosystems across the northeast coastal Bay of Bengal are highly productive yet increasingly showing vulnerability to climate change. This study presents a comprehensive inventory of benthic foraminifera from the Indian Sundarbans mangrove and the Budhabalanga estuary along with surrounding mangroves by integrating published records with new observations. title: Developmental temperature induces consistent patterns of plasticity in lower, but not upper, critical thermal limits in threespine stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus)
abstract: Abstract Developmental plasticity, where early-life environmental cues shape developmental trajectories with lasting impact into adulthood, may play an important role in determining how species respond to changing thermal environments. We used marine threespine stickleback ( Gasterosteus aculeatus ) to investigate whether temperature experienced during embryonic development has persistent effects on critical thermal limits as adults. abstract: Abstract Bacterial resistance to heavy metals (HM) poses a significant risk to ecosystems and human health. This study evaluated resistance to HM of 24 bacterial isolates from two deep aquatic environments in southern Brazil: the Guarani Aquifer System (GAS) water and the Rio Grande Cone (CRG) marine sediment. title: Harem polygyny through resource defense territoriality in the sandperch Parapercis pacifica (Pinguipedidae)
abstract: In reef fishes inhabiting sandy rubble habitats, such as sandperches, a mating system with territorial female-type harems has been widely confirmed. Parapercis pacifica (Pinguipedidae) is a relatively large sandperch with large territorial home ranges. abstract: This study developed an antifouling polypyrrole (PPy) membrane on a hydrolyzed polyacrylonitrile (PAN) support incorporating a titania nanosheet-graphitic carbon nitride (TNS-GCN) nanocomposite interlayer for the treatment of aerobically treated crude oil-containing wastewater. title: Simulation analysis of self-excited oscillating water jet with petal-shaped nozzle under confining pressure
abstract: The self-excited oscillating water jet is widely used in ocean engineering. Its effectiveness stems from the impact of cavitation collapse driven by periodic pressure pulsations. This study investigated the flow field evolution and vortex stretching mechanisms of self-excited oscillating water jets using large eddy simulation. title: Hawksbill turtle (Eretmochelys imbricata) nesting enhances meiofaunal abundance and structure in an urban sandy beach
abstract: The northeastern coast of Brazil hosts some of the highest nesting densities of hawksbill turtles ( Eretmochelys imbricata ) in the South Atlantic, where nesting events represent an important pathway for marine-derived nutrient inputs into oligotrophic sandy beaches. Within this context, we evaluated the influence of hawksbill turtle nests on meiofaunal assemblages at a highly urbanized tropical beach during the 2020/2021 nesting season, a period uniquely marked by the COVID-19 pandemic. title: Morphology of glochidia and early developmental processes in Unio delicatus (Bivalvia: Unionidae)
abstract: In this study, embryonic development in the gonad and glochidia development in the gill marsupium of Unio delicatus (Bivalvia: Unionidae) were examined using morphological, visual, and statistical analyses. The study was conducted in Gölbaşı Lake (Hatay Province) from January to December 2024, with twenty individuals sampled monthly. title: Active nuclease inhibition over passive freezing secures the genomic archive of fish eye lenses
abstract: Fish eye lenses offer a chronological archive of individual life histories and preserve genomic DNA. However, integrating ecological and genetic data is hindered by post-mortem nuclease degradation, and standardized DNA preservation protocols for this tissue remain undefined. We evaluated chemical and thermal preservation methods to maximize DNA yield and integrity from fish lenses. title: Tetrodotoxin (TTX): What do we currently know? The state of the art
abstract: Tetrodotoxin (TTX) is one of the most potent naturally occurring neurotoxins and continues to attract considerable scientific, clinical, forensic, and regulatory attention. Historically associated with pufferfish poisoning in East and Southeast Asia, TTX has recently emerged as a global food safety concern due to its detection in an increasing number of marine and terrestrial organisms and its expanding geographical distribution, including European coastal waters. abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution and bacterial antimicrobial resistance are converging public health concerns. MPs provide persistent, mobile surfaces that can transport antibiotic-resistant bacteria and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). After aging and conditioning, MPs can develop biofilms in which resistance determinants accumulate, persist, and undergo horizontal transfer. abstract: The cross-hole sonic logging (CSL) method is a widely used nondestructive testing (NDT) technique for pile integrity assessment. However, conventional CSL methods are inadequate for precise defect identification due to low data utilization, limited testing efficiency and poor localization accuracy. To address these limitations, an improved ultrasonic tomography (UT) technique based on CSL and source-point ray tracing is proposed in this regard. title: “The Guy(s) from California”: Race, the Tax Code, and the Relational Geographies of Rental Housing in Memphis
abstract: This article examines how high net worth, individual investors from coastal markets have reshaped the rental market in Memphis, Tennessee, and could be playing a growing role in housing markets across the United States. Drawing on interviews with local “turn-key” real estate companies and a computational analysis of property data across Memphis, I show how the historical trajectory of racial capitalism, coupled with the fallout of the 2008 financial crisis, has enabled local property managers to channel out-of-state investment from high-cost markets like California into Memphis neighborhoods.

abstract: Collagen-rich marine biomass is a promising source of proteins, peptides, and glycosaminoglycans, but their recovery is constrained by the dense extracellular matrix. This study evaluated high-pressure processing as a short-duration, non-thermal strategy for systematically disassembling the mutable collagenous tissue of Stichopus fusiformiossa and promoting endogenous biotransformation without added water or exogenous enzymes. abstract: Context: Climate change and anthropogenic stressors are degrading coastal biogenic habitats, disrupting the vital pathways fish use to shift from nearshore nurseries to offshore reef environments. abstract: This study investigates the effects of inorganic salts and natural water matrices on the high-frequency sonochemical degradation of Naphthol Blue Black (NBB). abstract: ABSTRACT The Upper Assam Basin, forming the eastern segment of the Assam–Arakan Basin in northeast India, preserves an exceptional record of passive‐margin, marine shelf and foreland basin evolution associated with convergence between the Indian, Eurasian and Burmese plates. title: Modeling formula one’s path to net zero by 2030 - a systems approach for evaluating decarbonization strategies
abstract: In 2019, Formula 1 (F1) committed to achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2030 across its entire value chain; however, this target has drawn both support and skepticism from the academic community. abstract: Voltage-gated potassium channel Kv1.3 is a key regulator of membrane potential and ionic homeostasis, particularly in immune signalling. Despite its importance, tools for directly visualizing Kv1.3 dynamics in living mammalian cells are limited, which restricts the comprehensive evaluation of its biological functions. To address this gap, we developed an enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP)-tagged human Kv1.3 construct for expression in mammalian cells, enabling fluorescence-based visualization of the expressed fusion protein. abstract: Blind and low vision individuals experience difficulties in independently recognizing Indonesian banknote denominations, which may lead to errors in daily financial transactions. This study aims to develop an Internet of Things-based smart assistive device to identify Indonesian banknote denominations in real-time. abstract: Nature-based Solutions (NbS) offer promise for flood resilience in coastal communities, yet public support remains a barrier to implementation. In this exploratory cross-sectional study, we surveyed 165 residents in Wilmington, a flood-prone coastal city in North Carolina (NC), and used Protection Motivation Theory (PMT) as an organizing framework to examine the perceptions associated with support for government-led NbS. title: Institutionalizing the social values of land: a critical review of concepts, methods, and planning translation
abstract: Social values are increasingly acknowledged in land management and spatial planning, particularly amid urbanization and sustainable development. Yet many planning systems have not institutionalized these values, leaving land-use decisions largely shaped by economic and technical rationalities. This article presents a systematic literature review of how the social values of land (SVoL) are conceptualized, interpreted, and operationalized in the context of land management and spatial planning. abstract: This study aims to analyze and map the level of landslide susceptibility in accommodation areas in Kejajar District, Wonosobo Regency, using a Geographic Information System (GIS) approach. Scoring, weighting, and overlay methods were applied to integrate rainfall, slope gradient, soil type, geology, and land-use parameters. abstract: Microeukaryotes are important components of microbial food webs in saline and alkaline lakes, yet their diversity and distribution across distinct microhabitats remain poorly understood. abstract: Behavioural endpoints offer a sensitive, non-invasive alternative to traditional mortality assays. Yet, they remain underutilized in regulatory frameworks due to a lack of standardised methodologies and baseline behavioural data. This study investigates the baseline locomotion of the marine amphipod Marinogammarus marinus to external light triggers to support standardised laboratory behavioural assays. abstract: Abstract Bermudagrass ( Cynodon spp.) is one of the most common warm‐season perennial grasses utilized in the southeastern United States for pasture or stored forage. However, there is a paucity of data evaluating the fecal nutrient losses overtime by cattle grazing different bermudagrass cultivars. abstract: To address insufficient industry context, weak integration of value objectives with technical tasks, and a lack of process-based evidence of educational outcomes in curriculum-based ideological and political education for big data programs at higher vocational colleges, this study introduces a pedagogically adapted Automatic Identification System (AIS) vessel big data project into the course Big Data Analysis and Development and develops a teaching framework that integrates knowledge, competencies, and values. abstract: Perkembangan drone berbasis IoT meningkatkan kebutuhan sistem telemetry real-time yang stabil dan efisien. title: An Integrated Geospatial and Socio-economic Assessment of Flood Risk in North-western Nigeria Using Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis
abstract: Flood disasters have become increasingly frequent and severe in Nigeria, driven by a combination of climatic shifts and anthropogenic pressures. This research paper assesses flood risk vulnerability across the seven states of the Northwest geopolitical zone (Sokoto, Kebbi, Zamfara, Katsina, Kano, Jigawa, and Kaduna). title: Climate Change, Anthropogenic Stressors, and Livelihood Sustainability in the Sundarbans, Bangladesh: A Field-Based Analysis
abstract: The Sundarbans Forest is a vital mangrove ecosystem where environmental processes and human livelihoods are closely intertwined. In Bangladesh, the forests and adjacent bodies of water provide protection against coastal hazards, support a variety of flora and fauna, capture carbon and sustain communities that rely on natural resources. abstract: Accurate and up-to-date topographic information is essential for physical planning, infrastructure development and spatial management of institutional environments. title: Do salmon recipes work for cod? Environmental challenges and regulatory pathways in Norwegian aquaculture
abstract: Aquaculture governance in Norway has largely developed around the rapid expansion of Atlantic salmon farming, while repeated efforts to establish cod aquaculture have resulted in limited and discontinuous production. Recent improvements in breeding, biological performance, and market conditions have, however, renewed commercial interest in cod farming and raised a central policy question: to what extent can regulatory frameworks developed for salmon be transferred to cod aquaculture? title: Paper in the Floodplain: and other instructions for drawing
abstract: This essay will bring together a body of work that attempts to capture human performance and natural phenomena on paper as a way of drawing and scoring encounters with place. abstract: Seabirds are especially vulnerable to ingesting plastic pollution. However, we have a limited understanding of which traits might increase their risk of plastic ingestion. Here, we use a dataset of seabird plastic occurrence records (93 281 birds from 240 species) to investigate which species accumulate plastic and whether this is related to diet, foraging method, pelagic specialism, body mass or phylogenetic position. title: Avian cholera causes mass mortality at penguin mega-colonies amid H5N1 HPAI outbreaks in Antarctica
abstract: The characterization of pathogens affecting Antarctic wildlife has been historically limited and sporadic. With the introduction of H5N1 high pathogenicity avian influenza virus (HPAIV) in Antarctica in the austral summer 2023/2024, concerns about the health of Antarctic seabirds and mammals prompted immediate surveillance efforts. In China, short-video platforms, such as Douyin, have become important spaces where people living with HIV/AIDS share daily-life narratives and receive public responses. However, little is known about how public responses to these narratives vary geographically, or how regional sociodemographic and epidemiological contexts are associated with digital stigma and support. abstract: The efficiency of ship maintenance is essential to ensure operational readiness, minimize docking duration, and control maintenance costs. abstract: El proyecto se propuso evaluar integralmente las condiciones productivas, ambientales y socioeconómicas de los viñedos implantados en la costa del río Paraná (Entre Ríos), con el objetivo de generar conocimiento aplicado que oriente estrategias de manejo sustentable de artrópodos. abstract: Abstract Advanced scintillation materials capable of simultaneously delivering ultrahigh efficiency, exceptional stability, and multifunctional X-ray imaging remain elusive because of intrinsic trade-offs in conventional scintillators. Hernin, a defect-engineered Ce3+-activated borosilicate glass was developed. title: Deciphering coccolith formation: advanced microscopy insights from the biomineralization of Gephyrocapsa huxleyi
abstract: Coccolithophores are unicellular marine phytoplankton that produce complex and intricately shaped mineralized scales called coccoliths. Coccoliths are produced in an intracellular vesicle where crystal nucleation occurs, from which several individual calcite units develop with anisotropic crystallographic facets, prompting studies into the cellular mechanisms that control crystal growth within the cell. abstract: Abstract Cultivated kelps are a scalable marine feedstock for renewable polymers, but regional aquaculture supply chains lack engineering benchmarks for the alginate yield and quality. Here, we apply a lower-hazard citrate-based process to quantify bioplastics-relevant alginate metrics across cultivated northeast Pacific kelps from commercial farms in British Columbia (Canada) and Alaska (USA). abstract: ABSTRACT This work develops lightweight, sustainable PP/rPP/biocarbon composites targeting automotive applications. abstract: Abstract This study verified the effects of “experiential practice” and “visualizing” carbon dioxide reduction on the transformation of junior high school students' environmental awareness and pro-environmental behavior (PEB). We sought to propose measures for sustaining high environmental awareness and choice of appropriate actions. title: Health Risk Implications of PM₂. ₅, PM₁₀, Vocs, and Formaldehyde at Waterfront Residential Buildings of Port Harcourt Metropolis Rivers State
abstract: Indoor air pollution in waterfront communities of Port Harcourt poses significant public health concerns due to poor housing conditions, marine activities and inadequate ventilation. This study assessed the indoor air concentrations of PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, VOCs, and formaldehyde (HCHO) in ten waterfronts communities namely Rex Lawson Waterfront, Eagle Island Waterfront, Bundu Ama Waterfront Elechi Beach Waterfront, Enugu Waterfront, Ibadan Waterfront, Marine Base Waterfront, Okirika Waterfront, Slaughter Waterfront and Woji Waterfront and ten residential building in each of the communities. title: Development of Hazard Atlas from Flood Inundation Patterns in Makurdi Local Government Area of Nigeria
abstract: Flooding is a recurrent environmental and socio-economic challenge in Makurdi, Nigeria, driven by a combination of climatic variability, topography, drainage constraints, land-use change, and urban expansion. This study presents a comprehensive assessment of flood risk in Makurdi over the period 1984 – 2024 using a GIS-based approach. title: Can passive samplers replace biota in risk assessment of resuspended contaminated sediments?
abstract: Resuspension of contaminated sediments elevates turbidity and mobilises sediment‑bound polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) into the water column, increasing their bioavailability and toxicity to aquatic organisms. Passive samplers (PS), which accumulate the freely dissolved fraction of contaminants, have the potential to replace biota as a non‑invasive tool for estimating exposure and toxicity. title: Multi‐Scale Assessment of Population Exposure to Landslides in Vietnam
abstract: ABSTRACT Vietnam's complex terrain and monsoon climate create extensive landslide‐prone conditions, yet the population exposure patterns of its urban, rural, and demographic groups remain insufficiently quantified. This study combines the Global Landslide Non‐Susceptibility Map (GLNSM), high‐resolution population layers, urban–rural settlement data, and GADM administrative boundaries in ArcGIS 10.8 to estimate population exposure to landslide‐prone areas from the national scale to the district scale. title: Emergence of nonequilibrium Lieb excitations in periodically-driven strongly-interacting bosons
abstract: We study the exact nonequilibrium spectral function of a gas of strongly correlated Tonks-Girardeau bosons subjected to a strong periodic drive. Utilizing the theory of Floquet spectral function in conjunction with the Bose-Fermi mapping theorem, we show that nonequilibrium Lieb modes emerge if the underlying mapped fermions form a Floquet-Fermi sea. In the low-frequency regime, the exact analysis reveals the emergence of characteristic linear Lieb excitations for the bosonic system, while the underlying mapped fermions displays the wide Dirac-like linear dispersion.

title: Integrating land-use dynamics, water quality, and multi-criteria ecological suitability for fish sanctuary prioritization in three major river basins of Bangladesh
abstract: Riverine ecosystems in monsoon-dominated regions are increasingly constrained by interacting pressures from land-use change, hydrological alteration, and water-quality degradation, yet these drivers are rarely assessed within a unified framework. abstract: This paper argues that the Mauryan empire could not have been held together under a single authority without a system for acquiring, moving and verifying information, and that this proposition — which no surviving document states in so many words — can be established by correlating four independent bodies of evidence: the Aśokan inscriptions, the Arthaśāstra, the Greek testimony as transmitted by later authors, and the Buddhist literary tradition. abstract: Background Postmortem vitreous chemistry is an understudied analytical test in marine mammals.Methods We assessed the analytical precision of pooled common bottlenose dolphin vitreous humor (VH) samples using the Heska Corporation Element DC chemistry analyzer and to examine the short-term stability of pooled VH when stored at room temperature and in a hot environment (inside a vehicle).Results The within-run and between-run CVs for all detectable analytes were <20%, with most <5%, indicating acceptable repeatability within the pooled matrix. title: Global patterns are key to understanding macroevolution
abstract: Regional diversification patterns are increasingly being used to investigate spatial heterogeneity in biodiversity evolution and its drivers. However, estimating and interpreting regional diversification rates is complicated by the fact that regional diversity fluctuations reflect multiple biological processes and may be more sensitive to temporal sampling bias than global patterns. title: A Holistic Mapping Approach to the Seine River Basin and the Port City Territory of Paris: Developing Historically Informed Awareness for Future Designs
abstract: Rivers and ports have historically shaped European cities, yet their wider territorial and spatial relationships remain insufficiently understood. This article proposes a multi-scalar, holistic and historically informed mapping approach to examine river port city territories as interconnected systems linking hydrology, logistics, urban form, governance and heritage. title: Using spatio-temporal models to assist ecosystem-based fisheries management: a New Zealand case study
abstract: Tools to understand or predict ecosystem changes (e.g., fish community analyses) and the impacts of management measures on ecosystem components (e.g., ecosystem simulation models) are instrumental to the success of ecosystem-based fisheries management (EBFM). We developed a workflow using vector autoregressive spatio-temporal (VAST) models to assist EBFM in the Chatham Rise middle depth (CHAT MD) region, located in New Zealand waters. abstract: Background Assessing home ignition zone attributes is essential for reducing wildfire risk in wildland–urban interface (WUI) communities; however, traditional satellite imagery often lacks sufficient spatial resolution and timely updates to capture localized fuel conditions near structures. Aims This study develops and validates a smartphone-based framework for real-time detection, mapping and 3D visualization of building features and defensible space fuel to support wildfire risk assessment and mitigation in WUI environments. abstract: Arcuatula japonica (Dunker, 1857) (Mollusca: Mytilidae: Crenellinae) is a marine mussel distributed primarily in the northwestern Pacific. To clarify its evolutionary position and evaluate the taxonomic status of Crenellinae, we sequenced and characterized the complete mitochondrial genome of A. japonica. title: The geographic and elevational distribution of the genus Natalus Gray, 1838 (Mammalia, Chiroptera) in Guatemala, including the first record of N. lanatus Tejedor, 2005
abstract: We document the first confirmed record of Natalus lanatus from Guatemala, increasing the national bat fauna to 107 species, and present the first country-level synthesis of the geographic and elevational distribution of the genus Natalus . Morphological analyses of N. lanatus ( n = 8) and N. mexicanus ( n = 8) show clear differentiation, with the first two FAMD dimensions explaining 61% of total variance. abstract: Fishing vessels require good hydrodynamic efficiency to limit propulsion power and energy consumption. Adding a fin stabilizer can modify the flow pattern, pressure distribution, wetted area, and consequently the total resistance; however, studies specifically addressing its resistance effect on a 100 GT fishing vessel remain limited. abstract: Abstract Quantifying the structure and heterogeneity of complex spatial patterns remains a key challenge in spatial data analysis. Recurrence plots (RPs) offer a powerful method for visualizing the recurrent spatial patterns in such data. abstract: Sustainable recovery of critical resources from complex aqueous streams is constrained by membranes that fail to combine rapid ion transport with precise mono/multivalent discrimination. abstract: Abstract Microbial biomass is a central functional trait governing nutrient turnover and trophic transfer in aquatic ecosystems, yet how chemical stress reshapes biomass at the level of individual cells remains poorly resolved. Conventional toxicity assays primarily detect population-level growth inhibition and overlook sublethal physiological responses and heterogeneity within microbial populations. abstract: In conditions of increasing complexity and intensity of transportation systems, ensuring road safety requires a transition to proactive and predictive methods of integral risk management. In this work a hierarchical model based on fuzzy logic has been developed to assess the safety of vehicle fleets by aggregating heterogeneous real-time data. abstract: Abstract Nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) is a major urban air pollutant, yet assessment of population exposure remains challenging across West Africa due to lack of uncoordinated sparse monitoring infrastructure. We present the City-Level Nitrogen Dioxide Exposure (CLeNE) platform, an interactive exposure intelligence system that integrates Sentinel-5P TROPOMI NO 2 observations, population data, and city boundaries to quantify and visualize urban exposure burden. This study delineates groundwater potential zones (GWPZs) using an integrated Geographic Information System (GIS), Remote Sensing (RS), and Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) approach. abstract: Despite the importance of the Galápagos archipelago as a key site for the study of biodiversity and evolution, significant components of its invertebrate biodiversity, particularly Hymenoptera, remain insufficiently documented. Occurrence records of Hymenoptera from 1959–2025 were combined from structured surveys of non-formicid Hymenoptera, long-term ant sampling, museum collections, literature, and online sources to assess the richness, distribution, and species composition of hymenopterans across the archipelago. abstract: The Mesozoic and early Paleogene of Morocco provides a rich and extensive record of crocodylomorphs encompassing a wide range of skull, dental morphologies, and paleoecologies. abstract: Colombo, the executive and judicial capital of Sri Lanka, is located on the southwestern coast of the country and has experienced rapid urbanization in recent years, driven by infrastructure development, land use changes, and the growing impacts of climate change. abstract: Open data has become an important component of contemporary urban governance, contributing to transparency, accountability, and data-driven decision-making. However, the effectiveness of open data systems depends not only on data availability but also on interoperability, standardization, and the ability of data infrastructures to support reuse and integration within urban service ecosystems. abstract: Increasing salinity threatens coastal mangrove ecosystems worldwide by impairing plant growth, physiological function, and biochemical processes, ultimately reducing productivity and survival. The present study was conducted to examine the impact of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) on Avicennia marina under different salt concentrations (9, 14, and 19 dS/m). abstract: Flooding has become one of the most frequent and destructive environmental hazards in Nigeria, with increasing impacts on lives, livelihoods, and infrastructure, particularly in rapidly expanding peri-urban communities. Despite the recurrent occurrence of flood events in Ogbese, limited empirical information exists on the combined influence of physical and socio-economic factors that shape flood vulnerability and risk. abstract: This study examined the role of pre-boarding training in enhancing the mental health preparedness, safety awareness, and professional preparedness of Filipino seafarers who entered maritime service after March 2020. title: Digital transformation and third places: Mapping public spaces in Bekasi Regency
abstract: As an urban and industrial area, Bekasi Regency faces challenges in providing inclusive and multifunctional public spaces that support social interaction, community cohesion, and economic activities. abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial light at night (ALAN) across India is increasingly transforming nocturnal environments with significant ecological consequences. abstract: Digital technology is now central to competence-based Geography education, yet access and pedagogical use remain uneven in Tanzanian public schools. This study examined how ICT integration supports Geography teaching and learning in Temeke Municipality. Its main objective was to assess whether available technology was being converted into subject-specific, learner-centred practice. A mixed-methods approach and cross-sectional survey design were used. The sample comprised 120 participants: 100 students, 16 Geography teachers, and four Ward Education Officers. title: Evaluating Carniolan honey bee (Apis mellifera carnica) lines under contrasting ecological zones
abstract: This study evaluates four breeding lines of the Carniolan honey bee, Apis mellifera carnica, across distinct ecological zones of Serbia and Montenegro. The objective was to assess phenotypic, morphometric, and isoenzyme polymorphism of local populations adapted to contrasting climatic and altitudinal conditions. Two Serbian lines (lowland Vršac and mountainous Vranje) and two Montenegrin lines (mountainous Bijelo Polje and coastal Sutomore) were examined. title: Improved estimation of lake storage variation via DEM reconstruction integrating elevation and morphological constraints
abstract: High-quality Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) are essential for accurately estimating lake storage variations, but the high cost of in-situ measurements limits their large-scale application. Reconstructing DEMs from remote sensing-derived lake contours is a promising low-cost alternative. However, most existing methods primarily rely on elevation-matched contours and discard those without elevation data. title: Experimental investigation of transient bed shear stress and scour formation at seawalls under tsunami bore impact using particle image velocimetry (PIV)
abstract: Abstract Tsunami bores generate short-duration, highly turbulent flows that impose intense bed shear stress on coastal structures, often leading to toe scour and structural instability. This study experimentally examines the transient evolution of bed shear stress and scour formation at four seawall geometries (box, curve, slope, and step types) using a dam-break wave testing facility and high-resolution Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV). title: Synergistic Co‐Fermentation of Ulva and Waste Activated Sludge for Sustainable Resource Recovery: Mechanistic Insights From Dissolved Organic Matter Transformation and Multi‐Omics Analysis
abstract: Anaerobic fermentation for volatile fatty acids (VFAs) production represents the sustainable and resource-recovery strategy for waste activated sludge (WAS) treatment, yet its efficiency is often hampered by low substrate C/N ratio and limited hydrolysis. Ulva, a macroalga responsible for extensive "green tides" that burden coastal ecosystems and economies, emerges as an ideal co-substrate for WAS anaerobic fermentation due to its high C/N ratio and biodegradability. title: Time capsules of infection: Updating the distribution of Aphanomyces astaci in Croatia using archived crayfish specimens
abstract: The crayfish plague pathogen Aphanomyces astaci Schikora, 1906 is one of the most damaging invasive pathogens affecting European freshwater ecosystems, causing declines in native crayfish populations. In Croatia, crayfish plague was first reported in the late 19 th century and was subsequently molecularly confirmed in 2016. However, its national distribution remains incompletely resolved because the initial molecular survey covered only a limited number of localities. institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: The Impact of Virtual Dental Clinic Color and Image Modifications on Anxiety Reduction in Undergraduate Dental Students
abstract: Dental students often experience stress due to the curriculum’s theoretical and practical demands, whichcan negatively affect their well-being. Previous research suggests that room colors and images can reduceanxiety in certain populations. However, no studies have examined this effect among dental students. Therefore,this study investigated how color and visual imagery in dental clinics affect anxiety levels in dental students.Participants were dental students experiencing state anxiety. title: Mobilizing Dynamic‐Capability Microfoundations for Sustainability‐Oriented Innovation: The Role of Innovation Champions
abstract: ABSTRACT Organizations face growing pressure to respond to environmental and social challenges, yet research has not sufficiently explained how organizational actors mobilise dynamic‐capability microfoundations across the development of sustainability‐oriented innovations. Drawing on 68 semistructured interviews conducted between March and November 2024 across 18 EU and UK marine firms, this qualitative study examines how innovation champions and related actors support sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring. title: Nutritional diversity and bioactive potential of thirteen wild edible insects in India: implications for sustainable food and nutrition security
abstract: Background Edible insects are increasingly recognized as sustainable alternative food resources owing to their high nutritional value, diverse bioactive compounds, and low environmental footprint. However, comprehensive nutritional characterization of many wild edible insect species remains limited. Therefore, this study evaluated the nutritional composition, amino acid and fatty acid profiles, bioactive properties, and multivariate nutritional relationships of 13 wild-harvested edible insect species traditionally consumed in Nagaland, India. title: Assessment of Flood Risks on Power Infrastructure and Renewable Energy Installations in Ogba-Egbema-Ndoni Local Government Area, Rivers State
abstract: This research evaluated the flood hazards that impact power systems and renewable energy setups in the Ogba-Egbema-Ndoni Local Government Area (ONELGA) located in Rivers State, Nigeria. The primary goals included investigating how vulnerable energy infrastructure is to factors such as flood depth, speed, and duration; studying the vital interconnections between energy networks and other crucial services including water provision, healthcare, and transport; and calculating the economic damage and downtime caused by flood effects. title: Multiple introductions and spread of novel reassortant highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses via wild birds, South Korea, 2024–2025
abstract: Between 14 October 2024 and 24 March 2025, 43 cases of clade 2.3.4.4b highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) type A (H5N1) infections in wild birds and 1 case in a leopard cat were detected through the national HPAI surveillance program. We performed whole-genome sequencing of 51 isolates and investigated their phylogenetic relationships. Phylogenetic analyses identified nine distinct genotypes, designated Kor24-25A to Kor24-25I. title: Far-Red Turn-On Fluorogenic Probe for Versatile Detection of Inorganic Polyphosphates
abstract: Abstract Inorganic polyphosphate (polyP) is a ubiquitous phosphate biopolymer involved in diverse cellular processes. Despite its significance, selective detection of polyP remains challenging because of its simple and highly charged structure. Here, we report a far-red fluorogenic turn-on chemosensor for selective polyP detection and imaging, SiX-DPA-Zn. It integrates a silicon-xanthene fluorophore with a Zn(II)-coordinated 2,2’-dipicolylamine recognition unit. title: Favorable habitats of endangered halophytes harbor unique soil properties and bacterial communities, with a dominant root-associated genus promoting host plant growth
abstract: Understanding how edaphic factors and root-associated bacterial communities interact to shape plant growth is essential for effective conservation of halophytic species in coastal ecosystems. We investigated relationships among bulk soil, rhizosphere, and root bacterial microbiota; soil physicochemical properties; and Salicornia europaea growth spanning three distinct areas (Lakeside Park, Ubaranai and Misaki) within a brackish lake in Japan. title: SMART TOURISM GOVERNANCE: A SCIENTOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF GOVERNMENT ROLES
abstract: Smart tourism governance has become increasingly important as digital technologies reshape tourism management, public services, and destination development. However, existing studies have predominantly emphasized technological innovation, destination competitiveness, and tourist experiences, while the evolving administrative roles of government remain fragmented. This study aims to examine the intellectual development of smart tourism governance and map the evolving roles of government through a scientometric analysis. title: Youth and the future of labor- and knowledge-intensive small-scale farming in West Africa under climate change and political instability
abstract: Debates on the future of smallholder farming in sub-Saharan Africa often interpret rural youth mobility and non-farm work as withdrawal from agriculture. This article examines how rural youth in coastal Guinea-Bissau engage with labour- and knowledge-intensive, climate-vulnerable mangrove swamp rice farming, and the conditions under which agriculture remains part of their imagined futures. title: Sympatric pikas partition microhabitats differently across a spatial-elevational gradient
abstract: Abstract How closely related, ecologically similar species co-occur and navigate competition remains a central question in community ecology. Microhabitat partitioning in patchy environments can support the co-existence of sympatric species on small spatial scales. We quantified niche spaces and directional niche overlaps of three cold-adapted, high-altitude pikas (Ochotona spp.) from the Trans-Himalayas to understand their responses to interspecific competition across elevational and spatial scales. title: Nature-based flood assessment for vulnerable educational infrastructure under tropical urban conditions
abstract: Worldwide, urban rainwater flooding is increasingly affecting small-scale public infrastructure in tropical cities. Consequently, drainage decisions are often made with limited hydrometric data. Therefore, this study aims to evaluate flood control alternatives using the Nature-based Solutions (NBS) approach through participatory assessment and modeling with the Stormwater Management Model (SWMM) at a vulnerable educational infrastructure (VEI) in Durán, Ecuador. title: Durability of TiAlCrN coated Ti6Al4V in saline and acidic media via multiphase analysis of passive film stability
abstract: Ti 6 Al 4 V components in aerospace and marine applications frequently suffer from coupled mechanical wear and corrosive degradation across severe temperature regimes. While TiAlN-based systems offer good wear resistance, tailoring Cr incorporation to concurrently enhance passivity without triggering microstructural embrittlement remains underexplored. title: Smart Interactive System for the Enhanced Bioimaging and Multi‐Drug Synergistic Therapy in Tumor‐Microenvironment
abstract: ABSTRACT Tumor microenvironment (TME) interactive platforms are promising for accurate diagnostics and therapeutics. Herein, a smart interactive system (G⊂H) consisting of a hypoxia‐acid dual triggered multifunctional guest (G) and an amphipathic metal‐organic capsule (H) was successfully established for bioimaging and treatment. title: Passive acoustic monitoring for the estimation of density of the singing lemur ( Indri indri )
abstract: Abstract Passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) has emerged as a valuable tool for estimating animal density and abundance, particularly in challenging environments where traditional methods face limitations. In this study, we applied PAM techniques to study the indri ( Indri indri ) in the Maromizaha New Protected Area, a tropical forest in Eastern Madagascar. Leveraging advancements in acoustic monitoring methodologies, we aimed to assess the efficacy of PAM in estimating indri density and its implications for conservation efforts. title: Facade and Opening Design Strategies for Enhancing Natural Lighting Efficiency in Classrooms at SD Labschool UPI
abstract: Natural lighting is an essential aspect of elementary school building design, as it significantly influences visual comfort and learning effectiveness. However, many classrooms in Indonesia do not meet the minimum illuminance standard of 350 lux specified in SNI 03-6197-2020. This study aims to evaluate and optimize facade and opening design strategies to improve the performance of natural lighting at SD Labschool UPI. title: Phased ecological responses and effectiveness assessment of subtidal oyster reef restoration: a case study from Dashentang, Bohai Bay
abstract: Subtidal oyster reef restoration presents greater challenges for implementation and monitoring than intertidal restoration, and evaluations of relatively large-scale ecological restoration projects remain limited. This study evaluated the restoration project of Dashengtang using monitoring data from five field surveys collected from 2022 to 2026, and evaluated stage-specific ecological changes in oyster populations, aquatic environments, and macrobenthic communities. title: Public health emergencies in Jordan: appraising multi-agency preparedness
abstract: Jordan faces a complex landscape of public health threats arising from infectious disease outbreaks, environmental hazards, technological incidents, humanitarian crises, and regional instability. These risks place sustained pressure on national institutions responsible for preparedness, response, and resilience. While multiple governmental and non-governmental agencies contribute to public health emergency preparedness and response (PHEPR), coordination gaps, overlapping mandates, and fragmented governance structures continue to challenge the effectiveness of a unified national response. title: Joint determination of factors influencing adoption of climate smart agricultural practices in modern rice production in Southwest Bangladesh: a multivariate probit approach
abstract: Climate change and environmental degradation are increasingly threatening rice production in the coastal regions of the developing world, where the goals of raising productivity and building resilience became a joint priority. Climate smart agriculture offers a portfolio of practices that serve both goals, yet knowledge on how farmers in saline rice systems combine these practices, and why adoption remains often partial, is still limited. title: Thinking with Objects. Understanding Non-Representational Cognitive Artifacts
abstract: This paper defends the notion of cognitive artifacts that do not serve representational functions. Contrary to the standard account of cognitive artifacts as representational, we argue that it is possible to distinguish a special class of artifacts that fulfill cognitive roles without performing representational functions. title: Mechanical and Electrical Characterization of Hybrid Polymer Composites Reinforced with Natural and Synthetic Fibers
abstract: This study examines the effects of optimized stacking sequences and NaOH surface treatment on the mechanical and dielectric performance of hybrid polyester composites reinforced with natural fibers (flax, sisal) and synthetic fibers (carbon, glass). Twelve laminates were fabricated using hand lay-up technique to assess hybridization effects on strength, insulation, and cost efficiency. title: Institutional Adoption and Economic Feasibility of Rainwater Harvesting in Existing University Buildings: A Review
abstract: Rainwater harvesting in existing university buildings requires an appraisal that connects institutional priorities, feasible retrofits and financial consequences. Selected reviews address system design, research trends and implementation barriers, providing a basis for examining how these considerations inform successive appraisal decisions. title: Duplex ultrasound as an initial imaging clue to spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection: A case report
abstract: Spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection is uncommon and is usually confirmed with computed tomography angiography (CTA). Duplex ultrasound may provide an initial clue when the lesion and its flow abnormalities are directly visualized. A 56-year-old woman with untreated hypertension presented with acute persistent epigastric pain radiating to the back. abstract: Dual-bell nozzles (DBNs) provide passive altitude compensation by adapting their effective expansion ratio through controlled flow separation and reattachment. In this study, the flow-regime evolution of an axisymmetric DBN is investigated numerically over a nozzle pressure ratio (NPR) range from 10 to 100. The nozzle geometry was generated using an in-house Method of Characteristics (MoC) design procedure combined with a constant-pressure extension contour. title: SARIMA-based forecasting of mangrove vegetation indices across India
abstract: Abstract Mangrove ecosystems are crucial to the ecological and climatic dynamics of the Asia–Pacific coastline. However, the ability to predict long-term changes is limited, hindering evidence-based resilience and adaptation strategies. The study presents a remote-sensing framework that integrates data from multiple sensors with time-series analysis to predict changes in mangrove ecosystems along India’s coastlines, aiding in conservation planning. abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT) has emerged as a promising strategy for managing infections associated withCandidaspp. In this context, nanoformulations of photosensitizers have been investigated to enhance the antimicrobial effects of established compounds, such as curcumin (CUR). title: Impacts of needle-leaved forests landscape pattern and environmental factors on the spatial differentiation of pine wilt disease in China
abstract: Following its emergence in China, pine wilt disease (PWD) has continuously expanded, creating substantial risks to regional forest ecosystems. However, most existing research emphasizes climate and other macro-scale associated factors, and lacks long-term and systematic analysis approached through the lens of forest landscape patterns. The research focuses on describing the spatiotemporal dynamics of PWD in China across the period 1982–2020 and identifying the dominant factors influencing its distribution. title: Land of opportunity? Settling and social organization of the early Corded Ware groups in Central Jutland, Denmark
abstract: The breakthrough of aDNA research during the mid-2010s fundamentally shifted the dominant focus of research on the Corded Ware period in Europe, redirecting attention to questions about migration and the interdisciplinary integration of new and older approaches. title: How Visual Resources Support Reading Comprehension: A Multimodal Analysis of English for Nusantara for Grade VIII
abstract: This study examines how visual resources accompanying reading materials in English for Nusantara for Grade VIII may support reading comprehension. A qualitative textbook content analysis was conducted on all 18 explicit Reading and Your Turn: Reading sections in Chapters 1-5. Meaningful visuals were defined as images or visual compositions that contributed information, organization, genre cues, or task meaning beyond decoration. abstract: ABSTRACT Fireflies are semelparous beetles whose immature stages are largely unknown. The comparatively few larvae known span diverse ecological niches, such as ground‐dwellers, aquatic (freshwater or marine), semi‐aquatic and arboreal. Psilocladus costae Vaz, Silveira & Rosa, 2020—a bromeliad dweller—is the only species of its genus and subfamily in which immature stages were studied. title: Regional tau burden tracks with lower microglial HLA class II transcription in the human brain
abstract: Background Human leukocyte antigen class II (HLA-II) genes mark several microglial states in Alzheimer’s disease, but it remains unclear how their average transcription relates to tau measured in the same brain region. title: Optimizing Logistics Ecosystems: Evaluating the Performance of Smart Port Enterprises
abstract: Abstract The rapid development of smart ports has revolutionized the maritime industry, leveraging advanced technologies and data analytics to enhance efficiency, productivity, and sustainability. However, assessing and optimizing the performance of smart ports remains a complex challenge. This study proposes a comprehensive framework for evaluating and improving smart port efficiency using a Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) approach. title: Compound and cascading climate risks in urban infrastructure governance and resilience across North America
abstract: North American cities are increasingly exposed to climate-related hazards that do not occur in isolation. Extreme heat, drought, flooding, hurricanes, wildfires, wildfire smoke, and sea-level rise interact with aging infrastructure, uneven urbanization, social vulnerability, and fragmented governance systems. As a result, an initial climate shock can trigger cascading failures across energy, water, transport, telecommunications, housing, health, and emergency response systems. title: Layer-specific microbial community structures in the meromictic lake, Lake Suigetsu, unveiled by 16S rRNA gene amplicon and metagenomic analyses
abstract: Meromictic lakes serve as natural laboratories for investigating microbially mediated biogeochemical cycling because their stable redox stratification supports diverse metabolic processes. Lake Suigetsu is a typical meromictic lake in Japan characterized by a permanent oxycline separating the oxic brackish mixolimnion from the anoxic saline sulfidogenic monimolimnion. abstract: When a satellite observes the Earth at an angle, the apparent position of elevated features, such as mountains, clouds or fires in high terrain, can be shifted from their true ground location. title: Morphodynamic response to extreme basin flooding and its mechanism in a tide-dominant estuary
abstract: Extreme basin floods can strongly reshape tide-dominated estuaries, but their effects are often conditioned by antecedent channel geometry and human-induced river-bed incision. Here, we investigated the annual-scale morphodynamic response of the North Branch of the Changjiang (Yangtze) Estuary to the 2020 extreme basin flood using hydrological records, bathymetric surveys, surficial sediment samples, and Delft3D scenario experiments. title: Differences between PM2.5 chemical sources at semi-closed transport environments: comparing bus depots and metro platforms
abstract: Chemical composition and source contributions of PM 2.5 were investigated at a public-restricted bus depot in Valladolid (Spain) and two metro stations (Alto dos Moinhos and Quinta das Conchas) in Lisbon (Portugal) using positive matrix factorization (PMF). Locally derived sources dominated PM 2.5 in both environments, with OC-rich combustion emissions prevailing at the bus depot and Fe-rich wear processes at the metro stations as major components. title: Polycentric governance of cruise environmental impacts
abstract: Rapidly growing cruise ship tourism in northern regions has been a double-edged phenomenon, bringing monetary benefits to otherwise limited economic futures but also undesirable environmental impacts such as air pollution, wastewater discharge, and noise. This paper examines responses from five northern communities to these challenges, using a polycentric governance lens characterized by multilevel and overlapping decision-making centers. abstract: The environmental behavior of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in tropical nearshore sediments remains poorly understood, particularly with respect to the contamination characteristics of emerging PFAS and precursor-related compounds. In this study, surface sediments from the tropical nearshore waters of Sanya, China, were investigated, and 46 PFAS, including legacy, emerging, and precursor PFAS, were systematically analyzed. title: Enhanced greywater treatment in a two-stage green wall system by incorporating waste-derived adsorbents
abstract: Greywater reuse offers a sustainable approach to alleviating freshwater scarcity, but concerns about treatment reliability limit its adoption. This study investigates a two-stage green wall system for greywater treatment, integrating vegetated units planted with Carex secta and vertical flow post-treatment columns (PTCs) packed with waste-derived adsorbents—calcinated kina (sea urchin) shell, ZnCl 2 -activated apricot stone biochar, and natural zeolite. abstract: This study identifies the main factors and trends in green economy development across the Gulf and Levant countries and examines their spatial patterns. The environmentally significant processes observed in these countries suggest the possible, though not predetermined, onset of a long-term transition toward more sustainable economies. However, it remains too early to conclude that a genuine transition toward decarbonization is underway. title: Same hospital, same price, different protection: out-of-pocket expenditure for emergency trauma under public insurance, private insurance and self-payment in India
abstract: Background Out-of-pocket expenditure (OOPE) finances 43.4% of total health expenditure in India, and emergency trauma—unforeseeable, unpostponable and costly—is among the sharpest tests of whether a health-financing mechanism protects households from catastrophic spending. Insured and uninsured patients are normally treated in different facilities at different tariffs, confounding the effect of the payment mechanism with the setting in which care is given. title: Biophysical modelling and network analyses can inform strategic site selection for mangrove restoration
abstract: Modelling how mangroves disperse can help prioritize site restoration selection by identifying source populations and linking appropriate restoration efforts with potential site-specific propagule availability. Dispersal modelling approaches are particularly impactful in regions with limited empirical data, like the Middle East. abstract: The article addresses the scientific and practical problem of developing a computer simulation model of a ship mobile robot (SMR) to further automate maintenance processes for ships and port infrastructure facilities (pipelines, storage tanks, floating docks). Based on a review of existing solutions, the advantages of all-wheel drive wheeled platforms over tracked and legged counterparts in terms of manoeuvrability and energy efficiency are substantiated. abstract: The Ébrié Lagoon, in the Grand-Bassam area, is exposed to various anthropogenic pressures that may alter is morphological and environnemental charactéristics. This study aims to characterize the morphobathymetric and hydrodynamic structures of this lagoon sector and to assess its physicochemical status. Bathymetric surveys provided 18,474 depth measurements, ranging from 0 to 19 m, over an area of approximately 42 ha. title: Species-dependent water and salt migration drives lipoprotein remodeling and quality formation during rapid curing of separated egg yolks
abstract: Rapid curing of separated egg yolks provides an efficient strategy for accelerating salted egg production; however, how species-dependent intrinsic yolk organization regulates small molecule migration and subsequent lipoprotein remodeling remains poorly understood. In this study, egg yolks separated from hen, duck, and sea duck eggs were used as model systems to elucidate the relationships among water and NaCl migration, lipoprotein structural evolution and quality formation during rapid curing. title: Mitochondrial and retroviral markers reveal high genetic diversity and regional structure in the Lebanese Awassi sheep
abstract: Abstract The Awassi is a native sheep breed of Lebanon with high historical and economic value. Despite its importance, its genetic background has not been characterized, leaving limited understanding of its origins, diversity, and regional connections. This study aimed to characterize the genetic diversity and population structure of Awassi sheep from Lebanon and neighboring Syria using two complementary genetic systems that trace distinct evolutionary histories: maternal mitochondrial DNA and insertional polymorphisms of endogenous Jaagsiekte sheep retroviruses. title: Assessment of Flood Impacts, Losses and Adaptation Practices in Bhajani Municipality, Kailali District, Nepal
abstract: Floods are the most frequent and damaging hydro-meteorological hazard in the Terai region of Nepal, yet municipal-scale evidence that links hazard mapping, community perception, historical losses and local adaptation remains scarce. This study assesses flood impacts, losses, and adaptation practices in Bhajani Municipality, Kailali District, Sudurpashchim Province, a low-lying municipality with nine wards (176.25 km²) and crossed by the Mohana, Kandra, Kanda (Kadha), and Patharaiya rivers. title: Evolution of Research on Satellite-Based Monitoring for Algal Blooms in the African Great Lakes
abstract: Abstract Algal blooms pose significant environmental and economic challenges worldwide. As their impact increases, there is an urgent need to improve forecasting models that predict their occurrence, development, and trends. Understanding recent research developments in satellite-based monitoring of algal blooms in the African Great Lakes provides a vital foundation for creating effective early warning systems and improving both short- and long-term prediction accuracy. title: More seeds yield more shoots, but not higher per-seed establishment in a clam-mediated seagrass restoration experiment
abstract: Seagrass restoration increasingly relies on seed-based approaches, yet optimal seeding densities and deployment methods remain poorly resolved. We evaluated the relative effects of seed density and clam-mediated seed placement on eelgrass ( Zostera marina ) establishment in a field restoration experiment in Back Sound, North Carolina. title: Microplastics as evolving particle–chemical–microbial interfaces: plastisphere ecology, ecotoxicity, and safety-informed remediation
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are not environmentally static particles; aging, fragmentation, contaminant acquisition, organic conditioning, and microbial colonization progressively convert them into dynamic particle–chemical–microbial interfaces. This transformation is central to their environmental fate and risk because plastisphere communities can alter particle transport, contaminant partitioning, nutrient cycling, antimicrobial-resistance dynamics, and polymer transformation. title: Intelligent fault diagnosis of bearings using dynamic weighted Markov transition field and hybrid attention ResNet
abstract: To address the insufficient characterization of long-range temporal dependencies in rolling bearing vibration signals and the indiscriminate treatment of impulse features and stationary components in conventional Markov Transition Field (MTF) encoding, this paper proposes a fault diagnosis method incorporating dual attention enhancement in both the signal and image domains. In the signal encoding stage, a Dynamic Weighted Markov Transition Field (DWMTF) is designed. title: Long-term preservation of early-formed silicate reservoirs in the deep mantle: New insight from 146Sm-142Nd systematics in Hawaiian basalts
abstract: Short-lived radiogenic isotope systems provide unique constraints on the preservation of early-formed reservoirs in Earth's mantle. We present the largest high-precision μ 142 Nd dataset for a single hotspot, comprising 55 analyses of 29 shield-stage tholeiitic basalts from the Hawaiian Islands. Samples span the full geochemical range of the Loa and Kea trends and were analyzed using multiple chemical purification procedures and thermal ionization mass spectrometry to assess analytical reproducibility. title: Decoupling stress-corrosion-hydrogen interactions in Mg-Zn-Ca-Sn alloys: Achieving enhanced stress corrosion cracking resistance via Ga/In alloying
abstract: Despite recent advancements in corrosion resistance, magnesium (Mg) alloys still face significant challenges in structural applications due to their susceptibility to stress corrosion cracking (SCC) under combined mechanical stress and corrosive environments. The underlying mechanisms of SCC, particularly the interplay between stress, corrosion, and hydrogen, remain insufficiently understood, impeding the development of effective mitigation strategies. title: KAJIAN POLA PERGERAKAN WISATAWAN DI KAWASAN KOTA LAMA SEMARANG
abstract: Abstrak Kota Lama Semarang merupakan kawasan wisata warisan budaya yang memiliki nilai historis tinggi dan arsitektur kolonial khas, tetapi kunjungan wisatawan cenderung terkonsentrasi pada beberapa objek di zona inti sehingga menimbulkan ketimpangan pemanfaatan ruang wisata. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pola persebaran objek wisata dan pola pergerakan wisatawan serta mengidentifikasi objek wisata yang paling diminati di Kawasan Kota Lama Semarang. title: Simulador de Laboratorios Edulab Diseñado para la Educación Media Superior Bajo el Marco del MCCEMS
abstract: The didactic prototype, Virtual Laboratory Simulator "EDULAB," is an initiative designed to improve the learning of experimental sciences in Upper Secondary Education. Its main objective is to enhance students' experimentation, observation, and scientific analysis skills through the use of a virtual laboratory simulator, promoting a more active, safe, and accessible learning experience aligned with current educational trends. title: Comparative physiological and photosynthetic responses of three mangrove species to salinity stress and exogenous melatonin
abstract: Extreme salinity is a major environmental constraint affecting plant growth and physiological performance in coastal ecosystems. Although mangroves are naturally adapted to saline environments, their tolerance and physiological responses vary among species, and the effects of exogenous melatonin (MT) under different salinity levels remain insufficiently understood. This study compared the physiological and photosynthetic responses of Aegiceras corniculatum , Kandelia obovata , and Rhizophora stylosa under NaCl-only and corresponding NaCl + MT treatments. title: Genetic and morphological insights reveal the hidden and colorful diversity in Oscarella sponges
abstract: Abstract The identification and classification of new taxa are crucial for understanding biodiversity. However, assigning samples to new taxa requires cautious and rigorous approaches. Historically, taxonomy has heavily relied on morphological traits, which can be subjective and may not always reflect underlying genetic divergence—particularly in organisms with few diagnostic morphological traits. title: In-flight cosmic radiation doses along the current alternative routes between Tokyo and Frankfurt
abstract: Background Calculation-based dose assessment for aircraft crew is required worldwide by authorities, as cosmic radiation dose rates at aviation altitudes are substantially higher than at sea level. The accuracy of the calculated in-flight dose onboard aircraft (“route dose” hereafter) should be confirmed periodically, particularly when the flight route is significantly changed. title: Shifting Dominant Air Pollution Sources in Sub-Saharan Africa’s Changing Urban Environment: Analysis of Elemental Composition and Source Contributions of Ambient Fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5) Pollution in Accra, Ghana
abstract: Abstract Urban and economic expansion across Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) may be shifting the relative contributions of dominant ambient air pollution sources, influencing both pollutant concentrations and composition, along with their associated health risks. However, city-scale data on the composition and source contributions are scarce, hindering source- and sector-specific policy interventions. Using samples from a large-scale, citywide monitoring campaign, we characterized the elemental composition and source contributions of PM2.5 pollution across the Accra metropolis, a major SSA city. title: Geographically close nearshore sites exhibit contrasting dissolved oxygen dynamics and ecosystem metabolism in eastern Lake Taihu
abstract: Diel dissolved oxygen (DO) dynamics integrate biological metabolism and physical forcing and provide a powerful tool for investigating ecosystem metabolism in shallow lakes. However, whether geographically close sites exhibit similar metabolic behavior and environmental controls remains poorly understood. Here, three years (2022–2024) of high-frequency DO observations from three contrasting nearshore sites in eastern Lake Taihu were used to quantify diel and seasonal variability in net ecosystem production (NEP), gross primary production (GPP), and ecosystem respiration (R). abstract: Background Desmodium molliculum is an Andean medicinal plant traditionally used for various ailments, whose chemical composition and antioxidant activity require investigation. To determine the phytochemical profile using high-performance liquid chromatography with diode array detection (HPLC-DAD) and to evaluate the antioxidant activity of the aqueous extract of D. molliculum from Ayacucho, Peru. title: Mechanisms of Overpressure Formation and Distribution Prediction in Ultra‐Deep Carbonate Reservoirs in the YB Area, Sichuan Basin
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the formation mechanisms and predicting the distribution of abnormally high pressure in marine carbonate reservoirs are fundamental to ultra‐deep hydrocarbon exploration. This study investigates the ultra‐deep carbonate grain‐beach reservoirs of the second member of the Feixianguan Formation in the YB area, northeastern Sichuan Basin. title: Microplastic contamination in agricultural systems: impacts on plant productivity, economic losses, and supply chain resilience
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) have transitioned from a predominantly marine concern to a defining threat facing terrestrial agroecosystems, where croplands now function as one of the largest global reservoirs of plastic particles. This review synthesizes evidence to construct an integrated narrative that links the entry of MPs into farmland with declining plant productivity, quantifiable economic losses, and the erosion of agricultural supply chain resilience. title: Distribution and life-history of spurdog (Squalus acanthias) along the Norwegian coast inferred from a five-year fishery-independent longline survey
abstract: Abstract Northeast Atlantic spurdog ( Squalus acanthias ) has recently shown signs of recovery from overfishing following international conservation measures. As the fishery slowly reopens, ensuring its sustainable long-term trajectory will require an understanding of its contemporary population structure, habitat use, and life-history traits across its distribution range. title: Evaluation of micro-litter pollution in the Antarctic asteroid Odontaster validus Koehler, 1906 at Deception Island (South Shetland Islands)
abstract: Micro-litter (ML) pollution is increasingly being reported in Antarctic benthic ecosystems and the organisms inhabiting them. In this study, we assessed ML abundance and characteristics in the Antarctic asteroid Odontaster validus at Deception Island (South Shetland Islands), an area with significant human presence. Additionally, we considered the potential influence of local factors, including proximity to research stations and the bay entrance, as well as depth (5 and 15 m), on ML pollution. title: All Different All Equal: High Polymorphism in Nebela (Amoebozoa: Arcellinida) Revealed by Additional Sampling and Barcoding
abstract: Hyalospheniids are a conspicuous group of testate amoebae whose rich morphology has allowed their classification based on the characterization of their shells. However, recent studies showed the occurrence of convergences and phenotypic plasticity, which complicate their taxonomy. Molecular barcoding is the method of choice to resolve this diversity in an objective manner and accurately delineate species.
