title: The Feral Life of Plastic Waste: Third Nature and Speculative Aesthetics
abstract: This article explores the interactions between plastic waste and non-human animals from a non-anthropocentric and future-oriented perspective. After a first introductory section, I argue for a plane of analogy connecting animals and plastics. If extended into the future, this plane of analogy shows a new feature: ferality. Contra Hegel, Heidegger, and some contemporary scholars, I contend in the third section that ferality cannot be framed as a regression of “second nature” (human culture) to “first nature” (non-human nature), but should be understood as post-domestic “third nature”. title: Environmental factors associated with abundance and bioindicator potential of Australomicrodeutopus in tropical brackish water ponds

title: Distant water fishing and its effects on domestic food security
abstract: Governments around the world have identified distant water fleets (DWFs) as a key threat to ecosystem health, domestic economic opportunities, and food security. With a high prevalence of undernutrition and micronutrient deficiencies in countries where DWFs operate, the aquatic foods caught by DWFs represent a vital opportunity to shift policy and improve nutrition outcomes. abstract: This study investigated selected aspects of the ecology of two gobiid fishes, Bostrychus africanus and Periophthalmus barbarus, inhabiting Bomu and Kono Creeks, Rivers State, Nigeria. Fish specimens were collected from the intesrtidal mudflats using basket traps between May 2023 and April 2024. title: From Return on Investment to Return on Environment Investing in a Sustainable Planet
abstract: This desk-review article examines the ecological damage and lost investment opportunities associated with the prevailing economic paradigm. It proposes Return on Environment (RoEn) as a complement to Return on Investment (ROI) for evaluating and encouraging regenerative, nature-positive investment. The global economy has transgressed seven of nine planetary boundaries, while more than half of global gross domestic product depends moderately or highly on nature. title: The influence of climate change on temporal shifts in food systems and diets in Kiribati: a scoping review
abstract: Background Kiribati has undergone substantial changes in its food systems and diets, transitioning from traditional to contemporary diets that rely heavily on imported foods. This shift has been shaped by interconnected social, economic, and climate-related drivers, including the progression from traditional food sources to retail markets, food aid, colonialism, global trade, open-market policies, and climate-extreme events. title: Integrating the economic valuation of ecosystem services for sustainable futures: methodological variability, scale effects, and policy implications
abstract: This study analyzed how valuation methods and spatial scale influence reported ecosystem service values. A systematic literature review following PRISMA guidelines and the PICO approach screened 222 articles from the Scopus database (2016–2025); after applying rigorous inclusion criteria, 38 studies were selected. title: Modulation of precession-forced Asian–African monsoon and arid climate variability by obliquity
abstract: Precession and obliquity play vital roles in orbital-scale climate change. However, their combined effects remain poorly understood. In this study, we examine how obliquity modulates precession-driven climate responses across Asian–African monsoon and arid regions (AAMAR). Results demonstrate that under high obliquity, the minimum-precession-induced precipitation increase is weakened in the Asian–African monsoon regions but enhanced in the Asian–African arid regions. title: Bioaccumulation, food web transfer, and tissue distribution of polonium-210 and lead-210 in Canadian freshwater ecosystems
abstract: Understanding the bioaccumulation and trophic transfer of naturally occurring radionuclides is essential for assessing ecological risk in freshwater systems. This study provides a large-scale assessment of polonium-210 ( 210 Po) and lead-210 ( 210 Pb) bioaccumulation, trophic transfer and tissue-specific biodistribution in freshwater food webs across Canada. title: Depth and inter-annual variation of crustacean diversity within Ecklonia maxima holdfast communities in the Benguela-Agulhas transition zone of the South African coast
abstract: Abstract Kelp holdfasts form complex, three-dimensional biogenic habitats that support diverse macroinvertebrate assemblages, yet the crustacean fauna within these structures which are an important contributors to secondary production and trophic transfer in kelp forest food webs remains poorly quantified. We characterised crustacean assemblages associated with holdfasts of the kelp Ecklonia maxima at Miller’s Point, False Bay, South Africa, to test for effects of depth and interannual variation. abstract: ABSTRACT In offshore wind power development, offshore wind farm siting (OWFS) is a crucial yet complex decision process, often compromised by expert linguistic ambiguity, multidimensional expert evaluation and conflicting criteria. To tackle these challenges, this study proposes an integrated multicriteria group decision‐making (MCGDM) framework that integrates the entropy weight method (EWM) with the cubic q‐rung orthopair fuzzy extension of TOPSIS (Cq‐ROF‐TOPSIS). title: Proteomic insights into the antifouling molecular responses of nature-inspired gallic and bile acid derivatives in Mytilus galloprovincialis
abstract: Nature-inspired compounds are increasingly recognized as promising sources of effective and environmentally safer antifouling (AF) agents. However, the development of new AF solutions under current regulatory frameworks requires a better understanding of the biological responses associated with their activity. title: Hospital wastewater as a significant source of microplastics in Northern Iran: Abundance, polymer composition, and environmental risk assessment
abstract: BACKGROUND: Microplastics (MPs) are ubiquitous contaminants increasingly detected in aquatic environments and wastewater systems, raising concerns regarding ecosystem and human health. Hospital wastewater has been identified as a source of MPs entering municipal systems; however, data on their occurrence, characteristics, and associated risks remain limited. This study aimed to characterize MP contamination in hospital wastewater and assess the associated environmental and health risks. title: Pine trees, wind and limestone degradation, South Florida, USA
abstract: Exposed limestone is subject to numerous pedogenic processes, many which cause surface degradation. The uprooting of windthrown trees is a major pedogenic process, as demonstrated in South Florida pine forests. The effects of Hurricane Andrew’s winds on two forest stands are documented; the Pine Island forest is rooted in exposed level Late Pleistocene limestone bedrock, and Lostman’s Pines in quartz sand overlying the level mid-Pliocene limestone bedrock. abstract: La producción solar de sal depende de algo elemental y, a la vez, difícil de aislar: clima, agua marina y conectividad hidrológica. abstract: ABSTRACT Microbialites vary widely in organic matter abundance and preservation, making their hydrocarbon‐generating potential uncertain. abstract: Abstract Water quality patterns reflect spatially heterogeneous associations among topography, drainage connectivity, land use configuration, and soil hydrologic structure, whereas concentration-based assessments and global models may obscure where these relationships emerge and at which spatial scales they operate. Using monitoring data from 2020 to 2024, this study examined six water quality indicators: total organic carbon (TOC), total nitrogen (TN), total phosphorus (TP), dissolved oxygen (DO), pH, and electrical conductivity (EC) across 67 mid-basins in South Korea. abstract: Abstract In tropical rivers, aquatic macrophytes constitute complex habitats that mediate predator–prey interactions and support diverse fish assemblages. In the present study, we examined how seasonality influences prey use and the trophic network structure of macrophyte-associated ichthyofauna in the lower São Francisco River, Brazil. title: Evidence for cortisol production in a shark
abstract: Corticosteroids are essential regulators of numerous physiological functions in vertebrates, including energy balance, immune responses, osmotic balance and metabolism. The terminal corticosteroids are highly conserved across jawed vertebrates, where cortisol or corticosterone mediates these physiological responses. Elasmobranchs, however, have a unique dominant circulating steroid, 1⍺-hydroxycorticosterone, and since its discovery it has been presumed that elasmobranchs do not produce cortisol. title: Non-exchangeable K sustains plant K uptake in alkaline Mediterranean soils
abstract: Abstract Aims Potassium (K) fertilization recommendations commonly rely on exchangeable-K soil tests, assuming that this fraction represents the soil’s capacity to supply plant-available K. However, limited crop response to K fertilization at insufficient exchangeable-K concentrations suggests contributions from additional soil K reservoirs. abstract: Baleen whale strandings are rare in the southern Gulf of Mexico and can provide valuable molecular information where species are infrequently documented. We analyzed tissue from a highly decomposed whale stranded on the central coast of Veracruz, Mexico, by amplifying and bidirectionally sequencing the mitochondrial DNA control region. title: Ontogenetic changes in phototactic behavior of Pacific bluefin tuna (Thunnus orientalis) larvae and juveniles
abstract: In this study, to elucidate the development of visual function in Pacific bluefin tuna (PBT; Thunnus orientalis ), we analyzed ontogenetic changes in the expression of visual opsin genes from hatching through the juvenile stage and evaluated wavelength- and intensity-dependent photobehavior using projected light. title: Timing matters: earlier planting leads to increased seedling emergence success in Zostera marina seeds
abstract: Globally seagrass restoration efforts have been increasing in recent years. Seed-based restoration is often favoured, as it provides higher genetic diversity and less impact on donor meadows. Restoration success is highly dependent on site-selection, methods and timing. To increase the success of seedling establishment for restoration programmes we carried out experiments investigating timing, planting methods and sediment type under semi-controlled conditions in a mesocosm setup. title: Redox distribution of Asgard archaea and co-occurring taxa in microbial mats from an early Proterozoic ecosystem analog
abstract: Abstract Increasing evidence supports that eukaryotes originated from the symbiosis of an Asgard archaeon, the alphaproteobacterial ancestor of mitochondria, and possibly additional bacterial contributions. Eukaryogenesis likely occurred in redox-transition environments such as microbial mats or shallow sediments ~2 billion years ago, when atmospheric oxygen was far lower than today. title: Tribological performance of PTFE/polyimide pulp/GCNT composites
abstract: Abstract Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) is widely used as a solid lubricant but suffers from poor wear resistance, limiting its application in demanding mechanical components. title: Seasonality and maximum wind gusts correlate with microplastic concentrations in a freshwater stream system
abstract: Abstract We evaluate how meteorological and environmental variables relate to stream microplastic concentrations using regression-based models. Forty-nine water column samples were collected bimonthly over an annual cycle (September 2024–September 2025) from a stream in southeastern Pennsylvania, USA. Microplastic particles were isolated and quantified by light microscopy, and polymer types were characterized using scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM–EDS) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). title: Toxicological impacts of sulfamethoxazole on freshwater organisms – toxicity and oxidative stress
abstract: The continuous expansion of the pharmaceutical sector has intensified aquatic contamination, as persistent active compounds enter water bodies through urban, industrial, and agricultural runoff. Among these contaminants, sulfamethoxazole (SMX)—a widely used sulphonamide antibiotic—raises ecological concerns due to its persistence and potential for bioaccumulation. abstract: Abstract Cleaning mutualisms provide a useful framework for examining how cooperation and conflict are regulated, yet the extent to which client condition influences these dynamics remains unclear. We tested whether reef manta ray (Mobula alfredi) injury status is associated with cleaner engagement and behavioural dynamics at a cleaning station in the Philippines. abstract: The effects of temperature and irradiance, including light spectral quality, on the photochemical efficiency of the edible red alga Gloiopeltis frutex (Endocladiaceae) were determined using a pulse-amplitude-modulated (PAM) chlorophyll fluorometer. title: Enhancing Antarctic terrestrial conservation through biodiversity informatics
abstract: Area-based and species-specific protection provide complementary benefits for biodiversity conservation. Yet, their application to key Antarctic terrestrial invertebrates has been hindered by biodiversity shortfalls, including the prevalence of cryptic species. abstract: Our study examines the diversity of values within a superficially homogeneous recreational fishery and its relationship to angler diversity. We collected data on fishing preferences, behaviors, catch usage, and sociodemographics from 443 shore anglers across 10 cities in the lower Great Lakes. We identified five coherent dimensions, including food, cultural, leisure, challenge/performance, and social-financial centrality, consistent with multidimensional value structuring in recreational fisheries. abstract: Archaeological shell remains are widely used to reconstruct littoral ecology and human foraging behavior at sites throughout the world, yet most models generally assume that shells are harvested and either consumed, or processed, at or near the shoreline. title: Microplastic Pollution in a Small River with an Agriculture-dominated Catchment under Different Rainfall Conditions: Transport Scaling, Characteristics and Ecological Risk Assessment
abstract: The agriculture cluster is recognized as a cryptic hotspot of microplastic pollution. Especially, rainfall-driven microplastic (MP) dynamics in small agricultural rivers have not been adequately quantified under various hydrological conditions. This study quantified MP concentrations, loads, characteristics, and ecological risks under baseline dry conditions and during four rainfall events of varying intensities in a small agricultural river. abstract: Understanding the spatiotemporal association between ecosystem service value (ESV) and human activity intensity (HAI) is essential for coordinating regional ecological protection with sustainable socioeconomic development. Using geospatial data for the Chengdu Metropolitan Area from 2000 to 2020, this study estimated ESV and HAI with an ESV accounting model and an HAI assessment model, and examined their spatiotemporal patterns and associations using bivariate spatial autocorrelation and coupling coordination degree models. title: Biology and conservation of the European mudminnow (Umbra krameri Walbaum, 1792): an update of the monograph 30 years after the first international workshop
abstract: During the three decades following the publication of the first comprehensive monograph on the European mudminnow ( Umbra krameri Walbaum, 1792), knowledge of the species’ biology, distribution, genetics, ecology, and conservation has expanded substantially. In several countries, a dynamic distribution pattern has become apparent, with many local populations seemingly disappearing while new populations continue to be documented. title: Application of Professional Ethics Principles and Prevention through Design (PtD) in Power Plant Layout Based on Site Investigation
abstract: The feasibility study (FS) is an early phase that largely determines the success of a power plant development project, in which the plant layout is one of the key decisions affecting technical, safety, cost, construction, and operational aspects. This study analyzes the application of Prevention through Design (PtD) in developing the layout of the Java Bali 2 Combined Cycle Power Plant (PLTGU) by using Site Investigation (SI) results. title: Orthotropy and aging effects on the nanomechanical properties of Perumytilus purpuratus nacre
abstract: Mollusks developed protective shells early in their evolutionary history, with nacre emerging as a highly optimized hierarchical structure that combines stiff aragonitic tablets with compliant organic interfaces to achieve remarkable toughness. Although its mechanical properties are well studied, the influence of aging on its nanomechanical response remains unclear. title: Linking environmental variability to diatom assemblages in seasonal wetlands
abstract: Seasonal wetlands undergo recurrent inundation and contraction, creating strong hydrochemical variability and non–independent observations within pans. We tested whether this variability translated into diatom differentiation in five pans within each of two South African Ramsar wetland systems, Makuleke and Nylsvley, during cool–dry and hot–wet seasons. title: Variability in blue carbon stocks across mangrove forest types in Jamaica
abstract: Mangroves are among the most carbon-rich tropical forests, with much of their carbon stock located in underlying sediments. They play a vital role in climate mitigation and adaptation by offsetting carbon dioxide emissions linked to global warming. Despite their importance, blue carbon ecosystems remain poorly represented in climate policy across the Caribbean, with Jamaica and Belize being the only Caribbean countries to incorporate blue carbon stock values into their Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). title: Non-destructive GARField NMR profiling to characterize release from opaque antifouling coatings
abstract: In this work, high-resolution one-dimensional (1D) 1 H NMR profiling is employed, enabling a novel non-destructive approach for characterization of release processes in optically opaque antifouling coatings. As a first case, the release of copper pyrithione (CuPy) from PDMS-based polymer networks is investigated. abstract: This paper presents an AI-enabled predictive procurement model that integrates probabilistic demand forecasting, supplier lead-time prediction, and multi-echelon inventory optimization to secure target service levels while lowering working capital. The framework couples hierarchical time-series forecasting with gradient-boosted trees and lightweight sequence models, capturing seasonality, promotions, and regime shifts. title: Estimation of seafood byproducts generated by freezing companies in the Souss-Massa Region, Morocco
abstract: The seafood processing industry generates substantial quantities of byproducts that remain underutilized despite their potential for recovery and further utilization. This study aimed to assess the generation and management of seafood byproducts within the freezing industry of the Souss-Massa region, Morocco. A voluntary semi-structured survey was conducted among 21 of the 39 regional freezing companies, focusing on raw material supply, processing activities, byproduct generation, and management practices. title: Environmental control of morphological color changes in the Bigfin Reef Squid, Sepioteuthis lessoniana
abstract: ABSTRACT Phenotypic plasticity enables organisms to adjust their traits in response to environmental conditions, yet studies of animal coloration—particularly in cephalopods—have largely focused on rapid neural control while overlooking slower, substrate-level changes. Here, we investigate whether morphological color change contributes to phenotypic plasticity in the bigfin reef squid ( Sepioteuthis lessoniana ). title: Interfacial Salt Redistribution Enables Rapid Atmospheric Water Harvesting in a Biomimetic Multi‐Layer Hygroscopic Membrane
abstract: ABSTRACT Sorption‐based atmospheric water harvesting (SAWH) offers a promising route for decentralized freshwater production, but practical water output is often limited by slow sorption kinetics in salt‐loaded hydrogel sorbents. Here, a biomimetic multi‐layer heterogeneous hygroscopic (MHH) membrane is developed to decouple vapor capture from bulk liquid storage. title: Foliar polystyrene nanoplastics modulate cadmium uptake and root-to-shoot translocation in hydroponic Spinacia oleracea L.: Time- and concentration-dependent responses
abstract: The accumulation of plastics and heavy metals (HMs) in the environment has become a significant global concern due to their persistence, ubiquity, and potential ecological impacts. Atmospheric micro- and nanoplastics (MP, NP) are capable of undergoing long-range transport and can be deposited onto plant shoots through precipitation, thereby exposing aerial plant tissues to these particulate contaminants. title: Spatial clustering of COVID-19 cases and mortality at the global scale
abstract: Understanding the spatial distribution of COVID-19 cases and mortality is important for identifying high-risk areas and strengthening global public health preparedness. Although many COVID-19 spatial studies have been conducted at national or regional scales, fewer have applied a consistent global spatial framework to compare the clustering of both reported cases and deaths. This study analysed global spatial clustering of COVID-19 cases and deaths using country- and territory-level data from the WHO COVID-19 Global Dataset. abstract: During embryonic development, cells undergo differentiation into highly specialized cell types. Capitalizing on single-cell RNA sequencing, many initiatives and substantial resources are cataloguing these differentiated cell types by their transcriptomic profiles. abstract: Long-term demographic monitoring is critical for understanding population stability and responses to environmental disturbance. Bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ) inhabiting Sarasota Bay, Florida, have been studied by the Sarasota Dolphin Research Program since 1970. While most dolphins in the resident community are individually identifiable via photographic-identification (photo-ID), direct census datasets are largely unavailable elsewhere. title: Robust trajectory tracking of an underactuated ROV under compound flow disturbances using ADRC-GISMC
abstract: Abstract Trajectory tracking of remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) remains difficult when hydrodynamic coupling, plant uncertainty, actuator constraints, and spatially varying flow disturbances act simultaneously. This study presents a simulation-based evaluation of an ADRC-GISMC strategy for an underactuated ROV under an engineering-oriented compound disturbance model combining background-current and local outfall-plume components. abstract: Abstract The heterogeneity of carbonate reservoirs constitutes a critical control on fluid flow. title: Design and hydrodynamic analysis of a new web-type mooring system
abstract: ”Y”-type branching is a common load-bearing topology in natural networks such as spider webs, where pretensioned radial and circumferential threads provide multiple load-transfer paths and enhance resistance to local damage. Inspired by this mechanism, this study proposes a taut web-type mooring layout for offshore floating platforms, with the main objective of redistributing mooring loads rather than significantly reducing platform motions. abstract: Model Predictive Control (MPC) is applied to track control of unmanned surface vessels. To adapt to dynamic changes in speed and water depth, a water depth and speed dependent predictive model, with coefficients identified from free running tests (e.g., acceleration and zigzag trials), is developed. title: Biomechanical analyses point to dense collagen fibre architecture in an Ediacaran frond
abstract: Ediacaran macrofossils record the earliest large and complex organisms on Earth. Despite extensive study, fundamental aspects of their internal anatomy and tissue composition remain poorly known, limiting understanding of how these organisms were constructed and functioned, as well as how their complex anatomies evolved. abstract: This research investigated the multi-sectoral readiness of Barcelona, Sorsogon, to implement the Department of Science and Technology (DOST) Smart and Sustainable Communities Program (SSCP). Utilizing a qualitative descriptive research design through the lens of the Quadruple Helix model, the study evaluated the insights and perceptions of twentyfive purposively sampled key informants from the Government, Academe, Industry (farmers and fisherfolks), and Civil Society Organization (CSO) sectors to transition into a "Smart Community". abstract: Introduction The lower Cambrian Niutitang Formation shale in the western margin of the Xuefeng uplift (WMXU), South China, possesses favorable material conditions including significant thickness, high organic carbon content, and high thermal maturity. title: A balanced set of standardized affective environmental images for climate change research
abstract: Evocative visual imagery is central to research on affective pathways of environmental engagement, yet existing stimulus sets often overrepresent negative imagery and make it difficult to compare positive and negative affective responses under comparable conditions. We developed a balanced database of affective environmental images designed to support controlled comparisons of positive and negative environmental imagery. abstract: Algal blooms are a global problem that lead to the formation of excessive algal organic matter, resulting in the deterioration of water sources and the disruption of water treatment processes. Methods for the extraction of algal organic matter from algal cells are time-consuming and sometimes ineffective in achieving cell lysis. title: The cost of regulatory delay: quantifying how permitting timelines affect offshore wind energy costs
abstract: Abstract Rapid deployment of offshore renewable energy and transmission infrastructure can be a major contributor to energy system decarbonization. However, regulatory obligations frequently impose deployment delays that are typically not quantified in cost terms. The costs of such delays should be incorporated in project and technology assessments. title: Sexual dimorphism shapes the plasma metabolome of the endangered Iberian lynx
abstract: Sexual dimorphism is a key but still incompletely resolved determinant of mammalian systemic metabolism, particularly in endangered species where physiological organization remains poorly characterized. Here, we integrate untargeted plasma metabolomics to dissect hierarchical determinants of systemic metabolic organization in the Iberian lynx ( Lynx pardinus ), one of the world’s most endangered felids. title: Evaluating alternative trade network configurations under geopolitical risk: a multi-scale systems approach
abstract: Rising geopolitical risks and supply-chain disruptions have increased interest in transport-network diversification and alternative connectivity systems. This article presents a scenario-based comparison between a traditional maritime chokepoint configuration centered on the Strait of Hormuz and a prospective diversified multimodal corridor connecting the Middle East and Europe. title: Thailand Land Surface Temperature Variation and Forecasting
abstract: Climate change has emerged as a global challenge, influenced by human activities, industrial operations and energy systems that depend on non-renewable energy such as carbon, gas, and petroleum. These activities have contributed to long-term shifts in temperature and broader climatic conditions. Land Surface Temperature (LST) has become an important standard for informing weather-related strategies at regional scales. abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a growing global health challenge at the interface of human, animal, and environmental health. Reptiles—including wild populations, pets, farmed species, and internationally traded animals—are increasingly recognized as participants in One Health AMR networks, occupying ecological interfaces that facilitate interactions among wildlife, domestic animals, humans, and the environment. title: Molecular Mechanisms of Microbial Biomineralization: Protein Molecules
abstract: Microbial biomineralization is a ubiquitous natural process involving the formation and accumulation of inorganic minerals. It plays a crucial role in biogeochemical cycles and the development of biological structures. Despite recent progress in studying this phenomenon, the underlying molecular mechanisms mediated by proteins and extracellular polymers remain insufficiently systematized. abstract: Abstract Combinations of seasonal normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) metrics that serve as proxies for aboveground biomass, primary productivity, and phenology can be used to define ecosystem functional types (EFTs), discrete areas with similar carbon gain dynamics. EFT richness, the number of unique EFTs within a prescribed area, represents the spatial heterogeneity in the seasonal dynamics of primary productivity across a landscape, and can be used as an index of functional diversity. abstract: Timely and accurate projections of when global warming will exceed the Paris Agreement’s 1.5 °C threshold are essential for effective climate policy. abstract: Health benefits from emission controls are often inferred from reductions in fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) mass, yet this metric can underrepresent toxicity from PM 2.5 -bound metals. abstract: Understanding the sources of metals in hydrothermal ore systems is fundamental for improving exploration models. abstract: Abstract Teleost fishes display diverse swimming modes supported by functional specialization of skeletal muscle. abstract: Soil microbes are crucial in maintaining soil and plant health, underpinning agronomic productivity. This study investigates antimicrobial copper- and zinc-laden cow and pig slurry applications on soil microbial community structures in an approximately 50-year long-term slurry experiment on a permanent grassland located in County Down, Northern Ireland. abstract: Abstract Flood extent, depth, duration, and connectivity are key attributes of the seasonal flood pulse in Amazon floodplains, but characterizing them consistently remains difficult in forested, low-relief terrain. abstract: Abstract. Upland peatlands are a major terrestrial carbon reservoir that may play an important role in the global carbon cycle. abstract: Abstract Ti-6Al-4V (TC4) is extensively utilized for oral implants due to its excellent mechanical properties and biocompatibility. Here, electrochemical, surface, and corrosion product analyses were used to investigate the MIC of selective laser melted (SLM) TC4 induced by mono- or dual-species biofilms of Streptococcus mutans ( S. mutans ) and Veillonella dispar ( V. dispar ). title: A histidine-mediated supramolecular mechanism links temperature and pH activation of the sperm channel CatSper
abstract: The cation channel of sperm, CatSper, is a sperm-specific calcium channel essential for male fertility across metazoans. CatSper is activated by intracellular alkalinization, membrane depolarization, and elevated temperature, which together ensure maximal current generation. However, the structural mechanisms by which these physiological stimuli jointly regulate channel activation remain poorly understood, in part because CatSper is an unusually complex ~15-subunit assembly organized in zigzag supramolecular arrays along the sperm flagellum. title: Multi-source geospatial modelling of direct economic losses from rainstorm-related disaster events in Guangxi, South China
abstract: Rainstorm-related disasters cause substantial economic losses in Guangxi, China, but event-level loss estimates are complicated by spatially clustered events, changing socioeconomic exposure, and heterogeneous reporting. We compiled 1,811 county-event records from the official disaster archive for 2012–2021 and linked them to event-period precipitation, year-matched gridded population and GDP, and selected vulnerability-related proxies. title: Mycosphere microbiome assembly and metabolic reprogramming in Phallus rugulosus revealed by multi-omics integration
abstract: The mycosphere, defined as the soil zone influenced by fungal hyphae, hosts a distinct microbiome that plays a critical role in host development. Nevertheless, the assembly rules and metabolic functions in macrofungi remain poorly understood. This study aims to disentangle these processes in the edible fungus Phallus rugulosus . We integrated metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and untargeted metabolomics to compare mycosphere soil (MS) and bulk soil (BS) of P. rugulosus . title: Prediction and Model Validation of Corrosion Fatigue Life for BFRP Tendons Under Combined Acidic Environment and Temperature
abstract: ABSTRACT The widespread application of fiber‐reinforced polymers (FRP) in engineering is primarily attributed to their superior durability compared to traditional materials. However, under prolonged exposure to harsh service environments, the material inevitably undergoes progressive degradation. The existing durability studies and life prediction models have largely overlooked the synergistic effects of combined environmental actions and mechanical loading conditions. title: Clay minerals of modern alluvial deposits of the Indigirka River and its tributaries as indicators of depositional sources
abstract: To address the question of how the geological structure and composition of rocks in the Indigirka River basin influence the mineral composition of modern alluvial deposits, samples collected from the lower reaches of the river were analyzed. The composition of the samples was studied using X-ray diffraction analysis. title: Surgical management of reproductive disease in aquarium managed female elasmobranchs
abstract: Introduction Reproductive disease in female elasmobranchs has been increasingly reported in the literature, though there are limited descriptions of therapeutic intervention. Methods This retrospective case series details the surgical management of 20 female elasmobranchs representing nine species. Data for this study were collected from the medical records and necropsy reports of elasmobranchs at six separate zoos and aquaria. title: On the edge: habitat patchiness and island isolation fracture the distribution of the endemic Kimberley rock-rat
abstract: We integrate demography, morphology and genetics to assess the biology and population structure of the endemic Kimberley rock-rat (Zyzomys woodwardi), a habitat specialist of the monsoonal tropics. The species is confined to the extreme north-west of the continent and 16 adjacent islands that were part of the mainland during the last Pleistocene glaciation. Islands became isolated from ~6500 years before present (BP), with their current populations being considered relictual. title: 16S rRNA amplicon profiling of Salvadora persica -associated rhizosphere bacterial communities under saline agricultural conditions
abstract: Salvadora persica (Arak) is a facultative halophyte adapted to arid and saline environments, yet its rhizosphere microbiome remains poorly characterised. We profiled bacterial communities associated with S. persica at Arak Farm, Rabigh, Saudi Arabia, using Illumina MiSeq sequencing of the V3–V4 16S rRNA region and ASV-based analysis. Three rhizosphere composites and one adjacent bulk-soil composite were analysed. title: Cost-driven design and optimization of steel support structures for offshore energy platforms: a review of CAPEX cost models
abstract: Steel support structures for offshore energy platforms require large volumes of steel and complex manufacturing, making them one of the most expensive elements of any offshore project. Capital expenditure (CAPEX), which includes material procurement, manufacturing, transportation, and installation, typically makes up around 70% of the total lifecycle cost of these structures. Although many studies have proposed cost models to support design and optimization, the approaches used vary considerably in terms of scope, methodology, and level of detail. title: Unravelling the phylogenetic complexities of Ischyropsalis (Opiliones: Dyspnoi: Ischyropsalididae) in the North Iberian Peninsula, with the description of three new species
abstract: Ischyropsalis C.L. Koch, 1839 is a genus of harvestmen inhabiting both terrestrial surface habitats and caves in central and southern Europe. The accepted number of species is controversial due to feature similarities and their strong sexual dimorphism. The northern part of the Iberian Peninsula harbours 16 accepted species, seven of which are epigean, while the other nine exclusively live in caves. title: Groundwater Contamination in India: Regional Variations, Hydrogeochemical Controls, Health Risks, and Integrated Management Strategies
abstract: Groundwater plays a critical role in meeting drinking and agricultural water demands in India. This review focuses on regional variations in groundwater quality, contamination sources, and remediation strategies. The evaluation encompasses pH, electrical conductivity, total dissolved solids, hardness, major ions, and contaminants including fluoride, arsenic, nitrate, and heavy metals. Results reveal significant regional variations, with contamination driven by intensive agriculture, industrial activities, mining, urbanization, and geological factors. title: Experimental investigation of ground fissure reactivation and differential deformation under layered groundwater pumping–recharge conditions
abstract: Groundwater-level fluctuations can induce differential deformation at ground-fissure sites, yet systematic experimental investigations of hydraulic and layered deformation responses across fissures during pumping-recharge remain limited. This study focuses on the F 4 ground-fissure area in Yuhuazhai, Xi’an, and employs a large-scale physical model to investigate hydro-mechanical responses under layered groundwater pumping-recharge conditions. title: Spatial distribution and environmental drivers of wild honey bee nesting patterns in the Eastern Cape Province, South Africa
abstract: Spatial clusters of animal nests can be driven by mating behaviors, social benefits, and landscape heterogeneity. Unmanaged honey bees (Hymenoptera: Apidae: Apis spp.) have been documented nesting in clustered spatial distributions. However, environmental features influencing unmanaged honey bee nesting patterns have been largely understudied, especially for wild honey bees ( A. mellifera ) across Africa. title: Retracing the olive (Olea europaea L. subsp. europaea) origin and its early history diffusion among the civilizations overlooking the Mediterranean coasts: an integrated approach
abstract: The olive tree is one of the most important crops in the world, but even more, one of the most identitarian plant for the countries of the Mediterranean basin. In this article, the vast consultation of scientific literature, archaeological, historical and anecdotal sources, allowed to outline a global reasoned vision on the olive origin, its spread during early history and how olive fruit fly may represent as proxy for tracing its early diffusion. title: Between Development and Loss: Residential Expansion and Transformation of Rural Habitat in Vía a la Costa and Posorja, Urban Edges of Guayaquil
abstract: The urban growth of Guayaquil has reconfigured the boundaries between the city and the countryside, giving rise to new urban edges were residential expansion advances on previously rural territories. Vía a la Costa and Posorja sectors have become contrasting but complementary scenarios of the same phenomenon: the progressive loss of rural habitat in the face of the dynamics of accelerated urbanization. title: Innovative performance indicators for effective Quality, Safety, and Environment management in oil drilling operations
abstract: Abstract Effective management of Quality, Safety, and Environment (QSE) performance is critical in high-risk oil drilling operations. Despite extensive research on generic Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) frameworks, there remains limited guidance on context-specific, operationally validated methodologies that integrate leading and lagging indicators within unified QSE systems for drilling operations. title: Long-term patterns in phenotypic plasticity of chironomid head capsules in small high-elevation subarctic lakes: exploring possible mechanisms using multi-proxy paleolimnological records
abstract: Abstract We quantified temporal variation in the head capsule (HC) length of subfossil chironomids from two high-elevation subarctic lakes in northern Sweden and explored its potential drivers using chironomid assemblages, sedimentary pigments, and stable isotope analyses. Although establishing a reliable chronology was challenging because of the macrofossil-poor sediment context, radiocarbon dating indicates that the cores span approximately the last 5000 years, corresponding to the long-term cooling trend of the Late Holocene in this area. title: Undertow Structure and Stress Partition Beneath Plunging Breakers
abstract: Abstract Undertow beneath breaking waves controls nearshore mass balance and sediment transport, yet the transition between the lower wave–bottom-influenced region and the overlying flow affected by breaking-generated turbulence lacks a clear dynamical definition. This study investigates the vertical structure of undertow and turbulence beneath two regular laboratory plunging waves propagating over a sloping bottom, based on detailed velocity measurements. title: Assessing the eco-efficiency of offshore wind energy using a combined life cycle assessment and data envelopment analysis approach
abstract: This study develops an integrated Life Cycle Assessment (LCA)–Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) framework to evaluate the material eco-efficiency of 20 operational offshore wind farms in the United Kingdom. The framework incorporates a contribution-analysis step to identify the most environmentally relevant inventory flows before efficiency assessment. Harmonised cradle-to-grave inventories were constructed from the MEAOW model and remapped to ecoinvent v3.12 background processes. title: Emergency Response and Management of Pandemic Disasters and Their Environmental Dimensions: A Review of Lessons from COVID-19 in Bangladesh
abstract: Pandemics are disasters whose causes and consequences are both rooted in the environment, yet emergency management and environmental management are usually reviewed apart. This narrative review synthesizes 74 documents published between 2008 and 2026, comprising peer-reviewed studies, reports of intergovernmental and national agencies, and selected news and NGO records, to examine the emergency response to COVID-19 in Bangladesh, with the European Union as a comparator, and to connect that response to its environmental dimensions. title: Fluoride enrichment, hydrogeochemical processes, and health risks from groundwater ingestion in the Zabzugu District, Ghana
abstract: Groundwater quality in the Zabzugu District, Northern Ghana, is increasingly affected by geogenic processes and anthropogenic activities, particularly agriculture. This study examined the hydrogeochemical characteristics, controlling mechanisms, and health implications of groundwater in the district. Groundwater samples from thirteen (13) locations were analysed using physicochemical measurements, hydrogeochemical modelling, and multivariate statistical techniques, including correlation, factor, and cluster analyses. title: Modulation of quasi-biennial oscillation by volcanic sulfate aerosols
abstract: Large and moderate volcanic eruptions significantly impact the stratosphere by releasing sulfur dioxide, thereby affecting atmospheric dynamics. Mt. Pinatubo erupted in 1991 and induced a warming of 3 K in the stratosphere that led to prolonged easterly wind regimes of the Quasi-biennial oscillation (QBO). Using a three-member ensemble mean obtained from the ECHAM6-HAMMOZ model, we show the impact of eruptive volcanoes on the tropical stratosphere and the QBO from 2003 to 2013. title: Optimal dietary glycerol monolaurate supplementation improves growth performance, antioxidant capacity, immune responses and intestinal microbiota in juvenile largemouth bass
abstract: Introduction Plant-derived functional additives have gained increasing attention as sustainable alternatives in aquafeed. This study aims to investigate the effects of dietary monolaurin on productive performance, innate immune indicators, antioxidative effects, and gut flora in largemouth bass ( Micropterus salmoides ). abstract: ABSTRACT Acute hepatopancreatic necrosis disease (AHPND) is caused by a plasmid bearing strain of Vibrio parahaemolyticus ( Vp AHPND ), which produces PirA and PirB toxins that specifically target and damage hepatopancreatic and epithelial cells of the shrimp gastrointestinal tract. The impact of AHPND, together with concerns regarding antibiotic resistance, has necessitated investigations into alternative forms of disease prevention. title: Stresses in Above‐Ground Storage Tanks Subjected to Flood‐Borne Debris Impact
abstract: ABSTRACT The objective of this study is to investigate the structural response of above‐ground storage tanks (ASTs) subjected to flood‐borne debris impact, a critical yet understudied aspect of flood‐induced loading. While past research has extensively examined AST performance under hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads, limited attention has been paid to debris impact, which can contribute significantly to tank damage during floods. title: Assessment of the Drainage Network Systems and Their Effects on Stormwater Flow and Flooding in Orogun, Ughelli North, Delta State, Nigeria
abstract: Flooding has become a recurring environmental challenge in many Nigerian urban centers, with Orogun town in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State experiencing increasing vulnerability to stormwater inundation. This study assesses the drainage network and its effects on stormwater flow and flooding in Orogun, employing a quantitative research methodology that integrates field surveys, hydrological measurements, and geospatial analysis. title: Glacier change at the ISM-MLW transition: multi-decadal evidence of spatial heterogeneity from the Sara Umga watershed, western Himalaya
abstract: This study presents a multi-decadal assessment of glacier change in the Sara Umga Watershed (SUW), between the Parvati and Chandra basins. The region receives a majority of its annual precipitation from Indian Summer Monsoon (ISM) and a comparatively lower share contributed by winter Mid Latitude Westerlies (MLW). Using multi-temporal satellite data, we quantify changes in glacier length, area, surface velocity, elevation, debris cover, ice cliff dynamics, and high-faltitude lakes, supplemented by long-term climate trend analysis. title: Concentrations of uranium, cesium, and rubidium in drinking water and Monte Carlo–based age-specific health risk assessment of uranium
abstract: Freshwater is essential for life and the economy, yet its scarcity is worsening due to population growth, climate change, and unequal distribution. This study measures concentrations of uranium (U), cesium (Cs), and rubidium (Rb) in drinking water supplies across Arsanjan County, Iran, and evaluated the associated carcinogenic and non-carcinogenic risks of U using Monte Carlo simulation. Uranium concentrations were consistently below EPA and WHO guideline of 30 µg/L. The maximum Cs concentration was 0.63 µg/L, whereas Rb concentrations ranged from 2.04 to 13.94 µg/L. title: Distribution of Microplastics in Freshwater Mussels across a Watershed
abstract: Microplastic research is an emerging field of study, and we do not yet fully understand the scope or effects of microplastic pollution. Microplastics are ubiquitous in the environment, but the field suffers from a lack of unified, accessible protocols and an ecosystems approach to evaluating microplastic contamination. During autumn 2020, we collected water, mussel, and sediment samples from five sites along the Yadkin–Pee Dee River Basin, North Carolina. title: Effectiveness of Geotechnical Investigations on Structural and Highway Construction in Nigeria
abstract: Geotechnical investigations are widely regarded as a crucial component of the safe, durable and cost-effective construction of structural and highway infrastructure in Nigeria. Rapid urbanization and increasing infrastructure demand have forced the need for detailed subsurface characterization in Nigeria, but lack of geotechnical research is still one of the leading reasons for construction failure. title: How climate change affects mosquito-borne infectious disease: The different trajectories of malaria and dengue
abstract: As climate change increases temperatures, additional warmth combines with rainfall and humidity to enhance conditions for mosquito populations to thrive. Greater spread of Anopheles and Aedes vectors increases the risk of transmission of the world’s most prevalent mosquito-borne infectious diseases, malaria and dengue. Yet the impacts of climate drivers on disease transmission are complex: Relationships are nonlinear, effects are seasonal, and there is substantial local variability. title: Microplastics and nanoplastics as potential ecological oncogenic co-drivers: rewiring host–microbe interactions in cancer
abstract: Microplastics and nanoplastics (MPs/NPs) are increasingly recognized as biologically active interfaces that may reshape host–microbe interactions in carcinogenesis. This review proposes a hypothesis-generating mechanistic framework in which MPs/NPs may influence cancer-related processes through the integration of environmental exposure, epithelial barrier disruption, immune dysregulation, and tumor microenvironment remodeling. title: Reconstruction of an Ecosystem-Based Law Enforcement Model: Transformation of the Principle of Utility for the Restoration of Protected Forests
abstract: Indonesia, as a megabiodiverse country, faces serious challenges from the degradation of protected forests caused by land conversion into illegal agricultural areas. This study aims to analyze current law enforcement efforts against forest land conversion and formulate an environmental restoration-based law enforcement model grounded in the principle of legal utility. title: Correlating InSAR-derived ground movement rates with landslide activity class and causal factors: a case study from Cyprus
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the statistical correlation between ground movement rates in landslide areas, as derived by Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) results, with geological, geomorphological, environmental and geotechnical causal factors in southwestern Cyprus. The analysis examines ground velocities derived using Multi-Temporal Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (MT-InSAR) for both active and inactive landslides that are recorded in an existing inventory, using ascending and descending orbit datasets. title: Data-driven accessibility to critical facilities using connected vehicle data: implications for future mobility and urban systems
abstract: Accurate measurement of accessibility to critical facilities is essential for equitable and efficient transportation and land-use planning, particularly in data-driven mobility systems. This study develops a novel hybrid framework to estimate travel time–based accessibility to schools and libraries using high-resolution connected vehicle (CV) data supplemented with Google Distance Matrix API to ensure complete spatial coverage. title: Exploring Bacteria from Extreme Environments in Chilean Patagonia for Antitrypanosomal Metabolites
abstract: Abstract Extreme environments are recognized as valuable reservoirs of microbial diversity and chemical novelty. Adapted to harsh environmental conditions, bacteria isolated from extreme environments exhibit unique biosynthetic capabilities associated with the production of structurally diverse bioactive metabolites. Chagas disease (CD), caused by the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi, remains one of the most important neglected tropical diseases, affecting approximately eight million people worldwide. title: Taxonomic advancements in the Calotrichaceae: Resolving phylogenetic ambiguities and describing five novel species of Dulcicalothrix from the Konkan region of India
abstract: The taxonomy of heteropolar, tapering, and unbranched heterocytous cyanobacteria has undergone significant changes over time. Several novel species, genera, and families have been established using a polyphasic approach, which has provided a greater resolution in the systematics of these organisms. The Calotrichaceae, as of today, stands as a well-resolved and monophyletic clade with at least five genera. The family has had some major revisions as well as additions. title: Assessing the resilience of water supply infrastructure to climate variability: a current status assessment in rural India
abstract: Abstract Rural Indian communities, characterised by the decentralised and informal nature of water governance, are extremely vulnerable to climate shocks that impair local water supply infrastructures (WSIs). This study assesses WSI resilience in the face of current climate variability and examines the multidimensional elements that influence resilience results. The research uses a participatory, bottom-up, mixed-method approach to apply the “How Tough is WASH (HTIW)” framework across four rural communities—Srayikkadu (Kerala), Ahirpurwa (Bihar), Kali Nagar (West Bengal), and Kanti (Haryana),

title: Ontogeny of rake mark scarring on common dolphins ( Delphinus delphis ): insights to aggression and affiliation?
abstract: Abstract Aggressive and affiliative interactions shape resource allocation, social structure and reproduction in social species. In delphinids, rake marks (parallel scars from tooth raking) indicate social interactions. When examined alongside ontogeny, demographic traits and scar position, rake marks can inform social dynamics. We assessed rake marks on common dolphins (Delphinus delphis) in Aotearoa New Zealand (2006–2024; n = 102) during post-mortem examinations to explore drivers of social behaviour. title: Evaluation of Atmospheric Correction Methods with Sentinel-2 Imagery
abstract: To reduce the atmospheric effects on remote sensing imagery, there are methods to correct them, called atmospheric correction, which is an important stage of satellite image preprocessing. title: High diversity but limited expression of biosynthetic gene clusters in a peatland microbial community
abstract: The in situ relevance of biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) remains poorly understood. We apply meta-omics to characterize BGC diversity and activity along a peatland redox gradient. title: Environmental Sustainability and Climate Challenges in Local Urban Indonesia
abstract: This paper studies the partial relationship between environmental sustainability and climate challenges in local urban Indonesia, with an attempt to explain cross-level interaction among ecological stress, climate vulnerability as well as governance capacity taking place within medium cities of a developing country. This study attempts to provide a more integrated approach of local urban sustainability beyond the usual concerted focus on large metropolitan areas. abstract: Aquatic nitrogen (N) pollution is a global problem, and understanding where best to implement mitigation strategies to reduce transfers from land to water is becoming increasingly urgent. Watershed nutrient budgets, using commonly available census data, can successfully predict riverine export spatially, albeit with variation related to fractional export. abstract: Rising global temperatures are expected to affect natural ecosystems, but predicting the consequences is challenging given the complexity of ecological communities. Natural communities are complex networks of interacting species, and temperature changes can thus influence species directly and indirectly via changes in their various interactions with other community members within and across trophic levels. abstract: Reconciling development and biodiversity conservation remains a critical challenge in contemporary conservation planning. Our study is based on a case study for the assessment of the Harike wetland, a Ramsar site and a Protected Area, a human-made reservoir, for understanding the impacts of proposed desilting operations and mitigation planning. abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Thawing affects fillet color, determining consumer acceptance and market value of aquatic products. abstract: ABSTRACT Olive fruit fly ( Bactrocera oleae , Rossi) is one of the most significant pests in the Mediterranean olive groves, causing both quantitative and qualitative losses. Understanding its spatial and temporal dynamics is essential for effective and sustainable control of the pest. This study analyses an eight‐year dataset (2017–2024) of the olive fly populations on Samos Island, Greece, based on an extensive monitoring network of McPhail traps. abstract: Abstract Socio-environmental conflicts over natural commons represent a growing challenge for sustainability governance, yet their dynamics remain poorly understood within complex Social-Ecological Systems (SESs). This study examines six emblematic conflicts in the Venice Lagoon (Italy), a complex SES undergoing profound transformations driven by land-use change and the privatisation of natural commons. abstract: Hydropower remains a major source of affordable, clean, and reliable energy; however, aging infrastructure must be modernized to meet evolving environmental and operational requirements. title: Tribal nations’ flood exposure and the U.S. national flood insurance program
abstract: Tribal nations experience significant flood impacts, yet participation in the National Flood Insurance Program remains limited. We analyze flood events, claims, and 57 Tribal Hazard Mitigation Plans, and insights from a tribal representative, to identify disparities in insured recovery. We show administrative, financial, and capacity constraints hinder mitigation progress. Strengthening equitable access to flood insurance, mapping, and federal mitigation resources could play an important role in improving tribal flood resilience.

title: Physicochemical and microbiological qualities of shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei) coated with pectin incorporated with green tea spent extract during refrigerated storage
abstract: This study developed and characterized a pectin (PEC) based coating incorporated with green tea spent extract (GTSE) and/or nisin. Further, Pacific white shrimp were treated with the developed coating and investigated for physicochemical, textural, microbial, and melanosis formation during refrigerated storage for 12 days. Among the four coating solutions, PEC-2 had higher homogeneity (583.6 nm) and antioxidant activity (DPPH: 76.73% and ABTS: 70.95%). Shrimp coated with PEC-4 showed higher quality parameters, maintaining pH (7.12), minimizing weight loss (5.07%), preserving textural integrity
journal: Journal of Food Composition and Analysis

title: ANALISIS LAJU EROSI DAN AKRESI PANTAI TELUK SEPANG MENGGUNAKAN DIGITAL SHORELINE ANALYSIS SYSTEM (DSAS)
abstract: Pantai Teluk Sepang merupakan kawasan pesisir yang dinamis dan berhadapan langsung dengan Samudera Hindia. Perubahan garis pantai dapat memengaruhi keberlanjutan infrastruktur, permukiman, dan ekosistem pesisir sehingga diperlukan pemantauan yang konsisten. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis laju erosi dan akresi Pantai Teluk Sepang menggunakan Digital Shoreline Analysis System (DSAS) berdasarkan tiga tahun pengamatan, yaitu 2020, 2022, dan 2024. Citra satelit diinterpretasi secara visual untuk menentukan batas darat–laut, kemudian garis pantai didigitasi dan dianalisis menggunakan baseline
journal: PERISAI Jurnal Pendidikan dan Riset Ilmu Sains

title: Conventional diversity metrics underestimate gut microbiome disruption under florfenicol exposure in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
abstract: Abstract The gut microbiome is an integral component of fish health and growth performance and therefore represents an important production factor in aquaculture. Antibiotics are a major stressor, not only by disturbing microbial diversity, but also by altering microbial interactions involved in digestion, colonization resistance and functional redundancy. Current risk assessments, however, rely largely on diversity-based evaluations and rarely consider changes in network topology. title: Synergistic effects of climatic drivers and anthropogenic land degradation on cascading geomorphic hazards in Iran
abstract: Environmental hazard adaptation frameworks have predominantly focused on susceptibility to isolated hazards, often overlooking the complex dynamics of cascading land degradation. This study assessed the synergistic impacts of anthropogenic and climatic drivers on cascading geomorphic hazards in Iran. Our framework integrated land degradation models (MEDALUS and RUSLE) with downscaled outputs from 23 General Circulation Models. title: Indigenous Planning: Utilising Kupuna Lensing for Pacific Disaster Risk Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines Indigenous planning as a vital epistemological and practical framework for disaster risk reduction in the Pacific, centering Hawaiian knowledge systems. Through case studies of the 2018 Kīlauea eruption and the 2023 Lahaina wildfire, this paper demonstrates how ʻike Hawaiʻi—utilising kupuna lensing (Hawaiian analytic research method), moʻolelo (stories) and Hawaiian naming practices—offers culturally grounded approaches to reducing risks from disasters. title: Multi-method non-parametric assessment of river water-quality trends and change-points in the Danshui River basin, metropolitan Taipei (2010–2026)
abstract: The Danshui River drains metropolitan Taipei, where two decades of expanding sewer connection and riparian constructed wetlands have targeted river pollution. Using a continuous monthly record of 1,921 samples from 11 Ministry of Environment stations (2010–2026), we assessed trends and change-points in six measured water-quality variables and the River Pollution Index (RPI), a composite index calculated from four of them, through a multi-method non-parametric design: the Mann–Kendall and seasonal Mann–Kendall tests, a variance-corrected modified test, Theil–Sen slopes, the Pettitt and sequenti

title: Transportation facility assessment for bat use in Contra Costa County
abstract: Transportation facilities such as bridges provide critical roosting habitat for bat species throughout California.This assessment analyzed 607 transportation facilities in Contra Costa County from the Federal Highway Administration's National Bridge Inventory dataset.The primary objective was to analyze the structural design elements of transportation facilities with confirmed bat use in Contra Costa County.The assessment prioritized facilities for field surveys using existing spatial datasets of predicted suitable habitat for bat species known to utilize bridges in Contra Costa County.The ass

title: MDBTabNet: An enhanced tabnet with feature enhancement and biological consistency for intelligent abalone plumpness classification
abstract: Abalone is a high-value mollusk whose aquaculture relies on industrial production. Quality assessment and selective breeding are important for industry efficiency, with plumpness as a key indicator. However, available public datasets are not designed for plumpness, and conventional TabNet models have limited capacity for geometric feature extraction and nonlinear interaction modeling. title: The complete mitochondrial genome of Neoporphyra hollenbergii (E. Y. Dawson) L.-E. Yang & J. Brodie, an endemic species from the Gulf of California, Mexico
abstract: Neoporphyra hollenbergii is an endemic red alga from the Gulf of California, a region with notable cryptic diversity. We report its first complete mitochondrial genome and the first Bangiales mitogenome from the region. The circular mitogenome measures 31,565 bp (30.6% GC) and contains 50 genes, including 22 protein-coding genes, two rRNA genes, 24 tRNA genes, tatC, and orf813. The cox1 and rnl genes contain introns, reflecting red algal mitogenome complexity, while gene organization is conserved across Neoporphyra. title: Management of headwater catchments: cultural background, science and policy
abstract: Headwater catchments serve as water towers and initial regulatory buffers against hydrometeorological hazards, yet they face several forms of degradation from unsustainable land use and accelerating climate change. We argue that effective headwater control requires an integrated approach combining watershed governance, science, policy, and cultural background. Old societies showed considerable capacity to solve hydraulic problems but did not fully understand watershed runoff formation and downstream impacts. title: Metagenomic insights into viral community restructuring and microbial interactions in waste stabilization ponds
abstract: Abstract Waste stabilization ponds (WSPs) operate as sequential ecological compartments in which physicochemical gradients, microbial succession, and trophic interactions increase toward the final polishing stage. Among these units, the maturation pond represents the terminal control point for pathogen attenuation and effluent quality; however, its role in shaping viral community structure remains insufficiently resolved. title: Magma Supply Dynamics at Mt. Etna (Italy) Inferred from Peripheral Soil CO2 Emissions: Insights into the 2018 Flank Eruption and the 2021 Paroxysmal Activity
abstract: Open-conduit volcanoes are characterized by continuous magma supply and persistent degassing, whereas eruptive activity occurs intermittently and is controlled by magma transfer and accumulation processes within the feeding system. At Mt. Etna, temporal variations in peripheral soil CO2 emissions provide a sensitive tracer of deep magma intrusions and can be used to quantify magma inputs into the feeding system. title: ANALISIS DAN OPTIMASI PERFORMA MODEL YOLOV8 DALAM MENDETEKSI DAN MENGHITUNG POPULASI IKAN DI DALAM AIR
abstract: Pemantauan populasi ikan pada keramba jaring apung (KJA) secara manual memakan waktu dan rentan menghasilkan data tidak konsisten. Penelitian ini menguji kemampuan YOLOv8n, varian ringan YOLOv8, untuk mendeteksi dan menghitung ikan otomatis pada KJA di Ambon. title: The Reflection of Conceptual Debates in Ottoman Naval History on High School Curriculum and Teacher Education: A Pedagogical Analysis
abstract: This study aims to examine the conceptual debates in academic Ottoman maritime historiography and their instructional reflections in the 2025 secondary school (10th and 11th grade) History textbooks approved by the Ministry of National Education, alongside History Education undergraduate curricula. title: Introducing a new normalized cryospheric index (NCI) to categorize sub-watersheds on arid environments
abstract: Abstract. This study examines sub-watersheds in the arid northern region of Chile (26°41’–28°24’S), situated within the broader Copiapo watershed. The primary water source for this watershed originates from cryospheric reservoirs. The region exhibits pronounced physiographic and climatic diversity, with its northern sector situated within the South American Arid Diagonal (SAAD), where cryospheric features exhibit greater spatial isolation. title: Molecular shape evolution of cyanobacterial circadian clock protein KaiC
abstract: A primitive form of clock protein KaiC has diverged into autonomous or passive time-measuring system. Here we traced molecular shape evolution of ancestral KaiCs using X-ray solution scattering and structure prediction techniques to date this diversification. The results show that the oldest KaiC emerged approximately 3.5–2.8 billion years ago as a moderately expanded and asymmetric double-ring hexamer, and subsequently evolved over approximately 1 billion years into a compact and symmetric form essential for the self-sustained rhythmicity in extant cyanobacteria. title: Uncovering rainfall dynamics in Pernambuco, Brazil, through innovative polygon trend analysis
abstract: Abstract This study applied the Innovative Polygon Trend Analysis (IPTA) and the Trend Polygon Star Concept (TPSC) to high-resolution precipitation records (1961–2022) across Pernambuco, Brazil, to assess the spatial variability of monthly rainfall trends and transitions. Monthly precipitation totals derived from 820 BR-DWGD grid cells were analyzed to characterize long-term changes in rainfall patterns across the semiarid Sertão, humid Zona da Mata, and transitional Agreste regions. title: Copper Tolerance and Transcriptomic Response After Prolonged Cu2+ Exposure in the Antarctic Psychrophile Rhodoglobus galactosidasius Strain CPHL_1T
abstract: Abstract The Antarctic psychrophilic actinomycete Rhodoglobus galactosidasius strain CPHL_1 T was investigated to characterize its physiological and transcriptional responses after prolonged copper exposure. Although copper is an essential trace element for microbial metabolism, it becomes toxic when cellular homeostasis is disrupted. While copper resistance mechanisms have been extensively studied in model bacteria, the responses of poorly characterized microorganisms to sustained copper stress remain comparatively underexplored. title: A hybrid MCDM approach for site selection of electric vehicle battery swapping station
abstract: A promising strategy for decarbonising the transportation segment, both commercial and domestic, is based on transitioning from traditional to electric mobility, which is dependent on the Electric Vehicle (EV), their adoption is hindered by range anxiety, insufficient charging infrastructure, and long waiting times. This research aims to commission a battery swapping station (BSS) at a significant location selected through a data-driven hybrid Multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) technique to satisfy the urban sustainable mobility needs while minimising charging congestion. title: Europium Oxide Disrupts Metabolic Homeostasis and Antioxidant Defenses in African Catfish ( Clarias gariepinus ): Integrated Physiological and Molecular Docking Approaches
abstract: ABSTRACT Chemical pollution from rare earth elements (REEs) has emerged as a significant threat to the stability of freshwater ecosystems. Among these elements, europium oxide (Eu 2 O 3 ) is widely used across various industrial sectors; however, its specific impacts on fish physiology, health, and immune function remain poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of Eu 2 O 3 on growth, hepatic markers, intestinal enzyme, systemic immune response, and cytokine expression in African catfish ( Clarias gariepinus ). title: Thiamine availability and uptake in lake trout (Salvelinus namaycush) eggs and embryos: contrasting natural and artificial environments
abstract: Thiamine Deficiency Complex (TDC) is a reproductive disorder that affects recruitment of salmonine populations globally. Symptoms include behavioural and neurological abnormalities and high offspring mortality. TDC has typically been studied in hatcheries that rear embryos obtained from wild populations, and symptoms are mitigated by thiamine treatment. Few studies have evaluated TDC in wild embryos, largely due to logistical challenges. title: Pluvial flood risk assessment and nature-based mitigation in urban environments: a pragmatic Curve Number and Initial Abstraction approach
abstract: Urban pluvial flooding represents a growing threat to contemporary cities, driven by the compounding effects of climate change, rapid urbanization, and inadequate stormwater infrastructure, prompting the study of nature-based solutions (NBS) as potential interventions for mitigating the detrimental effects of urban flooding. Two-dimensional (2D) hydrodynamic assessments of pluvial flood risk and NBS mitigation potential require a detailed description of the urban drainage system that is not always available. title: Assessing agricultural drought intensification and spatiotemporal pattern in the central Rift Valley using multi-source indices
abstract: Drought is a complex and multifaceted phenomenon that includes meteorological, agricultural, hydrological, and socio-economic components. Both single and composite drought indices were used in this study to assess agricultural drought in the East Shewa Zone of Central Ethiopia. The Precipitation Condition Index (PCI), Temperature Condition Index (TCI), Vegetation Condition Index (VCI), and Soil Moisture Condition Index (SMCI) were used as single indices. title: Gradual mitochondrial collapse underlies cytotoxicity induced by a B-type prymnesin-containing Prymnesium parvum extract in rainbow trout gill cells
abstract: Abstract Bioactive secondary metabolites produced by the haptophyte microalga Prymnesium parvum are key mediators of ichthyotoxicity during harmful algal bloom events. In the present study, we investigated the effects of a P. parvum extract containing B-type prymnesins, from an isolate obtained during the 2022 Oder River bloom, on mitochondrial health and cellular homeostasis in the rainbow trout gill epithelial cell line RTgill-W1, a widely used model in aquatic toxicology. title: Touring “Our USA”: Seeing US Empire in the Maps of Ruth Taylor White, 1920–1940
abstract: This article adds to histories of US empire, gender, race, and visual culture by more fully addressing white women’s role in sustaining colonial power through their production of an imperial visual culture between 1920 and 1940. It investigates the maps of a woman cartographer, Ruth Taylor White, across different geographical sites of US empire in the Pacific, Caribbean, and North American continent during a key moment in the history of US empire. title: Manta ray foraging optimization algorithm with dynamic penalty function and chaos switching factor to solve combined economic emission dispatch problem
abstract: The Combined Economic and Emission Dispatch (CEED) problem plays a vital role in balancing energy efficiency and environmental protection. To address its multi-objective characteristics, this paper proposes an improved Manta Ray Foraging Optimization (MRFO) algorithm. It introduces a chaotic switching factor to dynamically regulate the transition between exploration and exploitation phases, thereby enhancing global search capability. title: Comparative Analysis of Nature-Inspired Strategies in Building Engineering: A Multilevel Biomimicry Perspective
abstract: This study investigates the integration of biological strategies into building systems and engineering through a multilevel biomimicry perspective. A systematic evaluation framework is established, categorizing biomimicry into two approaches (problem-oriented and solution-oriented), three levels (organism, behavior, and ecosystem), and five imitation dimensions: form, material, construction, process, and function. title: A longitudinal analysis of diet quality, groundwater depletion and glacier thicknesses with implications for the sustainable development goal 2
abstract: Abstract The United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 2 (SDG) underscores the need for eliminating hunger, improving nutrition, and promoting sustainable agriculture. For achieving SDG2, it is critical to address several factors such as agricultural production, groundwater depletion, and glacier decline under climate change. title: Non-Excessive Natural Resource Use and Sustainable Development: The Indigenous Environmental Wisdom of Lubuk Larangan
abstract: Sustainable development has guided global environmental governance for nearly four decades, yet continuing environmental degradation indicates persistent limitations in its implementation. This article examines whether clearer normative limits on natural resource use can strengthen sustainable development. It explores the Indonesian customary institution of Lubuk Larangan and identifies the principles of non-excessive utilization, sufficiency, and simplicity embedded in its Indigenous environmental wisdom. publisher: Cardinal Stefan Wyszynski University in Warsaw

title: Sustainable Freight Transportation via Inland Waterways: Challenges and Strategic Solutions in Bangladesh
abstract: Inland water transport (IWT) is crucial for socio-economic development, facilitating rural connectivity, trade logistics, energy provision and tourism. Nevertheless, it is neglected due to historical underinvestment, inadequate infrastructure and regulatory inefficiencies in Bangladesh. This study evaluates the current state of freight movement via inland waterways, identifies key challenges and proposes strategies to improve sustainability. abstract: Pelayanan administrasi desa yang masih dilakukan secara manual sering menimbulkan berbagai permasalahan seperti keterlambatan pelayanan, antrean masyarakat, dan kesulitan pengelolaan data administrasi. Untuk mengatasi permasalahan tersebut, dikembangkan aplikasi pelayanan administrasi Desa Wargasara berbasis mobile menggunakan Flutter dan Laravel 12. title: Analysis of urban heat islands in the study of urban environmental problems based on remote sensing
abstract: As global urbanization accelerates cities increasingly face ecological challenges, most notably the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect. This study investigates the formation and spatial distribution of UHI’s in the cities of Mingachevir, Shirvan and Yevlakh, located in the central region of the Republic of Azerbaijan. Utilizing ArcGIS, the analysis processed Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS satellite imagery from August 2023. title: First record of Phlebotomus sergenti (Diptera: Psychodidae) in China and its potential epidemiological implications
abstract: BACKGROUND: Leishmaniasis is a severe parasitic disease transmitted by sand fly bites. Phlebotomus sergenti is a principal vector of Leishmania tropica, causing anthroponotic cutaneous leishmaniasis (ACL) across the Mediterranean, North Africa, South Asia, and West Asia. The Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, located in northwestern China, is a well-recognized endemic focus of visceral leishmaniasis (VL), with sporadic cutaneous leishmaniasis cases also documented in the region. title: Bromide-mediated enhancement of far-UVC/peracetic acid process for selective micropollutant abatement
abstract: Abstract Far‑ultraviolet 222 nm (UV 222 ) effectively activates oxidants to degrade organic micropollutants (OMPs) in advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), but its synergy and ecotoxicity with bromide (Br − ) are unclear. This study investigates the synergy of peracetic acid (PAA) and Br − by UV 222 (UV 222 -PB) for OMPs degradation.
