title: How Wisconsin Extension Educators Talk About Climate Change Without Talking About ``Climate Change''
abstract: Climate change touches all areas of Extension's programming. To understand how educators approach talking about climate change with constituents, we interviewed 15 Extension educators and three program managers in Wisconsin. Crops and Soils educators view climate change as interwoven with their work, Financial Education educators view it as mostly disconnected, and Community Economic Development educators range between these extremes. title: Assessing the use of inland wetlands by fishes in the Lower Tagus Basin, Portugal
abstract: Although inland wetlands are among the most important and impacted biodiversity hotspots worldwide, they remain poorly assessed. This is particularly concerning in regions harboring endangered endemic species and facing strong anthropogenic pressures, such as the Lower Tagus Basin in Portugal. Here we aimed to assess the use of inland wetlands in the Lower Tagus basin by native and non-native fishes and examine the environmental factors influencing community structure. title: Comparison of Environmental Signals Between Contemporary and Subfossil Cladocera (Crustacea) Assemblages: A Case Study of Shallow Urban Ponds
abstract: ABSTRACT Cladocera are an important component of freshwater zooplankton and serve as proxies in paleoecological reconstructions. However, the similarity of environmental signals reflected in the dominant species structure of contemporary (CC) and subfossil (SC) cladoceran communities remains an open question. The objective of this study is to assess how changes in the dominant species structure of SC correlate with those in CC and with corresponding environmental conditions in artificial ponds. title: Deer disturbance influences avian acoustic activity across functional groups in temperate forests
abstract: Cervid overpopulation is increasingly altering temperate forest ecosystems worldwide, when browsing pressure exceeds ecosystem resilience, with consequences that extend beyond individual species to the structure and functioning of entire communities. While the impacts of deer ( Cervidae ) on specific bird species are well studied, there remains a critical gap in understanding how deer influence avian communities across a spectrum of functional traits. title: Mass movements in the southern Black Forest, Germany
abstract: Despite their importance as geomorphological processes and natural hazards, systematic inventories of mass movements remain limited for many Central European mid-mountain ranges. This study presents an inventory map of mass movements in the southern Black Forest (Germany), on the area of the Late Pleistocene Feldberg glaciation. High-resolution digital elevation models combined with field surveys were used to map and classify mass movements. Potential preconditioning factors (aspect, slope angle, lithology) were analysed. abstract: This study provides a comprehensive assessment of scour processes in the Santa Eulalia River, Peru, considering projected climate scenarios for 2050. Hydrological and hydraulic modeling was conducted using Hydrologic Engineering Center–Hydrologic Modeling System (HEC-HMS) and Hydrologic Engineering Center–River Analysis System (HEC-RAS) to estimate design peak discharges and corresponding flow depths for 10- to 140-year return periods. abstract: Three agricultural farms in Lokoja, Kogi State, Nigeria - Federal University Lokoja (FUL), Kogi State Polytechnic (KSP), and the Kogi State Ministry of Agriculture (KSM) - were the subjects of this study, which created a baseline evaluation of the soil micronutrient status. title: Wolbachia infection and its effects on mitochondrial ND5 gene variation in Aedes albopictus from Shandong Province
abstract: Introduction Wolbachia , a matrilineally inherited endosymbiont, has the potential to influence host mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) diversity through cytoplasmic hitchhiking and selective sweeps. Aedes albopictus naturally harbors Wolbachia , making it an ideal model for studying host-symbiont interactions. title: Isolation, identification and immuno-pathogenesis of snakehead rhabdovirus-Indian strain (SHRV-In) in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
abstract: Snakehead rhabdovirus (SHRV-In) is the most potentially destructive pathogen of snakehead, capable of causing up to 100% mortality within five days. The present study aimed to screen freshwater fishes in Tamil Nadu for the occurrence of SHRV-In and to assess its immuno-pathogenesis potential in Nile tilapia. abstract: Recent experiments in monolayer and trilayer graphene have observed incompressible even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states within narrow regions of parameter space associated with crossings of zeroth Landau levels. title: Assessment of sky brightness in central Portugal: the Dark Sky destination "Aldeias do Xisto" case study
abstract: A combination of remote sensing techniques, open space data and field testing was developed to derive astronomical and meteorological parameters and assess Dark Sky brightness of the hitherto unstudied Schist Villages region in the mountainous Interior Center of Portugal. This study covered the period 2012-2017 and established the methodology for regular light pollution and sky brightness studies in the region using satellite imagery to reduce cost and time and increase accuracy of the final analysis. title: FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution
abstract: LLM-guided evolutionary methods, such as AlphaEvolve, have emerged as powerful approaches for challenging computational optimization problems, such as circle packing. abstract: Automated snow depth retrieval from time-lapse cameras is constrained by site-specific annotation and manual image quality screening, thus limiting scalability across deployments. We present a fully automated, zero-annotation pipeline that integrates text-prompted segmentation for snow pole detection with a vision language model for image quality control. title: Faker Island: Profiling misinformation sharers on the French Twittersphere
abstract: What are the distinctive characteristics of misinformation sharers? So far, most studies have focused on the U.S., a two-party system with a highly polarized media landscape, leaving open the question of what misinformation sharers look like in other socio-political contexts. Research has also prioritized testing causal links between cognitive or political variables and misinformation sharing, while paying less attention to fine-grained descriptions of who these users are. abstract: The Socotra bluet (Azuragrion granti) is an endemic, Near Threatened damselfly restricted to the Socotra Archipelago whose persistence depends on scarce freshwater refugia under a changing climate. abstract: Urban neighborhoods used to be fairly straightforward—residential here, commercial there. That is less and less true, and planners need ways to keep up. abstract: This mixed-method multiple-case study evaluates climate-adaptive design in three transport terminals in Lagos State: CMS Ferry Terminal, Oshodi Bus Terminal, and Five Cowries Ferry Terminal, and translates the findings into a design framework for futurecoastal transport infrastructure. abstract: Background: The first five years of a child’s life are essential for growth. abstract: Abstract. Accurate beam pointing is essential for vertically pointing cloud radars, as even small tilting off zenith introduces projections of horizontal wind into Doppler velocity measurements. abstract: Abstract Fish-killing harmful algal blooms (HABs) continue to inflict severe economic losses on marine aquaculture worldwide, yet monitoring systems designed around microalgal cell counts frequently fail to anticipate acute mortality events. The dominant surveillance paradigm was inherited from shellfish-toxin monitoring, where a filter-feeding bivalve integrates exposure to intracellular phycotoxins and toxin burden in tissue triggers regulatory action. title: Dietary exposure to toxic trace elements through soybean oil consumption in Bangladesh and associated health risks
abstract: Toxic trace elements in edible oils pose public health risks because of their persistence, bioaccumulation, and, for some elements, carcinogenic potential. This study quantified Pb, Cd, Cr, As, Hg, Mn, Ni, and Cu in 21 commercially available soybean oil samples collected from Dhaka, Bangladesh. abstract: The present overview raises questions regarding the degree of regulation of educational network cooperation between domestic and foreign universities. abstract: Access to safe and reliable water remains a persistent challenge for rural communities in Malaysia, where infrastructural limitations, spatial constraints, and governance fragmentation continue to undermine water security. While technological solutions have been widely promoted, their long-term effectiveness in rural contexts is often constrained by limited community ownership and weak institutional coordination. abstract: Background. Ginger is a horticultural commodity and a biopharmaceutical crop with many benefits and high economic value. Ginger is widely used as a raw material in the functional food, cosmetics, and herbal pharmaceutical industries. Water content is a critical parameter affecting the quality, storage stability, and activity of bioactive compounds in ginger rhizomes. Purpose. abstract: The continued spread of invasive species represents a major threat to biodiversity and ecosystem functioning, yet the extent to which invasive species are approaching spatial saturation remains poorly understood. abstract: Crucian carp ( Carassius carassius ) has declined across much of Europe and is listed as critically endangered in the Czech Republic. Main obstacles are assembling training labels at national scale without extensive manual annotation and obtaining reference data sufficiently independent of the mapping process to support credible accuracy assessment. abstract: This article examines conflict dynamics in the Arctic using a framework that includes the state, regional, and systemic (international) analysis levels. abstract: Abstract Stable isotope analyses of faunal remains have demonstrated significant potential to enhance understandings of human-animal relationships during periods of European colonization. abstract: Abstract Emerging water pollutants such as pharmaceutical (PhACs) and microplastics (MPs) are progressively detected in aquatic environments, raising alarms about their mutual toxicological effects on non-target biota, particularly fish. abstract: Niche diplomacy is a notable characteristic of the foreign policy of middle powers - states that have the capacity to play a prominent role on the international stage, but are not powerful enough to impose their will on others. abstract: Climate change is altering microbial ecosystems at a global scale, yet the role of free-living amoebae within these shifting microbiomes remains incompletely understood. Free-living amoebae occupy soil, water, air, and built environments, where they contribute to microbial diversity, regulate nutrient cycling, and host diverse bacterial, fungal, and viral microorganisms. abstract: Oil plays a significant role in the Brazilian and global energy matrices. Brazilian oil production is predominantly offshore, particularly in pre-salt fields. abstract: Ship recycling plays a central role in the circular economy of the maritime industry, yet significant disparities persist in safety, environmental performance, and regulatory compliance across global Ship Recycling Facilities (SRFs). abstract: Polymeric tea bags act as dynamic vectors for micro-particle shedding and chemical leaching, raising public health concerns as global tea consumption rises. Along with contributing to terrestrial carbon cycling and food webs, colourful snow algal blooms formed on snow surfaces can substantially reduce albedo and accelerate snowmelt. To enable low-cost, high-precision, noncontact structural plane interpretation, this study targets the southern slope of the Shitoumei No. 1 open-pit coal mine and presents a joint recognition method that integrates unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) close-range photogrammetry with an octree-based adaptive statistical outlier removal (SOR) filter using two-layer locality-sensitive hashing (2 L-LSH). title: Occurrence and seasonal distribution of persistent organic pollutants in air and soil across agricultural urban and industrial landscapes
abstract: Soil represents a major terrestrial reservoir of persistent organic pollutants (POPs) that influence their atmospheric concentrations through volatilization processes. This study examines the distribution, seasonal variability, and air–soil exchange of key organochlorine pesticides (OCPs) (i.e., ΣDDTs, ΣHCHs), and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) in soils and air from industrial, agricultural, and urban areas in three Khyber Pakhtunkhwa cities (Peshawar, Swabi, Haripur), Pakistan. title: Natural Diversity of Grass Pollen in Europe—An EAACI Perspective
abstract: Grass pollen, the most clinically relevant outdoor aeroallergen in Europe and worldwide, presents a complex challenge due to the diverse nature of its subspecies. This diversity complicates the interpretation of their contribution to the overall pollen burden during the grass pollen season and the selection of the appropriate allergen immunotherapy. title: Compound dry-to-wet transitions and intensifying wet-day rainfall in monsoon-exposed Southern Nghe An, Vietnam
abstract: Monsoon rainfall hazards depend on event intensity and sequence, not annual totals alone. We analyzed 8,766 daily observations from four gauges in southern Nghe An during 1998–2021, together with daily 0.05° Climate Hazards Center InfraRed Precipitation with Stations (CHIRPS) rainfall at Nam Dan. Thirteen indices represented amount, wet-day frequency, intensity, extremes, and persistence. title: Assessment of trace metal contamination and associated health risks in the Chaliyar river basin, Kerala
abstract: Water sustains life but water resources are degraded by industrial discharges and agricultural runoff in which heavy metals are concerning pollutants. This study focuses on an integrated approach for riverbank soil assessments in the Chaliyar river of Kerala, India using a comprehensive multifactor risk assessment. Thirteen surface water samples and riverbank soils were analysed for heavy metal concentrations (As, Cd, Cr, Cu, Ni, Pb and Zn). abstract: The implementation of the Ballast Water Management Convention (BWMC) is an important instrument in controlling ecological risks due to the movement of aquatic organisms through ship ballast water. Although Indonesia has ratified the BWMC, the effectiveness of its implementation at the port operational level, especially river ports, still requires empirical evaluation. This study aims to evaluate the implementation of the BWMC at Samarinda Port by examining the level of technical and regulatory compliance of calling ships. title: CoRSEER: the calculator of rock surface exposure age and erosion rates for luminescence rock surface exposure dating
abstract: Abstract. Rock-surface luminescence dating estimates the duration of rock surface exposure and the rate of erosion by analysing changes in luminescence with depth below the surface. The wider use of this method has been slowed by three practical issues: the subjective selection of the deep plateau for profile normalisation, inconsistent modelling choices across studies, and the lack of a unified inverse-modelling workflow that delivers both parameter estimates and uncertainty bounds. title: Transportation Safety, and Supply Chain Resilience in Road-Based Crude Oil Logistics: Evidence from a Conflict‐Affected Region
abstract: Abstract Crude oil transport is a vital component of global energy supply chains; however, it is riddled with systemic risks, including human error, infrastructure fragility, security vulnerabilities, and regulatory deficiencies. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of crude oil transport, with particular emphasis on the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRG), a semi-autonomous territory that has emerged as a significant oil producer despite enduring geopolitical instability. title: Non-sewered sanitation systems reshape microplastics into chemically complex and reactive contaminants
abstract: Non-sewered sanitation systems (NSSSs) are gaining global attention as decentralized solutions, yet the transformation of microplastics (MPs) within these systems remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate MP characteristics in the influent and effluent of two NSSSs using laser direct infrared spectroscopy, Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS), and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). title: Spatial And Temporal Assessment of Atmospheric Nitrogen Using Hypnum Cupressiforme Mosses and Kjeldahl Analysis
abstract: This study aimed to explore the experiences of Palestinian Nitrogen content in mosses was investigated in a semi-rural area in Lebanon. CALPUFF dispersion model was used to estimate the annual average NOx and NH3 concentrations. Three sampling campaigns were conducted over the course of a year where 33 samples of the moss Hypnum cupressiforme were collected during each campaign. Kjeldahl method was used to determine the total nitrogen content in the collected samples.

title: Quantifying metal transferability in soil and its relationship to metal-related health risks in the strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa)-human food chain
abstract: Understanding metal transfer in soil-strawberry systems is indispensable for sustainable strawberry production. To date, much attention has been paid to metals in strawberries, while metal transferability in strawberry-growing soil has been ignored. title: Groundwater sustainability in hard rock terrains and related health risks assessment in semi-urban Nigeria
abstract: Ten representative groundwater samples were randomly collected from public hand dug wells in the Igarra Town and analyzed to assess their quality for drinking purpose and associated health risks following established methodological standards. The results revealed that pH values ranged from 5.25-6.63, indicating slightly to moderately acidic conditions and deviation from World Health Organization (WHO) and Nigeria drinking water standards (NSDWQ). title: A STUDY OF UNIVERSITY STUDENTS' SEAFOOD CONSUMPTION BEHAVIOR: SOCIO- ECONOMIC FACTORS AND CONSUMPTION TRENDS
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the seafood consumption behaviors of university students and the factors influencing these behaviors. The study was conducted with 118 students, and the relationships between consumption frequency, reasons for consumption, reasons for non-consumption, purchasing preferences, and demographic variables were analyzed. The findings revealed that students generally consumed seafood rarely or only 1–2 times per month. title: Pedological and geochemical characteristics of highly weathered soils derived from ophiolitic rocks in Samar, Philippines
abstract: Limited information is available on the pedology of highly weathered soils derived from ophiolitic rocks in the Philippines. This study evaluated red, highly weathered soils across the ophiolitic landscape of Eastern Samar. Five soil profiles were described and sampled for laboratory analysis. The geochemical composition of the parent materials ranged from mafic to ultramafic. abstract: SThe application of live probiotics in food preservation is often limited by the risk of horizontal gene transfer. In this study, cell-free supernatant (CFS) from Lactobacillus johnsonii KD1 was characterized for its antimicrobial efficacy through minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) assays against Vibrio parahaemolyticus, Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium, and Listeria monocytogenes . title: Localization in the internet of things based on game theory with applications in the healthcare
abstract: Accurate indoor localization is critical for healthcare Internet of Things (IoT) applications such as patient tracking and asset management. However, maintaining localization accuracy under node mobility, signal attenuation, and faulty or adversarial behaviors remains challenging. Existing schemes either assume benign environments or employ rigid filters that permanently exclude noisy nodes, causing unacceptable losses in patient monitoring coverage. title: Development of a Jamʿ al-Āyāt Procedure in Mawḍūʿī Tafsir: An Integrated Model of Syntagmatic Analysis, Tafsir Verification, and Corpus Selection
abstract: Verse collection (jamʿ al-āyāt) is the second of seven steps in al-Farmāwī's mawḍūʿī tafsir, but the step does not specify how the thematic relevance of an individual candidate verse is to be assessed once it has been identified. This article develops a four-stage procedure — textual and syntagmatic analysis, preliminary thematic evaluation, tafsir verification, and synthesis and position determination — that operationalizes this step while keeping it within al-Farmāwī's seven-step framework. title: The investor gaze: recognition heuristic, social liability and legal disillusionment among foreign tourism entrepreneurs on Sri Lanka's southern coast
abstract: This study examines investment failures among foreign visitors and tourism entrepreneurs on Sri Lanka’s southern coast, exploring what can go wrong after tourism-related familiarity encourages investment. It introduces the “investor gaze” as the epistemic position emerging when tourists become resident investors, distinguishing it from familiarity-based confidence and “substitutional collapse,” a specific failure mechanism. title: Turning data into green action: how the environmental value of digitalization emerges in maritime supply chains
abstract: As digital transformation accelerates and environmental regulations become more stringent, increasing attention has been paid to how maritime firms translate digital resources into environmental value. Drawing on organizational information processing theory and the natural resource-based view, this study develops a multistage model to examine the relationship between supply chain digitalization and environmental performance. title: Muslim-Friendly Tourism Facilities, Tourism Services, and Government Support as Determinants of Indonesian-Tourist Visit Intensity
abstract: The growth of halal tourism underscores the need to understand tourist behavior in multicultural destinations. This study contributes to halal tourism literature by examining how Muslim-friendly facilities, tourism service quality, and government support influence tourist visit intensity in Singkawang, Indonesia, a culturally diverse destination. Grounded in Demand Theory, Customer Satisfaction Theory, and the Theory of Planned Behavior, the study employed a quantitative design involving 550 Muslim tourists with at least two prior visits. title: Beyond single-element toxicity: chromium-salinity interactions, food-chain transfer and mitigation in sugarcane agroecosystems
abstract: Chromium contamination in sugarcane soils is often combined with co-metals and salinity caused by tannery effluent, electroplating effluent, paper mill wastewater, vinasse fertigation and filter cake. Hence, single element toxicity assessment does not provide realistic assessment of its exposure. The present review summarizes research on chromium behaviour along the soil, root, stalk and cane juice in sugarcane. title: A comparison of consumer preferences for cell-based seafood across European countries
abstract: Global seafood consumption has been increasing and is expected to continue rising, driven by population growth and evolving dietary patterns. Cell-based seafood has the potential to complement capture fisheries and aquaculture in meeting this growing demand. However, the long-term viability of this emerging sector will depend largely on consumer acceptance. This study examines consumer preferences and acceptance of cell-based seafood in four European countries—Italy, the Netherlands, Portugal, and Hungary. title: Technical–ethical–governance circuit–breaker framework for safe and sustainable AI governance
abstract: The growing use of large language models and autonomous AI systems in high-risk settings has created safety risks that cannot be addressed through technical safeguards alone. Existing approaches often treat technical failure control, ethical oversight, and institutional governance as separate domains, making coordinated intervention difficult when risks escalate across these boundaries. This study proposes the technical–ethical–governance (TEG) framework as an integrated circuit-breaker architecture for managing risks in high-risk AI systems. title: Crude Oil Theft and Environmental Degradation in Oil-Producing Communities of Rivers State, Nigeria: Evidence from Bodo And Rumuekpe
abstract: This study examines crude oil theft as a direct driver of environmental degradation in Bodo (Gokana LGA) and Rumuekpe (Emuoha LGA), two oil-producing communities in Rivers State, Nigeria, using a descriptive survey design anchored on Strain Theory, Resource Curse Theory, and Environmental Justice Theory. Two communities were purposively selected for their contrasting exposure profiles; within them, 200 respondents were drawn through stratified random sampling across six occupational categories. title: Beyond cichlid diversification: environmental drivers of biodiversity across the Nicaraguan lake system
abstract: Abstract The Nicaraguan lake system, comprising two Great Lakes and several isolated crater lakes, is a natural laboratory for investigating how environmental heterogeneity and isolation shape biodiversity and a classic model for Midas cichlid diversification. We asked whether lake characteristics associated with cichlid diversification are also linked to prokaryotic and eukaryotic diversity patterns. title: Locking Down Science Gateways with Landlock and Seccomp
abstract: Abstract The most recent Linux kernels have a new feature for securing applications: Landlock. Like Seccomp before it, Landlock makes it possible for a running process to selectively relinquish access to certain system resources including network and filesystem access. Rather than being a proper successor to Seccomp, Landlock has different and somewhat complementary capabilities. title: A validation framework for translating ethnomicrobiology into microbiome-enabled desert restoration
abstract: Microbiome-based dryland restoration is promising but weakly validated. We develop ethnomicrobiology, the study of how human communities manage microbial processes, as a discovery-and-validation framework. A structured evidence map of 42 systems shows food fermentation is most mature, whereas restoration practices lag. We propose a five-level evidence-maturity ladder, from traditional observation to governed field deployment, and apply it to waste-biomass valorization, converting traditional practices into mechanistically tested, ethically governed restoration interventions.

title: Combined effects of brewer’s spent grain biostimulation and Bacillus bioaugmentation on crude oil biodegradation in contaminated soil
abstract: Abstract Background Petroleum hydrocarbon contamination is a major environmental challenge because of its persistence and adverse effects on soil quality and ecosystem functioning. This study evaluated the combined effects of brewer’s spent grain (BSG) biostimulation and Bacillus bioaugmentation on crude oil biodegradation in contaminated soil. abstract: Health tourism (HT) is an umbrella domain encompassing medical tourism and wellness tourism. While these subdomains have developed substantial research, service models increasingly connect hospitals, clinics, hotels, resorts, and wellness providers, creating overlaps between healthcare, hospitality, and travel. This study uses innovation to connect these subdomains and explain the development of HT and identify future directions. abstract: Abstract Rainfall runoff can activate non-point source pollution and generate short-term water-quality anomalies in plateau lake basins, but event-scale multi-indicator responses remain difficult to identify using conventional mean-based assessments. Here, continuous water-quality records from the Lake Center, Jiangwei, Xiaoguanyi, and Jinhe sections of Erhai Lake from June 2021 to December 2024 were combined with daily precipitation data to identify 127 rainfall events. title: Combination of instrumental and biomonitoring approaches elucidate the contributions of multiple and contrasted sources of atmospheric exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons
abstract: A combined approach was implemented to investigate the origins of elevated PAH concentrations in a complex urban environment where numerous emission sources coexist. This approach integrated one year of atmospheric measurements PM10 filters and continuous atmospheric monitoring), alongside lichen biomonitoring and soil analyses. title: SYSTEM FOR LAND-BASED EMISSIONS ESTIMATION IN KENYA(SLEEK) AND LAND-SECTOR CARBON ACCOUNTING IN KENYA: EVIDENCE FROM EMISSIONS AND REMOVALS ACCOUNTING, 1990-2015
abstract: Developing countries face persistent constraints in producing transparent, consistent and nationally owned greenhouse-gas inventories for the land sector. Kenya responded through the System for Land-based Emissions Estimation in Kenya (SLEEK), a national programme designed to integrate activity data, country-specific parameters, spatial modelling, reporting tools and institutional capacity. abstract: Abstract Warm rain is plagued by a longstanding droplet growth bottleneck, one that turbulence may alleviate by enhancing droplet coalescence in the late condensation phase. Here, we combine collocated nationwide millimeter cloud radars, radar wind profilers, Himawari‐8/9 satellite cloud‐top temperature retrievals, and surface gauges to compile 819 warm rain events over China during the warm seasons of 2024–2025. title: Memorandum: corrosion protection in structural engineering
abstract: This educational position paper proposes a competence-based reference framework for corrosion protection in structural engineering. It organizes corrosion-related learning objectives across the structural life cycle, links them to the six cognitive processes of the revised Bloom taxonomy, and distinguishes Bachelor, Master, professional practice, and research pathways. abstract: Abstract Urban rivers receive substantial organic matter and nutrients, but seasonal changes in their microbial communities remain poorly understood. In this study, water and sediment samples were collected from four urban rivers in Changzhou during winter and summer. 16S rDNA, ITS amplicon sequencing and metagenomic analysis were used to characterize microbial composition and its functional potential. abstract: Large dam vibrations will be assessed by using a sensor network as part of the proposed protocol. The other main components of the proposed protocol are dual-threshold selective reporting and structurally-based clustering methods which provide for nodes to report only vibration readings that have deviated from what is normal operationally; all vibration readings need not be reported. abstract: The growing demand for self-powered systems in distributed sensing, Internet-of-Things devices, and structural health monitoring has stimulated increasing interest in flow-induced piezoelectric energy harvesting. By converting flow-driven vibrations into electrical energy, piezoelectric harvesters offer a promising route toward maintenance-light and energy-autonomous operation in environments where battery replacement is inconvenient or impractical. abstract: The transition from conchocelis to conchosporangial branches is not only a key stage in the life cycle of Pyropia/Porphyra but also directly affects the yield and quality of economically important species such as Pyropia haitanensis . However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the maturation of P. haitanensis filaments remain poorly understood. title: Assessment of post-construction quality of projects: cases from Sinja valley of Nepal
abstract: Post-construction quality determines whether public investment is converted into durable and usable service, yet small public works in remote mountain municipalities of Nepal are rarely assessed after handover. This study assesses the post-construction quality of completed projects in Sinja Valley of Jumla district, Karnali Province. abstract: The cultivation of Stropharia rugosoannulata involves substantial organic substrate input and fungal mycelial activity, which may influence soil nutrient transformation, microbial communities and functional gene profiles. abstract: This study was conducted to determine the effect of the implementation of the occupational safety and health management system (SMK3) on employee work productivity at KSOP Utama Makassar. title: Ética y bioética en el Laboratorio Clínico: una revisión narrativa
abstract: En la actualidad, los dilemas éticos y bioéticos existen en todos los ámbitos, especialmente en los laboratorios clínicos. title: Changes in arbovirus risks and responses from 2020 to 2026
abstract: Abstract Since 2020, viruses spread by mosquitoes and biting midges have become a larger and less predictable public health challenge. Dengue continues to cause the greatest burden, but chikungunya, Oropouche, and other viruses are re-emerging or spreading into new areas. In this narrative review, we summarize major changes in arbovirus epidemiology, surveillance, diagnosis, vaccination, treatment, vector ecology, and mosquito control from 2020 to 2026. title: Bioash amendments from biomass energy systems reshape rhizosphere bacterial communities and reduce metal bioavailability in contaminated soils
abstract: Biomass-derived ashes (bioash) from energy production are increasingly promoted within circular bioeconomy frameworks as soil amendments that recycle nutrients and mitigate soil acidity. However, their impacts on rhizosphere bacterial communities in metal-contaminated soils (MCS) remain poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Bats are hosts to diverse zoonotic viruses which can cause high case fatality rates in humans. Since detecting viruses in bats is difficult, antibodies are often used for surveillance, though their significance remains unclear in the absence of in vivo immunological studies. title: A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
abstract: Adaptive radiations provide powerful models to study the origins of phenotypic novelty and species diversity. Darwin's finches constitute a classic example of adaptive radiation, in which beak morphology is a key trait related to fitness. Here, we focus on Camarhynchus tree finches by analyzing whole genomes in combination with morphological data to revisit long-standing questions regarding their origins raised before genetic evidence became available. abstract: Fire detection and monitoring are essential for mitigating the environmental and societal impacts of wildfire events. Earth Observation (EO) satellites have long played a central role in this domain, with polar-orbiting sensors such as MODIS and VIIRS providing global fire detections twice daily. However, their limited revisit frequency constrains the timeliness of fire alerts. title: TREND ANALYSIS ON SEASONAL RAINFALL ONSET, CESSATION, AND LENGTH USING MANN–KENDALL AND SEN’S SLOPE (1995–2025) IN JOS, NIGERIA
abstract: Rainfall seasonality is the most critical climatic factor governing the agro-ecological stability of the Jos Plateau, a highland region in North-Central Nigeria renowned for cultivating high-value crops such as Irish potatoes, tomatoes, and exotic vegetables. This study investigates the temporal trends and variability in rainfall onset, cessation, and rainy season length in Jos over a 31-year period (1995–2025), using high-quality monthly rainfall records from the Nigerian Meteorological Agency Synoptic Station. title: Differential testicular toxicity of deoxynivalenol: insights from juvenile and adult mice
abstract: Deoxynivalenol (DON) is a mycotoxin that contaminates approximately 60% of food worldwide and can impair reproduction. Although puberty represents a critical window of susceptibility to toxic insults, the effects of DON exposure during this period remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the effects of DON on testicular structure, oxidative status, inflammatory responses, and sperm parameters in prepubertal and adult mice. title: Estacionalidad y variabilidad espacial de las lluvias en la Patagonia Austral Continental
abstract: La precipitación es uno de los fenómenos meteorológicos con mayor variabilidad espacial y temporal, y su estacionalidad influye de manera directa en la provisión de servicios ecosistémicos y en la productividad primaria neta de pastizales y cultivos, especialmente en ambientes áridos y semiáridos. En este estudio se analizó la estacionalidad de la precipitación para el período 1995-2014 y su variabilidad espacial y temporal en la Patagonia Austral Continental. Se utilizaron datos mensuales normalizados y reticulados, disponibles en el Banco de Datos Hidrometeorológicos de INTA EEA Santa Cruz.

title: Indigenous Acceptance of Migrants on Sebatik Island at the Indonesia–Malaysia Border
abstract: This study analyzes the host community’s acceptance of migrants in international border areas amid increasing global mobility. Drawing on the concept of social harmony, this study aims to understand the factors shaping local acceptance and the dynamics of interaction between Indigenous peoples and migrants. The research uses a qualitative approach, combining participatory observation and in-depth interviews along the Indonesia–Malaysia border to identify social spaces that facilitate cross-community interactions. title: Antibiotics in aquatic environments: A review of occurrence, fate, ecotoxicity and advanced removal technologies
abstract: Antibiotics are among the most widely distributed contaminants of emerging concern in aquatic systems, entering water from hospital effluent, pharmaceutical manufacturing, livestock production, aquaculture and municipal sewage. Their principal hazard is not acute toxicity but sub-inhibitory selective pressure, which enriches antibiotic resistance genes and drives their horizontal transfer at concentrations of nanograms per litre. title: The Conspiracist and Occultist Origin of the Asia Pacific Imaginary
abstract: The Asia Pacific region, now a vital economic and strategic framework institutionalised in APEC, presupposes an imaginary through which the region can be perceived as a coherent whole. Contrary to widespread assumptions, this paper traces the imaginary not to post-WWII diplomatic developments but to the occultist and conspiracist currents in interwar and wartime Japan. It focuses on the intellectuals of the Sumera group, who perceived Japan as the centre of the world. abstract: Abstract This study investigates the combined effects of geology, land use and land cover, hydrological seasonality, and disturbance history on the hydrogeochemistry of surface waters in the Paraopeba River Basin (PRB), located in Minas Gerais State, southeastern Brazil, and forming part of the São Francisco River Basin, a region characterized by high lithological complexity and intense anthropogenic pressure. title: One health perspectives on pharmaceutical and clinical effluents driving multidrug resistance in aquatic ecosystems: a comprehensive review
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has emerged as one of the most pressing global health challenges, yet the contribution of environmental reservoirs to the spread of multidrug resistance (MDR) remains insufficiently integrated into mainstream discussions. This systematic review synthesizes evidence from 167 peer-reviewed studies published between 2000 and 2026 to examine how pharmaceutical manufacturing effluents and clinical waste drive the dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and multidrug-resistant bacteria in aquatic ecosystems. abstract: This study aimed to investigate whether the degree of polymerization (DP) influences intestinal health benefits of pectic oligosaccharide (POS) in broilers. abstract: The Smart Multi-Species Milk Bank System (SM²BS) is proposed as an integrated digital platform to improve milk supply chain management through cold chain management, digital traceability, and nutritional profiling. This study adopts a qualitative approach involving literature review, observation of milk handling processes, and stakeholder discussions to identify operational challenges and develop a conceptual framework for managing cow, goat, sheep, mare, and buffalo milk. title: A three-year study reveals a strong association between NO2 and COVID-19 in the state of Oklahoma, United States
abstract: Background Air pollution has been linked to adverse COVID-19 outcomes. However, studies of the US to-date have generally focused on the US as a whole or large cities on the east and west coasts. Few studies have considered the Midwest, and no comprehensive study of the four most common gaseous pollutants has considered Oklahoma. Oklahoma, a fossil fuel-dependent state with a relatively high respiratory disease burden, provides a unique context to evaluate pollutant impacts on COVID-19 case numbers. abstract: This study aimed to determine heavy metal contents in the fish of Nguru Local Government Area (LGA), Yobe State, Nigeria, and assess the potential health risks associated with their consumption. The work seeks to enhance public health awareness and promote environmental sustainability in the region. Heavy metals, including Lead, Cadmium, Chromium, Arsenic, and Copper, pose significant threats to aquatic ecosystems and human health. title: Photoaging-driven amplification of polystyrene microplastic toxicity in wheat: physiological and multi-omics insights
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) in agroecosystems displayed phytotoxicity; however, the differential effects of pristine and photoaged MPs remain unclear. Herein, we examined the effects and mechanisms of polystyrene (PS) MPs on wheat ( Triticum aestivum L .) based on pristine and photoaged treatments. abstract: Our research addresses the limited applicability of traditional reliability assessment methods by implementing a hybrid framework for the Branson 2000X AED ultrasonic welding system in mass production. We aimed to align the quantitative technical framework with the causality and financial impacts of identified failures. abstract: Data on microplastics in Central African inland waters remain limited. This study assesses contamination in the surface waters and surficial sediments of four Pool Malebo sites: Maluku, Kinkole, Kingabwa-Baramoto, and Kinsuka, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Sampling was conducted in June 2024, with three independent replicates per site. Water samples were vacuum-filtered, and sediments underwent KOH digestion followed by vacuum filtration. abstract: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is an acute zoonotic disease caused by orthohantaviruses. title: Naming and Shaming to Protect Civilians During Peacekeeping: Lessons from South Sudan
abstract: Abstract What can the United Nations do to strengthen the protection of civilians when it fails? When missions struggle to protect civilians, high‐level naming and shaming of non‐responsive units within the operation can occur to reorient the operation. Shaming helps rehabilitate the operation and achieve the protection of civilians. title: Ferroptosis Regulates the Biofilm Formation and Antifungal Drug Resistance of Candida albicans
abstract: Objectives Candida albicans ( C. albicans ) biofilm serves as a major cause of Candida-related infections. However, the available antifungal agents are limited in variety, and the emergence of drug resistance has complicated clinical treatment. Ferroptosis shows promise as a novel therapeutic strategy for combating fungal infections. This study aimed to investigate the effects of ferroptosis on the biofilm formation of C. albicans , as well as its susceptibility to antifungal agents. abstract: Abstract Layer melt crystallization (LMC) is a promising green separation technology for ultrahigh‐purity chemical production, particularly for challenging isomeric mixtures. This work develops an experimentally validated semi‐analytical framework for static LMC, integrating spatiotemporal temperature modeling, heat‐flux decomposition, crystal growth kinetics, interfacial solute partitioning, and three‐dimensional impurity‐field simulation. abstract: When Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae described a Chinese move against Taiwan as a threat to Japan’s survival within weeks of taking office in late 2025, the remark was widely read as a gaffe. This article asks whether the aggression in Takaichi’s discourse is an isolated incident or a recurring pattern, and whose interest that pattern serves. abstract: Acrossocheilus fasciatus is an economically important freshwater fish species in China. In recent years, Citrobacter freundii infection has caused significant harm to the aquaculture industry. In this study, we performed histological observation and RNA-seq analysis of the intestines and spleens of control (CK) and C. freundii infected A. fasciatus (EG). abstract: Abstract Most biological control programmes against invasive alien plants (weeds) utilise agents collected from indigenous populations of the target weed that are thought to have a long coevolution history between the target weed and the agent. These biocontrol agents are referred to as old associations. There are, however, several examples of cactus weeds being successfully controlled by new associations, which are agents collected on other cactus species rather than the target weed itself and are thought to lack any significant coevolutionary history with the target weed. title: Population genetic data for 23 STR loci of the Miskito ethnic group in Honduras
abstract: The Miskito constitute Honduras’s largest indigenous population (~ 80,000 individuals), yet population-specific genetic databases essential for accurate forensic analysis remain unavailable. Allele frequencies for 23 autosomal short tandem repeat loci were determined from 100 unrelated Miskito individuals (52 females, 48 males) from four settlements in Gracias a Dios department. abstract: Fruits such as cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarponAiton), that contain several phenolic substances, are processed commercially as juices, requiring treatments to extend shelf-life. Thermo-sonication, the synergistic application of mild heat and ultrasound, is a promising non-thermal liquid foods processing technology. abstract: Plastic-waste combustion in small-scale food production may create particle-rich environments with potential for deposition onto exposed foods, yet paired environmental–food evidence remains limited. This cross-sectional study quantified atmospheric particle deposition and anthropogenic microparticles in tofu at 11 plastic-waste-fueled sites in Tropodo Village, Sidoarjo, Indonesia. abstract: 1. Phylogenetic comparative methods require species names in a trait dataset to match tip labels in a phylogenetic tree. Yet this apparently simple prerequisite is often one of the most fragile steps in a comparative workflow. Names may differ because of, for example, formatting, taxonomic revisions, synonyms, or spelling errors. abstract: Cold food chain logistics plays an important social role in maintaining the quality and safety of perishable products and ensuring the sustainability of supply chains. The purpose of the study is to identify the dynamics of development, thematic structure, and promising areas of scientific research in the field of logistics and management of the cold food chain. abstract: Abstract This study presents TSI-AsphaLab , an open-source software developed to calibrate and simulate the Thermo-Stiffness Integration (TSI) model. Based on thermodynamics concepts and the time-temperature superposition principle, the TSI model accurately represents the stiffness modulus of asphalt mixtures along a wide range of loading conditions (i.e., frequency and temperature) without requiring shift factors. abstract: Jatropha curcas L. (locally known as “duduk” in East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia) has traditionally been used as an anti-inflammatory agent. This study aimed to formulate and evaluate the physical stability and anti-inflammatory activity of a topical gel containing standardized ethanolic leaf extract of J. curcas using carbomer 940. abstract: The study aimed to assess the availability and utilization of resources for implementing mothertongue medium education in the Universal Basic Education (UBE) program in Bayelsa State, Nigeria. Four research questions were formulated, and two null hypotheses were tested at a 0.05 significance level. abstract: Many of the most challenging decisions facing natural resource managers today can be understood as time dependent. The concept of time-dependent decisions is useful when considering natural resource management decisions that are characterized by nonstationarity in the underlying ecological system, uncertainty surrounding key ecological relationships, efficacy of management interventions, and difficult trade-offs between the present and the future. abstract: This study evaluates potential cultural ecosystem service (CES) supply, potential demand and modelled least-cost accessibility pathways across Jiangsu Province on a common 1 km grid for 2014, 2019 and 2020. Nine indicators are organised into a six-indicator supply block and a three-indicator demand block. After direction adjustment and min-max standardisation on the common valid-cell mask, entropy-derived within-dimension weights are normalised to sum to one and the supply and demand blocks are each assigned an equal block weight of 0.5 before the relative supply-demand balance is calculated.

abstract: Introduction Regurgitation and reingestion (R&R) is a widely observed, yet poorly understood, abnormal ingestive behavior among zoo-housed apes, including gorillas. While frequently characterized as a stereotypical behavior, emerging hypotheses suggest R&R may serve metabolic or self-regulatory functions in response to altered feeding patterns in captivity. abstract: Contributing to the burgeoning interdisciplinary literature on affective and emotional governance of borders, this paper explores recently emerging strands of affective border governance literature to contextualize Middle Eastern borders. This contextualization highlights areas where Middle Eastern border studies are developed and where they remain underdeveloped in relation to the affective governance of borders. abstract: ABSTRACT Established under the Disability Inclusion Act 2014 (NSW), Disability Inclusion Action Plans (DIAPs) are public accountability instruments through which New South Wales (NSW) councils translate statutory disability inclusion obligations into place‐based inclusion planning. Many of the local environments, services and systems through which inclusion is experienced fall within council responsibilities. abstract: Many animal species replace histones with protamines during spermatogenesis. Although essential for sperm function, protamines evolve rapidly for reasons that remain unknown. title: LSD treatment affects working memory-related brain function in patients with major depressive disorder
abstract: Abstract Classic psychedelics, including lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), are currently under investigation for the treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD). Cognitive dysfunction is common in MDD, but effects of psychedelic treatment on cognitive brain function, measured by magnetic resonance imaging, are sparsely reported. The present study investigated effects of LSD treatment on working memory-related brain function in patients with MDD. title: Geofysiske anvendelser af satellitaltimetri
abstract: Artiklen demonstrerer, hvordan præcise højdemålinger fra satellitter anvendes til at bestemme havniveauvariationer og dermed geofysiske processer. Skourup gennemgår de fysiske principper bag radaraltimetri, signalrefleksion og korrektioner for atmosfæriske effekter. Artiklen illustrerer, hvordan præcisionsmålinger i centimeterklassen muliggør analyse af globale dynamiske systemer. title: Ultraconserved element phylogenomics reveals novel insights into the historical biogeography of euophryine jumping spiders (Araneae: Salticidae)
abstract: The Euophryini is one of the largest tribes of jumping spiders (Salticidae), with diverse morphology, ecology and behaviour, and is an important focus of systematic and evolutionary studies of jumping spiders. Notably, it is the only salticid tribe that has diversified nearly equally across both the Old and New Worlds, making its historical biogeography particularly intriguing. However, understanding its biogeography has been challenging without the application of phylogeny-based biogeographical analytical approaches. title: Analyzing the cultural landscape of Chinese art districts through online social media: a text mining and theoretical interpretation using user-generated content
abstract: Abstract The study examines three Chinese art districts—Beijing 798, Hangzhou Xiangshan, and Jingdezhen Taoxichuan—using 28,661 social media posts. Integrating LDA modeling, irony-aware sentiment analysis, and semantic networks, it uncovers tensions among commercialization, cultural authenticity, and urban identity. Findings reveal 31.2% negative sentiment toward Beijing 798’s over-commercialization, 63.8% positivity for Jingdezhen’s heritage revitalization, and 40% neutrality toward Hangzhou’s emerging spaces. title: Phytochemical Composition of Gleditsia triacanthos L. Grow in Nickel- and Lead-Artificially Contaminated Soil
abstract: —Plants in the Fabaceae family are rich in phytochemicals, and their composition can be influenced by environmental factors such as heavy metals. A factorial experiment using a completely randomized design was conducted in an open field in an open field in the Koya district, Erbil, Iraq to evaluate the effects of soil contamination with NiCl2 or PbCl2 (0, 15, 30, and 45 mg/kg soil) on eight phytochemicals in Gleditsia triacanthos L. leaves. title: Farmers’ knowledge, attitudes and perceptions of green hydrogen in Oshikoto Region, Namibia
abstract: Introduction: Commercial farmers in Namibia’s Oshikoto Region operate under drought, water scarcity, high agricultural input costs and uneven rural energy access. Although Namibia has prioritised green hydrogen within its industrial and energy strategies, limited farmer-level evidence explains how potential agricultural applications are understood and evaluated. Materials and methods: The study adopted an exploratory qualitative design grounded in interpretivism. title: From AFISMA to AES: ECOWAS, Subsidiarity and the Failure to Own Sahel Security, 2012–2026
abstract: When the withdrawal of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger from the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) took legal effect on 29 January 2025, the Community lost the three states whose insecurity had dominated its agenda for more than a decade. This article asks how the regional organisation with the continent's most developed conflict-management architecture came to be a bystander to the Sahel's security crisis. title: A case series of Burkholderia pseudomallei from a tertiary care hospital, Eastern India
abstract: Background: Burkholderia pseudomallei, a saprophytic bacillus, causes melioidosis, a potentially fatal disease. This disease is an emerging infection in India, often misdiagnosed as tuberculosis. Patients generally present with comorbidities such as diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney and pulmonary disease.Materials and Methods: This medical records-based study included 16 male microbiologically confirmed melioidosis cases between September 2019 and November 2025 at a tertiary care hospital in West Bengal. title: Articulations of poisoning: historicity, relationality, and contextuality of Chlordecone pollution in the French Antilles
abstract: Chlordecone, a highly persistent organochlorine insecticide, was widely applied to banana plantations in Martinique and Guadeloupe from 1972 until being banned in 1993. Decades later, its residues still permeate soil, waterways, food systems, and human bodies in the two islands. Classified as both a carcinogenic and an endocrine disruptor, the chemical compound has generated widespread protests, epidemiological debates, and political critique. title: A comprehensive analysis of pyrimidine, pyrazine, pyridazine, and piperazine derivatives as effective organic corrosion inhibitors within corrosive aqueous environments
abstract: Corrosion represents a substantial challenge across various industries, frequently resulting in the pronounced degradation of metallic structures. Organic corrosion inhibitors contribute to alleviating this challenge by establishing a protective film over metallic surfaces, thus diminishing or preventing corrosion. Among these inhibitors, nitrogen-based heterocyclic compounds are widely employed due to their ability to form robust coordination bonds with metal atoms. title: Cross-cultural translation and psychometric validation of the Arabic Intermittent Catheterization Adherence Scale (ICAS): a bicentric study
abstract: Clean intermittent self-catheterization (CISC) is the reference treatment for neurogenic and non-neurogenic voiding dysfunction, yet adherence falls over time. The Intermittent Catheterization Adherence Scale (ICAS) measures this adherence, but no Arabic version has existed. We translated the ICAS into Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) and tested its psychometric properties in 84 Tunisian adults on CISC at 2 rehabilitation departments. title: Antecedents Influencing Behavioral Intentions at Abadi Pelaruga Pool Tourism
abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to determine and analyze the influence of cognitive imagery of natural soundscapes on pleasure and arousal, as well as the effects of pleasure and arousal on behavioral intentions.Research Methodology: An exploratory quantitative research model was employed and analyzed using SmartPLS 4.0. title: Preserving Indigenous Peoples’ values and rights in food composition programmes: A call for agreed international guidelines
abstract: Preserving Indigenous Peoples’ values, rights, and sovereignty within food composition programmes is both an ethical obligation and a scientific necessity. This paper argues that embedding Indigenous Peoples’ knowledge, spirituality, and governance principles across the stages of a food composition programme—designing, sampling, compilation, dissemination and use—ensures ethical research, protects cultural heritage, and prevents exploitation. title: Multiscale Method for Estimating the Thermal Properties of Sandwich Materials Using Infrared Thermography
abstract: Characterizing the thermal properties of sandwich materials remains complex because it demands a method that can independently analyze both the thin and thick layers within the same sample. We propose combining flash and step thermography methods with analytical modeling based on the quadrupole method, which allows the thermal response to be reproduced over a period of six orders of magnitude. This approach facilitates the identification of the thermophysical parameters of each layer. title: Investigation of the Effects of Interactions Between Deltamethrin and Acrylic Paint Particles on Embryonic Development in Xenopus laevis
abstract: The co-occurrence of pesticides and paint-related contaminants in aquatic ecosystems may result in interactions that modify their individual toxic effects; however, the developmental consequences of their combined exposure remain insufficiently understood. This study investigated the individual and combined effects of the widely used pyrethroid insecticide deltamethrin (DM) and two acrylic paints, which have a high potential for microplastic formation, on Xenopus laevis embryonic development, with particular emphasis on their interaction during co-exposure. title: Molecular detection of Acanthamoeba genotypes and Pneumocystis jirovecii in bronchoalveolar lavage specimens from immunocompetent patients with respiratory disorders
abstract: Opportunistic pathogens such as Acanthamoeba spp., Microsporidia , and Pneumocystis jirovecii are well recognized causes of pulmonary infections in immunocompromised patients. title: Long-term malaria exposure in pathogen-endemic environments is associated with distinct immune states
abstract: Abstract Long-term exposure to malaria may shape baseline immune function, yet its effects in healthy adults remain unclear. Here we show that healthy Kenyan adults living in regions with higher malaria transmission and broader infectious exposure have distinct baseline immune profiles. Using blood-cell gene expression and circulating immune mediators from 60 adults across regions with differing malaria endemicity, we identify 658 differentially expressed genes. title: Joint optimization of detection, task allocation, and path planning for multi-agent cooperative interception under partial observability
abstract: Safety-critical autonomous systems often require multiple agents to detect, assign, and intercept non-cooperative mobile targets using only partial observations. These subtasks are tightly coupled because the same agents must balance spatial exploration for detection with goal-directed motion for interception, while target maneuvers remain uncertain. abstract: MT construction requires effective interdisciplinary collaboration across AEC disciplines. However, MT-related competencies remain fragmented within many AEC curricula. This study developed an MT competency framework using employed DACUM-based mixed-method approach that combined quantitative and qualitative strategies to evaluate three discipline-specific MT competency panels of architects, engineers, and CMs 251 MT-related duties and tasks were identified and thematically coded into 18 competency areas. abstract: Abstract Background Bangladesh has achieved major reductions in maternal mortality, yet progress has slowed despite high facility delivery coverage. In 2022, 65% of women had facility delivery, suggesting that increased utilisation has not translated into proportional health gains. We estimated effective coverage of facility-based delivery services by linking household and health facility data and examined equity-related differences in coverage. title: Practical Pendulum Viscometer Design for a Wide Measurement Range and High Accuracy
abstract: Abstract We developed a new low-cost, easy-to-use, and reliable physical-pendulum-based viscometer that can be employed for a wide range of research, educational and commercial applications. The viscometer can measure a very wide range of viscosities with excellent accuracy. We demonstrated its viability to study a wide range of viscosities from that of water up to 1000 times as high and to reliably resolve oscillation angles as small as 10-5 rad. title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of urbanisation induced environmental quality in arid city using a grid-based analysis in Jodhpur India from 2001 to 2021
abstract: Rapid urbanisation in arid regions intensifies heat exposure, vegetation loss, and particulate pollution, yet medium-sized desert cities remain underrepresented in integrated environmental assessments. We quantified spatiotemporal changes in environmental quality in Jodhpur, India, from 2001 to 2021 using a novel grid-based Environmental Quality Index (EQI). title: From local practices to national narratives: the micro-construction of Ningxia’s medical cooperation with Benin and China’s health diplomacy in Africa
abstract: Background China’s health diplomacy with Africa is a core part of China-Africa cooperation. Existing studies mostly focus on macro-level strategies and policies, lacking micro-level analysis of local actors and a bidirectional examination of mechanisms linking local practices and national narratives.Objective This study takes Ningxia’s over 40-year medical aid to Benin as a case, explores the interaction between local actions and national narratives, and reveals the micro-construction path of province-country linkage.Methods A single-case embedded research design was employed, drawing on in-de

title: The limits of regionalism in achieving effective spatial outcomes
abstract: Institutional quality matters and decentralisation and regionalisation should be in service of this overall aim. This paper, in putting forward this simple proposition, lays out evidence on regionalisation, decentralisation and institutions. Despite an assumption that the establishment of regional bodies can solve a series of problems - such as subsidiarity and multi-level governance co-ordination - and help to secure aspirations for economic growth, we sketch out concerns that regions may exacerbate rather than improve such issues in some instances. title: Structural Safety Certification in India: Evaluating Regulatory Fragmentation, Institutional Accountability and Enforcement Gaps
abstract: India’s recurring building collapses expose a regulatory paradox: an elaborate body of technical standards coexists with a certification system that cannot reliably demonstrate whether a building was safely designed, constructed, altered and maintained. This article evaluates structural safety certification as a problem of public law and regulatory governance rather than a narrow engineering formality. title: Environmental Microbiome as a Hidden Reservoir of Opportunistic and Antibiotic-Resistant Pathogens in Hospital Surroundings: A Molecular Ecology Study
abstract: Background: The hospital environment represents a dynamic microbial ecosystem where diverse bacterial populations can establish and persist in various environmental compartments such as soil, water, air, and surfaces. Some of these microorganisms have opportunistic-pathogenic potential and may be relevant to clinical practice, while others carry antibiotic resistance determinants. title: Decision Support for Tourism Risk and Heritage Management: A Case Study of Ha Long Bay
abstract: Tourism firms at heritage destinations must manage operational risks and protect the resources on which their businesses depend. Online reviews could inform managerial follow-up, but sparse mentions and high ratings may limit their value. This study examines these limits through a transparent business analytics pipeline applied to 240 English-language TripAdvisor reviews of 30 cruise, hotel and restaurant listings in Ha Long Bay, Vietnam, published between 2024 and 2026. title: Extract-Mediated Synthesis of ZnO Nanostructures for Enhanced Antibacterial Activity against Multidrug-Resistant Bacteria
abstract: The emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria poses a serious public health problem that calls for the development of new antibacterials. This work describes the eco-friendly production of zinc oxide nanostructures through the use of Azadirachta indica (neem) leaf extract and assesses the antibacterial potential of the synthesized zinc oxide nanostructures against MDR Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. To investigate the pathogenic mechanisms of XLID-98, a double knock-out zebrafish model ( nexmifa/b −/− ) was generated using CRISPR/Cas9 technology. title: Under-platformization: platform literacy and the interplay between multiple actors in developing rural e-commerce in Central and Western China
abstract: Abstract Rural e-commerce in China’s central and western regions is often framed as a scalable pathway to rural revitalization. Yet, platformization may also stall, even when there is already a profitable rural industry. Drawing on interviews, fieldwork, and local archives, we examine the Bai silver handicraft cluster in Xinhua Village, Yunnan Province, which despite being a nationally recognized Taobao village, still exhibits under-platformization. title: Toward human-centered AI-assisted terminology work
abstract: Abstract Generative AI is likely to transform terminology work by creating new opportunities for automation. At the same time, it raises concerns about the future of terminologists and terminological resources, as efficiency pressures may encourage excessive automation based on the perception that human expertise can be replaced by AI. abstract: Intensifikasi akuakultur dapat meningkatkan kepadatan ikan dan jumlah pakan yang diberikan, sehingga berpotensi menyebabkan akumulasi sisa pakan dan feses, penurunan kualitas air, stres, serta meningkatnya risiko penyakit pada ikan. title: Reading Culture in the 21st Century Education: Exploring Epistemological and Technological Dimensions
abstract: This study has explored the ways of developing a reading culture in the 21st century educational setting, employing a qualitative research design. The information was gathered from 28 purposively selected participants comprising students, teachers, librarians, parents, and local government officials from the Far Western Province. Semi-structured interviews were conducted to gain an in-depth understanding of reading practices and reading supports. Thematic analysis was used to capture the salient patterns in the data. abstract: Tour guide attributes’ roles have emerged as a crucial element affecting tourists’ memorable experiences and intention to revisit destinations along Thailand Andaman Coast, especially within the foreign tourist context. However, few studies have investigated the influences of specific tour guide attributes individually. Based on the stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) model, this study examined the influences of tour guide attributes (TGA) on memorable tourism experience (MTE) and revisit intention (RVI) among foreign tourists along Thailand's Andaman Coast. title: The politics of environmental peacebuilding: global agendas, advocacy networks, and domestic policy arenas
abstract: This article examines how environmental conflict narratives emerge and are used in peacebuilding policies. It advocates for a multi-level perspective that systematically connects global intervention agendas to political struggles in domestic policy arenas. Through a comparative analysis of four case studies—Liberia, Colombia, Côte d’Ivoire, and Lebanon—it investigates how environmental considerations are framed as security issues and incorporated into peacebuilding agendas. abstract: Background: Cardiac troponin elevation after strenuous exercise can mimic the biochemical profile of acute coronary syndrome (ACS), risking misdiagnosis in athletes and active individuals presenting to the emergency department. This review synthesises 31 sources to establish an evidence base on release kinetics and washout duration of cardiac biomarkers after exercise relative to ACS. title: Are Palestinian Children Beautiful Too?: Islamic View of Beauty in Picture Books About Palestine and Palestinians
abstract: ABSTRACT The ongoing genocide in Palestine is a challenging topic for many teachers, who remain silent to avoid being labeled antisemitic. Children's literature centered on the Islamic view of beauty (soul, body, action, Deen) can help teachers focus on the beauty of Palestinian children and foster empathy and global connection.

abstract: Introduction Numerous studies have used the Assessing Levels of Physical Activity and Fitness (ALPHA) battery to evaluate physical fitness (PF) and its positive impact on the health of school-age children, assessing various components of fitness. Despite its widespread use, no bibliometric review has systematically examined research trends or scientific output related to the ALPHA-Fitness battery. abstract: Abstract. Agriculture is the largest anthropogenic source of nitrous oxide (N2O), primarily due to nitrogen (N) fertilization. Understanding how the influence of key drivers and the relative contribution of source processes change throughout the cropping season is crucial for developing effective strategies to mitigate N2O emissions. abstract: Abstract Legacy oil and gas wells are an incompletely quantified source of greenhouse gas emissions and offer leakage pathways for subsurface gas migration if inadequately isolated. We present a high‐resolution, process‐based characterization of leakage dynamics at an integrity‐compromised legacy gas well in northeastern British Columbia using five spatial flux surveys and approximately 70 hr of continuous hotspot measurements of methane (CH 4 ) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), integrated with co‐located soil and meteorological observations. title: Performance and uncertainty analysis of rural waste-to-energy systems under stochastic feedstock supply
abstract: This study evaluates the operational performance of three configurations of an Integrated Resource and Recovery Centre (IRRC) as a decentralised rural waste-to-energy (WtE) system using Monte Carlo simulation. Twelve months of empirical feedstock data were incorporated into a probabilistic, scenario-based model to assess how stochastic variations in the availability of vegetable waste and manure affect daily electricity generation. abstract: Colors have capacity to elicit human emotions in philosophy, arts, science, and many industrial areas. There is a lot of interest in natural color substitutes due to rising concerns about the detrimental effects of synthetic colorants on consumers and the environment. Although, plants serve as major non-viable sources of natural pigments with several limitations. abstract: Steel mill scale is an iron-oxide-rich by-product of hot rolling that is generated at roughly 1%–3% of the mass of steel processed and is still largely landfilled or downcycled. Its high iron content, high specific gravity and fine flake morphology have prompted a growing number of laboratory investigations into its use in concrete and mortar, principally as a partial replacement for fine aggregate and, far more rarely, for cement. abstract: Water from the Ganga River and its tributaries is the main freshwater resource in the northern parts of India and has experienced rigorous ecological deterioration because of the continuous discharge of untreated polluted industrial and household effluents, resulting in increased chemical and microbial loads of pollution. title: BUILDING SURVEYORS’ COMPETENCIES IN SUPPORTING SUSTAINABLE CONSTRUCTION ACROSS DEVELOPMENT PHASES: EVIDENCE FROM MALAYSIAN PRACTICE
abstract: Gaps in building compliance and maintenance planning often lead to performance issues after project completion. This study examines the competencies required of building surveyors in supporting sustainable construction across development phases in Malaysia. A structured questionnaire survey was administered to construction professionals from various disciplines. The data were then analysed using the Rasch Measurement Model to establish item reliability, dimensionality and competency domains. title: Sustainable green-synthesized chitosan/red barberry dye doped polymer with structural disorder and tuning optical band gap for flexible optoelectronics
abstract: The development of sustainable optically active materials from natural polymers is important for emerging flexible optoelectronic, photonic, and functional coating applications; however, the intrinsically wide bandgap and limited optical response of pristine chitosan restrict its direct use in such applications. In this study, chitosan-based composite films were prepared through a green functionalization approach using red barberry fruit extract as a natural dye dopant at different concentrations. title: Racial and Ethnic Disparities in the Utilization and Outcomes of Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation and Flutter: a State-of-the-Art Review
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Catheter ablation (CA) has become a first-line option for rhythm control strategy for atrial fibrillation (AF) and atrial flutter (AFL). We synthesize recent evidence regarding racial and ethnic disparities in CA utilization in the United States and examine the structural mechanism driving them. RECENT FINDINGS: Black patients are 28 to 36% less likely to undergo CA for AF or AFL compared to White patients, with similarly reduced odds (22 - 35%) observed among Hispanic and Asian patients for AF. title: Parental responses to climate threat: Italian Validation of the Climate Self-Protection Scale and the role of eco-defenses, epistemic stances, and eco-anxiety
abstract: Climate change has psychological repercussions that challenge individuals’ basic assumptions about stability and safety and contribute to emotional suffering. Parents may be particularly vulnerable to eco-anxiety, given concerns about the long-term impact on their children’s well-being. This research, conducted in Italy, examined how defenses against climate change (“eco-defenses”) and epistemic stances (trust, mistrust, credulity) shape parents’ eco-anxiety across two studies. In Study 1 ( N = 1,259 Italian-speaking adults), we validated the Italian version of the Climate Self-Protection Scal

title: A compound seismic screening index for global nuclear power plant sites combining probabilistic rock-PGA hazard with vs30-based site conditions
abstract: Abstract Seismic safety assessment of nuclear power plant (NPP) sites depends critically on the simultaneous characterisation of ground motion intensity and the capacity of the local soil to amplify that motion. While global probabilistic seismic hazard models and global shear-wave velocity (Vs30) compilations are now available, no prior study has combined these two open global datasets into a single, reproducible screening metric spanning the multi-country reactor-unit inventory. title: Impact of Motor Transport on the Ecological and Geochemical State of the Soil Cover of Olkhon Island
abstract: This study examines Olkhon Island, the largest island in Lake Baikal, located within the Pribaikalsky National Park. The research was motivated by growing tourist flows and Russia Tourism Development Strategy through 2035, which includes specially protected natural areas. To assess recreational impacts on soil cover, the authors analyzed visitation statistics, including vehicle and air transport, and described road types and their transformation. Institute for System Dynamics and Control Theory

title: “We will get you”: linguistic ideology, power, and the distortion of meaning in Twitter discourse
abstract: This is a case study of the meaning of a tweet by @KyleHibbee007 in the context of the 2021 Scottish Parliamentary elections. As a consequence of the tweet’s wording, KyleHibee07 was charged with and convicted in an Edinburgh (Scotland) court of threatening behaviour towards unionist politician @georgegalloway. This study explores how the architecture of Twitter facilitates the distortion of meaning when tweets are decontextualised, the vulnerability of subtle meaning when tweets are recontextualised, and the role that power and linguistic ideologies in conflict play in distorting meaning.
