title: Genome-resolved metagenomics reveals potential biochemical capabilities of a microbial community in an industrial wastewater membrane bioreactor during performance deterioration and recovery
abstract: This study investigates the microbial community composition and biochemical capabilities within a membrane bioreactor (MBR) system treating industrial wastewater during two operational states: a period of marked performance deterioration and a subsequent early recovery phase. The MBR system experienced a prolonged decline in treatment performance, with Total Organic Carbon (TOC) removal efficiency decreasing from approximately 90% to approximately 70% and effluent Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) increasing to more than 70 mg/L. title: The structural dynamics and molecular coupling in the slow inactivation of a prokaryotic voltage-gated sodium channel
abstract: Voltage-gated sodium (Nav) channels initiate and propagate action potentials in many excitable cells. Upon repetitive activation, the fraction of Nav channels available for excitation gradually decreases on a timescale ranging from seconds to minutes, a phenomenon known as slow inactivation. This process is crucial for regulating cellular excitability and firing patterns. Slow inactivation is proposed to result from the collapse of the selectivity filter pore coupled with the opening of the primary helix bundle crossing gate. title: Jerusalem Contexts of the Early Renaissance (In the Footsteps of Shota Rustaveli’s Legacy)
abstract: Shota Rustaveli’s poem The Knight in the Panther’s Skin is a masterpiece of Georgian, European, and world literature. Its principal characters are epic heroes distinguished by personal virtue, moral integrity, spiritual elevation, and physical perfection–figures who embody free thought and tolerance. Written during Georgia’s Golden Age, the poem may be regarded as a precursor to, and an analogue of, Early Renaissance masterpieces in Europe. title: Trichloroethylene and perchloroethylene metabolites have fetal sex-specific RNA expression impacts in a full term placental villous explant model
abstract: Exposure to volatile organic chemicals (VOCs) like trichloroethylene (TCE) and perchloroethylene (PCE) has been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes. We conducted an analysis of gene expression responses to the TCE metabolite S-(1,2-dichlorovinyl)-L-cysteine (DCVC) and the PCE metabolite S-(1,2,2-trichlorovinyl)-L-cysteine (TCVC) in placental explants. Explants from placentas with male and female fetuses were treated with either metabolite at 10 μM or 20 μM (n=4). title: Development and Characterization of Punica granatum Fruit Gel with Anti-Acne Properties
abstract: This study is for development of a modern herbal gel formulated with Punica granatum extracts for dermatological applications, with a primary focus on acne management.A comprehensive approach was adopted, including phytochemical screening, chromatographic profiling, antimicrobial testing, and formulation evaluation, to ensure safety, efficacy, and quality.Pharmacogenetic analysis confirmed the potency of the extracts through acceptable ash and extractive values, while chromatographic studies provided insights into their chemical composition, supporting standardization and quality control.The g

title: Influence of milking methods on microplastic contamination of milk from cows and buffaloes
abstract: Microplastics (particles of <5 mm) are synthetic polymer contaminants with growing environmental concern. Raw milk samples (n = 52) were collected from hand- and machine-milked buffaloes and cows from dairy farms in Multan, Pakistan. Samples were examined visually and subsequently analyzed by Fourier Transform Infrared spectroscopy. Fibers (59%), fragments (24%), and films (17%) were the dominant microplastic particles identified. title: An NKX2-3/5/6 homolog is required downstream of BMP signaling to pattern the sensory-adhesive organ of a tunicate larva
abstract: Tunicates are the sister group to vertebrates within the chordate phylum, yet unlike other chordate groups, they evolved a biphasic lifecycle alternating between motile larvae and sessile adults. The papillae of most tunicate larvae are the key sensory-adhesive organ regulating their settlement and metamorphosis. The papillae are nearly always arranged as a group of three morphologically identical organs that arise from an anterior neural plate border region nested between ventral epidermis and more dorsal/posterior neural tube progenitors. title: Feminist anthropologies in the contemporary world: A conversation on theory, praxis, and politics
abstract: Abstract This article brings together the voices of members of three major feminist anthropological associations to discuss the state of feminist anthropology as a distinct subfield of anthropology, as well as its state of affairs as an increasingly expanding, as well as increasingly threatened, approach to anthropological theory and praxis worldwide. Composed as a conversation, it is based on a roundtable discussion that took place at the 2022 American Anthropological Association (AAA) Annual Meeting, which followed in the footsteps of an important roundtable discussion on Latin American femi

title: Old water, rapid responses: Process-based hydrogeological domains reveal hydraulic–age decoupling and implications for recharge assessment in a complex aquifer system of the Heuningnes Catchment, South Africa
abstract: Abstract Groundwater-level fluctuations are commonly used as recharge indicators because groundwater-level rises are often assumed to represent additions of recently recharged water to aquifer storage. In heterogeneous, multilayer aquifer systems, this assumption remains uncertain because groundwater-level variations may also reflect hydraulic connectivity, pressure transmission, storage redistribution, and groundwater mixing. title: Talking risk, enacting resilience: a case study of risk communication in a climate frontline community
abstract: Communities on the frontlines of climate change face disproportionate risks of multiple hazards. Although community resilience depends on effective risk communication, most research focuses on the information that individuals receive from authorities rather than that which they produce or exchange themselves—that is, “community-based risk communication”. In this mixed methods case study, we examined how community-based risk communication about climate change unfolded and informed community resilience over 6 months in San Bruno, California, using monthly surveys and follow-up interviews. title: Distinct T cell correlates of COVID-19 risk before and after a second booster in previously SARS-CoV-2 infected versus naïve COVAIL trial participants
abstract: The relationship between SARS-CoV-2-specific T cell responses and COVID-19 risk is incompletely understood, particularly after variant-adapted booster receipt. We assessed Spike-specific and Nucleocapsid-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses, measured by validated 27-color intracellular cytokine staining assay, as correlates of COVID-19 risk over 6 months in COVAIL recipients of a second SARS-CoV-2 booster on Day 1 (D1). title: UAV-based dynamic crowd monitoring for rescue prioritization using subspace-driven localization
abstract: Abstract Rapid and reliable localization of survivors is critical in post-disaster search and rescue operations. However, conventional sensing methods such as visual imaging are often ineffective due to smoke, dust, or debris, and traditional RSSI-based localization suffers from severe multipath interference and noise. This paper proposes a subspace-driven multi-UAV system for dynamic crowd monitoring and rescue prioritization. title: N-acyl-homoserine lactonase–nanosilver composite modulates the bacterial community of an in vitro enriched biofilm model of early childhood caries
abstract: Objectives This study investigated the effects of a nanocomposite comprising N-acyl -homoserine lactonase Est816 and silver nanoparticles (Ag-Est816) on the microbial community of an enriched in vitro biofilm model derived from supragingival plaque of children with early childhood caries (ECC). Materials and methods Supragingival plaque samples were collected from 30 children aged younger than 6 years (15 males and 15 females) diagnosed with ECC. title: From life cycle assessment to life cycle thinking in agri-food systems: lessons from the avocado supply chain
abstract: Agri-food systems face growing pressure to demonstrate environmental performance and support sustainability transitions. In this context, Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) generates evidence on environmental impacts, while Life Cycle Thinking (LCT) helps integrate that information into decision-making across supply chains. This review evaluates LCA and LCT for the avocado sector by synthesising current LCA evidence, analysing the transferability of results to LCA‑based ecolabels and certifications, examining how LCT related food‑policy instruments create or limit incentives for supply‑chain actors a

title: Load- versus concentration-based water quality metrics: Field assessment of permeable pavement and filter drain under Mediterranean rainfall in Valencia, Spain
abstract: Study Region Valencia, Spain. Study Focus Two full-scale Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems (SUDS), a permeable pavement (PP) and a filter drain (FD), were monitored over one year at a residential street in Valencia under Mediterranean rainfall conditions. Hydraulic and water-quality performance were evaluated using concentration-based (Event Mean Concentration, EMC) and mass-based (Pollutant Mass Loading, PML) indicators. title: Probiotic potential of Enterococcus faecium ED22: evidence from genomic analysis and in vitro characterization
abstract: Abstract Enterococcus species are ubiquitous members of the human microbiota, but their potential to act as opportunistic pathogens requires careful, strain-specific safety assessment. This study characterized Enterococcus faecium ED22 using a polyphasic approach combining whole-genome sequencing (WGS) with in vitro phenotypic assays. The strain was initially identified by MALDI-TOF/MS and subsequently confirmed by WGS. Genomic analyses included genome assembly and annotation, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and virulence-associated gene screening, plasmid characterization. Functional character

title: CENTRALIZATION VERSUS DECENTRALIZATION IN TOURISM GOVERNANCE: COMPARING PAKISTAN AND UZBEKISTAN, 2010–2026
abstract: Tourism governance is a political economy, institutional design and economic development field. In this paper, the authors have done the comparative study of the management of tourism sector in two nations with diverse modes of governance: Pakistan and Uzbekistan, from 2010 to 2026. After the implementation of 18th Constitutional Amendment (2010) which made the tourism sector the responsibility of four provinces, Pakistan Tourism Development Corporation (PTDC) remained a basket case with lack of any clear mandate for almost ten years. title: The vaccination paradox: how East Africa’s success in Ebola vaccine preparedness may be creating new public expectations for future outbreaks
abstract: This perspective synthesizes published evidence on Ebola vaccination and outbreak preparedness in Africa. Successful vaccination against Zaire ebolavirus has strengthened vaccine-based outbreak control but may also create a preparedness risk when public expectations exceed species-specific vaccine availability. We propose the Vaccine Expectation Gap, Vaccine Anticipation and Species-Specific Vaccine Literacy as linked, hypothesis-generating constructs, supported by a Preparedness Trust Contract for practical implementation. title: Popski’s Private Myth: Vladimir Peniakoff, the Libyan Arab Force and the Problem of Memoir Evidence
abstract: Abstract Vladimir Peniakoff’s Popski’s Private Army remains one of the most influential published accounts of the Libyan Arab Force (LAF) during the Second World War. This archive-led article reassesses Vladimir Peniakoff as a problematic source for the LAF, showing how his memoir preserved valuable traces of LAF activity while distorting chronology, agency, reputational memory and attribution. This has contributed to the marginalisation of Libyan, and specifically Senussi, wartime agency. title: Automatic Radiance Level Data Quality and Signal-to-Noise Assessment for Hyperspectral Imaging
abstract: Raw hyperspectral imaging (HSI) data require multiple processing steps before physically meaningful reflectance products can be derived. Quality issues at the radiance level – e.g., detector artifacts, low-signal regions, or excessive noise – can propagate through the processing chain and compromise subsequent analyses. HSI workflows typically focus on calibration and correction but often lack standardized integrity checks prior to atmospheric compensation. title: Phenotypic and genotypic characterization of listeria monocytogenes strains isolated from meat industries
abstract: Listeria monocytogenes is a major foodborne pathogen of concern for the food industry due to its ability to persist in processing environments and contaminate ready-to-eat foods. This study aimed to characterize phenotypically and genotypically L. monocytogenes isolates recovered from meat-processing environments in Greece, with emphasis on antimicrobial susceptibility, resistance determinants, plasmid content, and sequence types. title: Polymer Identification of Dominant Microplastics in Wastewater Using FTIR and RSM Imaging
abstract: ABSTRACT Microplastics (<5 mm) have emerged as persistent environmental pollutants, and wastewater treatment plants (STPs) are recognized as major pathways for their release into aquatic environments. The present study investigated the abundance, morphology, and polymer composition of microplastics in wastewater using an integrated approach combining RSM‐based imaging and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. A total of 45 influent and effluent samples were collected over one year from the Erandwane STP, Pune, India. Microplastics were extracted through filtration, density separation

title: Structural and Evolutionary Analysis of Non-specific Lipid Transfer Proteins (nsLTPs) in Cereus (Cactaceae)
abstract: The genus Cereus (Cactaceae), widely distributed across arid and semi-arid environments of South America, exhibits adaptive capacity that is partly associated with proteins involved in lipid metabolism and stress responses, such as non-specific lipid transfer proteins (nsLTPs). Although well-characterized in model plants, the structural diversity and functional roles of these proteins in cacti remain largely unexplored. In this study, we characterized the nsLTP repertoire of Cereus by integrating transcriptomic data, phylogenetic analyses, structural modeling, and ligand-binding site mapping.

title: Piloting Digital Leadership, Technology Acceptance, and Literacy–Numeracy Instruments in Early Childhood Education
abstract: Strengthening foundational literacy and numeracy in early childhood education (ECE) may depend partly on how principals lead digital change and how educators perceive technology, but, to our knowledge, no published instrument set measures these constructs together for Indonesian ECE. journal: Indonesian Educational Administration and Leadership Journal (IDEAL).

title: Análisis de frecuencia de calcificaciones de tejidos blandos en radiografías panorámicas
abstract: Las calcificaciones de tejidos blandos pueden identificarse incidentalmente en radiografías panorámicas y requieren una interpretación que considere su localización y morfología. El objetivo fue determinar su frecuencia y distribución por tipo, sexo y lateralidad en radiografías de un centro privado de Guayaquil, Ecuador. Se desarrolló un estudio observacional, descriptivo, retrospectivo y transversal de imágenes obtenidas entre enero de 2025 y enero de 2026. title: Assessment of antibacterial and antioxidant potentials of Aspergillus fumigatus crude extract, the isolated endophyte from Centella asiatica (L.) urban supported by molecular docking
abstract: The growing burden of infectious and chronic diseases associated with bacterial infections and oxidative stress highlights the need for novel antibacterial and antioxidant agents. Fungal endophytes are promising sources of bioactive metabolites with pharmaceutical potential. This study focused on the isolation, characterization, and biological evaluation of endophytic fungus extract obtained from the leaves of Centella asiatica (L.) Urban. institutions: Bangladesh Council of Scientific and Industrial Research

title: Provenance and competence for CHIKV and DENV of Aedes albopictus populations
abstract: Abstract Background Aedes albopictus is one of the world's most hazardous invasive species, increasingly implicated in the autochthonous transmission of Chikungunya (CHIKV) and Dengue (DENV) viruses in newly colonized areas. Since invading the Mediterranean Basin several in the early 1980s, recurrent introductions of distinct lineages have driven extensive genomic admixture within adventive populations. title: Debt of gratitude: The pilgrim teen caught in a vicious cycle in Karen Tei Yamashita’s Through the Arc of the Rain Forest
abstract: Debt comes in all shapes and sizes: from minuscule economic baggage to downright bankruptcy, whether financial or psychological. In Through the Arc of the Rain Forest by Karen Tei Yamashita, one of the chief characters, Chico Paco, turns his life around when encountering the metaphorical rainbow of Brazilian culture, falling into an intriguing form of debt. Carrying on the will of his aged neighbor, the so-called angel becomes entangled in a seemingly mystical whirlpool of performing pilgrimage on behalf of others unable or less able to do so. title: Endangered mammal occurrence records from Environmental Impact Assessment and post-EIA monitoring in the Republic of Korea
abstract: Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and post-EIA monitoring generate substantial biodiversity information through ecological surveys conducted before, during and after development projects. In the Republic of Korea, these records have accumulated in individual assessment reports, but their reuse has been limited because occurrence information is dispersed across documents and is not generally available in a structured format. title: Designing a multifunctional peptide with biofilm-disrupting and fibroblast migration-promoting activities for infection management
abstract: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) remain difficult to manage due to the emergence of antibiotic-resistant pathogens and the persistence of biofilm-based infections. Thus, novel therapeutic strategies beyond conventional antibiotics are needed. In this study, we designed a multifunctional antimicrobial peptide, TR‑MOD, based on venom gland–specific transcriptomic data from the spider Araneus ventricosus . title: Mechanism-guided protease-based strategies for foodborne biofilm control: From EPS protein targets to green delivery systems
abstract: Background Foodborne bacterial biofilms formed on food-contact surfaces and processing equipment are persistent contamination reservoirs because their resistance to sanitation is strongly linked to the chemically diverse and spatially heterogeneous extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix. Proteinaceous EPS components, including adhesins, amyloid fibers, scaffold proteins, and surface-associated assemblies, play key roles in adhesion, cohesion, matrix mechanics, and adaptive remodeling. title: Implementing sustainable procurement through category management and ESG-based supplier evaluation: an EPC case study supported by the Operational Ethical Dilemma
abstract: Sustainable procurement has become a strategic organizational priority as companies increasingly seek to integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) principles into procurement decision-making while maintaining operational efficiency and long-term competitiveness. Despite the growing body of literature on sustainable procurement, limited research has examined its practical implementation within complex project-based industries. title: The Many Struggles of Anton Kajfež: The Rise and Fall of a Kočevje Merchant from Political and Economic Perspectives
abstract: This paper presents a case study of the entrepreneur and landowner Anton Kajfež and his successors, owners of one of the largest companies in Kočevje and Lower Carniola before World War I and during the interwar period. The company focused primarily on the timber and wine trade and became a significant shareholder in many regional companies and banks. Kajfež promoted the local Slovenian economy and used his wealth to strengthen it through a series of projects aimed at surpassing the Gottscheers, a local group of German origin, in the Kočevje economy and politics. title: From Religious Gathering to Ethnic Visibility: The Danu Son See Yar Day Festival and Identity Construction in Myanmar
abstract: This article examines how the Danu Son See Yar Day (DSSYD) festival functions as a religious-cultural medium for strengthening ethnic visibility and identity among the Danu community in Myanmar, addressing the limited scholarly attention to festival-based minority identity formation. Using a qualitative research design, the study draws on documentary materials, participant observation, semi-structured interviews, and group discussions, with the data analyzed thematically. publisher: Sunan Gunung Djati State Islamic University Bandung

title: The orthodox left organizations in Israel: between theological rejection and humanistic reframing of redemption and messianism
abstract: This article examines how Orthodox Left civil society organizations in Israel engage with messianic ideas in relation to dominant Religious Zionist interpretations that frame the establishment of the State of Israel as the beginning of a divine redemptive process. Focusing on organizations such as The Faithful Left, Tag Meir, and the Yashar platform, the study analyses how Orthodox activists reinterpret, reject, or reframe messianic theology within a religious nationalist context. title: Stabilization of expansive soil using talcum powder and cement: swelling reduction and strength development
abstract: Abstract Expansive soils are considered one of the most problematic soil types worldwide due to their significant volume change behaviour in response to variations in moisture content. This study investigates the stabilization of expansive soil using a combination of cement and talcum powder in order to improve its engineering performance. Different percentages of talcum powder, combined with a constant cement content, were examined to evaluate their effects on swelling pressure, compaction characteristics, unconfined compressive strength, and stiffness. title: Structured information extraction from geoscientific literature with GeoExtractor
abstract: Earth science research increasingly depends on the integration of large volumes of heterogeneous data distributed across publications. A substantial amount of quantitative information remains embedded in unstructured literature, making large-scale data compilation labor-intensive and difficult to maintain. Here, we introduce GeoExtractor, a large language model (LLM)-powered multi-agent framework designed to automatically extract structured information from geoscience literature. title: Genomic tracking of Campylobacter jejuni along poultry and pig value chains in Northeast India: Implications for food safety
abstract: Campylobacter jejuni is the predominant causative agent of human campylobacteriosis. A total of 864 samples (poultry cloacal swabs, chicken intestine, chicken meat, pig rectal swab, pig intestine, pork) were screened for the presence of C. jejuni using standard methods. A total of 27 isolates were confirmed with PCR with an overall occurrence rate of 3.13%. Highest isolation rates were from chicken intestine samples (9.72%), followed by pork (7.64%) and chicken meat (1.39%). title: Use of insects as an alternative protein source in tambaqui (Colossoma macropomum) feeding
abstract: The use of alternative protein sources in fish diets has gained increasing attention due to the need to reduce costs and dependence on conventional ingredients in aquaculture. In this context, insects have considerable nutritional potential as feed ingredients, particularly the black soldier fly, Hermetia illucens. However, information regarding the effects of these ingredients in tambaqui (Colossoma macropomum) diets remains limited and scattered across different studies. title: Dual Cuisine Nationalism: Food, Identity and the Making of the Nation in the United Arab Emirates
abstract: ABSTRACT The United Arab Emirates (UAE) presents a distinctive case of nation‐building, as its citizens constitute a demographic minority. Nation‐building in the UAE involves accommodating non‐citizens while maintaining a distinct citizen‐centred national identity. This study argues that the UAE constructs national identity through a dual process of culinary nationalism, in which food serves both as a symbol of indigeneity and a marker of cosmopolitan inclusion. title: Differentiated mosquito adaptive strategies underlie regional dominance of three ECSA sub-lineages in chikungunya virus
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) has emerged as a rapidly expanding global health threat and has been reported in 119 countries and territories, with recent outbreaks across Asia, Europe, and the Americas. The East/Central/South African (ECSA) genotype has increasingly predominated in multiple regions, yet the molecular basis of its competitive advantage remains unresolved. Here, we demonstrate that three ECSA sub-lineages-ECSA-IOL, ECSA-2.1, and ECSA-2.2-have independently evolved distinct vector-associated evolutionary patterns that underlie their divergent geographic dominance. title: Seasonal runoff-driven transport of oxytetracycline from swine feces and its effects on soil bacteria and antimicrobial resistance risk
abstract: Inroduction The environmental dissemination of veterinary antibiotics through livestock feces represents a relevant concern within the One Health framework due to its potential effects on ecosystem functioning and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) selection. Oxytetracycline (OTC), widely used in swine production systems, is excreted largely as parent compound and may reach surrounding environments through rainfall-driven runoff. title: Climate Change Disinformation| Unraveling Debunked Climate Change Disinformation and Responses to Fact-Checks: Evidence From the United States, Netherlands, and Philippines
abstract: Although climate change skepticism and denialism have been considered influential narratives in the contemporary digital information landscape, we know little about how such narratives are legitimized in climate change disinformation across different national settings. Against this background, this study relies on an in-depth qualitative content analysis of fact-checked disinformation in the Netherlands, the United States, and the Philippines as contrasting global cases. title: Validating national reuse indicators from regional demolition data: a Swedish example
abstract: Construction accounts for a substantial share of global emissions and waste, highlighting the need to shift from linear to circular resource flows and to prioritise deconstruction and reuse over demolition and disposal. Enabling this transition requires reliable methods for identifying and quantifying products embedded in existing buildings. abstract: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between three types of social media use and four dimensions of political participation on Facebook. Taking Vietnam as a context, we further looked into the mediating role of two related but distinct concepts of nationalism and patriotism in this process. Findings from a cross-sectional survey revealed that active nonsocial Facebook use was positively related to nationalist and patriotic attitudes. abstract: Abstract Existing interconnected power systems (IPSs) are facing increasing challenges due to the expansion of industrial and residential sectors, alongside the integration of renewable energy sources, which result in significant fluctuations in frequency, voltage, and tie-line power threatening system stability and power quality. Automatic Voltage Regulation (AVR) and Load Frequency Control (LFC) loops aim to ensure stable and secure IPS operation by minimizing deviations in frequency, voltage, and tie-line power, thereby delivering high-quality power to consumers. abstract: Spodumene [LiAl(Si 2 O 6 )], as an important Li source, is crucial for sustaining the global Li supply. Lithium isotopes have been a powerful geochemical tracer for unravelling magmatic‐hydrothermal processes within pegmatite systems. title: WorldBench: Evaluating LLMs on Three.js Voxel World Generation
abstract: Large language models can now write complete, interactive 3D worlds as code, but grading those worlds automatically is unreliable. Existing judges take one view of the output: a vision-language model scores a few rendered snapshots, or a language model reads the source. On worlds written by five frontier models we find that the two views disagree on 32% of required items, mostly code that no frame shows, and that fixed views miss small close-up contents. abstract: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre ensembles are leading room-temperature magnetometers, but their sensitivity is usually extracted from a single resonance and relies on external microwave and bias-field hardware. This work proposes a chip-scale NV magnetometer built around a one-dimensional YIG/CoFeB magnonic crystal, in which a single structural defect forms a passive magnonic cavity and integrated permanent magnets supply the bias field. abstract: In September 2026 the U.S. Department of War released an infrared video recorded from a military aircraft over the Middle East, with a mission report describing six small spherical objects moving at an estimated 480 miles per hour. We measure the brightness of each object in every frame. All six brighten and dim steadily at 7.1-7.9 times per second, each at its own rate and out of step with the others. abstract: LLM-based agents face challenges in personalized interactive tasks due to heterogeneous, multi-typed, and implicitly constrained long-term traces. Existing memory mechanisms struggle with accurate routing and retrieval, especially on-device where personalization is critical. Most methods use single-vector representations, blurring type distinctions and relational structure. We propose HGP, a hybrid graph memory framework. This capacity reflects a form of humanity's sixth sense: an intuitive reasoning mechanism that recovers implicit information beyond raw sensory perception. abstract: Recent advances in large language model (LLM) pretraining highlight the role of high-quality training data in improving performance. While model-based filtering has proven effective in selecting high-quality subsets from web-scale corpora, especially for high-resource languages, low-resource languages face challenges due to limited availability of annotated data. abstract: The CosmicWatch Desktop Muon Detector (v3X) is a compact and low-cost scintillator-based instrument designed to detect ionizing radiation, including cosmic-ray muons. Built around a plastic scintillator, a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM), and a dual-core Raspberry Pi Pico microcontroller, the v3X achieves a 400 microsecond dead time per event, sustained event logging at 700 Hz, and two-detector coincidence triggering for more accurate counts. title: Estimation and inference in penalized function-on-function regression with dependent residual curves
abstract: Penalized function-on-function regression, as implemented in the R package refund, treats all grid values of all curves as independent. Residual curves are smooth, so values within a curve are dependent. We study what this does to point estimates and pointwise confidence intervals, in a simulation with Gaussian, count and binary responses and in a plasmode study built on nine real datasets. title: Split Skies: Operational Experiences Extending a Multi-Cloud Network Telescope into the Asia-Pacific
abstract: Comprehensive visibility into Internet Background Radiation (IBR) requires diverse measurement infrastructure. Recent work showed that cloud IBR depends on the provider making single-provider telescopes systematically biased. These studies relied entirely on Western providers and left the Asia-Pacific region as a blind spot. In this report we extend a multi-cloud network telescope onto Tencent Cloud inside mainland China. abstract: One of the challenging components of modern lattice-QCD computations of the leading hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muon $(g-2)_μ$ is the isospin-breaking correction due to electromagnetism. Dominated by long distances, this correction suffers from severe signal-to-noise issues and finite-volume effects. title: Sociotechnical Aspects of Tor Relay Rejection
abstract: In 2019, the Tor Project enforced an end-of-life (EoL) policy for Tor versions, leading to the rejection of outdated relays, amounting to a notable fraction of consensus weight. While this policy aids network maintenance, reduces backporting efforts, and shortens vulnerability exposure, its sociotechnical implications remain unstudied.

abstract: We introduce HyperBrowseComp, a multilingual and multimodal browsing benchmark comprising 423 manually authored and human-validated questions across 13 languages, written by native or highly proficient speakers. Questions are designed to be extremely challenging. title: AdHImEx: Adaptively High-Order Implicit-Explicit Transport for Large Time Steps
abstract: Adaptively Implicit-Explicit (AdImEx) time stepping provides stability for large time steps for mass-conservative transport, making it attractive for the numerical representation of advection in weather and climate prediction. Existing AdImEx transport schemes become first-order accurate in the large-time-step, implicit regime and may require multiple sparse matrix solutions per time step. This work introduces AdHImEx, a new AdImEx scheme that addresses both limitations simultaneously. title: SoK: Privacy-Preserving Order Matching
abstract: Privacy-preserving order matching enables traders to discover and execute compatible orders while limiting disclosure of sensitive trading information. Existing systems span financial markets and blockchain-based asset exchanges and employ diverse market structures, privacy mechanisms, and trust assumptions, making their privacy guarantees difficult to compare. title: AI-Generated Disinformation in the UK: Risk of Harm, Context, and Classification
abstract: More people across the UK are today exposed to more AI-generated and AI-altered disinformation and misinformation than ever before - exposing individuals and society to a growing range of harmful consequences and potential consequences. We analyse evidence from a dataset of 112 pieces of AI-generated or AI-altered disinformation or misinformation seen tens of millions of times across the UK between 1 January 2025 and 31 March 2026. abstract: We develop a field-redefinition-invariant description of hadronic amplitudes outside the WZW sector at $\mathcal{O}(1/f_a)$, including general flavour-conserving and flavour-changing quark couplings. Starting from the most general CP-conserving Lagrangian for ALP interactions with the QCD sector, we identify invariant Wilson coefficient combinations and match them onto the $U(3)$ chiral theory. abstract: The nature of ultra-luminous X-ray sources (ULXs) is shrouded in mystery as they're believed to be point sources with luminosities above the classical Eddington limit for a 10$M_{\odot}$ black hole (BH), but generally fit into the classification tree of super-Eddington X-ray binaries. title: ULTRADISCOVERY: Abductive Exploration in an Interconnected, Epistemically Open Universe
abstract: Scientific discovery often begins when scattered clues call for a new way of describing the world. Such abductive exploration can require constructing the representation in which an explanation is stated, when the world is epistemically open, and composing evidence scattered across contexts, when it is structurally interconnected. abstract: Neutrino oscillation probabilities computed with the Magnus expansion, for an arbitrary number of flavors and any Hamiltonian, time-dependent or not. Every truncation of the series lives in the Lie algebra, so the evolution operator it exponentiates is unitary exactly rather than to the accuracy of the truncation.

abstract: Sampling-based quantum advantage raises a basic resource question: how much non-Gaussianity is needed to reproduce the random-matrix statistics often associated with quantum chaos? Passive fermionic linear optics preserves Gaussian structure, and even Haar-random mode mixing fails to anticoncentrate for Slater inputs. title: StegoMemory: Agentic Memory Acts as Covert Steganographic Channel
abstract: Is agentic memory robust against stealthy steganographic attacks? We carry out a large-scale red-teaming exercise to test whether agents can encode attacker-controlled strings in one session and recover them in another without triggering safety oversight. Following SHADE-Arena-style tasks, we embed malicious side tasks to encode secret strings using steganography within otherwise benign tasks and evaluate them using independent task-completion and safety oversight. abstract: Modern critical software infrastructure is largely written in C. Since C lacks memory safety, researchers are investigating automatic translation of C to safer languages like Rust. abstract: Language models frequently generate outputs in unintended languages or scripts, a phenomenon known as off-target generation. While existing research has focused on language selection, the dimension of script knowledge remains understudied: before any linguistic understanding can occur, users must recognize the graphic symbols in a model's response. abstract: Flood protection by coastal vegetated systems depends on the persistence of vegetation structures, but it is currently impossible to predict vegetation survival during extreme storms. abstract: The rapidly changing ocean environment is driving shifts in fish distribution, fishing effort, catch, and catch rates. abstract: Abstract The early Eocene Climatic Optimum (EECO; 53.3–49.1 million years ago) represents the period of greatest sustained warmth in the Cenozoic (last 66 million years), with proxy‐data indicating global‐mean temperatures 10–16°C above preindustrial and atmospheric concentrations of 1,200–2,500 ppmv. title: Lubricant-Engine Suitability Evaluation for Fuel Efficiency in Fishing VesselUsing Temperature and Color Degradation
abstract: Engine performance in fishing vessel depends on the reliability and efficiency of diesel engine, in which the lubrication system plays a key role in reducing friction, controlling operating temperature, and minimizing component wear. However, field observations in small-scale fisheries indicate that many fishermen select lubricants based on habit, price, or availability rather than manufacturer specifications, which may reduce engine efficiency and increase fuel consumption. abstract: Linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE) is the dominant polymer in agricultural films, mulch covers, and packaging throughout Ecuador and Latin America, where intensive agricultural economies drive high per-capita consumption. Its prolonged outdoor use under intense equatorial UV radiation accelerates photooxidative degradation, generating microplastic particles that have been detected in remote ecosystems including the Antarctic region, underscoring the global reach of local plastic degradation. title: Projecting the real through active inference: a unified model of reality construction from neuronal dynamics to social consensus a neuroscientific framework for psychopathology
abstract: How does the brain transform a chaotic stream of sensory signals into a stable, shared experience of reality? This theoretical paper proposes that the brain does not passively receive the world, but actively projects it – it continuously generates predictions about sensory inputs and updates its internal model when predictions fail, a process formally described by the free energy principle and active inference. title: Comparing literature-guided, LLM-assisted, and data-driven models for predicting angler pressure
abstract: This study compared three models-a literature-guided, a large language model (LLM)-assisted, and a data-driven model-all developed using Bayesian networks as the framework for predicting angler pressure measured by the number of boats observed in aerial surveys. The models used meteorological data from 98 lakes in Ontario, Canada, during 2018 and 2019, as well as platform-derived variables, including angler-reported fishing trips, fishing duration, and catch rate, together with lake webpage views. abstract: The study aimed to assess, in practical terms, how technical, hydrological, operational and design factors influence the accuracy of determining cargo mass based on the vessel’s draught using the draught survey method. The study was conducted using a computational case study of the initial and final draught surveys, incorporating the vessel’s hydrostatic data, water density, variable masses and error scenarios. title: Feature-level fusion of Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery for crop-type mapping in humid tropical mountainous terrain
abstract: Accurate crop-type mapping in humid tropical mountains is challenged by persistent cloud cover, rugged topography, and fragmented smallholder parcels. This study evaluates a feature-level fusion workflow that integrates Sentinel-2 optical indices and Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter for crop-type mapping in Candipuro District, Lumajang, East Java, Indonesia. Sentinel-2 surface reflectance and Sentinel-1 IW data acquired in June–July 2023 were harmonised in Google Earth Engine to a common 10 m pixel grid, so that all comparison maps were evaluated on the same spatial support. title: Fossil flora and palaeoclimate of the Upper Cretaceous Horseshoe Canyon Formation, Horsethief Member, at Morrin Bridge, Alberta, Canada
abstract: The Horseshoe Canyon Formation in southern Alberta, Canada, preserves abundant plant fossils from the upper Campanian to upper Maastrichtian. However, studies describing the macroflora are taxonomically out of date, and limited work has been done to utilise the flora for palaeoclimatic reconstruction. Fifty-eight plant taxa are documented from the Morrin Bridge locality within the lower Maastrichtian Horsethief Member of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation. title: The Chemical Effects of Nitrogenous Substances in Two Different Grades of PVDF Used in Offshore Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT In this work, two different grades of poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) commonly used in offshore applications, one with 3% of dibutyl sebacate (DBS) plasticizer and the other a copolymer containing chlorotrifluoroethylene (CTFE), were subjected to an aging process in contact with a fluid containing hydrocarbons, pyridine, and aniline at high temperature for 90 days. title: Relationship between land-use change and flow patterns: a duration curve analysis in the Babahoyo River basin, Ecuador
abstract: Anthropogenic land use and land cover changes alter watershed hydrological processes by modifying the partitioning of precipitation into evapotranspiration, infiltration, and surface runoff. This study aimed to analyze the relationship between land-use change and flow regime in three sub-basins of the Babahoyo River basin, Ecuador, by using flow duration curves, Mann-Kendall test and Runoff coefficient: Zapotal (2,980 km 2 ), Echeandia (382 km 2 ), and San Pablo (1,387 km 2 ). title: Dynamic and reversible bonds in polymeric membrane fabrication: towards recyclability-by-design
abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable separation technologies has intensified interest in polymeric membranes due to their energy efficiency and versatility. However, many conventional membranes are fabricated from permanently crosslinked or non-degradable polymers, limiting their recyclability and contributing to environmental waste. In this review, the integration of dynamic bonds into membrane materials is explored, focusing on their potential to enable reprocessability, repairability and recyclability. title: Necessity or Indulgence: Reconsidering Space Exploration
abstract: Taking the debate over whether space exploration constitutes a necessity or a mere indulgence as its starting point, this essay adopts a philosophical and interdisciplinary perspective to re-examine the value of human space activities inspired by the Pale Blue Dot photograph. The study breaks down the binary opposition between necessity and indulgence, arguing that this distinction is not purely economic but hinges on definitions of resource purposes and human civilisational goals. title: On-line analysis of N 2 O isotopic composition during biological nitrogen removal in wastewater treatment to disentangle production and reduction processes
abstract: Abstract. Nitrous oxide (N2O) is a potent greenhouse gas, and emissions from wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) represent a significant and highly variable source. Understanding the dynamics in microbial pathways of N2O formation and reduction during biological nitrogen removal is essential for targeted mitigation strategies. Stable isotope analysis of N2O (δ15Nα, δ15Nβ, δ18O, and 15N site preference) provides a powerful tool to disentangle and quantify N2O production and reduction processes, yet conventional analytical approaches lack temporal resolution. title: Development trends and driving mechanisms of coordination in the Digitalization–Urban development–low-carbon transition system
abstract: Against the backdrop of sustainable development and China’s Dual Carbon Goals, Digitalization, Urban Development, and Low-carbon Transition continuously interact to shape urban sustainable development. However, the long-term coordination of the Digitalization–Urban Development–Low-carbon Transition (DUL) system and its underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. title: Coupling of VIIRS and Sentinel-2 observations to generate Landsat-scale TIR imagery for estimating landscape evapotranspiration using the Simplified Surface Energy Balance (SSEB) model
abstract: : Satellite thermal infrared (TIR) data are essential for remote sensing of energy exchange processes at the Earth-atmosphere interface. Current satellite sensors are subject to a trade-off between spatial resolution and temporal coverage. Daily TIR observations from MODIS and VIIRS are limited to coarse spatial resolutions of ∼400–1000 m, whereas higher-resolution Landsat TIRS observations (∼100 m) provide infrequent temporal coverage (∼8 days). Downscaling methods that correlate TIR imagery with higher-resolution multispectral data can improve the availability of fine-scale TIR observations.

title: Nutritional, Physicochemical and Sensory Evaluation of Geblek, a Traditional Food from Kulon Progo Regency Enriched with Ulva sp. from Gunungkidul Coast
abstract: Geblek is a traditional cassava-based snack from Kulon Progo, Yogyakarta, that generally has limited nutritional value because of its relatively simple ingredient composition. Ulva sp., a green seaweed, contains macro- and micronutrients, antioxidants, and other bioactive compounds, making it a potential functional food ingredient. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of Ulva sp. supplementation on the nutritional composition, physicochemical properties, and sensory characteristics of geblek. title: Global distributions and environmental correlates of community leaf length and width in forests
abstract: Leaf length and width are key dimensions of tree leaf size and can influence leaf boundary-layer development and leaf-environment heat exchange. However, their global patterns and environmental correlates remain poorly understood. By integrating tree leaf traits and community data, we mapped community leaf length and width and identified their environmental correlates in global forests. Both community leaf length and width decreased toward higher latitudes, although leaf width showed an additional peak at mid-latitudes. title: Land use change, driving factors, and multi-scenario projections of ecosystem service supply in the Yangtze River delta urban agglomeration
abstract: Rapid urban expansion has intensified regional human-land conflicts and ecological risks. This study examines the Yangtze River Delta Urban Agglomeration the key urban cluster development areas in China, using multi-source spatial data and integrated modeling approaches, including the Integrated Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Tradeoffs (InVEST) and Patch-level Land Use Simulation (PLUS) models, to analyze land use changes from 2000 to 2020 and assess ecosystem service dynamics for 2010–2020, and project future land use patterns under three development scenarios for 2030 and 2060. title: Energy-Efficient Routing Protocols for IoT-Based Wireless Sensor Networks in Nuclear Facility Monitoring
abstract: Reliable and energy-efficient wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are important for continuous monitoring in nuclear facilities, where limited battery resources, restricted maintenance access, and safety-critical operation require stable and efficient communication. This study evaluates four routing protocols for IoT-based WSN monitoring: Low-Energy Adaptive Clustering Hierarchy (LEACH), Power-Efficient and Balanced Aggregation in Sensor Networks (PEBAIS), Threshold-sensitive Energy Efficient Network (TEEN), and Geographic Adaptive Fidelity (GAF). abstract: This study presents δ¹³C isoscapes for modern human tissues in Brazil, based on paired analyses of dentine collagen and fingernail keratin. Using a random forest modeling approach combined with climatic and socio-economic covariates, we reveal spatial patterns in dietary carbon source assimilation across the Northeast and Southeast regions. While δ¹³C values in dentine correlated mainly with environmental variables, those in fingernails were more closely tied to socio-economic indicators such as municipal GDP and income inequality. title: Acid Leaching for Carbon Sequestration with Prospects for Critical Metal Recovery
abstract: Abstract Reducing carbon emissions and supplying critical metals for the green energy transition are essential to limiting global warming to below 1.5 °C. Here, we propose heap leaching ultramafic material with sulfuric acid followed by sequential precipitation for nickel recovery and carbon sequestration. Ultramafic materials were subjected to benchtop-scale acid leaches using 0.08–0.8 M H2SO4. title: A method for characterising fire events in high fire frequency landscapes: case study application to North Kimberley fire regimes, Western Australia
abstract: Background Identifying fire events provides insights into fire size distribution, the timing of significant fire events, their behaviour and ignition causes. However, this can be challenging when using temporally coarse datasets across high-fire-frequency savanna landscapes. Aims Develop and validate a fire event delineation (FED) methodology. title: MONKI: a three-dimensional Monte Carlo simulator for transfer of polarised light in planetary atmospheres
abstract: Abstract. Spectropolarimetry is a powerful tool for characterising planetary atmospheres and surfaces. For the design and operation of spectro(polari)metric instrumentation, numerically simulated signals of the measured radiation are essential. Here we present MONKI (Monte Carlo KNMI), an efficient and accurate radiative transfer code written in Fortran, based on the Monte Carlo method. title: A dual role of precipitation amount and temperature determines precipitation isotopic trends in Southeast Alaska
abstract: Southeast Alaska is one of the wettest places in the world, with some locations within the region receiving upwards of 6 metres of precipitation annually. Given the region's abundant precipitation, it is important to understand the mechanisms controlling the hydrologic cycle to better constrain past and future trends in climate. Accomplishing this requires the evaluation of isotopes in precipitation, as this is key to untangling the many drivers of the water cycle. title: Herpetofaunal diversity and potential indicator species in a Mediterranean maquis ecosystem of the Chréa National Park, Tell Atlas, Algeria
abstract: Mediterranean maquis ecosystems of North Africa harbor unique fauna, but their herpetofaunal diversity remains poorly documented despite increasing anthropogenic pressures and habitat fragmentation. In this study, we conducted field surveys across nine one-kilometer transects spanning natural, rural, and urban landscapes along an elevational gradient (175-1245 m) in the Chréa National Park, Tell Atlas, Algeria. title: Hybrid Physics-Informed Reinforcement Learning for Plasma Characterization in Electrical Wire Explosions
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of discharge observables in electrical wire explosions is challenging due to the inherent nonlinearities in plasma behavior, especially when experimental datasets are limited. This study presents a hybrid physics-informed modeling framework that combines analytical scaling laws with a reinforcement learning-based residual correction strategy to improve prediction accuracy across the charging-voltage range of 9.0–12.9 kV. abstract: Abstract. Post-launch characterization of the receiver telescope of the laser altimeter is essential for achieving precise georeferenced planetary measurements and for radiometric calibration to passively measure surface reflectance. For the Ganymede Laser Altimeter (GALA) aboard the Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice), such in-flight calibration was originally planned during a lunar flyby but could not be performed due to an unexpected reboot of the instrument. title: Multi‑temporal investigation of brine hydrogeochemical evolution under sustained potash mining in the Qarhan Salt Lake, Qaidam Basin, China
abstract: Abstract The Qarhan Salt Lake, located in the eastern Qaidam Basin of Qinghai Province, China, is the largest potash-producing base in the country. Decades of sustained brine extraction for potassium chloride (KCl) production have profoundly altered the subsurface hydrogeological and hydrogeochemical regime. abstract: We investigate the apparent thermality of Hawking radiation in the semi-classical limit of quantum black holes using the mean-field limit of a chiral spin-chain simulator, which models fermions propagating on a black hole space-time in the continuum. In this free-theory regime, no genuine thermalisation occurs. abstract: The compression deformation of a flexible cushion will lead to a decrease in thermal resistance. Based on this characteristic, a surface heat source method for earth pressure monitoring was proposed in this paper. Effective reservoirs in this region are relatively thin, and seismic responses between gas-bearing layers and dry layers differ only slightly. abstract: Abstract Robust traffic sign detection is an important factor of safe autonomous driving, allowing vehicles to accurately interpret and comply with dynamic road regulations. However, real world deployment remains heavily challenged by distant, extra-small signs, as well as partial occlusions from trees, structures, or other vehicles. title: Evaluation of a commercial mushroom-derived product as a dietary immunomodulator and its effects on disease resistance in European seabass (Dicentrarchus labrax) juveniles
abstract: The use of natural bioactive ingredients is a promising strategy to improve fish health and enhance disease resistance in sustainable aquaculture. The present study evaluated the effects of dietary supplementation with Hifas Aqua , a mushroom-derived product containing Pleurotus ostreatus , Lentinula edodes , and Herimax ® (fermented Hericium erinaceum mycelium), on the immune response and disease resistance in European seabass ( Dicentrarchus labrax ). abstract: The study of bird migration timing is pivotal for the identification of the onset of pre-breeding migration, when, according to the European regulatory framework, the hunting seasons should end following Article 7.4 of the EU Birds Directive. Member States may use different data sources, including citizen science platforms, to determine this onset. title: Metastable and Stable States in Covalent Organic Frameworks Controlled by Synthetic Selection Pressure
abstract: The synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) has long followed a thermodynamics-driven approach, aiming to obtain highly ordered stable crystalline materials while overlooking metastable structures with unique dynamic characteristics. Inspired by the biological concept of "selection pressure," we propose that the harshness of synthetic conditions serves as a key selection pressure governing the final state of COFs. title: Geotechnical parameters estimation using electrical resistivity tomography data: Case study of Jorf Lasfar, western Morocco

abstract: Abstract There is a growing interest in utilizing plastic waste to produce olefins and aromatics, which serve as essential building blocks for polyolefin production. In this paper, a novel microwave-assisted catalytic process is developed for converting polypropylene plastic waste into propylene, with simultaneous co-production of ethylene, aromatics, and alkanes, thereby closing the material loop by returning end-of-life plastic waste back into the petrochemical value chain as a high-value chemical feedstock, a key principle of the circular economy. abstract: ABSTRACT High efficiency inverted perovskite solar cells often rely on nickel‐containing hole‐selective interfaces such as NiOx. abstract: ABSTRACT Extreme rainfall events frequently trigger flash floods, which cause widespread damage to ecosystems, infrastructure, and livelihoods. Accurate rainfall estimation is therefore essential for flood modeling and early warning systems. This study assessed the performance of the Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM) and the Global Precipitation Measurement Integrated Multi‐Satellite Retrievals for GPM (GPM‐IMERG) against weather station rainfall observations collected across KwaZulu‐Natal, South Africa, between 2000 and 2022. title: Findings on the efficacy of sonic debridement in chronic wound management – a case series
abstract: OBJECTIVES To evaluate the physiological rationale, mechanism of action, and emerging clinical evidence supporting sonic debridement as an adjunctive approach for wound hygiene and maintenance debridement in chronic wound management. METHODS A structured review of wound healing principles, biofilm biology, and current debridement modalities was performed alongside analysis of clinical observations and case series data using a sonic debridement device. title: Numerical calculations of neutron star mountains supported by crustal lattice pressure
abstract: Abstract Gravitational waves may set the spin frequencies of neutron stars in low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs). One mechanism for facilitating such emission is the formation of a mass asymmetry - or ‘mountain’ - supported by elastic strains driven by thermal gradients. title: A Multi‐Domain System‐Level Framework for Floating Photovoltaic Systems With Comparative Analysis of Thermal Configurations
abstract: A multi‐domain modeling framework for the performance simulation of floating photovoltaic (FPV) systems is presented. As an initial stage of this framework, the present study implements and couples only the thermal and electrical subsystems, evaluating four interchangeable configurations of varying fidelity; the implementation of the mechanical and hydrodynamic subsystems is deferred to future work. title: A Spectral–Semantic integration framework for hydrothermal alteration characterization using Landsat-8 OLI and AlphaEarth Foundations in the Eastern Tien Shan, China
abstract: Remote sensing-based hydrothermal alteration mapping plays an important role in regional mineral prospectivity analysis but remains challenging in structurally complex regions because of spectral mixing, weak peripheral anomalies, and fragmented spatial distributions. This study proposes an integrated spectral–semantic framework that combines Landsat-8 OLI multispectral imagery with AlphaEarth Foundations (AEF) semantic embeddings for hydrothermal alteration characterization and prospectivity evaluation in the Tuwu copper belt, Eastern Tien Shan, China. abstract: Abstract A proposed theoretical description of the latent heat entrainment flux at the top of a convective boundary layer (CBL) was tested. title: Assessment of seismic velocity changes from ambient noise single-station cross-component analysis in Altamira, Brazil
abstract: Methods capable of monitoring groundwater systems are essential to support decisions and resource management. In recent years, techniques based on the analysis of ambient seismic noise have consolidated passive seismic methods as valuable monitoring tools. abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate estimation of evapotranspiration (ET) is essential for sustainable water management, particularly in arid and semiarid regions. This study aimed to establish relationships between the normalised difference vegetation index (NDVI) derived from satellite imagery and stress‐adjusted crop coefficients ( K c_adj ) obtained using the METRIC (mapping ET at high resolution with internalised calibration) model and to develop efficient models for rapid ET estimation. abstract: Abstract The efficient synthesis of poly(ester amide)s (PEAs), which combine polyamide-like mechanical strength with polyester-like biodegradability, has remained a longstanding challenge. title: Cellulose-Based Nanosponges with PEDOT:PSS as Pressure Sensors with Tunable Elasticity: A Study on Modulation of Mechanical Properties and Pressure Response

title: Dynamic quantitative photoacoustic tomography under sparse sampling via residual-driven Kalman filter assisted reconstruction
abstract: Mechanically scanned photoacoustic tomography (PAT) provides high detection sensitivity and flexible system configurations, but its application to dynamic quantitative imaging is limited by the trade-off between temporal resolution and spatial sampling density. We propose a coordinated acquisition–estimation–reconstruction (AER) framework for dynamic quantitative PAT under sparse-pattern sampling. title: A life cycle-based Green Manufacturing framework for environmental decision-making: an application to heavy-duty vehicle chassis frame rail manufacturing
abstract: Abstract Heavy-duty vehicles (HDV) are essential to global transportation and logistics systems, yet environmental assessments have predominantly focused on the use phase, leaving the environmental impacts of the manufacturing stage comparatively underexplored. This study evaluates the cradle-to-gate environmental performance of steel chassis frame rail manufacturing using a process-level Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) based on primary industrial data collected directly from the shop floor. Environmental impacts were assessed using the ReCiPe 2016 Midpoint (H) and Environmental Footprint (EF) 3.1

title: Which One Tastes Better? Testing Distinct Baits to Evaluate Fruit‐Feeding Butterfly Assemblages (Lepidoptera: Nymphalidae) in a Subtropical Region
abstract: ABSTRACT Standardised sampling protocols are essential for improving biodiversity assessments, particularly for indicator groups such as fruit‐feeding butterflies. Although fermented banana is the most widely used bait in tropical regions, rotten fish is the best bait for catching fruit‐feeding butterflies in high‐altitude sites. Few studies have evaluated the effectiveness of alternative attractants in the subtropical region worldwide, where environmental conditions and resource availability differ markedly. title: Assessing climate change perceptions and climate-smart agriculture adoption among root, tuber and banana farmers in Eastern D.R. Congo
abstract: Perceptions shape human practices, including agricultural decisions, yet their influence on climate-smart agriculture adoption remains insufficiently understood in climate-vulnerable eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). This study compared farmers’ perceptions of climate change with empirical climate data of the past three decades across South-Kivu’s agroecological zones (AEZ), eastern DRC. title: Style transfer mapping with ensemble learning for cross-subject EEG-based neuropsychiatric disease recognition
abstract: Cross-subject electroencephalogram (EEG) recognition remains a fundamental challenge because large inter-subject variability causes severe distribution shifts that substantially degrade the generalization ability of existing learning models. Most existing transfer learning methods attempt to align global feature distributions but often overlook subject-specific structural variations, resulting in unstable adaptation under limited calibration data. title: An analytical model for rotors in confined flow across operating regimes
abstract: Rotors operating in confined flows, or blockage, are commonly encountered in wind and water tunnels, as well as in shallow or dense deployments of hydrokinetic turbines. Confinement induces a streamwise pressure gradient in the channel, modifying the rotor induction, thrust and power. To account for these effects, physics-based or empirical blockage corrections are used as a transfer function between the dynamics of an object operating in confined and unconfined settings. title: Fine Assessment of Water Abundance and Water Inflow Potential in Coal-Bearing Strata Based on Water Storage Space Microelements
abstract: Abstract Mine water inflow is one of the primary hazards threatening the safety of coal-mining production. Groundwater in coal-bearing strata serves as the direct water-filling source for coal mining, and its water abundance significantly impacts the intensity of the mine water inflow. The coal-bearing strata in the Ordos Basin, China, were formed during the Jurassic period, and the coal measure sandstones are characterized by short diagenetic times, weak cementation, and significant variations in the water abundance. title: Circular Transformation in the Silk Sector: A Fuzzy Delphi–DEMATEL Analysis of Critical Factors
abstract: ABSTRACT The circular transformation in the silk industry is crucial for enhancing resource efficiency and minimizing waste. Despite growing interest in circularity within the textile sector, the silk industry remains underexplored. This study addresses this gap by systematically assessing the barriers and enablers influencing circular economy adoption in silk. A two‐stage methodology was applied. title: The Promise and Perils of Private Enforcement under EU Law: The Digital Services Act in Context
abstract: Abstract This article offers a conceptual account of private enforcement under EU law, focusing on the DSA. It argues that the damages action under the DSA derives directly from Union law and cannot be reduced to a declaratory reference to national law. Situated within regulatory theory, it shows how private enforcement may complement public enforcement while raising concerns about access to justice, compliance incentives, and democratic legitimacy. journal: Cambridge yearbook of European legal studies

title: Assessing forest ecological sustainability through wavelet decomposition and stationarity tests: a comparative analysis of major forest product producers
abstract: Introduction Forest ecosystems are central to environmental sustainability, yet the persistence of forest-specific ecological conditions remains insufficiently explored, particularly across different time horizons. Existing research has predominantly examined CO₂ emissions and aggregate ecological footprint indicators, while relatively limited attention has been devoted to the stochastic properties and frequency-dependent persistence of forest ecological balance (FEB). This study addresses this gap by examining the temporal persistence of FEB in nine major forest product-producing countries—Au

title: Mechanisms of long-term degradation in plasticized PVDF pressure barriers under offshore service exposure
abstract: ABSTRACT Poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) is commonly used as a pressure sheath material in offshore flexible pipelines; however, there is limited experimental data from long-term service exposure. In this study, three PVDF layers recovered from a flexible riser after ten years of offshore operation were examined to understand the degradation mechanisms that occurred under field conditions. institutions: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

title: Flow Dynamics with Jet-induced Vortex Control in a Slotted Vertical-axis Wind Turbine
abstract: This study investigates the aerodynamic impact of passive blade slots on the unsteady flow dynamics of a Darrieus vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT) operating at low tip speed ratios. A two-dimensional URANS-based numerical investigation using the k–ω SST turbulence model was performed to analyze the creation of slot-induced internal jets and their interaction with the surrounding flow field. title: Bridging Albanian monitoring and Water Framework Directive oriented assessment: A surface water quality index
abstract: The implementation of the European Union Water Framework Directive (WFD) presents an important methodological challenge for countries whose established environmental monitoring systems are not yet fully harmonised with WFD compatible surface water body delineation and assessment structures.This situation is particularly relevant for EU candidate countries, where existing station-based monitoring programmes must increasingly support integrated river basin assessment and alignment with the environmental acquis.This study addresses this challenge by developing a composite surface water quality in

title: Energy expenditure of bonobos across their locomotor repertoire
abstract: Unlike quadrupedal mammals, primates use diverse locomotor modes adapted to arboreal environments. Such diversity of movements challenges allometric models, which underestimate energetic costs by focusing on steady-state walking. To address this, we combined ethological and biomechanical approaches to estimate the net metabolic cost of transport in bonobos (Pan paniscus). Using three-dimensional tracking and a point-mass model, we derived this estimate from net mechanical power and muscle efficiency across locomotor modes. title: Conservation genetics of the spotted bat: Insights from ancient, historical, and modern samples
abstract: Spotted bats (Euderma maculatum) are cryptic (nocturnal, volant, and roost solitarily) and thus their biology remains largely undescribed. Only 35 specimens were known to science before the mid-1960s. Hence, they are ideal candidates for genetic studies to uncover population genetic diversity and structure, and thereby inform conservation. title: Assessing earthquake potential and fault activity from a newly estimated high-resolution geodetic velocity field in Hispaniola
abstract: Abstract The transpressive plate boundary between the Caribbean and North American plates in Hispaniola is a complex system of strike-slip faults, subduction zones, fold-and-thrust belts, and normal faulting. Tectonic deformation studies in this region have traditionally relied on sparse Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) networks. Here we present a new assessment of deformation in Hispaniola using a dense 3D velocity field generated by integrating existing GNSS observations with new Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) velocities. title: Resolving sub-daily variability in the GPP–SIF relationship and its implications for GPP estimation at a temperate savanna site
abstract: Savannas cover approximately 20% of the global land surface and contribute nearly 30% of terrestrial net primary production, making them an important component of the global carbon cycle. Solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF), which is closely linked to photosynthetic activity, has shown considerable potential for estimating ecosystem gross primary productivity (GPP). However, temporal variability in the GPP–SIF relationship, particularly at sub-daily timescales, remains insufficiently understood, limiting the accurate estimation of high-frequency GPP dynamics. title: Improved desalination by polymer grafting
abstract: Freshwater scarcity demands desalination technologies that are efficient, scalable, and sustainable. Capacitive deionisation (CDI) is promising but remains limited by inefficient ion adsorption and poor charge utilisation. Here, we show that suitably chosen polyampholytic block copolymer grafting can substantially enhance CDI performance, via a combination of dipolar response and steric effects. title: A Parallel One‐Field Fictitious‐Domain Finite Element Method for Large‐Scale Fluid–Structure Interaction
abstract: ABSTRACT We present a distributed‐memory finite‐element framework for large‐scale incompressible fluid–structure interaction (FSI) based on a monolithic one‐field fictitious‐domain formulation. The velocity and pressure are defined on a fixed Eulerian background mesh and discretized using Taylor–Hood finite elements with quadratic velocity and linear pressure approximation, while the immersed solid is represented by an updated Lagrangian mesh. journal: International Journal for Numerical Methods in Fluids

title: Complementary root and mycorrhizal foraging strategies for phosphorus acquisition among arbuscular and ectomycorrhizal trees in a subtropical forest
abstract: Abstract Phosphorus (P) availability is widely recognized as an important constraint on plant growth in many subtropical forest ecosystems, yet how contrasting mycorrhizal strategies mediate the use of inorganic and organic P forms remains unclear. In a subtropical forest, we integrated a 50‐ha survey of adult tree dominance, a seedling growth survey across six 1‐ha plots and a shade‐house experiment to examine how arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) and ectomycorrhizal (ECM) trees adjust root‐fungal foraging strategies across gradients of inorganic and organic P availability. title: Spatiotemporal evolution and coupling of “Forest–Cropland–Water” ecosystem vulnerability in the Yangtze River Economic Belt
abstract: The Yangtze River Economic Belt (YREB), China's "golden waterway" and "green barrier", relies on its "Forest-Cropland-Water" system for carbon sequestration, grain production, and water conservation. Tracking its vulnerability and coordination on a spatiotemporal scale reveals barriers to balancing ecological security with sustainable growth. Our study innovatively proposes a multi-system coupling evaluation framework. title: Increasing exposure to potential flooding in high-mountain catchments
abstract: Abstract Exposure to flood hazards in high mountain catchments is expected to increase alongside natural hazards, driven by climate change, glacier retreat, and landscape evolution, yet temporally consistent, high-resolution exposure data remain scarce. Here we quantify changes in the exposure of buildings and people to flooding in Nepal and transboundary regions of India and China. Validation against a manually derived reference dataset revealed considerable differences in accuracy and completeness across five building footprint products. title: Physically constrained Mamba forecasting supports multiobjective reservoir water quality decisions
abstract: Reservoir water-quality management requires forecasts that remain dynamically plausible and scenario choices that balance water-quality objectives against the magnitude of requested trajectory change. Historical monitoring archives, however, rarely contain labelled control actions. We develop a physics-informed inverse-decision framework that combines a decomposition–interaction Mamba forecaster, observation-space oxygen-balance diagnostics, a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) and preference-conditioned multi-objective search. title: Effects of pre-harvest salicylic acid and irrigation interval on rhizome yield and phytochemical accumulation in Curcuma aromatica Salisb.
abstract: Curcuma aromatica Salisb. is a medicinal plant valued for its rhizomes rich in essential oils and phenolic compounds. This study aimed to determine (i) an optimal concentration of salicylic acid (SA) to improve plant performance and secondary metabolite accumulation, and (ii) the effects of different pre-harvest irrigation intervals on plants pre-treated with the selected SA concentration. Salicylic acid was applied as a foliar spray at 50, 100, 150 and 200 ppm at 18, 24 and 30 weeks after planting. title: Artifact-to-true seepage detection in RGB images using CLIP representations
abstract: Red-Green-Blue (RGB) vision based supervised learning is demonstrated for the purpose of identifying subsurface groundwater seepage for low-cost and accurate inspection of dams and slope embankments using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Supervised learning is constrained by the scarcity of confirmed true seepage-positive images. Our study investigates artifact-to-true seepage detection at the earliest intervention point. title: Agroecological zoning of mezcal and tequila agaves in Mexico through MaxEnt ecological niche modeling: Sustainability and climate resilience implications
abstract: Agave‑based distilled‑beverage production in Mexico, particularly mezcal and tequila, is facing intensifying sustainability challenges driven by climate change, monocropping expansion, and degradation of socio‑ecological systems. In this context, agroecological zoning represents a strategic tool for improving territorial planning and strengthening climate resilience. title: Flood risk assessment and protection measures in the Nura River basin, Kazakhstan
abstract: Spring floods represent one of the major natural hazards in snowmelt-dominated river basins of Central Asia. The Nura River basin in Central Kazakhstan is particularly vulnerable because of pronounced interannual runoff variability, limited reservoir regulation capacity, and the hydraulic connection between the Nura and Ishim river systems. This study aimed to provide an integrated basin-scale assessment of spring flood hazards and to identify key hydraulic constraints relevant to flood-risk management. title: Structure–Processing–Property Relationships in PVOH/PBAT Blends Plasticized with Dipentaerythritol, ε-Caprolactone, and Water
abstract: Abstract Water-soluble poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVOH) offers high tensile strength and an excellent oxygen barrier, but its dense hydrogen-bond network places its melting point close to its decomposition temperature, making it difficult to melt-process. Poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) is melt-processable and ductile but has low strength and dimensional stability that restrict its use.
