title: Life-cycle incremental cost-benefit model for passive buildings and a case study in Zhejiang Province, China
abstract: Passive buildings (PBs) offer substantial advantages in reducing carbon emissions and improving energy efficiency, making their promotion a strategic priority for China’s carbon goals. However, high upfront costs, unclear long-term benefits, and long payback periods hinder adoption. This study develops a Life-Cycle Incremental Cost-Benefit Model (LCICBM) covering design, construction, and operation. The model quantifies and monetizes economic, environmental, and social benefits. title: Understanding environmental adaptation in intermediate wheatgrass
abstract: Abstract Intermediate wheatgrass (IWG; Thinopyrum intermedium ) is a perennial grain crop that offers many environmental benefits through extensive root systems in addition to food production. IWG's distribution across broad environmental gradients in Eurasia provides a model system for studying climate adaptation genetics essential for developing climate‐resilient varieties, and exploring this can help provide opportunities for allele mining and population improvement for breeding programs. title: Plateau–Rayleigh Instability–Driven Shell-First Growth of (Ge, Si1– x Ge x )–AlN Core–Shell Crystals Exhibiting Telecom E-Band Photoluminescence
abstract: Abstract Si and Ge are technologically important semiconductors for electronic, photovoltaic, and optoelectronic applications. Herein, we report mixed-source hydride vapor phase epitaxial growth of (Ge, Si1–xGex)–AlN core–shell crystals on Al-based nanoabsorbers. Nano-CT and microscopy resolve hollow, partially filled, and filled morphologies that together support a Plateau–Rayleigh-instability-mediated shell-first model in which an Al-derived shell-like structure precedes filling by Ge-containing or Si–Ge-containing material. title: Detection of Personal Privacy Information in Social Data Taking Into Account Data Augmentation and Mask R‐ CNN
abstract: ABSTRACT Visual privacy‐sensitive objects in social images are often small, partially occluded, and unevenly represented in available training data, which limits the reliability of automatic privacy detection. This study develops a privacy‐sensitive object detection framework combining multi‐strategy image augmentation with SE‐Mask R‐CNN. title: Global disaster risk assessment from Emergency Events Database (2013–2023)
abstract: Abstract. This paper defines an Accumulated Risk Index (ARI) to quantify regional risk levels in a global perspective utilizing Emergency Events Database (EM-DAT) from 2013 to 2023. Building on the World Risk Index (WRI) released from World Risk Report 2023, the ARI focuses more on major events caused by multiple natural hazards within 5°×5° latitude-longitude grids, and calculates their accumulative effects during the period. title: Adaptive neuro-fuzzy risk index for safe and interpretable lane-change decisions in Level-3 autonomous driving
abstract: Introduction Highway lane-change maneuvers pose a safety challenge for SAE Level 3 autonomous driving because conventional threshold-based decisions and isolated surrogate safety measures may inadequately capture the coupling between longitudinal braking demand and evolving inter-vehicle gaps. This study develops an interpretable, risk-aware framework for continuous lane-change assessment during maneuver initiation and execution. title: Insights into life cycle assessment and rapid removal of malachite green by biochar derived from shrimp shell and sheep manure
abstract: Malachite green (MG) contamination of water resources poses significant ecological and human-health risks, while the environmental sustainability of its treatment strategies has rarely been evaluated. This study addresses this critical gap by integrating the synthesis of hybrid biochar from sheep manure and shrimp shells at a 2:1 ratio for MG removal with a comprehensive life cycle assessment (LCA). title: Rural place leadership across the Anglo-Scottish border: analysing the evolution, resilience and success of the Borderlands partnership
abstract: This paper explores the evolution of the Borderlands Partnership, a cross-border initiative seeking to address common challenges in the Anglo-Scottish rural periphery. Utilising a path-tracing methodology, a timeline was constructed to identify key events in the evolution of the Borderlands Partnership which created opportunity spaces for institutional entrepreneurship and generative place leadership. title: Economic Losses Associated With Tropical Cyclones in Mexico: A Two-stage Model
abstract: Tropical cyclones (TCs) are among the primary drivers of disaster declarations in Mexico, causing substantial economic losses. This study assesses reported TC-related economic losses in Mexican states from (Funk 1980 ) to 2023 and identifies the hazard and socioeconomic determinants of both the probability of loss occurrence and loss magnitude. title: Temporal dynamics and species-specific responses to biotic and abiotic drivers shape seedling establishment in a subtropical forest
abstract: Abstract Seedling establishment is a critical demographic bottleneck for species regeneration and diversity maintenance in forests, yet the temporal contributions of biotic and abiotic factors remain poorly understood. This is because most previous studies focused disproportionately on biotic factors or limited abiotic factors and used observational data lacking standardized baselines for seedling age. title: Study on students' exercise load monitoring in PE classroom based on the fusion of FedAvg and Grey relationship analysis
abstract: Real time observation of students' exercise load is very important for scientific sports teaching and injury prevention. However, the traditional centralized monitoring paradigm faces significant privacy challenges when it processes highly sensitive physiological and biological characteristics. At the same time, existing federated learning algorithms often degrade global model performance due to "client drift" arising from Non-IID data caused by individual differences among students. title: Forward self-similar solutions to the MHD-Boussinesq system with Newtonian gravitational field
abstract: This paper is concerned with the existence of forward self-similar solutions to the three-dimensional Magnetohydrodynamic-Boussinesq (MHD-Boussinesq) system with a Newtonian gravitational field. By employing a blow-up argument and the Leray-Schauder theorem, we construct a forward self-similar solution to this system without imposing any smallness assumptions on the self-similar initial value.

title: Robust site-specific radiometric calibration of PlanetScope NDVI using UAS-based reference data for precision agriculture
abstract: Index images provide opportunities for monitoring phenotypic characteristics such as plant height and disease symptoms, as well as the detection of pest presence. This allows for targeted application of agrochemicals and the implementation of preventive measures, leading to increased yields and reduced environmental impact. The study focuses on the radiometric inconsistencies between satellite-based imagery and high-resolution unmanned aerial system (UAS) imagery. title: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF GREEN SPACES AND THE URBAN HEAT ISLAND (UHI) EFFECT IN GEORGE TOWN, PENANG
abstract: This study investigates the influence of green space on environmental quality and its role in mitigating the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect, with a specific focus on George Town, Penang. By conducting a comparative analysis of two sites- Sia Boey Archaeological Park (Site A) and Little India (Site B)- within the urban setting, the research assesses variations in the Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), land surface temperature (LST), and the Urban Thermal Field Variance Index (UTFVI) to evaluate their respective UHI impacts. title: Endotoxins and Biological Implications—Review
abstract: Endotoxins, also known as lipopolysaccharides (LPSs), are structural components of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria and some cyanobacteria. They are among the most potent pyrogens and remain a persistent challenge in environmental, occupational, and clinical settings. This review brings together current understanding of their structure, stability, and methods of detection, while also highlighting the main routes through which humans are exposed. title: Bayesian‐Based Mixed‐Integer Optimization for Resonance Fatigue Testing of Large‐Scale Wind Turbine Blades
abstract: ABSTRACT Fatigue testing of large wind turbine blades is a critical step in ensuring their operational reliability, however, repeatedly developing loading fixtures for different test phases (such as static and fatigue testing) often entails significant time and financial costs. title: Tree-ring chronologies reveal unexpected geographic patterns of drought vulnerability in western Canadian forests
abstract: Adaptive reforestation under climate warming will increasingly involve northward or upslope movement of tree species and seed sources. However, in western Canadian boreal and sub-boreal forests, release from cold constraints may be offset by emerging drought limitations, where low evapotranspiration has historically supported tree growth despite modest precipitation. abstract: A key challenge in inferring gene regulatory networks (GRNs) governing cellular processes such as differentiation and reprogramming from experimental data lies in the impossibility of directly measuring protein dynamics at the single-cell level, which prevents establishing causal relationships between regulator activity and target responses. title: Atomic oxygen-induced oxidative degradation of carbamazepine: Mechanistic insights from reactive molecular dynamics
abstract: Abstract Carbamazepine (CBZ) is a persistent pharmaceutical contaminant that is poorly removed by conventional wastewater treatment processes. Although non-thermal plasma can promote efficient CBZ degradation, the elementary molecular mechanisms governing its initial oxidative transformation remain incompletely understood. title: Recharge Performance of Pond-Based Managed Aquifer Recharge in the Ramganga Basin
abstract: Groundwater underpins India's water and food security but faces growing stress from overexploitation and climate change. This study evaluates the hydrologic performance of small-scale, pond-based Managed Aquifer Recharge (MAR) interventions implemented under government development programs, in the context of India's plan to construct 14 million additional recharge structures. abstract: Abstract Environmental Input–Output Analysis (IOA) incorporates feedbacks in coupled economic-environmental systems, driven by an exogenous demand and fixed input–output coefficients with a linearity assumption. title: Association of Long-Term Residentially Assigned Speciated Atmospheric Mercury Emission Flux with All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality
abstract: Abstract Mercury (Hg) is a persistent global pollutant, but population evidence on residentially assigned species-specific atmospheric Hg emission flux and mortality is limited. We analyzed UK Biobank cohorts for all-cause/other-cause (N = 322,666), cardiovascular disease (N = 344,333), and cancer mortality (N = 381,432). Annual EDGAR v8.1 fluxes of total Hg, gaseous elemental Hg (Hg0), gaseous oxidized Hg (Hg2+), and particle-bound Hg (Hg–P) were assigned to geocoded residences. title: Between Custom and Sanction: Theft in the Vinodol Code and the Poljica Statute
abstract: This paper addresses the regulation of theft as an illicit act in two major medieval Croatian legal monuments: the Vinodol Code (1288) and the Statute of Poljica. Rather than offering a systematic comparison of legal systems, the study concentrates on the legal nature, normative structure, and penal treatment of theft within these statutory frameworks, situating the offence in its broader social and institutional context. title: The effects of asynchronous interruption on arc motion characteristics of a triple‑break medium-voltage DC air circuit breaker
abstract: Abstract Multi‑break DC air circuit breakers are subject to asynchronous interruption due to dispersion of operating mechanisms, resulting in nonuniform transient voltage distribution among the breaks and thereby compromising interruption reliability. A controllable two-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic-external circuit coupled model is established for a 9 kV/100 kA triple-break DC air circuit breaker composed of three series-connected independent arc chambers. title: Implementation of the EU Nitrates Directive in Germany—a critical review
abstract: Abstract Background Under the EU Nitrates Directive, Member States are required to adopt suitable measures to comply with the limit value of 50 mg NO 3 l −1 in groundwater. In Germany, the Fertiliser Application Ordinance (Düngeverordnung; DüV) defines the code of good agricultural practice with regard to nitrogen fertilisation. title: Performance Optimization and Prospects of Double Network Hydrogels for Flexible Electronic Devices
abstract: Dual‐network (DN) hydrogels possess tunable polymer network architectures, exceptional mechanical robustness, and superior water retention capability. They demonstrate substantial potential in structural optimization and performance stabilization, thus garnering widespread attention from both the academic and industrial sectors in the field of flexible devices such as supercapacitors, temperature sensors, and zinc‐air batteries. title: Learning-enabled collaborative intelligence in search and rescue robotics: a survey of paradigms, models, and challenges
abstract: Search and Rescue (SAR) robotics increasingly depends on collaborative intelligence to operate effectively in dynamic, uncertain, and time-sensitive environments. Modern SAR missions require coordinated interaction among heterogeneous robotic agents as well as structured collaboration between humans and intelligent systems for perception, decision-making, and adaptive mission execution. abstract: Bioprospecting for Cd-tolerant rhizobacteria that naturally inhabit cocoa (Theobroma cacao L.) soils contaminated with heavy metals contributes to the development of effective bioremediation strategies.The objective of this study was to select rhizobacteria from cocoa soils in Ecuador with the potential for Cd mitigation.Soil samples were collected from the provinces of Cañar, Esmeraldas, and Manabí.Morphological and biochemical characteristics, Cd tolerance, and molecular identification of the 16S rRNA gene were evaluated.Twelve rhizobacteria morphotypes were selected for their capacity to to

title: Assessing OpenStreetMap Road Currency with Sentinel-2 Time Series: Seven High-Growth Sites in Türkiye
abstract: OpenStreetMap (OSM) is the most widely used open road dataset, yet how late it records new roads is rarely measured. This study assesses the currency of the OSM major road network at seven high-growth sites in Türkiye by comparing monthly reconstructions of the map from its full edit history with Sentinel-2 summer composites of 2020, 2022, 2024 and 2025. title: The final count-down: estimating the total value of all the world's natural resources and an estimate of how long they may last
abstract: Introduction We have attempted a final count-down of all resources available to human society in future and converted this to monetary value for 2026. Methods Simulations using the WORLD7 Integrated Assessment Model explore how long the available resources will support wealth and value creation in the global society. title: Spatial differentiation and potential influencing factors of land-surface heat exposure based on street-view imagery: a case study of Luolong District, Luoyang
abstract: Introduction Against the backdrop of increasingly frequent extreme heat events, mitigating land-surface heat exposure on urban streets is crucial for safeguarding public health. Existing studies have often overlooked the spatially differentiated effects of complex street environments on land-surface heat exposure and the associated cooling thresholds. Therefore, this study takes Luolong District, Luoyang, as a case study to investigate the spatially heterogeneous effects and nonlinear threshold characteristics of street-view metrics on land-surface heat exposure. title: H–D Exchange in Ultraviolet-irradiated Water: Methane Ice Mixtures
abstract: Abstract The deuterium-to-hydrogen (D/H) ratio in solar system volatiles is commonly used to diagnose volatile formation conditions. This ratio may be altered by a range of processes under solar nebula conditions, however, including energetic processing of icy grains. In this study, we investigate the effects of ultraviolet (UV) irradiation on the H/D exchange in mixed methane–water ices, a model system for water and organics ice mixtures. title: Petrographic and magnetic fabric evidence for magmatic emplacement and hydrothermal alteration in the Shadan Au porphyry deposit, Eastern Iran
abstract: Magmatic processes and subsequent hydrothermal alterations within porphyry deposits are well-documented through the analysis of mineral chemistry and the magnetic fabrics of their host intrusions. This study integrates structurs, petrography, mineral chemistry, and anisotropy of magnetic susceptibility (AMS) data to investigate the evolution of magmatic and hydrothermal fabrics in the Shadan porphyry Au-rich deposit, located in northeastern Iran. Fresh quartz monzodioritic intrusions exhibit primary magmatic fabrics characterized by oblate AMS ellipsoids, predominantly aligned with magnetite.

abstract: The dynamic behaviour of fluid-conveying double-walled carbon nanotubes (DWCNTs) is important in nanoscale fluid-transport systems because fluid–structure interaction, interwall forces, size-dependent effects and environmental loading can significantly influence their vibration characteristics. Therefore, this paper aims to control the dynamic vibration of flowing fluid through DWCNT systems to enhance their integrity and reliability. title: Electrification reshapes BRICS vehicle urban mining: Material flows and circularity by 2050
abstract: Vehicle electrification is increasing demand for critical battery materials and shifting end-of-life management from whole vehicle scrap toward component-level streams, especially retired vehicle batteries. The five BRICS founding countries—Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa—represent a critical and diverse testing ground for this transition because they combine large and growing vehicle markets, divergent electrification pathways, and uneven recycling capacities. title: Frequency-aware Mamba and dynamic optimization DETR for real-time tiny-object detection in UAV aerial imagery

title: EnCost: uplink-cost-aware cluster-head selection with sink-trajectory look-ahead for energy-efficient mobile-sink wireless sensor networks
abstract: In a mobile-sink wireless sensor network (WSN), the cluster-head (CH)-to-sink uplink periodically enters the distance-fourth-power multipath regime, where electing a CH far from the sink incurs a disproportionate energy penalty. We propose EnCost-CR , a closed-form CH-selection rule that scores each node by its residual energy minus the modelled energy of the uplink it would pay as a head, instead of the normalized distance used by existing energy- and distance-aware rules. title: A Repurposed Drug Combination Overcomes Paclitaxel Resistance and Minimizes Toxicity via Dual Metabolic and pH Modulation in Breast Cancer
abstract: Background: Paclitaxel (PTX) remains a cornerstone in breast cancer treatment, but its effectiveness is limited by both chemoresistance and significant side effects. A promising strategy to overcome these challenges is to repurpose existing drugs. The present investigation sought to explore the combined anticancer efficacy of a new triple-combination treatment. included paclitaxel, dapagliflozin, and pantoprazole, specifically targeting MCF-7 breast cancer cells. and evaluated the safety profile of this combination in normal human foreskin fibroblasts (HFF). title: From raw occurrence records to accessible knowledge: Transforming biodiversity infrastructure through evidence-manifesting design
abstract: Biodiversity informatics has made occurrence records widely accessible, yet many databases remain optimized for human browsing rather than structured machine consumption by large language models (LLMs) and AI agents. This creates a bottleneck: analytical capacity is accelerating while biodiversity evidence remains fragmented, weakly documented, and difficult to cite reproducibly. title: Environmental Perception and Intelligent Navigation for Autonomous Delivery Robots in Complex Scenarios
abstract: Autonomous delivery robots (ADRs) face perception and navigation challenges in complex scenarios. When operating in real world urban environments, ADRs have trouble negotiating upturned streets, uneven terrain, and moving obstacles. This review covers three key areas: environmental perception, navigation techniques, and mechanical adaptability of delivery vehicles. title: A meteorological big data-driven method for generating chaotic time-series curves of power supply loads for wind-solar-storage hybrid systems
abstract: The wind-solar-storage hybrid system represents an efficient and clean energy supply mode. However, its power supply load is influenced by multiple factors and exhibits complex chaotic time-series characteristics, which pose significant challenges to system operation scheduling and load forecasting. abstract: Abstract Mefite d’Ansanto (Southern Apennines, Italy) is one of the largest known non‑volcanic CO 2 degassing sites worldwide. The degassing process observed here is widely recognized as the surface manifestation of the interaction between mantle-derived CO 2 and a complex shallow fracture network. abstract: A hierarchical nonlinear control benchmark is presented for gust load alleviation (GLA) and maneuver load alleviation (MLA) in a highly flexible winged UAV. title: Through-thickness inductive imaging for monitoring of features in thin-ply CFRP unidirectional tapes
abstract: Thin-ply unidirectional (UD) carbon-fibre reinforced polymer (CFRP) tapes enable improved mechanical performance in advanced aerospace structures but remain highly sensitive to manufacturing-induced defects. Reliable monitoring at the tape level is therefore essential to ensure consistent fibre distribution and prevent defect propagation into subsequent laminate assemblies. abstract: Abstract. Great Britain’s variable maritime climate has until relatively recently limited the utility of seasonal hydrological forecasts. The latest generations of seasonal atmospheric forecasting systems have created new opportunities to improve flow forecasting across Great Britain, such as for the UK Hydrological Outlook. abstract: Human populations across Eurasia have long been connected through the steppe corridor and Silk Road, yet their paternal genetic history remains poorly understood. We integrated large-scale Y-chromosome data, including 1053 previously unreported sequenced genomes, to reconstruct Eurasian spatiotemporal paternal phylogeny. abstract: Cryptography is essential in many digital fields to provide information security and confidentiality. abstract: Understanding how civilization development interacts with land use transformation is critical for advancing sustainable human–land governance. However, existing studies have largely examined land use transitions from socioeconomic or ecological perspectives, while the dynamic feedback mechanisms between multidimensional civilization development and land use behaviors remain insufficiently understood. abstract: Understanding the spatiotemporal evolution, convergence trends, and influencing factors of ecological efficiency in Chinese cities is crucial for achieving coordinated development between socioeconomic progress and the ecological environment. This paper assesses the ecological efficiency level of 279 prefecture-level cities in China by adopting the super-efficient EBM model. abstract: Capsicum, often known as sweet pepper (Capsicum annuum var. grossum L.), is becoming more and more popular in Bangladesh as a vegetable. abstract: Hybrid design approaches are essential for developing porous lattice structures with integrated multifunctional performance. title: Distribution of TENORM-contaminated soils in residential areas of Bangka Island, Indonesia
abstract: Radioactive contamination in residential areas of Bangka Island, Indonesia, a major tin- and rare earth-producing region, has rarely been studied, although material stored near mineral-processing workshops may pose a long-term health risk. We collected 46 soil samples around 9 mineral-processing workshops in the Selindung District, Pangkal Pinang City: residential soils from 20 locations at two depths (n = 40) and 6 workshop-related sediments. abstract: Urban resource environment carrying capacity (RECC) is increasingly challenged by nonlinear interactions among socioeconomic development, resource depletion, and geological environmental degradation. However, existing assessments often neglect the cumulative feedback effects of groundwater depletion and geological responses. abstract: Abstract Understanding how fire activity reorganizes across space is key to interpreting long-term interactions among climate variability, land-use change, and integrated fire management in Brazil. Yet this reorganization is difficult to read directly: annual maps of millions of burn scars saturate the national territory, and year-to-year spatial shifts are visually indistinguishable at that scale. abstract: Reliable bedrock-depth information is essential for foundation design and seismic site characterization, yet borehole-only investigations provide sparse coverage and active-source surface-wave surveys may lack the low-frequency energy needed to resolve deeper interfaces. abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is primarily identified through behavioral and developmental assessment, which may require specialist expertise and considerable time. Electroencephalography (EEG) offers non-invasive neurophysiological information, but reliable ASD classification remains challenging because EEG signals are nonstationary and highly variable across individuals. abstract: This study examines the impacts of climate change on blue water flow (BWF), green water storage (GWS), and green water flow (GWF) components of water resources in the Tekeze Atbara watershed of the Nile basin. abstract: Abstract Amber is one of the most important national treasures in Lithuania, as well as in some other Baltic countries. In the recent era, some other materials that resemble amber have been introduced in the market, which are sometimes sold as real amber. abstract: Abstract High-entropy materials have emerged as a versatile platform for electrocatalysis because their multicomponent nature enables broad tunability of electronic structure, adsorption energetics, lattice distortion, defect chemistry, and chemical functionality. abstract: Abstract Remote-sensing-based slope stability monitoring is vital for railway safety. abstract: Abstract The meaning of targets in data-driven mineral prospectivity mapping (DD-MPM) is foremost dependent on the quality of data. abstract: Övergången till en cirkulär ekonomi har lett till en ökning av sysselsatta inom sektorerna återanvändning, avfallshantering och återvinning, sektorer där det tycks finnas betydande hälsorisker. abstract: Abstract How the convergent strain between the India Plate and the Tarim basin is partitioned by active faults and off‐fault deformation in southwestern Tibet is poorly understood due to limited knowledge of strain localisation and fault kinematics. title: Blue‒green water demand, water footprint, and productivity: an experimental study for effective agricultural water management in a semi-arid area of southern Ethiopia
abstract: Water scarcity constrains agricultural production in semi-arid regions and particularly affects water-sensitive crops such as haricot bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.). abstract: This study investigates the wood anatomical diversity and functional trait coordination of eight co-occurring timber species in a North Ecuadorian seasonal tropical rainforest, an ecosystem heavily influenced by the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ). We integrated traditional qualitative and quantitative descriptions under International Association of Wood Anatomists (IAWA) standards with the advanced multi-table Structuring de Tableaux à Trois Indices de la Statistique (STATIS DUAL) framework to resolve three-dimensional structural relationships without external environmental datasets. abstract: Digital transformation reshapes global economic paradigms and offers a pathway for resource-dependent regions to transcend the “resource curse.” By leveraging panel data from 111 Chinese resource-based cities between 2011 and 2019, this study empirically examines whether the burgeoning digital economy facilitates departure from resource-dependent stagnation. abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Environmental gradients structure plant communities at fine to coarse scales. Along elevational gradients, abiotic conditions influence community assembly by filtering species based on their functional strategies, which themselves may be phylogenetically structured. title: تقييم العلاقات بين عمق المظهر الهوائي والعوامل البيئية بناء على نموذج الانحدار الموزون جغرافيا وزمنيا (دراسة حالة: محافظة السليمانية، العراق ( 2020/2025)
abstract: عمق البصريات الهوائية (AOD) هو أحد المؤشرات المهمة لتقييم حمل الهباء الجوي وظروف الغبار في المناطق الجافة ونصف الجافة. وبالنظر إلى التباين الطوبوغرافي والمناخي والبيئي لمحافظة السليمانية في العراق، وتعريضها لنقل الغبار، كان هدف الدراسة الحالية تقدير AOD ودراسة التغير المكاني والزماني لتأثير العوامل البيئية باستخدام نموذج الانحدار الموزون جغرافياً وزمانياً (GTWR). في هذه الدراسة، تم نمذجة AOD باستخدام خمسة متغيرات تفسيرية تشمل رطوبة التربة وسرعة الرياح ومؤشر الغطاء النباتي المختلف المعياري (NDVI) ودرجة حرارة سطح الأرض (LST) وهطول الأمطار خلال فترة ست سنوات (2020-2025). تم تقييم أداء طريقة المرب

title: Team cognition in remote maritime operations: a scoping review and cross-domain theoretical synthesis
abstract: Introduction Remote maritime operations increasingly depend on complex, distributed socio-technical systems in which safe and effective performance relies on team cognition rather than on individual decision-making alone. Despite its importance, the conceptualisation and measurement of team cognition in this domain remain fragmented and underdeveloped. Methods A scoping review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). abstract: ABSTRACT Detection of magnetic nanoparticles (MNP) relies on their nonlinear magnetic response, changing with the local environment in vivo. Employing an effective viscosity model within stochastic coupled Néel–Brownian simulations, we quantify how viscosity (0.8–50 000 mPa·s) affects signal intensity of single‐frequency magnetic particle spectroscopy (MPS, 25 kHz) and frequency‐mixing MPS (FM‐MPS; f H = 40.5 kHz, f L = 0.063 kHz). title: Signatures of photospheric convection throughout the solar atmosphere: the EVE Sun-as-a-star mHz continuum
abstract: Abstract Convectively driven motions in the solar photosphere can generate broadband Doppler variability across the chromosphere, transition region and corona. Here we investigate this variability using “Sun-as-a-Star” observations from the Extreme Ultraviolet Variability Experiment (EVE) aboard the Solar Dynamics Observatory, constructing high signal-to-noise Doppler power spectra by incoherently averaging spectra from 3-hour sequences of the centroid wavelengths of emission lines that span wavelengths 35–104 nm. The spectra reveal a broad power-spectral continuum with two “Harvey” components
journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

title: Risk-aware hierarchical reinforcement learning for investment and operations in cross-border energy supply chains under the belt and road initiative
abstract: Abstract Cross-border energy supply chains under the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) face unprecedented challenges, including geopolitical instability, macroeconomic volatility, and operational disruptions. Traditional optimization or flat reinforcement learning (RL) methods often struggle to address the scale, uncertainty, and multi-stakeholder complexity inherent in such environments. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) framework that separates strategic investment planning from tactical operational control via a two-level archi
institutions: Changsha University of Science and Technology

title: Can the digital economy enhance urban ecological environment resilience?
abstract: Abstract Enhancing urban ecological environment resilience enables cities to more effectively withstand, adapt to, and recover from external risks and disturbances, thereby safeguarding the stability and sustainability of urban ecosystems. Investigating the impact of the digital economy on ecological environment resilience and its underlying mechanisms can further enrich our understanding of the environmental effects of digitalisation. title: A two-stage cascaded prediction framework for urban inundation depth using a dual-branch CNN-ConvLSTM network
abstract: Study region Shenzhen, China, is a densely urbanized subtropical megacity characterized by extensive impervious surfaces, rapid runoff responses, and frequent rainfall-induced inundation. Study focus To address the underestimation of urban inundation depth driven by severe zero-inflation, this study proposes a two-stage Cascaded Multi-scale CNN-ConvLSTM Network (CMC-Net). A Random Forest classifier first identifies hazardous inundation samples using a 0.15-m threshold. institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Staged digital transformation and firms’ total factor productivity: evidence from Chinese cultural firms
abstract: This study explores the effects of digital transformation (DT) on firms’ total factor productivity (TFP) across the digital technology application (DTA) stage and digital business model innovation (DBMI) stage. Using a sample of 245 Chinese listed cultural firms from 2011 to 2022, we examine how DT impacts TFP differently across these stages. The results show that DT significantly enhances firms’ TFP in both the DTA and DBMI stages. However, productivity gains materialize only after firms reach the transformation threshold in both stages. title: Detection of old-growth forests using airborne laser scanning and other auxiliary data combined with National Forest Inventory field plot data
abstract: Accurate detection and mapping of old-growth forests (OGFs) are essential for biodiversity conservation and forest management, yet remain challenging due to their structural complexity, rarity and varying definitions. In this study, we developed a framework for classifying OGFs in boreal forests by integrating airborne laser scanning (ALS) data, and multispectral Sentinel-2 imagery and aerial imagery with different modelling approaches. OGF classes were defined using Finnish National Forest Inventory data (26,411 plots) based on structural naturalness, deadwood continuity and human impact, res

title: A dual-functional antiviral and anticancer peptide to target intricate host-pathogen interacting proteins of human papillomavirus associated with head and neck cancer
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma is increasingly being reported worldwide, and a major contributing factor is the incidence of human papillomavirus infections. The viral infection activates proto-oncogenes and signalling mechanisms aiding in tumorigenesis. An efficient way to block the virus-induced carcinogenesis is to identify a common medicament that can effectively inhibit the viral and host proteins. In the present study, HNSCC transcriptomic profiles and HPV genes involved in host-pathogen interactions were retrieved. The overexpressed HNSCC genes were further considered for host-pa

title: Spatiotemporal mapping of agricultural drought using geospatial approach in the East Bale Zone, Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Agricultural drought significantly threatens food security, livelihoods, and ecosystem stability, especially in regions prone to drought, such as the East Bale zone. This study investigates the spatial and temporal patterns of agricultural drought over 30 years (1993–2024) by combining meteorological station data with satellite‐derived vegetation and thermal indices. To assess meteorological drought, the standardized precipitation index (SPI) was calculated at 3‐, 6‐, and 12‐month intervals. For agricultural and thermal stress analysis, remote sensing‐based indices including the veget

title: Microenvironment Design and Regulation of M‐N‐C Catalysts for Oxygen Reduction Reactions: Mechanisms, Synergies, and Future Pathways
abstract: ABSTRACT Fuel cells represent the core components of next‐generation high‐efficiency electrochemical energy conversion technologies. The performance of the cathode oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) catalyst determines battery efficiency and lifespan. Thus, developing efficient, cost‐effective ORR single‐atom catalysts is essential for fuel cell commercialization. title: Spatiotemporal patterns and driving mechanisms of cultivated land multifunctionality evolution: evidence from county-level data in Sichuan Province, China
abstract: The pursuit of socioeconomic development, food security, and ecological sustainability has driven the multifunctional evolution of cultivated land. Under the constraint of limited cultivated land resources, achieving synergy among the economic, food security, and ecological functions of cultivated land has become a major challenge for agricultural modernization in Sichuan Province. This study evaluates the spatiotemporal evolution of cultivated land multifunctionality (CLM) and investigates the driving mechanisms underlying the CLM synergy level. The results show that: (1) The overall CLM deve
institutions: Vaughn College of Aeronautics and Technology
Southwestern University of Finance and Economics

title: Climate policy uncertainty and agricultural digital-intelligent transformation in China: evidence from provincial panel data
abstract: Introduction Climate policy uncertainty can affect long-term investment decisions in agriculture, yet its influence on agricultural digital-intelligent transformation remains insufficiently understood. This study examines how lagged climate policy uncertainty affects agricultural digital-intelligent transformation and whether rural finance and agricultural service policies can moderate this relationship. Methods Using panel data from 31 Chinese provinces from 2013 to 2022, we construct an agricultural digital-intelligent transformation index. A two-way fixed effects model, instrumental variabl

title: Urea-loaded nanoclay biopolymer composites integrated with beneficial microbes enhance nutrient uptake and mitigate greenhouse gas emissions
abstract: Low nitrogen use efficiency of prilled urea contributes to substantial economic loss and environmental pollution through leaching, denitrification, and ammonia volatilization. This study evaluated urea-loaded nanoclay biopolymer composites (NCBPCs), synthesized from clay-acrylic acid + aczrylamide-based polymer composite grafted with maize flour (NCBPC-M) and mango kernel flour (NCBPC-MK), integrated with phosphorus- and zinc-solubilizing bacteria ( Lactococcus lactis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa ), as a sustainable alternative nitrogen source in a maize–wheat cropping system. title: Maternal edible THC consumption alters offspring neurodevelopment and emotional behavior in rhesus macaques
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prenatal cannabis exposure is associated with adverse offspring outcomes including altered neurodevelopment. However, there is insufficient evidence to establish a direct association. We sought to determine the impact of chronic prenatal delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) exposure on offspring neurodevelopment and emotional behavior in a translational rhesus macaque model. METHODS: Animals were divided into two groups, control and THC-exposed, with both groups receiving a daily edible (placebo or THC) pre-conception, throughout pregnancy, and postnatally. title: Unstable Vortices, Sharp Non-Uniqueness with Forcing, and Global Smooth Solutions for the SQG Equation

title: Robust and replicable effects of ageing on resting-state brain electrophysiology measured with MEG
abstract: Abstract Non-invasive recordings using brain electrophysiology provide credible insights into decline in neuronal functioning with age. New approaches are required to translate these results into compelling clinical metrics and meet the global challenge of preserving brain health in ageing. Changes in neuronal dynamics with ageing are observable in the power spectra of EEG and MEG recordings. Highly promising candidates for electrophysiological markers have been identified, but progress is hindered by substantial methodological variability across studies. title: Wave-induced erosion and notch development at the Fimbul Ice Shelf front
abstract: Abstract. Ocean waves erode the waterline of Antarctic ice-shelf fronts and carve a thermo-erosional notch. The notch is hidden from satellites, yet it preconditions front collapse and footloose calving, so the link between notch growth and observable front retreat matters for how wave-exposed ice shelves lose mass. We study this link at the Fimbul Ice Shelf, East Antarctica, in January–February 2024. The widely used White et al. title: Tame Discrete Sets on Affine Semisimple Homogeneous Spaces
abstract: Winkelmann conjectures that every smooth flexible complex affine variety of dimension at least two is a Rosay--Rudin space. We verify this for every positive-dimensional quotient $G/H$ with $G$ a connected complex semisimple algebraic group and $H$ a closed connected reductive subgroup. title: Gen-EBM: an energy balance model for terrestrial planets. Climate multistability from snowball to post-runaway greenhouse climates
abstract: Climate multistability and tipping points are fundamental properties of planetary climates that depend sensitively on climate feedbacks. We introduce the Geneva Energy Balance Model (Gen-EBM), a new 1-D latitudinal EBM for rapid exploration of terrestrial planet climates, and use it to investigate how planetary rotation, eccentricity, and thermal inertia shape climate attractors and multistability. title: Global well-posedness for the 2D primitive equations with subcritical horizontal dissipation
abstract: We establish global well-posedness of classical solutions to the two-dimensional primitive equations with fractional horizontal dissipation for arbitrarily large initial data in the full subcritical range $1<α\leq2$. Together with the known ill-posedness results for $0\leqα<1$, this establishes the sharp dissipation threshold for large-data global well-posedness in the corresponding solution framework. title: Global Existence and Partial Regularity for the Three-Dimensional Chemotaxis--Navier--Stokes System in a Half-Space
abstract: We establish endpoint partial regularity for suitable weak solutions to the three-dimensional chemotaxis--Navier--Stokes system with constant sensitivity and linear consumption in a half-space under no-slip and no-flux boundary conditions. The full space--time singular set, including its boundary part, has vanishing one-dimensional parabolic Hausdorff measure. abstract: We study global regularity and the infinite Prandtl number limit for temperature patches of the two-dimensional nondiffusive Boussinesq system on $\mathbb R^2$, with velocity dissipation $Λ^{2α}$, $\frac12<α\leq1$. We establish global well-posedness for $θ_0\in L^1\cap L^\infty$ and divergence-free $u_0\in W^{1,p}$, $2\leq p<\infty$. title: Model-Order-Adaptive Channel Estimation for AFDM Systems with Fractional Delay and Doppler
abstract: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) has emerged as a promising waveform for high-mobility communications owing to its ability to exploit multipath diversity. However, channel state information (CSI) acquisition remains challenging in channels with fractional delay and Doppler and an unknown number of propagation paths. In this paper, we investigate the channel estimation for AFDM systems. We first analyze the AFDM response in the presence of fractional-delay-induced frequency wrapping. title: Spectral gap for the stochastic primitive equations under degenerate Brownian forcing
abstract: We prove a weighted Wasserstein spectral gap for the three-dimensional primitive equations on $\mathscr E=\{u\in H^1\cap L^8: \partial_zu\in L^4\}$ under finite-rank additive Brownian forcing that is phase-complete finite Fourier and satisfies a quantitative quadratic saturation condition. In particular, four real forcing directions suffice and this number is optimal within the phase-complete class. title: MUNITE: Unified Multimodal Latent Inference for Any-to-Any Multimodal Generation
abstract: We introduce MUNITE, a latent-variable framework for flexible any-to-any multimodal generation that treats encoding and latent generation as the same inference problem under different amounts of observed evidence. Given any subset of modalities, MUNITE models the conditional distribution over the latent representation associated with the complete observation. abstract: We prove instantaneous loss of Sobolev regularity across a fixed gap for the inviscid surface quasi-geostrophic equation on $\mathbb R^2$. title: Enhanced analogue quantum computation with a logically-encoded XX gadget
abstract: The introduction of two-body XX interactions has been shown to improve the performance of quantum annealing in solving certain combinatorial optimisation problems and would enable the simulation of a broader class of many-body Hamiltonians. Due to experimental constraints, such interactions are typically not natively available on analogue quantum devices. To overcome this limitation we introduce the truss gadget. title: Binary Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes in 3+1 numerical relativity: mergers, fly-bys and gravitational waves
abstract: We present what are, to our knowledge, the first 3D numerical-relativity evolutions of wormhole binaries: pairs of massive Ellis-Bronnikov drainholes held open by a ghost scalar field. Each throat is an unstable fixed point whose e-fold time matches the González-Guzmán-Sarbach linear rate to within 1.9%. title: Multi-scale spectral statistics of intermediate quantum chaos in ultracold erbium collisions
abstract: Characterizing intermediate quantum chaos in systems with mixed phase spaces requires probing spectral correlations across multiple scales. Here, we present a multi-scale statistical analysis of the resonance spectra of ultracold 166Er and 168Er atoms using higher-order spacing ratios, spacing increments, and the accumulated power spectral density of decimated level sequences. title: Optimal Control of Prox-Regular Sweeping Processes with Variable Time
abstract: The paper is devoted to a broad class of optimal control problems governed by constrained sweeping processes with controlled dynamics, controlled prox-regular moving sets, and variable time included in the optimization process. Employing an advanced version of the method of discrete approximations, we verify its well-posedness with appropriate strong convergence of feasible and optimal solutions. title: The TIB Terminology Service and Its Terminology Collection for the Earth System Sciences
abstract: Advancing Earth System Sciences (ESS) depends on our ability to integrate highly diverse data from a range of disciplines, including geographical information sciences, palaeontology, marine science, biodiversity research, atmospheric sciences and biology. A major scientific obstacle to this integration is semantic heterogeneity: different disciplines use different methods and terms to describe data, resulting in fragmented vocabularies. We address this challenge by providing the ESS terminology collection, which is a source of state-of-the-art terminologies for this scientific community. This
institutions: Senckenberg - Leibniz Institution for Biodiversity and Earth System Research

title: Threshold Type Responses of Indo Pacific Coral Reefs to Local Human Induced Degradation
abstract: Coral reef ecosystems face cumulative pressures from ocean warming, ocean acidification and diverse coastal human disturbances. As ecologically critical habitats and socio economic resources for coastal human communities, reef systems require improved understanding of how local anthropogenic activities drive degradation trajectories. Existing monitoring datasets covering the Indo Pacific region provide large scale observational evidence to disentangle reef responses against human related stressors and distinguish threshold driven shifts from gradual dose response decline. title: From Digital Visibility to Completed Purchase in Online Retail
abstract: Online enterprises can buy digital visibility before they have earned confidence in the transaction that follows. This study develops and tests a dual pathway model in which digital promotion shapes purchase intention through attitude, while perceived transaction security operates through trust and post-purchase satisfaction. The model also separates purchase intention from completed-shopping behaviour, allowing the analysis to identify where favourable evaluation fails to become action. title: The bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) international database: an update and ongoing call for data
abstract: The Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis International Database (BIAID) is an initiative aimed at pooling, standardizing and harmonizing bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) data across populations. This report provides a synthesis of the data currently available in the BIAID and an overview of the actions undertaken to date. The repository, which is based on raw bioelectrical values as minimal required data, has expanded over the past two years to include 321,680 individuals across the lifespan, encompassing both healthy and clinical populations and representing all WHO regions. title: Governing access: Freedom of information, knowledge politics, and the limits of transparency in public health research
abstract: Introduction Freedom of Information (FOI) laws are presented as mechanisms of transparency and democratic accountability, yet their operation as tools of public health research remains under-examined. This study examines how FOI regimes shape, rather than simply enable, researchers’ access to institutional knowledge across Nigeria, the United Kingdom (UK), and the United States (US).Theory Drawing on governmentality and epistemic injustice, FOI is conceptualized as a site of knowledge governance through which legal exclusions, commercial secrecy, bureaucratic discretion, and institutional prac

title: From emergence to exposure: one health attribution of azole-resistant Aspergillus fumigatus in Southeast Asia
abstract: Southeast Asia is a hotspot for azole-resistant Aspergillus fumigatus yet remains underrepresented in global surveillance. Disciplinary approaches, including genomics, environmental sampling, and social science, have progressed but remain poorly integrated. We outline a One Health attribution framework linking selection pressures, environmental reservoirs, exposure pathways, and clinical resistance signals to prioritise surveillance, target interventions, and allocate resources where they will have greatest impact.

title: Ocean sunfish M. mola in the Mediterranean Sea: Shedding light on an enigmatic species through 14 Years of spatial and environmental assessment
abstract: The ocean sunfish M. mola is frequently sighted in marine waters worldwide, including the Mediterranean Sea, yet information on its distribution and ecology in this region remains limited. This study synthesizes current global knowledge on M. mola and investigates its spatial occurrence in the Mediterranean Sea using long-term visual observations from the Fixed Line Transect Mediterranean Monitoring Network, complemented by environmental DNA (eDNA) samples collected through the Life Conceptu Maris project. title: Keadilan Sosial dalam Pendidikan Bahasa: Interseksi Ras, Etnisitas, Gender, dan Seksualitas di Asia Tenggara
abstract: Keadilan sosial dalam pendidikan bahasa di Asia Tenggara menjadi isu kritis di tengah keberagaman etnis, bahasa, dan budaya kawasan. Penelitian ini mengkaji interseksi ras, etnisitas, gender, dan seksualitas dalam pendidikan bahasa di Asia Tenggara melalui tinjauan literatur sistematis. title: Coastal residents’ support for marine spatial planning: The role of values, place attachment, and community impacts
abstract: Coastal environments worldwide are subject to rapid transformations, including to mitigate against climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution. The potentially significant impacts of these transformations on coastal communities makes it imperative to understand their response to Marine Spatial Planning (MSP) decisions. title: Data Sharing in Nigerian Genomics: Addressing Legal Fragmentation and Ethical Dilemmas
abstract: This study examined the legal and ethical challenges associated with genomic data sharing in Nigeria with focused on issues of consent, privacy, data ownership and international collaboration. Using doctrinal method, the study reviewed scholarly literature, national policies, institutional practices and international instruments to identify gaps in genomic data sharing. title: Coastal Vegetation as Nature-Based Solutions: A Bibliometric and Proxy Matrix Review of Ecosystem Services and Coastal Protection
abstract: Climate change and coastal development are intensifying coastal hazards and increasing the need for evidence-based Nature-based Solutions (NbSs) in integrated coastal zone management. However, proxy-based evidence for evaluating the ecosystem services and coastal protection functions of coastal vegetation has not been systematically synthesized across these dimensions. This study combined bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer and CiteSpace with metadata-based proxy matrix analysis of 643 English-language Web of Science articles published between 1995 and March 2026. title: Current gender equality status in EU blue economy – Gaps and recommendations for a more inclusive and fair sector
abstract: Gender equality and the empowerment of women are core priorities of the European Union. However, strategic sectors such as the blue economy remain comparatively underexplored in terms of structural and cultural barriers to female participation with both traditional and emerging industries being still male dominated. Against this backdrop, this paper presents the findings of a systematic review of publications from 2010 to 2024 addressing gender equality issues in the European Union blue economy. title: Implementing Bow-tie analysis to assess the main concerns regarding biodiversity change in European Seas
abstract: Marine biodiversity is adversely affected by many human activities and their pressures. As such, there is the need for a cause-consequence-response method to objectively address the risks associated with those adverse changes. Such a method is the ISO-accredited Bow-tie technique as an objective and structured approach giving the causes, preventative control measures, mitigation and compensation measures and consequences of changes to biodiversity. title: From Scientific Evidence to Regulatory Action: Emerging Contaminants and Adaptive Water Governance in Brazil
abstract: Contaminants of emerging concern (CECs), including pharmaceuticals, synthetic hormones, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), bisphenol A, antibiotic-resistance determinants, and microplastics, are increasingly reported in Brazilian aquatic environments, yet the federal water-quality instruments examined here address them only in part. This review maps a structured, traceable body of evidence on CEC occurrence in Brazilian waters and examines how far that evidence has been translated into monitoring, standards, and treatment requirements. title: eData: A tool and format for rapid extraction of exposure data from scientific articles
abstract: Extracting and formatting data is among the most tedious elements of assessing environmental chemical occurrence and exposure. We present a toolkit (eData) to streamline this process, generate FAIR data, and maximise traceability and transparency: a FAIR Data Reporting Format (DRF) that provides data structure, vocabulary, and validation, and a Large Language Model (LLM)-based data extraction application that quickly formats literature data. title: Design and expert validation of the OEPR learning model for sea turtle conservation educational tourism in Pacitan, Indonesia
abstract: Background Sea turtle conservation sites can function as authentic learning environments, but educational visits frequently remain informal, knowledge-centred, and disconnected from sustained participation. This study developed and established the initial content validity of an experiential learning model for conservation-based educational tourism at Taman Beach, Pacitan, Indonesia. title: The obvious clue is not always the truth: evidence chains and misdirection in a marine pollution investigation game
abstract: In Last 3 Days , players investigate unusual marine animal deaths by examining samples and comparing test results with collection locations and reports. This paper analyses how the game's evidence chain develops from these comparisons, with particular attention to clues that suggest an incomplete explanation. Plastic inside a fish and an injury associated with a fishing net indicate harm to individual animals. abstract: Abstract When is a price just? This paper develops a new theory of justice in pricing, grounded in the Austrian market process tradition. abstract: ABSTRACT Floods rank among the most frequent and widely managed hazards worldwide. title: Occupational Stress and Psychological Well-Being among Seafarers
abstract: Seafaring is a demanding occupation characterized by prolonged periods away from home, long and irregular working hours, physical workload, fatigue, confined living conditions, limited shore leave, and reduced social interaction. These conditions can negatively affect the mental and physical health of seafarers and increase their vulnerability to psychological difficulties. abstract: For most of the post-Cold War era, the Arctic was governed as an exception to great-power politics: a “zone of peace” in which scientific cooperation, not strategic rivalry, set the tone. That exception is closing. As Arctic Amplification strips away the ice that once made the region marginal, it is exposing a geography rich in shipping lanes, hydrocarbons, and critical minerals, and drawing the United States, Russia, and China into overlapping contests for military advantage, economic access, and legal control. abstract: The role of Cabinet in the implementation of fisheries legislation and the promulgation of regulations relating to fishery-related offences remains under-studied. abstract: Introduction: This paper explores the intersection of ecopreneurship and sustainable business practices through the lens of Northeast Indian literature. abstract: Sustainable local economic development at the village level requires a balance between community welfare, environmental protection, and effective local governance. In Madura, the utilization of natural resources remains insufficiently aligned with environmental carrying capacity, creating challenges for achieving sustainable village development and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). abstract: Sathurukondan wetland in the Batticaloa District contains valuable mangrove resources, yet baseline ecological information remains rather scarce. abstract: Abstract The Antarctic region exerts a profound influence on the Earth system, making its conservation fundamental to sustaining planetary health and human wellbeing. The Antarctic Treaty System (ATS) holds near-exclusive authority for environmental protection across the region, yet questions remain regarding its capacity to address a growing range of conservation threats. title: How does climate risk affect fisheries? New evidence from the operating cash flows of Chinese listed firms
abstract: Listed fisheries companies depend heavily on natural conditions, leaving their operations particularly exposed to climate change. Using Chinese listed fisheries companies as the research sample, this study examines the effect of regional climate risk on operating cash flow and investigates potential mitigating mechanisms. The results show that regional climate risk significantly reduces operating cash flow. abstract: An estimated one billion children live at extremely high risk of adverse effects from climate change. abstract: Today European ports have moved beyond their traditional role as logistical gateways to become strategic infrastructure for energy, supply-chain resilience and urban development. In this context, port competitiveness can no longer be understood only in terms of logistical performance but must be assessed within a governance model capable of integrating environmental sustainability and territorial resilience. abstract: Geoscience in Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) operates amid persistent variability that challenges the continuity, credibil-ity, and public value of scientific work. This paper analyzes the resilience of the geoscience enterprise in the region—how science is designed, conducted, synthesized, and shared to serve public mandates—under shifting political, institutional, economic, environ-mental, and social conditions. abstract: ABSTRACT Magnesium–aluminum‐layered double hydroxides (MgAl‐LDHs) are used in flame retardants, remediation, and catalysis. Sustainability comparisons of industrial routes are insufficient. This study couples techno‐economic analysis with life cycle assessment (LCA) to evaluate two routes (hydrothermal synthesis and modification) at 1000 t/a using industrial data. abstract: Knowledge plays an important role in Disaster Risk Management (DRM). abstract: For decades, plant biology has relied on a narrow set of classical model organisms—such as Arabidopsis thaliana, Oryza sativa, and Zea mays —to uncover core physiological, developmental, and molecular pathways. abstract: Tourism is a pivotal driver of economic growth, cultural preservation, and social cohesion. abstract: The leopard tortoise (Stigmochelys pardalis) is the only large tortoise in southern Africa and is the most widespread of any sub-Saharan testudinid. title: Integrating Socioscientific Issues into Cypriot Science Education: Preparing Students for a VUCA World
abstract: In a world of rapid technological advancements and global challenges, education must equip students with the skills to navigate complexity, uncertainty, and ethical dilemmas. This paper explores integrating socioscientific issues (SSIs) into the Cypriot primary science curriculum to foster critical thinking, ethical reasoning, and interdisciplinary learning. The paper analyses the curriculum’s theoretical foundations, goals, and con- tent and identifies existing strengths and areas to enhance, preparing students to en- gage with real-world scientific and societal challenges. title: Sharing the benefits and costs of conservation: public preferences for transboundary lynx policy
abstract: Transnational conservation is becoming ever-more important, yet reaching consensus on international conservation agreements remains challenging when decision-makers prioritise national benefits. Whether such approaches align with public preferences, however, remains unclear. We conduct a Discrete Choice Experiment to understand preferences for Iberian lynx conservation in Spain and Portugal, with a focus on the distribution of costs and benefits across countries. title: Sustaining A World -Class Destination: A Comprehensive Assessment Of Tourism Challenges In Bali
abstract: Abstrak: Bali is one of the world's leading cultural tourism destinations and has attracted millions of international and domestic visitors for decades. Tourism has become the primary driver of Bali's economy and a significant contributor to Indonesia's national tourism sector. Despite its international success, Bali faces a range of sustainability challenges that may threaten its long-term competitiveness as a global tourism destination. title: Network diagnosis and governance-coupled optimization in seaport–dry port multimodal transport corridors under the Maritime Silk Road
abstract: Research into seaport–dry port corridors has tended to focus on the design of the physical network on the one hand and the coordination of governance on the other. It is hard to maintain this separation in well-established Maritime Silk Road corridors. A corridor might have routes, inland nodes and digital platforms, and still not function smoothly at the rail/dry-port interface. This article therefore tackles corridor optimization as a problem of diagnosis and governance. title: Divergent narratives: community perceptions of illegal bushmeat hunting dynamics in the Serengeti-Mara ecosystem
abstract: Conservation outreach programs (COPs) aim to reduce illegal bushmeat hunting by providing communities with tangible benefits and fostering positive attitudes toward wildlife, but their influence is difficult to separate from law enforcement and wider social change. We compared how COPs beneficiary and non-beneficiary communities perceived and explained illegal bushmeat hunting dynamics in the Serengeti-Mara ecosystem across 2018-2024. Using a comparative mixed-methods design, we surveyed 360 households (180 per category), conducted 12 focus group discussions, and interviewed 24 key informants

abstract: Background. Complementary feeding practices and timing are thought to significantly influence early life immune development, with the early introduction of allergenic foods being especially important for prevention of food allergy. We hypothesized that allergen-containing foods such as peanut, tree nuts and sesame may indirectly influence the immune system via their effects on gut microbiota composition and metabolism. Methods. title: ISLAMIC ARBITRATION (TAḤKĪM) AND INTERNATIONAL COMMERCIAL ARBITRATION: COMPATIBILITY AND INTEGRATION IN PAKISTAN’S LEGAL SYSTEM
abstract: International Commercial Arbitration has become the foremost means of dispute resolution in a globalized economy because of its efficiency, impartiality, and enforceability; yet, in Pakistan, the functioning of international commercial arbitration creates legal and theological complications on account of the coexistence of Islamic arbitration (Taḥkīm), an Islamic dispute resolution system founded on Sharī‘ah principles. title: Collateralization of the Body in the Central Sahara: On Forms and Effects
abstract: ABSTRACT This article tracks a transporter along the route linking Tripoli to the Saharan town of Ghadames in post‐2011 Libya, asking what secures an obligation when the institutions that normally underwrite it (offices, courts, recognized names) have receded. I distinguish the debt, the sum owed, from the security pledged to answer for it: what may be taken if the owing fails. To collateralize is to fix that security beforehand, and I follow this act along a road where enforcement is personal. title: Wastewater irrigation effects on contaminant fate soil quality nutritional traits and human health risks in rice agroecosystems with emphasis on microplastics
abstract: Freshwater scarcity, rapid urbanization, and rising agricultural demand have increased interest in wastewater irrigation, especially in water-intensive rice systems. Wastewater reuse can support crop production through nutrient recycling and reduced fertilizer dependence, yet it also introduces a persistent mixture of contaminants into soil–plant systems. title: Vertical distribution of pollution trapped by wintertime surface inversions in Fairbanks, Alaska, during the ALPACA experiment
abstract: Abstract. Air pollution in cold wintertime urban areas is a ubiquitous problem. Surface temperature inversions under low wind conditions and surface emissions lead to the formation of a shallow polluted surface layer (PSL). The presence of this PSL is well documented, but its height, the rates of exchange with the background atmosphere, and the interplay between vertical mixing and chemistry remain poorly quantified. abstract: LLMs are increasingly being embedded into a variety of distributed agentic systems, in the form of agents with APIs, microservices, workflows, and external tools for task completion. Systems need to be able to handle requests that are worded differently but mean the same thing, to make sure routing is consistent, caching can be reused, latency is reduced, reliability is ensured, and governance is supported. title: Oil and Gas Governance in the Nigerian Petroleum Industry: Imbibing the Good Governance Concept
abstract: This study appraised the governance structure in Nigeria petroleum industry, and as contained in the recent enacted PIA 2021 which is now the principal legal instrument as far as Nigeria’s petroleum industry is concerned. The challenges faced by regulators of the petroleum industry, being integral part of the system, are highlighted. It is observed that in seeking to proffer solution to tackle the problems facing Nigeria’s ailing petroleum industry the Norwegian model was resorted to. The Norwegian model consists of separation of roles and responsibilities into commercial, policy and regulator
journal: JOURNAL OF LAW AND GLOBAL POLICY

title: Reservoir-computing-based chaos synchronization and its application to medical image encryption
abstract: Abstract Chaos synchronization provides a physically interpretable route for generating common dynamical states at spatially separated terminals, but most existing schemes require an accurate model and explicitly injected actuation. This paper develops a data-driven synchronization framework based on reservoir computing (RC) that learns nonlinear state couplings directly from observed trajectories. title: Climate Litigation and Constitutional Courts: Advancing Intergenerational Environmental Rights Through Constitutional Adjudication
abstract: Climate change has intensified the need for legal frameworks that recognise environmental protection as an essential component of constitutional governance. In recent years, climate litigation has emerged as a significant pathway through which constitutional courts interpret and enforce environmental rights, particularly in relation to future generations. This paper examines how constitutional adjudication has contributed to the development of intergenerational environmental rights within environmental constitutionalism. title: In Hot Water? The Macroeconomic Impacts of El Niño
abstract: Despite their potentially major impacts, little is known about how El Niño impact the U.S. economy. El Niños are distinct from other commonly studied weather shocks because they are a global phenomenon, unfold over a period of months, can be forecast months in advance, are relatively infrequent, and have very different effects on weather outcomes depending on the time of year and region. These features make traditional analytical methods ill-suited to studying the economic impacts of El Niño events. title: Spatiotemporal modelling of post-COVID recreation reveals persistent and emerging pressures on freshwater ecosystems
abstract: Restrictions during the COVID-19 pandemic pushed large numbers of recreationists towards freshwater ecosystems, but whether this shift was temporary or lasting has remained unclear. Using 129045 freshwater-related Wikiloc records (2016–2024), we modelled how recreation changed in time and space along the entire river network of the Catalan River Basin District (NE Spain), separating the pandemic effect from the platform's own growth. journal: Journal of Outdoor Recreation and Tourism

title: The evolution of Pakistan and China’s engagement with Afghanistan since 9/1
abstract: This study examines how Pakistan’s and China’s interests toward Afghanistan have evolved since 9/11 in pursuit of their security and political and economic objectives. Existing scholarship tends to treat Pakistan–Afghanistan and China–Afghanistan relations separately and rarely trace continuity and change across the whole post-9/11 period. title: Biodiversity conservation and its associations with economic performance, inequality, and peace
abstract: Abstract Biodiversity conservation is increasingly recognized as a product of coupled social–ecological systems shaped not only by ecological processes, but also by economic capacity, social inequality, and geopolitical stability. Here, we examined whether national conservation performance is systematically associated with economic prosperity, income inequality, peace, and the importance of natural resources in the national economy across 142 countries. title: İngiliz Hukukunda Başkasının Haksız Fiilinden Doğan Sorumluluk (Vicarious Liability) Doktrini Çerçevesinde Otonom Gemilerde Donatan ve Uzak Operatör Arasındaki İlişkinin Değerlendirilmesi
abstract: Otonom gemilerin geliştirilmesinde temel odak noktası, bu gemilerin değişen derecelerde insan etkileşiminden bağımsız olarak hareket edebilmeleridir. journal: İstanbul Medeniyet Üniversitesi Hukuk Fakültesi Dergisi

title: Lightweight visual detection approach for apple ripeness perception in intelligent orchard harvesting scenarios
abstract: Apple ripeness detection in complex orchard scenarios is plagued by fruit occlusion, overlapping, intense illumination interference, and subtle maturity feature differences among similar fruits. Conventional lightweight detection models also suffer from low accuracy and severe feature loss in field environments. To address these problems, this paper proposes a real-time lightweight method for apple ripeness detection with optimized multi-dimensional network structures, which balances lightweight deployment and feature perception capability for complex orchard backgrounds. title: Virtual recreation of urban heritage of Jingdezhen for immersive VR display
abstract: To unify the decoupled dimensions of scientific rigor and contextual narrative in virtual heritage display, this paper uses the VR project developed for Jingdezhen’s bid for World Cultural Heritage as a case study, and establishes a workflow for the virtual recreation of urban heritage that includes data collection and processing, spatial script, virtual reconstruction, and asset production. title: Infrastructure and Inclusiveness in Election Administration: Insights from India’s General Elections
abstract: The Lok Sabha (Lower House of Parliament) elections of India, represent the world’s largest democratic exercise, requiring an extraordinary scale of logistics, manpower and infrastructural readiness. This paper analyses the operational magnitude of Lok Sabha elections by assessing candidates, electors, polling stations, mobility assets, observers, surveillance teams, home-voting facilities, etc. The findings suggest that India's electoral process is characterised by a strong emphasis on inclusiveness and involves substantial human and material resources and elector-friendly polling stations. title: Neotypification of Three Names in Myristica (Myristicaceae)
abstract: ABSTRACT In absence of the original materials, neotypes are proposed for three names. These are Myristica cagayanensis, Myristica hellwigii , and Myristica sulcata. These neotypifcations will be helpful in correct application of these three names.

title: A Curated Library Collection: Pacific Records and the Australian Joint Copying Project, 1939–54
abstract: This article examines the identification and acquisition of documents for the Australian Joint Copying Project (AJCP) from 1939 to 1954. It argues that the AJCP’s evolving scope reflected Australia’s shifting geopolitical identity and intellectual ambitions in the Pacific. Initially shaped by librarians’ efforts to address a national shortage of research materials, the AJCP expanded after World War II with the involvement of the Australian National University’s Research School of Pacific Studies. Drawing on administrative records and policy manuscripts held at the National Library of Australia

abstract: Abstract In 2024, the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) adopted two landmark treaties, the Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge (GRATK Treaty) and the Riyadh Design Law Treaty (DLT), that collectively advance the international legal framework for protecting genetic resources (GRs), traditional knowledge (TK), and traditional cultural expressions (TCEs). title: BIOSECURITY IN THE INDO-PACIFIC: BIOLOGICAL RISKS, REGIONAL COOPERATION, AND STRATEGIC COMPETITION
abstract: The Indo-Pacific is a major centre of global population, trade, and strategic competition, but it also faces growing biological risks from disease outbreaks, animal diseases, laboratory accidents, and the deliberate misuse of biological agents. This study examines how biological risks interact with regional cooperation and strategic competition in the Indo-Pacific. It addresses the problem of uneven regional cooperation, particularly in sensitive areas such as laboratory oversight, information sharing, and biosecurity governance. title: Nepalese Calamity of 2026: Manmade or Climate Driven
abstract: The flash floods of August 26, 2026, along the Nepal-Tibet border are one of the most devastating Himalayan disasters since the 2015 earthquake. Some believe that the event was driven by anthropogenic activities. Others attribute it to climate change. To have greater clarity of the primary cause and to draw lessons for the future, this paper examines the catalysts behind the disaster. Although the primary geological event may have been rooted in climate change, the catastrophic scale of downstream destruction seems to have been greatly amplified by manmade vulnerabilities. title: First evidence of Tahyna virus in Central Italy and seasonal dynamics of its putative vector, Aedes caspius
abstract: Tahyna virus (TAHV) is a neglected mosquito-borne Orthobunyavirus pathogenic to humans. In Italy, TAHV was first recorded in Friuli Venezia-Giulia and then repeatedly in Emilia Romagna Region (Northern Italy). This study was set up to verify the presence of TAHV in Central Italy and to identify its potential vectors. title: Access and Benefit Sharing in India: Reconciling Biodiversity Conservation, Sustainable Development and Community Rights
abstract: International environmental law has historically centered on the control and ownership of natural and biogenetic resources. Numerous environmental conventions have addressed this question, prioritizing benefit-sharing mechanisms. Among these, Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) emerged as a key solution, aiming to balance the interests of developed and developing nations while conserving biodiversity.
