title: Nature and interbeing: an ecocritical-postcolonial reading of Thich Nhat Hanh's poetry
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this research article is to explore nature and interbeing in the poetic works of Thich Nhat Hanh within the context of ecocritical-postcolonial theories. Design/methodology/approach This research article is designed to discuss two key dimensions: nature as a witness to war and colonization, and interbeing as ecology's resistance to colonial violence. title: Soil proteogenomics uncover microbial strategies for soil depth-specific carbon cycling under whole-soil warming conditions
abstract: Soils are Earth's largest carbon reservoir, yet microbial mechanisms controlling decomposition, and their warming response, remain poorly resolved, especially in subsoils. Using genome-resolved proteogenomics within a replicated whole-soil warming experiment (0-90 cm, +4 °C, 7.5 years) we map microbial traits, their depth stratification, and warming responses. title: Motif Migration and Visual Sovereignty: Chinese Export Porcelain and Early Modern Global Exchange
abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines Chinese export porcelain as a site of transcultural image production and proposes motif migration as an empirically grounded framework within global art history. Focusing on the Maritime Silk Road from the seventeenth to the nineteenth century, the study moves away from diffusionist and hybridity‐based explanations that frame decorative imagery as either copied or stylistically merged. title: An interaction perspective on situation awareness in human–AI teaming: A scoping review
abstract: Situation awareness (SA) is crucial for effective teaming and is becoming increasingly relevant in human-AI teaming as AI systems take on more active roles. AI systems rely on designed interactions to communicate information and coordinate with humans, which may influence how human teammates perceive, interpret, and anticipate task situations. title: Dual‐Timescale–Based Cache and Bandwidth Control Scheme in Integrated Satellite‐Terrestrial Networks
abstract: ABSTRACT Recently, the integrated satellite‐terrestrial network (ISTN) system offers a promising solution for extending wireless communication services to remote and underserved areas. To effectively provide a variety of services, it is essential to cache the corresponding services on satellites while dynamically allocating the satellite bandwidth. title: Prehistoric global migration of vanishing gut microbes with humans
abstract: The gut microbiome is crucial for health and is affected strongly by lifestyle1. Many microorganisms commonly found in non-industrialized populations are disappearing or have become extinct in industrialized populations2–6. Studying which microorganisms have been long-term residents of the human gut and may have co-evolved with humans2,7,8 could provide insights into how microbial biodiversity loss affects human health. title: Prioritizing climate-resilient housing recovery in conflict-affected Yemen: a district-level MCDA and uncertainty framework
abstract: Abstract Yemen’s housing recovery requires choices among districts where flood exposure, conflict, displacement and humanitarian need overlap. This study develops a district-level multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) framework to identify districts that remain high priorities for early climate-resilient housing recovery under alternative assumptions. The model combines seven dimensions: flood hazard, human exposure, built exposure, climate stress, conflict fragility, displacement pressure and humanitarian severity. title: Prospects and complexities in sustainability impacts of global residue-based bioenergy deployment
abstract: Amid rising global demand for sustainable energy, agricultural and forestry residues (AFRs) emerge as a key yet underutilized resource in energy transition. Mechanisms of how optimizing multipath AFR utilization advances sustainability contributions in varied socioeconomic contexts remain underexplored. title: Temporal and spatial variation characteristics of environmental iodine elements in the Gansu region, China
abstract: Objective This study investigates the spatiotemporal variation of iodine concentrations in drinking water and soil across Gansu Province, aiming to generate observational evidence for adjusting iodine deficiency disorder (IDD) prevention strategies, given inherent methodological limitations of historical unpaired cross-sectional surveys. Methods We collected data on water iodine from four surveys (1972, 1985, 2014, and 2017) and soil iodine from two surveys (1985 and 2014) in Gansu Province, along with related information. title: Reframing antimicrobial resistance as a land-system challenge through environmental pathways and climate interactions
abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a planetary health challenge, yet land-system change remains overlooked. This review examines how agriculture, urbanisation, waste management, deforestation, aquaculture and climate-driven transitions shape resistance through altered input intensity, habitat reorganisation and enhanced connectivity. It identifies evidence gaps across vulnerable settings and proposes pathway-based surveillance, integrated datasets, longitudinal studies and coordinated interventions to reduce resistance selection, persistence and transmission across connected landscapes

title: The prince and the scientists
abstract: Scientific institutions pose a peculiar leadership challenge: their ultimate purpose, scientific discovery, cannot be commanded or predicted. I argue that scientific leadership is less about exercising authority than about cultivating the trust, diversity, interactions and intellectual freedom from which scientific excellence can emerge.

abstract: Este artículo analiza la resignificación de un proyecto de escritura académica auténtica en un primer año universitario ante la irrupción de la Inteligencia Artificial Generativa (IAG). Basado en las alfabetizaciones académicas y el potencial epistémico de la investigación, lectura, escritura, oralidad y argumentación, el trabajo da cuenta del triple desafío que implica para los estudiantes elproceso de investigación teórica y empírica de un tema en profundidad, la comunicación de los resultados a través de una ponencia y su socialización en unas Jornadas Académicas. title: Advanced oxidation processes for 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid in aqueous media: evidence gaps, mechanistic insights and emerging directions
abstract: Abstract The herbicide 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) remains a relevant aquatic contaminant because parent-compound disappearance does not imply mineralization, detoxification or treatment readiness. This systematic review synthesizes recent evidence on advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) and closely related chemically coupled routes for aqueous 2,4-D treatment. title: Distinct prosocial behaviors associated with persistent symptom trajectories in psychiatric disorders
abstract: Prosocial behavior, the tendency to act for others' benefit, is essential for mental health. Although social contexts strongly shape prosocial behavior in healthy individuals, its relevance across psychiatric disorders remains unclear. We examined whether context-dependent prosocial behaviors were associated with baseline psychiatric symptoms and longitudinal symptom trajectories. title: Spatiotemporal patterns of antimicrobial resistance in shared human-animal waterpoints in the Maasai Mara Ecosystem, Kenya
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) presents an existential One Health threat. The spread of AMR in arid and semi-arid landscapes is modulated by ecological interactions and exacerbated by endemicity of livestock diseases and poor sanitation in shared human-animal systems leading to misuse of antibiotics. This study characterized the prevalence, resistance patterns, and spatiotemporal variations of AMR in surface water sources in the Maasai Mara Ecosystem (MME), a rapidly changing water-stressed socio-ecological landscape. title: Research on Communication Signal Coverage Methods Based on Recursive Genetic Algorithms
abstract: The availability of communication signals for dense wireless local area networks (WLANs) is being increasingly hindered by spectrum contention, interference, and traffic dynamics. Side effects of coverage can also be captured by higher layers, such as the transport or application layer; however, their sensing capabilities are limited, and their information may be strongly biased by the network conditions or the user traffic. title: Habitat Suitability Modeling of Bombus affinis under Climate Change
abstract: The North American bumble bee Bombus affinis (B. affinis) is an important wild pollinator that has experienced severe population declines since the late 20th century. However, spatially explicit assessments of how climate change and human activities jointly shape its distribution remain limited, constraining forward-looking conservation planning. abstract: Early human history shows that humans have always tended to survive by overcoming basic needs. However, as it transited into the neolithic age, the motivation of consumption has evolved beyond satisfying the basic human needs. Humans prioritized possessing properties including environmental resources. title: Decontamination Risk Management in Radioisotope Facilities: A Bibliometric Review
abstract: Background: Risk management in the decontamination process of radioisotope and radiopharmaceutical production facilities has garnered significant research attention due to its vital contribution to environmental safety and occupational health. While the volume of literary evidence regarding radiation safety continues to expand, study focuses and methodological approaches remains diverse. title: Fiduciary Internationalism: Reimagining the Trusteeship Council as a Representative Organ for the Voiceless
abstract: The Trusteeship Council, originally established under Chapter XIII of the UN Charter to supervise trust territories and guide them toward self-government or independence, has become largely dormant since the completion of decolonization. This article argues that the Council, rather than being treated as a historical relic, can be reconceptualized as a functional institutional mechanism to address persistent representation gaps in international adjudication. title: Topology-Aware Grey Wolf Optimization for Energy-Efficient and Stable Routing in 6G Cyber Defense Networks
abstract: 6G cyber defense networks have many challenges that make it difficult to ensure safe and efficient routing. These challenges come from the topology that changes constantly, the very dense connectivity that exists, the strict requirements for latency, the limited resources for energy, and the continuous exposure to various cyber threats which include jamming, spoofing, malicious relays, and denial-of-service attacks. title: Distribution, habitat, and population dynamics of the European weatherfish (Misgurnus fossilis L., 1758) in the north-easternmost part of Germany
abstract: This study analyses a distribution database of fishes and cyclostomes from the German federal state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and evaluates a monitoring programme initiated in 2008, with a focus on the ecology of the European weatherfish. Over 35 years, the species was recorded across nearly the entire state, but it was rarely found in high abundances. title: Likelihood assessment of major urban public health emergencies based on an improved fuzzy Bayesian network
abstract: Preventing and controlling major public health emergencies is a prerequisite for ensuring high-quality urban development. title: Highly pathogenic avian influenza as a systemic risk - implications for control and preparedness
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) has evolved from episodic outbreaks into a globally entrenched, multi-host panzootic, with recurrent spillover into mammals. Using an exploratory qualitative case study design, this research compares resilience dynamics in Shenzhen (high resilience), Bandung (medium resilience), and Dhaka (low resilience). abstract: Abstract Background Global identity (GI), a sense of belonging to a global society, is gaining attention as a key factor for promoting pro‐environmental behaviours (PEB) to tackle the global environmental crisis. Among such global predicaments, plastic waste and pollution remain pressing issues. Although prior research has established a link between GI and PEB, the underlying psychological pathways have not been comprehensively explored. title: Catchment hydrologic function is widely time-variant
abstract: Abstract Catchment hydrologic function describes how meteorological conditions are transformed into streamflow. Whether this transformation is stable or varies from event to event, and what controls that variability, remains unknown at the global scale, limiting confidence in flood-risk and water-security assessments. Here, we analyze about 1.7 million runoff-producing events across 4838 catchments on six continents. title: Constitutional Right to Land in Nigeria and Kenya: A Comparative Analysis
abstract: This article critically appraised constitutional right to land in Nigeria and Kenya. There is a constitutional right to land in Nigeria and Kenya respectively. Therefore, every citizen of Nigeria has the constitutional right to acquire and own land in any part of the country as guaranteed under the provision of section 43 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended). title: Uncovering the role of biogeography, resources, food web composition and time during microbial primary succession
abstract: Ecological succession is shaped by multiple processes that operate simultaneously across spatial and temporal scales. While classical succession theory generally focuses on a single trophic level within a single location, often in plants or other macroscopic organisms, recent efforts have extended this framework to microorganisms across multiple ecological dimensions. The aquatic micro-ecosystem within the pitcher plant, Sarracenia purpurea, provides a natural model of primary succession replicated across a continental latitudinal gradient. title: Protocol for integrative transcriptomic/metabolomic analysis: A case study on factors influencing the oyster-POMS disease
abstract: Deciphering the molecular mechanisms underlying complex biological interactions requires comprehensive approaches that capture these interactions across multiple regulatory and functional levels. Here, we present a protocol applied to the host-pathogen-environment interactions underlying Pacific oyster mortality syndrome (POMS) in Magallana gigas . title: Weaving History: A New Historicist Dialogue on Power, Anxiety, and Spider Imagery in Whitman and Yuan Mei
abstract: This study aims to examine the spider imagery in Walt Whitman’s and Yuan Mei’s poetry through a New Historicist lens. It reveals the role this imagery plays in a cross-cultural dialogue on power and anxiety. By integrating Foucault’s “power discourse”, Greenblatt’s “cultural negotiation” and Althusser’s “symptomatic reading”, the analysis proceeds from imagistic essence to strategic deployment and finally to structural metaphor. title: Beauty–bloodbath, vulnerability–vengeance: Representations of Draupadi in popular culture
abstract: This article examines postcolonial feminist re-imaginings of Draupadi, a central figure in the Mahabharata, across contemporary genres, specifically Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni’s novel The Palace of Illusions (2008), Mahasweta Devi’s short story “Draupadi” (1981), and Saraswati Nagpal’s graphic novel Draupadi: The Fireborn Princess (2012). Through a conceptual framework of four metaphoric binaries: “Beauty–Bloodbath and Vulnerability–Vengeance”, it interrogates the construction of female agency, mythic symbolism, and embodied resistance in a postcolonial feminist context. title: Beyond participation: procedural justice, relational legitimacy, and sustained engagement in evaluating the effectiveness of DDR programs
abstract: Evaluation of disarmament, demobilization, and reintegration (DDR) programs tends to focus on weapons collection, demobilization of combatants, reduction of violence, and participation in programs. These measures provide less insight into why people remain engaged in peacebuilding implementations after the programs have concluded. Drawing on qualitative data from Nigeria’s Niger Delta Presidential Amnesty Program, this article develops a procedural justice–relational legitimacy–sustained participation framework. title: Understanding and Rationalising the Relationship Between Global Environmental Politics, Mainstream, and Alternative Theories in a Globalised World
abstract: Global environmental politics is a field that combines the analysis and evaluation of environmental politics and policies with their practical application. While governments and wellknown political leaders are usually the focus of the traditional political perspective, nontraditional players like online-based civil society organisations are becoming more and more important in environmental politics at all levels. title: Balancing Profit and Planet: Introducing the CARE Framework for Firms' Ethical Climate Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate change presents an urgent ethical and strategic challenge for contemporary business, demanding responses that are both morally grounded and competitively viable. This paper proposes the CARE framework, Comprehend , Align , Refine , and Evaluate , a structured model for ethical climate strategy rooted in resource‐advantage ( R‐A ) theory and foundational ethical principles. Drawing on a systematic literature review and illustrative case analysis across firms such as Tesla, GM, Toyota, and Interface, the framework integrates normative reasoning with strategic action. title: Ecological responses of soil bacteria to rapid and slow temperature fluctuations
abstract: Fluctuating temperatures profoundly affect microorganisms' coexistence, biogeographic distributions and responses to future climate change. However, how microorganisms respond to fluctuating temperatures with different frequencies in natural communities remains unknown. We conducted a 120-day temperature manipulation experiment with soil-bacterial communities subjected to constant low, medium and high temperatures, as well as fluctuating temperatures with three different frequencies. title: Funny Bones
abstract: Judging from the sway of dystopian and (post)-apocalyptic scenarios in contemporary Anthropocene fiction, our concern for climate change and ecological upheaval has been particularly receptive to narrative forms derived from the catastrophic imaginary, with comic modes often getting evicted from the province of environmentalist thought. Chris Flynn’s novel Mammoth (2020) is a notable exception, deploying humor to culturally process loss, (ecological) grief, and memory. title: Proposed Culturally Responsive Skill Learning Device for Vocational Education Learners in India: A Mixed Methods Design and Feasibility Study Protocol
abstract: India’s vocational education and training settings serve learners with varied languages, prior work experiences, and access to digital resources. This proposed protocol describes the planned development and feasibility evaluation of a culturally responsive skill learning device. The device is conceived as a portable, offline-first aid for practical competency modules; it has not yet been built or tested. The protocol does not report study findings. title: The Role Of Trust In Mediating Price And Service Quality On Consumer Decisions To Use Gojek Online Transportation Services In Denpasar City
abstract: Background: The development of digital technology has driven changes in consumer behavior in using online transportation services. This study aims to analyze the influence of price and service quality on consumer decisions, with trust as a mediating variable, among Gojek users in Denpasar City. Method: The research method used was a quantitative approach with a survey technique on 200 respondents selected using purposive sampling. abstract: This study evaluates the spatio-temporal impacts of coal mining on environmental conditions in the Talcher coalfield region, India, using multi-temporal Landsat data (2000, 2014, and 2023) at 30 m resolution. Land use land cover (LULC) was derived using supervised classification (Maximum Likelihood Algorithm), while vegetation dynamics and thermal characteristics were assessed using the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Land Surface Temperature (LST). abstract: Objective: This bibliometric study presents a detailed research trends of current state on next generation bioresorbable, biocompatible and conductive polymeric drug delivery systems have evolved.By evaluating global research scientific output, this paper tracks how research area evolved from fundamental core-shell drug delivery architectures that have passive drug-encapsulating mechanics towards complex polymer-based structures that are highly responsive to their local biological environment.Methods: Studies from 2008-2026 were collected from Scopus database and analysed using Microsoft Excel

title: Quantifying the contribution of vegetation layer uncertainty to simulated forest fuels treatment placement
abstract: Background Western US forests face rising high-severity fire risk motivating increased investment in forest management. The high cost of treatments and vast areas needing work require efficient resource allocation. Forest landscape models can help scale up analysis and support management, but underlying uncertainties can limit their utility. title: Primal intellectual property rights: Re‐envisioning modern paradigms through a protodesmic perspective
abstract: Abstract Intellectual property (IP) is frequently approached through its codified forms and formal institutions, with less attention to the deeper social foundations from which protection of intangible creations arose. This study considers an earlier layer of such protection, termed primal IP rights, formed among communities that safeguarded creative works through custom, oral tradition, and social regard before the advent of codified law. title: Modeling microbial regulatory feedback in organic matter decomposition identifies copiotrophic traits as key drivers of positive priming
abstract: Abstract Microbial decomposition of complex soil organic matter (OM) is often regulated by labile organic carbon inputs, a phenomenon known as priming, which plays a critical role in belowground biogeochemical cycling. However, the strength and direction of microbial priming of soil OM pools varies significantly across ecosystems. abstract: This study provides a systematic exploration of whether neighbourhood-level built environment factors are associated with mental health service (MHS) utilisation by Indigenous peoples in South-East Queensland, Australia, while controlling for individual socio-demographic factors. title: Learning to Live Well With Places: Socio‐Ecological Systems Modeling for Just and Sustainable Futures
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper advances Systems Modeling for Just and Sustainable Futures (SMJSF) as a conceptual framework for ethical and epistemic socio‐ecological modeling in field‐based science education. Emerging from a decade of participatory, design‐based research co‐designed with youth, families, educators, and researchers within the Learning in Places project, we argue that SMJSF is both a representational activity and a relational process through which learners make sense of and act within the intertwined systems that sustain life. abstract: Introduction Medical image analysis is a significant research domain in contemporary healthcare systems, which helps to accurately diagnose diseases and support clinical decision-making. This domain consists of important operations, including image enhancement, fusion, segmentation, morphological processing, and denoising, which assist in the effective understanding of complex biomedical information. title: Soil metabarcoding reveals the distinct microbial signature of a remnant forest patch at a local restoration initiative in the Ecuadorian Chocó
abstract: The Tumbes-Chocó-Magdalena hotspot is a globally recognized center of endemism that is undergoing severe deforestation. While conservation and restoration efforts typically prioritize the recovery of aboveground macroscopic biodiversity, the response of soil microbial communities remains largely uncharacterized in this region. abstract: Nigeria's persistent fiscal crisis, characterized by escalating debt burdens exceeding 100% of revenue and chronic budget deficits, reflects a fundamental governance failure rooted in a systemic trust deficit rather than merely technical economic challenges. abstract: Abstract The May Measurement Month (MMM) campaign was conducted in Ecuador in 2023 to raise awareness of raised blood pressure (BP). Adults aged ≥18 years were recruited through convenience sampling at sites in Ecuador, primarily focusing on major cities and surrounding areas such as Quito, Riobamba, Guayaquil, Milagro, Loja, Duran, Cerecita, and Huaquillas. EXAMINING FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS JURISDICTION OF FEDERAL HIGH COURT AND STATE HIGH COURT IN NIGERIA
abstract: The constitutional jurisdiction of the Federal High Court and State High Courts in the enforcement of fundamental rights in Nigeria presents an important intersection between constitutional rights protection and the allocation of judicial jurisdiction. Section 46 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended) empowers a person alleging that a provision of Chapter IV has been, is being, or is likely to be contravened to apply to a High Court in the relevant State for redress. title: Influenza vaccine protection and contact patterns among outpatients with influenza-like illness during the 2024–2025 season in China: a test-negative case-control study
abstract: Background: Continuous monitoring of both influenza vaccine protection and behavioural determinants of infection is important for understanding related risks. Evidence on influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) in China during the 2024-2025 season, however, remains limited. We aimed to assess influenza VE among healthcare-seeking outpatients with influenza-like illness (ILI) and to examine the contact patterns associated with infection risk. abstract: The Earth Commission has proposed that 20-25% of every square kilometre of managed lands, including in cities, be reserved for nature to ensure its local functioning and human wellbeing -biosphere functional integrity boundary (BFI). This research adopted a multi-method justice-oriented approach grounded in the Earth System Justice framework to assess the challenges and opportunities of implementing this proposed biosphere functional integrity boundary in Rotterdam and Lagos. title: Who are roads for? Welfare, rights, and the politics of road infrastructure reframing in Ghana
abstract: While infrastructure is widely acknowledged as a catalyst for economic growth and national development, its role in promoting equity, citizenship, and social justice remains underexplored. This paper interrogates the normative and policy dimensions of road infrastructure provision in Ghana by reframing it as both a government obligation and a welfare good. abstract: Recommender systems often concentrate exposure on popular items, limiting catalogue utilization and leaving long-tail items underexposed. abstract: Abstract As ready-to-eat (RTE) meals and dining out become increasingly popular, limited empirical evidence exists on how domestically produced ingredients are positioned relative to other food values in these contexts. Using online survey data from Japanese consumers collected in 2024, this study applies best–worst scaling to samples of 786 respondents for RTE meals and 771 for dining out to estimate the relative importance of 11 food values. abstract: La incorporación de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en la justicia penal desafía el debido proceso y la igualdad ante la ley, afectando de forma especial a poblaciones vulnerables como los migrantes irregulares. Mediante la revisión sistemática de la literatura y de los marcos normativos, incluido el Reglamento (UE) 2024/1689, este artículo analiza el impacto de la IA en las decisiones judiciales, la policía predictiva y la gestión penitenciaria. abstract: Background: Employee retention is increasingly challenging as Generation Z enters the corporate workforce with distinct expectations regarding career growth, compensation, supervisory support, organizational culture, and work–life balance. Understanding these factors is essential for organizations seeking to retain young employees and strengthen workforce stability. title: Biotic and abiotic drivers of ecosystem functioning differ between a temperate and a tropical region
abstract: Abstract Any single ecosystem will provide many ecosystem functions. Whether these functions tend to increase in concert or trade off against each other is a question of much current interest. Equally topical are the drivers behind ecosystem function rates. abstract: Abstract The growing accumulation of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) waste and the increasing demand for clean hydrogen call for integrated electrochemical strategies. abstract: Just Transitions policies are gaining pace worldwide including a range of national, sub-national and sectoral Just Transition plans, with Scotland as a leading voice. The Scottish Government continue to develop a raft of strategic and policy responses to Just Transition. title: Cultural Heritage and Tourism Development of Rivers State
abstract: Rivers State, located in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria, possesses a rich cultural heritage that holds immense potential for tourism development. The state's diverse ethnic composition, traditional festivals, historical landmarks, and unique architectural expressions provide a significant opportunity to boost tourism and, in turn, drive economic growth. abstract: Female participation in some specializations within the senior high school Technical-Vocational-Livelihood (TVL) track is still low, which can potentially create gender-related challenges for female students. abstract: La expansión de la inteligencia artificial generativa en la educación superior ha intensificado la necesidad de distinguir entre escritura académica humana, escritura asistida y textos producidos automáticamente. abstract: This article examines an apparent paradox in contemporary Dutch society: the persistence of substantial empirical evidence of structural discrimination alongside continuing resistance to, or minimisation of, the concept of structural racism. title: Scaling paludiculture: stakeholder perspectives on adoption and enabling conditions in England
abstract: Paludiculture, the cultivation of wetland species on rewetted peatlands, is increasingly promoted as a nature-based solution for climate mitigation, biodiversity restoration and peat conservation; however, its adoption remains limited in the United Kingdom. This study examines stakeholder perspectives on the adoption of paludiculture and the enabling conditions required to support its scale-up. abstract: The study explores the impact of technology on the preservation and promotion of cultural heritage in Southwest Nigeria. This study used a mixed-methods approach, incorporating qualitative and quantitative methods to gather comprehensive data. abstract: The ideal of social justice mandated by the fifth principle of Pancasila remains challenged by persistent inequality, uneven access to welfare, and gaps between public policy objectives and their implementation in Indonesia. The Free Nutritious Meals (Makan Bergizi Gratis, or MBG) Program represents an important case for examining whether state welfare policies have realised substantive social justice or merely administrative distribution. abstract: Klebsiella variicola (KV) infections are being increasingly reported across diverse geographic regions and linked to high mortality. abstract: Abstract Receptor-like kinases (RLKs) are a large family of transmembrane receptors that play central roles in signal perception and transduction in plants. abstract: This article draws upon research undertaken in two rural communities in Malaysia under the program My Village My Future, a community-based entrepreneurship program initiated by the government to develop rural areas. abstract: The general opinion is that education is an instrument of ensuring positive changes in the society however; positive changes have not been achieved in Ogbomoso prior to the arrival of Christian Mission. abstract: This study examined the relationship between Computational Thinking Skills (CTS) and Higher-Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) among high school students majoring in biology in Jakarta, Indonesia, using a quantitative, correlational, and cross-sectional research design. abstract: Introduction: Ecopreneurship is the process of coming up with long-term solutions for social and environmental problems by applying creativity and entrepreneurial abilities. Through sustainable practices, ecopreneurship promotes peace and faster economic progress, aiding sustainable development, poverty reduction and job creation. abstract: Green total factor productivity (GTFP) represents a cornerstone for sustainable development; however, previous scholarship has primarily concentrated on market-based or technological determinants, frequently ignoring the impact of institutional governance. abstract: The Peruvian Andean Amazon is home to small-scale dairy livestock production that sustains numerous rural families, but whose heterogeneity complicates the design of targeted interventions. abstract: Social Key Performance Indicators (SKPIs) and the competitiveness they can bring is studied and applied to a case in the energy sector (district heating). title: A Territorial Approach to Transitioning Oil and Gas Producing Regions: Comparative Practices and Prospects for Canada
abstract: Abstract Oil and gas transitions are relatively new and especially difficult because the sector is large, economically central, and deeply embedded in national energy systems. Territorial approaches—grounded in regional political economies, institutions, and community impacts—offer a politically feasible way to begin meaningful oil and gas transitions in Canada's producing regions. Our article first traces the evolution of Canadian oil and gas governance within federal climate architectures and entrenched fossil regionalisms, then draws on comparative case studies of Esbjerg (Denmark), Taranak

title: Developing best practices for engaging and involving palliative care patients in research in sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patient and public involvement and engagement (PPIE) are pivotal to maximising the impact of research on clinical care. Despite growing recognition of its importance, there remains limited evidence on best practices for implementing meaningful and contextually appropriate PPIE particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. AIM: This study aimed to explore patients and caregivers perspectives on meaningful engagement and involvement in palliative care research in Africa and identify contextually appropriate recommendations for establishing, supporting and sustaining PPIE structures and network

title: Poetic Opacity and the Limits of Translation
abstract: Abstract This paper argues that translations of poetry cannot function as substitutive reproductions of their originals due to the medium-specific opacity of the poetic form. Drawing on the concept of poetic opacity and on type-token distinction, I contend that a poem’s aesthetic identity resides in a distinctive, linguistically rooted interplay of form and content, one that resists full transfer across languages. Through close readings of translations from Baudelaire, Keats, Plath, Eliot, and Apollinaire, I show that even competent translations dissolve the original’s form-content unity, gene

title: La inteligencia artificial como tótem
abstract: El artículo propone interpretar a los grandes modelos de lenguaje (LLM) no como sujetos conscientes ni como herramientas técnicas, sino como una nueva forma de objeto simbólico: el tótem algorítmico. Recuperando el totemismo durkheimiano y lévi-straussiano como mecanismo de proyección colectiva, se argumenta que los LLM concentran autoridad, sentido y cohesión simbólica para una comunidad sin poseer las propiedades que se les atribuyen. Se examina la amplificación del efecto ELIZA en los sistemas contemporáneos, los riesgos de autoridad epistémica desproporcionada y el papel del tótem algorítm

title: BCOF at eighty: new perspectives on the British commonwealth occupation force in the occupation of Japan
abstract: The British Commonwealth Occupation Force (BCOF) component of the Allied Occupation of Japan (1945-1952) has often been overlooked by researchers because of its minimal role in policy-making. Taking the opportunity of the 80th anniversary of the arrival of the first BCOF personnel in Japan, this special issue introduces new perspectives about the organisation based on a range of hitherto unused or under-utilised sources. The introduction begins by emphasising how BCOF’s commanding officer sought to draw attention to his troops’ contribution to the Occupation. There follows a brief overview of

title: Teachers’ Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices in the Implementation of Aral Program in Barili District 1
abstract: This descriptive-correlational study examined the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of 85 teacher-respondents toward the implementation of the Academic Recovery and Accessible Learning (ARAL) Program in Barili District 1, Division of Cebu Province, during School Year 2025–2026. A researcher-adapted questionnaire with a five-point Likert scale was used to assess KAP levels, identify implementation challenges, and examine relationships between selected profile variables and KAP, as well as among the KAP constructs. Data were analyzed using frequency, percentage, weighted mean, standard d
journal: Psychology and Education A Multidisciplinary Journal

title: Evaluación e incentivos al desempeño docente en la educación superior mexicana: una lectura foucaultiana
abstract: This essay critically examines the Faculty Performance Incentive Program in Mexican higher education from a Foucauldian perspective. Its objective is to examine the institutional rationality underpinning this evaluation and incentive mechanism, with particular attention to its connections with surveillance, the regulation of conduct, the intensification of performance demands, and the differential classification of academic staff. The analysis draws on specialized literature on the evaluation of academic work, studies of faculty incentive programs, and regulatory documents related to the progr
publisher: Instituto Tecnológico y de Estudios Superiores de Occidente

title: Resurvey of Boreal Earthworm Communities in Southern and Northern Finland
abstract: ABSTRACT In northern boreal Europe, the Last Glaciation Maximum resulted in a tabula rasa of earthworm species, post-glacial recolonisation of few peregrine species. Boreal forests represent 11.5% of the Earth’s land area, and their cold winters represent the harshest season for earthworms. These biotopes are subject to substantial global changes, notably climate change and land use intensification, which might impact earthworm populations. Yet, no study measuring temporal changes in earthworm population or diversity is known in this biotope. Here, we sampled earthworm communities in two north

title: A Systematic Investigation of Bias in Large Language Models for Advertising Relevance
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to judge how well an advertisement matches a query, but the fairness of these judgments has received limited attention. We conduct a systematic study of fairness in relevance judgments made by LLMs for queries and advertisements. Our counterfactual framework examines the effects of advertiser identity and possible popularity, input language, and demographic wording. We study GPT-4o as a categorical relevance judge and a Qwen-7B model trained specifically for relevance prediction. The advertiser and language experiments use query and advertisem

title: UA-Bench: Benchmarking Large Audio-Language Models on Underwater Acoustic Recognition
abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) are fast becoming a general interface to sound, yet how far their broad pretraining carries into specialized domains remains largely open. Vessel monitoring, maritime safety, and ocean sensing all depend on recognizing underwater signals, but to our knowledge LALMs have not been systematically evaluated on them. title: Collapse and causality in generalised trace dynamics: Record selection in Connes time and the causal consistency of emergent records
abstract: In generalized trace dynamics (GTD) the fluctuations proposed to select a measurement record come from unresolved pregeometric degrees of freedom and are ordered by Connes time rather than by a spacetime coordinate. The hypersurface on which collapse occurs is then not a question posed at the level at which selection happens; it returns as the requirement that the emergent records do not signal. title: WorkflowOps: Learning Agent Collaboration Priors for Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestration
abstract: Multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed for complex knowledge work, yet their orchestration layers remain largely memoryless: each new task is decomposed, assigned, and executed from scratch with no benefit from prior successful executions. We present WorkflowOps, a multi-agent workflow orchestration framework that learns agent collaboration priors from historical workflows and expands its agent pool on demand to cover new capability requirements. Our approach introduces three coupled mechanisms. First, a transition probability matrix captures pairwise agent collaboration frequencies fro
institutions: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

title: Understanding the Hierarchical Structure and Functional Landscape of the Model Context Protocol Ecosystem
abstract: AI agents increasingly rely on tools exposed through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to complete user tasks. Hundreds of thousands of MCP servers are listed across marketplaces, yet they are organized only by coarse, marketplace-specific server categories. This makes it difficult for agents and users to identify tools for a given operation, find functional alternatives, and assess how those alternatives differ. We present MCPacific, the largest tool-level, cross-marketplace map of the MCP ecosystem. MCPacific collects 368,754 MCP server listings corresponding to 124,267 unique servers across

title: From Video Clips to Creation Trajectory: Sora100K for AI-Native Video Creation
abstract: AI-Native video creation is shifting from isolated video clips toward iterative video creation workflows. However, existing datasets remain largely video clips, representing video generation and editing as separate tasks rather than connected stages of a video creation workflow. In this paper, we introduce Sora100K, a dataset that represents the AI-Native video creation workflow as a structured video creation trajectory. Specifically, we first identify video creation trajectories and decompose them into three subsets according to their structural roles: text-to-video generation records as root
institutions: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

title: Incremental Open-Ended Deep Research with Structured Harness
abstract: Existing Open-Ended Deep Research (OEDR) systems primarily generate reports from scratch, making them inefficient for scenarios where research reports need to be continuously maintained as new information emerges. We introduce \textbf{Incremental Open-Ended Deep Research (Incremental-OEDR)}, a research setting that treats a report as an evolving research state and incrementally updates it by preserving valid knowledge, revising outdated or incomplete content, and incorporating newly available information. To support this setting, we propose \textbf{Structured Harness}, which represents reports

title: Degree-conditioned anneal offsets reshape certified-optimum sampling for minimum vertex cover
abstract: Quantum annealers can sample degenerate optima unevenly, so the composition of finite-read output matters when multiple solutions are sought. We investigate whether problem structure can steer this output through node-dependent anneal offsets for Minimum Vertex Cover (MVC). In MVC, vertex degree equals the number of incident edge-cover constraints and therefore measures local constraint participation. title: Distributed Model-Free Turbine Repositioning for Wake Overlap Minimization in Floating Offshore Wind Farms
abstract: This paper presents a model-free method for turbine repositioning control in floating offshore wind farms. The method uses a distributed online optimization framework to mitigate the wake effect. Conventional approaches rely on centralized, model-based control architectures, which suffer from poor practical feasibility. To overcome this limitation and address nonconvexity and inaccessible gradient information, we incorporate physics-informed knowledge of wake dynamics into the control system design. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method by comparing it with a centralized, mod

title: Looking at radiative corrections to the $Σ^\pm\toΛe^\pm \barν$ semileptonic decay-rate ratio
abstract: We investigate the impact of radiative corrections on the ratio of the semileptonic decay rates $Σ^\pm\toΛe^\pm \barν$. Phenomenological analyses point to sizable radiative effects on the experimentally measured ratio. From a theoretical perspective, this observable is particularly appealing because several hadronic and electroweak contributions partially cancel in the ratio, providing a cleaner probe of electromagnetic effects. title: Debug2Fix: Can Interactive Debugging Help Coding Agents Fix More Bugs?
abstract: While significant progress has been made in automating various aspects of software development through coding agents, there is still significant room for improvement in their bug fixing capabilities. Debugging and investigation of runtime behavior remains largely a manual, developer-driven process. Popular coding agents typically rely on either static analysis of the code or iterative test-fix cycles, which is akin to trial and error debugging. We believe that there is a wealth of rich runtime information that developers routinely access while debugging code, which agents are currently deprive

title: Beyond the Transcriptome: Chromatin-Informed Prediction of Cell-State-Dependent Perturbation Responses
abstract: Predicting transcriptional responses to genetic perturbations is central to understanding gene function. Existing predictors primarily rely on transcriptomic measurements, although chromatin accessibility provides complementary information about the cellular context in which perturbations act. Using this information requires linking chromatin context to specific perturbations and accounting for baseline differences between independently sampled control and perturbed populations. We propose ChromaPert, a chromatin-informed framework for predicting state-dependent perturbation responses. ChromaP

title: TEIDAN: A Multilingual Multiparty Dialogue Corpus
abstract: Multi-party interaction is a central setting for human communication and a necessary target for human-agent interaction systems that must participate in group conversation. Yet available corpora often focus on meetings, task-oriented interaction, text-based interaction, or acted scenarios, and fewer resources support cross-linguistic comparison of spontaneous face-to-face triadic discussion. This paper presents TEIDAN, a multilingual multimodal corpus that currently consists of Japanese and English three-party conversations. TEIDAN records groups of three participants discussing open-ended top

title: GeopoliticalQA: Benchmarking Retrieval and Generation over Intelligence Reports
abstract: Geopolitical and strategic intelligence reports constitute a rich source of expert knowledge and have increasing value in the current political climate, but their heterogeneity and analytical complexity pose challenges for retrieval-augmented question answering. We introduce a benchmark for grounded question answering over 415 open-source geopolitical and strategic intelligence reports, comprising 5,525 document-grounded question-answer pairs spanning factual, inferential, comparative, and risk-oriented questions. We propose a document-aware generation pipeline that profiles reports before gen

title: GoNorth 2023 Cruise Report
abstract: Norway’s outer border north of Svalbard crosses deep-sea plains in the Nansen Basin and onto the southern flank of the Gakkel Ridge. Nansen discovered the mountain ridge when he drifted across the Arctic Ocean with the Fram and measured the ocean depth along the way. Today we know that this is the northernmost part of a 65,000 km long mountain ridge that extends from the Arctic Ocean through the Norwegian Sea and the Atlantic Ocean, further through the Indian Ocean to the Pacific Ocean. institutions: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

title: Enhancing AUV path planning via state-aware adaptive particle swarm optimization in complex marine environments
abstract: Path planning for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) in complex marine environments requires an optimizer that can account for coupled path-quality and safety criteria while adapting its search behavior to individual particles. This paper proposes Adaptive Elite Particle Swarm Optimization (AEPSO) for three-dimensional marine environments that include seabed terrain, obstacles, and ocean currents. title: Optimisation-based motion control for AUVs under non-linear wave-current disturbances
abstract: With the increasing exploitation of marine resources, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) are being applied more extensively in a variety of tasks, such as maritime search, rescue, and marine archaeology. The attitude stability of AUVs can be significantly disturbed by highly non-linear waves and currents near the sea surface, yet the influence of wave non-linearity on AUV motion and the associated control strategies remains insufficiently studied. journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Maritime Engineering

title: Modular dual-critic reinforcement learning control for AUV path tracking and collision avoidance
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) operating in complex and uncertain ocean environments require reliable path-tracking and obstacle-avoidance capabilities to maintain safety in the presence of currents and obstacles. Traditional end-to-end deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods often struggle with coupled navigation objectives, which can lead to oscillatory control and unreliable trajectory recovery. This paper proposes a modular dual-critic proximal policy optimization framework with prioritized experience replay (Modular DCPPO-PER) for AUV path tracking and collision avoidance. The fr

title: Effect of wave-induced motion on the energy harvesting performance of a floating solar-powered AUV
abstract: This paper proposes a novel concept of a solar-powered autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) featuring a foldable solar wing panel. The design enables energy harvesting during surface floating operations. We investigate the time-varying energy harvesting characteristics due to the combined effects of wave-induced motion and submergence depth. A real-time power calculation model based on computational fluid dynamics (CFD) solutions is established, and its accuracy is verified using sea trials. institutions: Qingdao Center of Resource Chemistry and New Materials

title: Customized Design of Power Electronics for Deep-Sea Energy and Industrial Applications: Environmental Adaptation, Technical Bottlenecks, and Development Pathways
abstract: This narrative review examines the design of power electronics for deep-sea energy and industrial systems, where converter performance is constrained by electrical demands and prolonged exposure to pressure, seawater, temperature cycling, and limited maintenance access. Targeted, non-systematic literature searches covering studies available through September 2026 were used to connect offshore renewable generation and hydrogen production, sub-sea distribution and motor drives, and autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) power and charging. title: Low-cost single-beam SONAR localization in AUVs: Systematic experiments with acoustic and optical perception
abstract: This work presents a low-cost acoustic sensing framework for underwater localization and perception using single-beam sonars (SBS) and a forward-looking sonar (FLS). A Kalman filter (KF) based sensor fusion approach is developed to integrate SBS measurements with inertial sensing, incorporating pre-filtering and confidence-based gating to mitigate acoustic outliers and reflective disturbances. Multiple motion configurations, including manual underwater robot guiding followed by thruster-propelled controlled motion are employed to evaluate robustness under controlled and non-ideal conditions. title: Consensus Collision‐Free Trajectory Planning for Multi‐AUV Formation Gathering
abstract: ABSTRACT Formation gathering of multiple autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) is a fundamental prerequisite for cooperative underwater missions. It enables AUVs initially located at dispersed positions to form a prescribed geometric configuration before formation‐based exploration, observation, or survey tasks. Each AUV must reach its assigned terminal position and heading while ensuring coordinated motion and inter‐vehicle safety. title: Direct Acoustic Versus AUV-Assisted Hybrid Reporting for Subsea Pipeline Monitoring: A Matched End-to-End Evaluation
abstract: Subsea pipeline monitoring must deliver urgent alarms quickly while moving much larger inspection records over constrained underwater links. This creates a deployment choice: send all data through a prioritized acoustic network, or collect routine records with an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) undertaking a finite collection mission. We compare these complete reporting architectures under identical traffic, geometry, deadlines, available retry choices, and surface infrastructure. title: Nonlinear hydrodynamic coupling effects of free-surface and bottom boundaries on an AUV
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) frequently operate in shallow waters, where they are simultaneously subjected to the coupling effects of free-surface wave-making and bottom boundary restrictions. Existing studies have primarily focused on single-boundary conditions, leaving the complex, non-linear coupled hydrodynamics in dual-boundary shallow water environments insufficiently understood. title: SA-SRDC-Loc: Single-AUV-assisted three-dimensional underwater localization via selective residual distance learning and depth-constrained robust optimization
abstract: Accurate three-dimensional localization in underwater acoustic sensor networks remains challenging because irregular acoustic propagation and multi-hop connectivity weaken the relationship between network topology and physical distance. This paper proposes SA-SRDC-Loc, a single-AUV-assisted localization framework that treats successive AUV reports as temporally ordered observations of one continuously moving platform rather than as independent anchors. title: Numerical investigation of the drag reduction mechanism induced by rectangular riblets on the aft-body of underwater vehicles
abstract: Abstract Surface riblets have emerged as a highly efficient passive drag-reduction strategy for enhancing the endurance of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). Nevertheless, current research less frequently deploys riblets in the complex aft-body region of underwater vehicles. To address this gap, we propose a drag-reduction scheme utilizing streamwise rectangular riblets distributed along the tail contraction section of the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency submarine (DARPA SUBOFF) bare-hull model. title: Integrating model predictive control and reinforcement learning for robust Six-DOF AUV trajectory tracking
abstract: To address model uncertainties, ocean-current disturbances, and real-time control requirements in six-degree-of-freedom AUV trajectory tracking, this paper proposes a residual-learning-enhanced MPC–PID hierarchical control framework. An outer-loop kinematic model predictive controller generates constraint-aware velocity references, while an inner-loop inverse-dynamics PID controller provides nominal dynamic compensation and fast velocity tracking. title: Frequency-adaptive wave disturbance observation and prescribed performance fast super-twisting control for ROV station-keeping
abstract: This paper addresses the station-keeping control problem of remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) under near-surface head-sea conditions, where narrow-band wave disturbances induce significant periodic motion. Instead of treating wave effects as unstructured lumped disturbances, a frequency-adaptive disturbance rejection framework is proposed by combining EKF-based frequency estimation, harmonic extended state observation, and prescribed-performance fast super-twisting sliding mode control. title: MOOS-IvP/ArduSub-Based AUV Three-Dimensional Path-Following Control System: Design and Implementation
abstract: To fulfill the requirements for rapid development of high-performance AUV motion control systems, a three-dimensional (3D) path- following control system is designed and implemented based on the MOOS-IvP/ArduSub architecture. Using Lyapunov stability theory, an adaptive line-of-sight (ALOS) guidance law with variable look-ahead distances (VΔ-ALOS) is designed. journal: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering

title: Underwater Platform for Long-Term Observation Using a Cable-Restricted Underwater Vehicle and Its Design Concept for Trajectory Planning
abstract: Long-term and repeated observation of shallow seafloor environments is required to evaluate temporal changes in seagrass meadows and other coastal ecosystems. In this study, we propose a cable-restricted observation system consisting of an underwater vehicle, a tether cable, and a seafloor station equipped with a reel. The vehicle can repeatedly cruise over a designated area along nearly the same trajectory using the cable constraint. title: Confidence-Gated Finite-Horizon Residual SAC–LSTM Control for Visual Target Tracking by a Rudderless Six-Thruster AUV
abstract: Autonomous visual tracking of a moving target by a rudderless underwater vehicle is complicated by nonlinear dynamics, intermittent visual observations, environmental currents, and constrained distributed thrust. This paper combines a recurrent SAC–LSTM policy with a finite-horizon model-based residual correction. The policy generates a baseline three-component virtual action, while the model branch predicts the terminal image error and computes a residual correction before constrained six-thruster allocation. journal: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering

title: Breeding emperor penguins show interannual recurrence in shelf-break associated foraging areas across contrasting sea ice conditions in the northwestern Weddell Sea
abstract: Abstract The emperor penguin Aptenodytes forsteri is highly sea ice dependent and vulnerable to climate change, yet the at-sea distribution and habitat associations of breeding adults remain poorly understood for colonies in the western Weddell Sea. We tracked nine breeding adults from Snow Hill Island, the northernmost known colony, during chick-rearing in 2023-24 and 2025-26, and analysed 38 foraging trips using kernel utilisation distributions, habitat-selection models and hidden Markov models. title: Design and Open-Water Validation of an Autonomous Underwater Robot for Physical Diver Safety Assistance
abstract: Diving accidents remain frequently fatal, and most stem from preventable human factors: panic, failed buoyancy control, and disorientation. Underwater human–robot interaction research has focused on observing the diver and offers little help when a diver must be pulled to safety. This paper presents the design and sea validation of NADIA, an autonomous underwater robot that combines diver guidance and following with diver-commanded physical assistance. title: Adaptive robust SINS/DVL/USBL integrated navigation using persistent homology-based USBL state classification
abstract: For autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), SINS/DVL/USBL integrated navigation provides continuous underwater positioning. However, multipath propagation, non-line-of-sight (NLOS) effects, and prolonged USBL outages can degrade acoustic measurements and yield innovations with heavy tails. This article develops an adaptive robust navigation framework that integrates USBL state recognition using persistent homology with state-dependent compensation and Student’s t robust fusion. title: Architecture in Coexistence with the Sea: Hanseok Lee on Water-Friendliness and Marine Habitation
abstract: How oceanic architecture defines its scope in relation to waterfront regeneration, marine habitation and climate adaptation is the central question of this interview. Drawing on his research into accommodation at sea and planning studies concerning the ports of Busan, Hanseok Lee, Professor Emeritus at Korea Maritime & Ocean University, discusses oceanic architecture as both a setting for coexistence between people and water and an emerging architectural culture. title: Navigating Inuit concerns: assessing management options for expedition cruise tourism in Nunavut waters
abstract: This paper examines the governance and regulatory frameworks for expedition cruise tourism in the Canadian Arctic, with a particular focus on Nunavut. The aim of the study was to assess effectiveness among these frameworks in addressing previously identified concerns among Inuit communities about increased marine navigation activities across their homeland. These concerns include potential impacts to a pristine environment, disturbance to wildlife and traditional harvesting activities, and effects on cultural and historic sites, among others. title: Deep reinforcement learning-based path following of a bio-inspired autonomous underwater vehicle under ocean currents
abstract: Bio-inspired autonomous underwater vehicles (BI-AUVs) offer high propulsive efficiency and maneuverability by imitating fish morphology and locomotion. However, oscillatory fin motion and fluid–structure interactions generate nonlinear hydrodynamic forces, making model-based controller design under environmental disturbances challenging. This study proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based path-following framework for ocean currents conditions. title: A review of the development, research progress and key challenges in underwater bionic soft robotics
abstract: Conventional rigid underwater robots possess high structural stiffness and exhibit a single mode of locomotion, showing poor adaptability in complex flow fields, narrow spaces and eco-friendly underwater operations. In recent years, underwater bionic soft robots have achieved rapid development boasting a rich variety of bionic prototypes as well as innovative actuation and control strategies. Nevertheless, most existing reviews focus on individual technologies, and few systematically integrate technological evolution, state-of-the-art progress and technical bottlenecks. title: Variations in Arctic aerosol iron solubility in relation to leaching methodology, air mass characteristics, and seasonality
abstract: Abstract. Atmospheric deposition of the essential micronutrient, iron (Fe), can have an important influence on primary production and marine biogeochemistry. In the Arctic Ocean, the ongoing shift towards seasonal ice coverage means that summertime atmospheric deposition increasingly takes place direct to the surface ocean, rather than onto sea ice. As a result, atmospheric deposition of material emitted from natural and anthropogenic sources may become a more relevant Fe input to the region. title: Haima Cold Seeps: Direct Evidence for the Occurrence of Gas Hydrates—A Case Study from the Qiongdongnan Sea Area, South China Sea
abstract: Cold seeps are natural “outcrop” evidence of marine gas hydrates and represent one of the most direct indicators of gas hydrate occurrence. This study used high-resolution 3D seismic data covering approximately 400 km2 in the deep-water southern Qiongdongnan Basin, northern South China Sea. Sub-bottom profiles and multibeam bathymetric data were also incorporated. title: Mechanism limiting the speed of wave gliders under high sea states
abstract: To elucidate the mechanism limiting wave-glider speed under high sea states, a hydrodynamic model of the semi-passive submerged glider was developed. Using Fluent overset meshes and UDFs, the passive motion of the submerged glider was coupled with tandem-hydrofoil passive rotation. Simulations for Sea States 2–5 were validated by South China Sea trials. The wave glider attained relatively high mean forward speed at wave heights of 1.2–1.3 m. title: On the possibility of deep seabed permafrost to occupy Ca. 7 million km2 in the Arctic Ocean
abstract: Abstract Arctic Ocean (AO) shelf permafrost is the most popular and best-known type of subsea permafrost. Genetically, it is analogous to the ordinary subaerial permafrost. Today, the following types of subsea permafrost are also known: i) ice-bearing sediment layers formed from porewater freshening of terrestrial origins, ii) thermokarst lake taliks refreezing under cryotic seabed conditions, iii) bottom-fast ice preserving permafrost due to efficient heat conduction from atmosphere-ice-sediment coupling in winter, and iv) similar permafrost aggradation processes occurring beneath small islan

title: Time-variant reliability analysis of pressure-resistant structures of disk-shaped underwater gliders in corrosive environments
abstract: Corrosion considerably affects the safety and life cycle of underwater vehicles. Using the linear buckling analysis method, the mesh sensitivity of the pressure hull of the glider was analyzed to determine the size of the finite element unit. Furthermore, the random uniform corrosion model of the pressure hull was also developed, and the statistical characteristics of time-variant degradation of ultimate strength were determined. title: Through the camera lens: a window into the underwater behaviour of white sharks (Carcharodon carcharias)
abstract: Context Observations of terrestrial animals in their natural ecosystems have formed the foundation for many hypothesis-driven studies. Aims Observing animals in the marine environment is logistically more challenging and comparatively scarce. Underwater camera technologies provide new opportunities to document animal behaviour, particularly for large marine predators. title: Understanding spatial heterogeneity of rocky reef demersal fish assemblages: Links to conservation plans in the Juan Fernández Archipelago Marine Protected Area in the Southeastern Pacific
abstract: Spatial heterogeneity linked to fish assemblages has been key to advancing conservation plans and assessing marine resources in remote ecosystems. The Juan Fernández Archipelago is a remote and highly heterogeneous geologic hotspot located on the Nazca plate (SE Pacific), comprising three islands, numerous seamounts and guyots, and a highly rugged coastal marine shelf. Hundreds of rocky reefs of various sizes characterize this insular coastal shelf, supporting diverse finfish populations of interest for the Robinson Crusoe Island artisanal fishing fleet. title: Improved robust trajectory tracking of underactuated AUVs via unified Tube-NMPC with proactive finite-time disturbance compensation in uncertain ocean environments
abstract: This paper presents a unified tube-based nonlinear model predictive control (TNMPC) framework for 3D trajectory tracking of underactuated autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) subject to parametric uncertainty and deep-ocean current disturbances. The proposed architecture integrates a nominal nonlinear model predictive planning scheme, tube-based ancillary feedback and a finite-time extended state observer (FTESO) within a single predictive control structure. T. gaudichaudii is generally associated with relatively warmer, ice-free waters, although it may co-occur with Euphausia superba and can also occur at low densities in colder regions. abstract: The prospects for the development of offshore fields and the growth in the volume of transportation of petroleum products along the Northern Sea Route inevitably increase the risks of accidental spills in the Barents Sea region. This determines the relevance of research on seashores as the most sensitive to oil pollution and difficult to clean up natural ecosystems. abstract: Underwater acoustic vector sensors (AVSs) are widely used for direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation in underwater surveillance and marine bioacoustics applications. Compared with conventional hydrophone arrays, a single compact AVS offers greater flexibility and simpler deployment while enabling DOA estimation using the acoustic active-intensity method (AIM). However, the in situ performance of AVSs for DOA estimation using AIM has been investigated only to a limited extent. abstract: Abstract Scleractinians are key components of Mediterranean mesophotic and bathyal benthic ecosystems, comprising 30 species known to occur below 40 m. title: Platformisation, Political Change and Democracy in Southeast Asia – for a Labour Turn in Digital Media Studies
abstract: Abstract In this paper, I examine the relationship between increasing digitalisation and platformisation on one side, and political mobilisation and political change in Southeast Asia on the other. abstract: Cooperative target-zone reaching by multiple autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) under active defense remains challenging because each vehicle must make sequential guidance decisions under nonlinear hydrodynamics, sonar-limited perception, obstacle constraints, and defender interference. This paper proposes a role-guided risk-aware attention variant of multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG), termed role-guided risk-aware attention MADDPG (RGRA-MADDPG), for attacker-side multi-AUV target-zone reaching under active defense. abstract: Deep-sea unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs) depend on reliable propulsion systems during cruising, docking, and observation missions. However, online propulsion health monitoring remains challenging because high-frequency reference states are difficult to obtain in real time, while the nonlinear dynamics of UUVs make the relationship between thruster inputs and state responses difficult to characterize accurately. abstract: Microplastic (MP) contamination of the open ocean is well documented, yet the vertical structuring of MPs and the role of water masses in shaping deep-water inventories remain poorly resolved along the eastern boundary of the North Atlantic Subtropical Gyre. abstract: Summary The North Anatolian Fault (NAF) in the Sea of Marmara is characterized by varying mechanical behaviors and fluid manifestations along its path. In the present study, we investigate an earthquake sequence including a Mw 4.6 earthquake that occurred on November 27, 2013, in the partially creeping section of the NAF in the Sea of Marmara. abstract: Abstract Oxygen Minimum Zones (OMZs) are expanding globally, reshaping marine ecosystems, and creating physiologically challenging conditions for many marine organisms. Vulnerable communities will likely shift toward taxa adapted to low-oxygen conditions. Such adaptations are rare in eukaryotes, but some foraminiferal taxa can survive, and even calcify, in severely oxygen-depleted environments. abstract: The bryoflora of Ryazhkov Island (408 ha) has been supplemented by 9 new moss species (Anomodon viticulosus, Dicranum leioneuron, D. septentrionale, Drepanocladus polygamus, Fissidens adianthoides, Pseudoleskeella papillosa, Scorpidium cossonii, Sphagnum fimbriatum, S. subfulvum), the first of which is included in the Red Data Book of Murmansk Region [2025]. title: RATES OF CHANGES IN THE POPULATION OF SEMIBALANUS BALANOIDES (L.) FOR TWO TYPES OF LANDSCAPE OF TERIBERSKAYA BAY DURING CLIMATE WARMING
abstract: A method for early detecting of climate-related changes in littoral communities has been developed using bioindication based on the dynamics of estuarine populations of the barnacle Semibalanus balanoides (Crustacea, Cirripedia). It has been established that climate-related changes in barnacle abundance depend on the slope and topography of the biotope. The population's response to environmental changes in a littoral biotope with a significant steep occurs later and is less pronounced than in a biotope with a flat landscape.

abstract: Geographic isolation, local ecology, and cultural context mediate shellfish use in the Gulf of Alaska. Chirikof Island, located at the southwest end of the Kodiak Archipelago in the central Gulf of Alaska, provides an excellent example of subsistence in a place of extreme isolation and exposure. abstract: Abstract Internal wave (IW) spectrum serves as a fundamental tool for characterizing IW fields, understanding their underlying dynamics and quantifying IW-driven mixing. Prydz Bay, as one of the critical hubs for energy transfer and water properties exchange in the Southern Ocean, however, remains poorly studied in terms of its IW spectrum. abstract: Ferromanganese (Fe–Mn) crusts are important archives of long-term oceanographic and redox conditions, but post-depositional phosphatization can alter their primary hydrogenetic geochemical signatures. This study investigates mineralogical and geochemical variations among representative stratigraphic layers in Fe–Mn crust cores recovered from western Pacific seamounts to better understand the effects of phosphatization on crust evolution. abstract: Critical raw materials (CRMs) are emerging inorganic pollutants because of their technological use and release into remote marine environments. However, their occurrence, distribution, and ecological significance in Antarctic waters remain poorly understood, and existing risk indices have not been adapted for CRMs in these systems. abstract: This paper presents a compact, integrated system for in-situ detection of fuel debris via simultaneous gamma-ray and neutron measurements, developed for application within the primary containment vessel (PCV) of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station Unit 1. abstract: The bathymetric gradient plays an important role in the formation of the structure of marine bottom communities. In this paper, the bathymetric distribution of shell Gastropoda off the coast of the Novaya Zemlya archipelago is analyzed. abstract: Reptadeonella Busk, 1884, is one of the most common bryozoan genera reported from warm waters across all oceans and is currently represented by 29 species. Almost half of this diversity has been described in the past 10 years, including the recognition of 12 new species and documentation of morphological variations. title: Exploring Spitsbergen’s Potential for Sustainable Development and Geopark Creation
abstract: There is growing evidence of environmental degradation in the Arctic, reflected in rising temperatures, ice melt, and more frequent extreme weather events. In this context, tourism development in Spitsbergen must be balanced with nature conservation. This study aims to examine experiences of tourism and opinions on sustainable activities, as well as to explore the potential for establishing a geopark on Svalbard. abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) is an indirect short-lived climate forcer with uncertainties both in sources and its role in atmospheric oxidation. abstract: Length-weight relationships (LWRs) are morphometric tools that allow body mass to be estimated from fish length, providing input for fisheries, ecological and biodiversity studies. For deep-pelagic fishes, however, LWR data remain fragmented and unavailable for most species. abstract: Background: The global and Indonesian maritime sector requires accounting systems capable of addressing distinctive transaction characteristics, operational risks, and sustainability demands. Maritime accounting refers to accounting practices adapted to shipping, port, marine, and fisheries industries. abstract: This paper examines the pivotal role of cultural tourism in safeguarding regional history and ethnic identity, focusing on the I.V. Savitsky State Museum of Arts in Nukus, Uzbekistan. Known globally as the "Louvre of the Desert," the museum holds a unique dual repository consisting of the world's second-largest collection of Soviet avant-garde art and an extensive archive of traditional Karakalpak applied arts alongside ancient Khorezm archaeological antiquities. title: Conservation Messages as Catalysts of Post-Visit Action: Insights from Zoo and Aquarium Visitors
abstract: Zoos and aquariums face an urgent challenge to convey conservation messages that motivate visitors to change their environmental behavior. This study explores the reflections of 768 visitors to one of twelve zoos and aquariums in Australia, USA, and Canada regarding the features of conservation messaging that prompted their post-visit involvement in specific environmental behaviors. title: Upper Palaeolithic mariners? Evaluating experimental evidence for intentional early seafaring
abstract: Brought to popular consciousness by Thor Heyerdahl in the 1940s, the role of seafaring in human migration has been intensely debated. Aiming to stimulate discussion around the ways in which experimental archaeology is used to support such grand narratives, the authors of this debate critically assess a recent claim for Upper Palaeolithic seafaring in the Japanese archipelago. Here, they argue that creating a boat for which there is no archaeological evidence with generic tools that were not widely available in the region risks a confounding circularity of logic.

abstract: Pemphis acidula J.R.Forst. and G. Forst. or santigi is a plant native to Indonesia, widely recognized for its high economic value. Although listed as Least Concern by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), its existence in the wild is increasingly threatened by land degradation, climate change, and it suffers from low natural seed germination rates. This study aimed to evaluate the seed viability and quality of P. acidula and assess the effectiveness of chemical and physical scarification techniques on the viability of santigi seeds.
