title: Dynamic Influence Based Fitness Shaping For Cooperative Coevolution
abstract: Multiagent settings are naturally characterized by coevolutionary dynamics, where agents must adapt and learn in the context of their teammates. A key challenge in such domains is determining how to credit an agent for its individual contribution to team performance. Fitness shaping approaches partially address this by identifying and isolating an agent's direct contribution to team success. However, when an agent's contribution is indirect, such as influencing other teammates to succeed, existing methods fail to capture its impact on the team. title: The Phantom Naturalist: What do we know about the nineteenth-century natural history collector Alfred Crossley?
abstract: Born in Halifax, UK, in 1839, and shipwrecked on Madagascar as a youth, Alfred Crossley had returned to the island by 1869 and in the ensuing eight years made hugely important collections of mammals, birds, butterflies, and other natural history specimens. Many of these are now in major museums in the UK and Europe (including numerous holotypes), but unknown quantities went to private collectors and are now lost. title: Spatial variation in aquatic arthropod biodiversity in floating photovoltaic host waterbodies
abstract: Abstract Floating photovoltaic (FPV) solar energy is a rapidly expanding renewable energy technology in which photovoltaic panels are deployed on floating structures atop waterbodies. While FPVs may alleviate pressure on terrestrial biodiversity, relatively little is known about aquatic biodiversity within FPV host waterbodies. Most FPV studies have focused on abiotic environmental changes, with comparatively few examining wildlife responses. title: Ruth Stephan’s Andean Journey: The Peña Pancho Fierro and Transnational Indigenism in The Tiger’s Eye Magazine
abstract: In 1946, shortly after World War II, U.S. poet Ruth Stephan travelled to Peru seeking artistic direction. In Lima, she joined the indigenist avant-garde of the Peña Pancho Fierro, led by Alicia and Celia Bustamante and José María Arguedas. This encounter reshaped her understanding of indigenous culture and informed her little magazine The Tiger’s Eye (1947– 1949), which placed pre-Columbian and contemporary indigenous art alongside Abstract Expressionism and Surrealism. title: Taxonomic and ecological assessment of an Antarctic Eocene Folivora (Mammalia) metacarpal using three‐dimensional geometric morphometrics
abstract: Here, we reassess the taxonomic affinities and functional morphology of TMM 44190-1, an isolated metacarpal II from the Eocene La Meseta Formation, Marambio (Seymour) Island, Antarctic Peninsula, previously referred to an indeterminate xenarthran. We evaluated its morphological similarities using three-dimensional geometric morphometrics. title: A Love Made of Stones: Contemporary Anishinaabe Lyric and Asiniig Sovereignty
abstract: This article delves into the literary motif of the stone (asiniig) in contemporary Anishinaabe poetry as an ontological assertion of Indigenous sovereignty. By synthesising Michelle Raheja’s “visual sovereignty” (2007) and Kenneth White’s “geopoetics” (1979; 2004), I trace how poets Kimberly Blaeser, Louise Erdrich, and Denise Sweet deploy an Indigenous geopoetics that challenges settler-colonial cartographies. abstract: The article analyzes the current state and prospects of implementing fiber-optic technologies in unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) as an effective response to the challenges of modern electronic warfare. Their potential applications are considered both in the field of intelligence gathering and for the delivery of explosives to designated targets.The classification features of drones are systematized, their main functional purposes are defined, and the advantages and limitations of traditional radio-controlled systems are examined. title: Analyzing Bunyaviruses from a One Health Perspective
abstract: Zoonotic viral diseases continue to pose major challenges to global health, particularly as environmental, social and economic changes increasingly influence interactions among humans, animals, vectors, and ecosystems. This review explores Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV), Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), and hantaviruses (HTVs) within the framework of One Health, emphasizing the ecological and epidemiological factors that govern their emergence and transmission. title: Where did the language of the northeastern Estonian Poluverniki come from?
abstract: This study examines the linguistic origins of the historical community of Poluverniki in northeastern Estonia. Members of this group were typically bilingual and spoke a distinctive blend of dialectal Russian and Estonian. The prevailing scholarly view — based largely on non‑linguistic evidence — holds that the Poluverniki descended from a Votic‑like Southern Finnic population that was later linguistically assimilated by neighboring Russian dialects. title: Influence Without Alliances: China, Pakistan, and Indirect Military Engagement in the Persian Gulf
abstract: This article examines how China expands security influence in the Persian Gulf without alliances, bases, or direct intervention. It introduces indirect military engagement to explain influence through technology diffusion, defence-industrial cooperation, intermediary partnerships, and partner adaptation. Focusing on Pakistan, it argues that Chinese systems gain regional relevance through Pakistani absorption, localisation, training, maintenance, and demonstration. title: Etymologies of Australian reptiles
abstract: Australia, covering almost 7.7 million km2 (3 million mi2), is a mega-biodiverse region with 19 recognised families, 164 genera, six subgenera, 1152 species, and 60 subspecies of reptiles. This study resolves the etymologies of their scientific names (nomina). Most generic and subgeneric names (69%) are derived from Greek, while half (50%) of species and subspecies originate from Latin. Greek-derived names are more often composites than Latin-derived ones. abstract: The behavioural activity of freely moving animals is a confounding factor that affects the recording, analysis, and final results of animal EEG experiments. Along with the lack of standardisation in animal in vivo electrophysiology experiments, this could lead to significant inconsistencies, especially in the analysis of centrally acting drugs. abstract: Background: Teaching in maritime higher education places simultaneous demands on instruction, assessment, student support, and administrative work. Objective: The study described stress management and perceived professional efficacy among instructors at a Philippine maritime college, and compared rank patterns across program-size groups. abstract: Outer space, once considered a frontier of peaceful scientific exploration and international cooperation, has undergone a dramatic transformation. Space-based military technologies are re-emerging as central elements of contemporary strategic competition. The weaponisation of outer space is no longer a hypothetical concern but an increasingly evident reality shaping the global security environment. title: First Exhaustive List and Distribution Pattern of Scorpions in Libya (Arachnida: Scorpiones)
abstract: Libya, one of the largest countries in North Africa, is characterized by a Mediterranean climate along its northern coast and an extensive hot desert climate across much of its territory. These environmental conditions provide suitable habitats for a diverse assemblage of scorpion species adapted to arid ecosystems. Despite this ecological suitability, the scorpion fauna of Libya remains inadequately documented, with previous studies largely restricted to individual species or limited geographic regions. title: Shaped by humans but increasingly threatened: pathways for the conservation of Palaearctic grasslands
abstract: Palaearctic grasslands are among the most species-rich ecosystems of the Northern Hemisphere, but their conservation depends on continued management that must be reconciled with agricultural production, rural livelihoods and other socio-economic demands. Introducing a special issue that brings together 18 contributions from across Eurasia, we synthesize the interacting pressures shaping these grasslands and identify pathways towards their effective conservation. title: Bodies of knowledge: experience, commodification and labour in the imperial wildlife trade
abstract: The production of zoological knowledge in the late nineteenth century and the early twentieth was closely tied to the supply of animal bodies to institutions like zoological gardens and university departments, sustained by a growing wildlife trade. This trade, however, used, developed and altered independent forms of knowledge that relied heavily on skills and competencies formed through experience and familiarization. abstract: The spider beetle genus Scaleptinus Borowski, 2006 (Coleoptera: Ptinidae: Ptininae) was created to reclassify two morphologically distinct, scale-covered species of Ptinus known from the arid western regions of Namibia and South Africa. In this same publication, two new species, S. beardae and S. similis, were each described from single male specimens. Morphological examination reveals that S. beardae is within the range of morphological variation seen in S. squamulosus and is here proposed as a junior synonym. title: Apatite Geochemistry as a Key to Typification and Petrogenesis of Pegmatites from Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica
abstract: Apatite is a sensitive indicator of magmatic and post-magmatic processes in granitic and pegmatitic systems. This study investigates accessory apatite from different types of pegmatites and granites of Larsemann Hills (East Antarctica) in order to classify the pegmatites and reconstruct their formation conditions. The results show the Types I and III pegmatites crystallized at higher temperatures than Type IV pegmatites with miarolitic cavities and the Progress granites. abstract: The Neoperla (Formosita) lushana-group is revised using an integrative taxonomic approach combining morphological and molecular evidence. Two new species of this group are described and illustrated: Neoperla foping Wang, Wang & Li sp. nov. from Shaanxi Province and Neoperla huangi Wang, Wang & Li sp. nov. from Hunan Province. title: Discovering the Unknown: The Functions of Push and Pull in Theroux’s Pacific Adventures
abstract: Travel serves as a doorway to other worlds and a tool for self-discovery, allowing travellers to transcend preconceptions and gain a more profound comprehension of individuals and locations. This paper explores how firsthand interactions with foreign cultures, environments, and social realities alter perception. Travellers frequently form opinions about a place before visiting it based on media, anecdotes, and other people's experiences. title: Further revisions to the catalogue of skeletal material from megatooth sharks, with a response to Sternes et al. (2024)
abstract: One specimen of Otodus auriculatus and three specimens of O. megalodon are added to the catalogue of skeletal material from megatooth sharks. Criticisms of the Lamnoidea hypothesis and reconstruction of Cretalamna sp. by Sternes et al. (2024) are responded to. Included is discussion of the validity of rostra, regional endothermy, and bauplans as evidence for the Otodontidae + Lamnidae clade, as well as phylogenetic analyses incorporating these families. This is the third installment in a series of papers compiling the catalogue.

abstract: Conversations about student debt frequently target attendees of four-year and professional institutions, since higher-cost institutions are more likely to lead to high levels of debt. While some research has focused on financial aid and college funding at community colleges, we have comparatively limited scholarship regarding conceptualizations of student debt. abstract: At the Ptolemaic Temple of 'Horus Behdet' at Edfu, Upper Egypt, the ‘legend of the Winged Disk’ is written on the walls and describes the battles between Horus and Seth. title: Disney's Location Strategy in China: Balancing Global Brand Identity and Local Adaptation
abstract: Multinational companies face a persistent tension between maintaining a consistent global brand identity and adapting to local consumer preferences. Disney's long-term presence in China provides a useful observation sample for examining this issue. Since the opening of Shanghai Disneyland in 2016, Disney has accumulated substantial operational experience in the Chinese market. title: Predominance of Externally Mixed Black Carbon Over the Tibetan Plateau During the Asian Summer Monsoon
abstract: Abstract The mixing state of black carbon (BC) strongly influences its lifetime and radiative forcing over the Tibetan Plateau (TP). abstract: Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) landraces collected before the widespread regional adoption of Green Revolution cultivars provide a historical record of locally maintained germplasm. abstract: We present a comprehensive systematic revision of the monotypic helicarionid genus Siamochlamys, in Thailand. abstract: Accumulation of ∼200 h of hypoxia exposure (pre-acclimatization) has been suggested to prevent the development of acute mountain sickness when a person is subsequently exposed to high altitude. These pre-exposures are typically undertaken intermittently at or near the place of residence, primarily during sleep in hypoxic tents, and are likely to induce effective ventilatory acclimatization. abstract: En el Neotrópico, los únicos murciélagos que poseen discos de succión en los pulgares y patas traseras pertenecen a la familia Thyropteridae. title: Source apportionment and risk assessment of potentially toxic elements in soils in industrial cities – a cross-regional study
abstract: Urban soils in industrial cities accumulate potentially toxic elements (PTEs) from mixed lithogenic and anthropogenic sources; yet cross-regional comparisons remain rare. title: Knowledge uprooted: Transimperial forestry and the hiring of foreign experts in the Dutch East Indies, 1920s–1930s
abstract: Abstract This article examines the global networks underpinning colonial forestry in the Dutch East Indies in the interwar period. In the aftermath of the First World War, a renewed surge towards the internationalisation of the forest sciences served to open up imperial knowledge systems to a wider pool of outside expertise. This provided opportunities for smaller, thus far underresearched parties like the Nordic states, as explored here through a case study of a group of international foresters employed by the Dutch colonial administration in the 1930s. title: A new subspecies of the genus Eisenia from the Yan Mountains, China (Oligochaeta, Lumbricidae)
abstract: The Eisenia nordenskioldi complex exhibits remarkable morphological stasis alongside profound genetic diversification, harboring extensive cryptic diversity throughout its range. Distributed broadly across the Palearctic realm, including northern and northeastern China, this species complex remains taxonomically poorly resolved. title: When heritage becomes a burden: an evidence-based reference class of tourism stress in historic cities
abstract: Overtourism and carrying-capacity models have traditionally explained heritage-city stress through visitor volume and density. However, these approaches provide limited explanation of why comparable tourism pressures produce different forms and levels of stress across historic cities. This study addresses this gap by examining heritage stress as a perception-driven, context-dependent process shaped by interactions among spatial, social, infrastructural, cultural, and governance conditions. abstract: Fungal diversity is an important component in maintaining ecosystem balance, especially in campus environments that have a variety of habitats such as soil, litter, and vegetation. abstract: This study aims to analyze less familiar Orthodox sites in Blagoevgrad District of Southwestern Bulgaria, defined here as “sacred places in a shadow” as a factor for religious tourism development, specifically through community-led charitable activities for their renovation. abstract: Climate change is not a distant risk but an everyday lived experience. This article examines climate change in Catalonia, Spain by focusing on daily routines, relationships, and emotions. In doing so, it moves beyond predominantly abstract, technical, and quantitative approaches to the climate crisis by foregrounding everyday experiences through three mutually constitutive dimensions: embodiment, intersectionality, and situatedness. abstract: Advancing renewable energy sources is crucial to meeting the growing energy demand. Solar energy conversion systems, such as photovoltaic (PV) cells and thermoelectric generators (TEG), play a significant role in addressing this need. PV systems primarily convert visible and ultraviolet (UV) light from sunlight, while TEGs utilize the infrared (IR) spectrum to generate electrical energy. title: Assessment of forensic evidence utilized in wildlife cases in the Australian judicial system
abstract: Australia’s endemic animals are poached from the wild to supply the global illegal wildlife trade. Wildlife forensic science is applied in Australian criminal investigations and has been documented in the scientific literature but lacks an evaluation on how forensic evidence is used in court. The aim of our study was to identify taxa and forensic evidence involved in cases and highlight where additional forensic evidence could have been valuable. title: From Difficult Heritage to Difficult Temporality: The Political Life of History in Cities With Scarce Heritage
abstract: This article examines the challenges in self-narration faced by cities with short, sparse, and monotonous histories. Moving beyond the concept of “difficult heritage,” which focuses on problematic historical content (e.g., legacies of forced labor), the authors introduce “difficult temporality” to describe a structural scarcity of historical events. Through case studies of five Russian cities (Kovrov, Chernogorsk, Inta, Dudinka, and Susuman), the article identifies core and supplementary strategies these communities use to construct a usable past. abstract: This article aims to reconstruct the origin, development, and spread of the Lontaraq script, the only script still in use among those once employed in South Sulawesi. title: Emotional geography of tourism resistance: Claiming the right to the city in overtourism destinations
abstract: Despite advances in resident–tourism discourse and overtourism research, it remains unclear how place-based emotions and perceptions of injustice become collectively articulated and connected to resistance. Drawing on emotional geography and the right to the city, this study challenges the assumption that resistance is a direct response to tourism pressures. abstract: The article considers the application of the concept of linguistic worldview in translation education at the university level from the perspectives of both the teacher and the students. Special attention is paid to those dimensions of translation that linguistic worldview can help elucidate, and thus help to formulate a strategic approach that balances creativity with awareness of the cultural specificity of the source material. title: Western Media Representation of Africa: The Role of Bad Governance
abstract: The Western media's depiction of Africa has long been entrenched in a narrow and conclusively negative narrative. Even in the digital age, mainstream Western outlets continue to present stories from Africa through a lens that perpetuates outdated stereotypes, portraying the continent as mired in a "dark age"characterised by archaic practices and perpetual strife. title: Beyond McManus’s “Hollow Space”: Reframing Historical Erasure in Atwood, Ballard, and Gibson
abstract: Dystopian fiction usually warns us about the future, but its most critical force often lies in what it erases from the past. Patricia McManus identifies a “hollow space” in dystopian narrative where history is suppressed, yet critical scholarship frequently treats this absence as a mere structural device. Re-examining Margaret Atwood’s The Handmaid’s Tale, J. G. abstract: Introduction This article examines relations between the Ulus of Jochi and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania in 1380–1395 in their military-political, diplomatic, and legal-fiscal dimensions. Aim and objectives. abstract: Abstract Understanding how ecological communities respond to environmental change over long timescales is essential for predicting modern ecosystem dynamics. Here, we reconstructed functional community composition and trophic network structure of seven mammal communities from the eastern region of Oregon. title: The scientific consensus on the beauty of snowflakes: A case study for the aesthetics of science
abstract: Philosophers of science interested in aesthetics have tended to privilege the epistemic and cognitive dimensions of science. Historians of science interested in aesthetics have largely focused on the aesthetics of scientific images and artefacts. Productive exchanges between these traditions of scholarship have been few and far between. Drawing inspiration from recent studies on the aesthetics of paleontology and geology, I aim to stimulate such exchanges by offering a historically rooted case study for the aesthetics of science, centred not on a theory or discipline but on an object: the snow

abstract: This article examines the European Union’s collective securitization of Russia across two critical junctures: the 2014 annexation of Crimea and the 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Why did the EU, long energy-dependent and internally divided, adopt substantial but fragmented measures that changed little in 2014, yet achieve unprecedented unity, scope, and institutionalization after 2022? title: Rethinking Community-Based Tourism for Sustainable Development: Evidence from Jaflong, Bangladesh
abstract: This study examines the potential of community-based tourism (CBT) as a pathway to sustainable development in Jaflong, Bangladesh, an ecologically sensitive and culturally diverse destination, where the uneven participation of different community groups remains insufficiently examined. title: Trascendencia en ciencia ficción: análisis comparativo de la Saga Ringworld y Childhood’s End
abstract: This paper examines the connections between science fiction and religion through the lens of transcendence in two iconic works: Ringworld by Larry Niven and Childhood’s End by Arthur C. abstract: This paper examines how complexity in the universe emerges from the interconnected roles of fundamental particles, forces, physical laws, and governing parameters. abstract: How did the United Nations, in their early years become an actor in the process of decolonization? This article shifts attention away from the diplomatic negotiations conventionally associated with international decolonization and toward the United Nations visiting missions, a largely overlooked instrument of the Trusteeship System entrusted with an epistemic mandate to investigate, inspect, and report on conditions in dependent territories. abstract: Background Improving the deployment of helitack crews is crucial for limiting the growth of newly ignited wildfires. Aims We evaluated whether an optimization model could improve deployment in areas where high-intensity fires could occur compared with the current heuristic approach. abstract: In the 18th century, the import of goods from the Muslim East to the Polish- Lithuanian Commonwealth was concentrated in the hands of large trading companies. abstract: Abstract Vervaeke and Mastropietro’s 4P model of knowing is a non-representational and process-oriented framework that integrates four interrelated ways of knowing: propositional, procedural, perspectival, and participatory. In this paper, we revise this model, drawing on the enactive approach and insights from Madhyamaka and Yogācāra Buddhist traditions of philosophy. title: Units, Assemblages, Compilations: The “Composite Nature of Early Chinese Texts” Reconsidered
abstract: Abstract The “composite nature of early Chinese texts” is a familiar way of thinking about textual formation in early China. It highlights how a text is comprised of small, movable textual units called “building blocks,” how an assemblage of building blocks stands either on its own or as part of a larger whole, and how a composite structure is the “norm” rather than exception in early Chinese writings. abstract: Underwater Wireless Optical Communications (UWOC) provide essential high data rates for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs), but reliable connectivity is critically affected by transmitter-receiver misalignment. abstract: Remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) are widely used to explore and inspect underwater environments such as caves, shipwrecks, and submerged infrastructure. These missions require accurate 3D understanding of the surrounding environment, which depends on both reliable vehicle localization and metric scene reconstruction. abstract: This paper addresses the control of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) operating in dynamic environments, where wave-induced forces, modelling errors, and actuator limitations make reliable control challenging. Active disturbance rejection control (ADRC), together with an extended state observer (ESO), estimates lumped uncertainties online, simplifying control design using nominal models. abstract: Transient supplies of nutrients to the surface ocean, both natural and artificial, stimulate blooms of phytoplankton and the formation of organic matter, driving air-sea gradients and uptake of CO$_2$. abstract: Model-based control of an aquatic robotic platform depends on a hydrodynamic model that is costly to identify and specific to the hull, payload, and conditions it was measured in. abstract: Thermodynamic cycles are the foundation of energy conversion across natural and engineered systems, transforming heat into useful work. However, these cycles traditionally operate between fixed thermal reservoirs, restricting them to specific locations and temperature differences. abstract: This paper presents a regression-based maneuvering model for inland waterway ships operating under realistic environmental conditions based on computational methods utilizing the unsteady Reynolds-Averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) equations, across a wide range of water depths, from deep to shallow water conditions. abstract: Rising sea level threatens coastal communities globally, making it important to understand long-term landscape responses to anticipate future changes. abstract: Accelerated sea-level rise, driven by ocean warming and land ice loss, is one of the most significant drivers of climate-related human mobility, understood as the temporary or permanent forced movement from people’s usual place of residence. title: Arctic climate tipping points under delayed CO2 emissions mitigation
abstract: The Arctic is warming more than three times faster than the global average – driven by increasing CO2 emissions – yet its response to the cessation of these emissions remains uncertain. abstract: Abstract Caribbean coasts face compounding ecological, social, historical, and economic pressures that current resilience conceptualizations do not fully capture. abstract: This essay interrogates the maritime as a concept and principle of colonization in Hegel’s philosophy of history and seeks to interrupt this imperializing logic with an alternative conception of the maritime from Coleridge’s The Rime of the Ancient Mariner . abstract: Manatees are charismatic, wide-ranging megaherbivores increasingly threatened with extinction across much of their distribution. Although many studies have documented threats to manatee populations, no standardized framework has been applied to quantify their vulnerability, leaving available knowledge scattered and lacking a comprehensive assessment of impact magnitude and spatial scale. To do this, a documentary review of scientific articles, theses, and institutional documents located in academic databases and open-access repositories was con-ducted, which allowed for systematizing the existing work and outlining the main theoretical and teaching approaches present in the literature. title: Resilience assessment of pile-supported wharves under the effects of sequential earthquake and soil liquefaction incorporating vine copula captured dependence
abstract: Pile-supported wharves (PSWs) constructed in seismically active coastal environments are susceptible to earthquake-induced liquefaction and the cumulative effects of sequential seismic events. This study develops a probabilistic framework to assess the seismic resilience of conventional and seismically isolated PSWs subjected to mainshock-aftershock (MS-AS) sequences while accounting for liquefaction-induced soil degradation. title: Aterian Lithic Technology and Functional Studies in North Africa: A Review of Current Evidence and Perspectives
abstract: Abstract In North Africa, the Middle Stone Age (MSA) has been associated with the emergence and evolution of Homo sapiens and is considered a pivotal period in the development of behavioral complexity. Recent archaeological discoveries have yielded a range of technological innovations, which are likely connected with ecological adaptations as well as new social and symbolic practices. title: Presence and characterization of microplastics in pet blood (dogs and cats): Evidence of environmental contamination
abstract: Increasing evidence identifies microplastics (MPs) as ubiquitous environmental contaminants, across marine, terrestrial, and atmospheric ecosystems. Their size and physicochemical properties facilitate widespread distribution and bioavailability, raising increasing concerns regarding their potential impact on animal and human health. Their presence in aquatic organisms (e.g., fish, mussels), marine mammals, and birds is demonstrated but evidence related to dogs and cats are relatively few. title: Widespread hybridization in sympatric populations of allis shad Alosa alosa (L.1758) and twaite shad Alosa fallax (Lacépède 1803): A transnational perspective for conservation and management
abstract: The dynamics of hybridization between co-occurring species in environments that have been modified by anthropogenic activities are important for generating new understandings of how species respond to disturbance and to support conservation management. Accordingly, the patterns of hybridization between anadromous allis shad Alosa alosa (L.1758) and twaite shad Alosa fallax (Lacépède 1803) were investigated, where these species historically co-occurred across rivers in Europe. title: Gendered landscapes of loss: climate change, disaster, and women's resilience in rural India
abstract: This article examines the gendered dimensions of climate-induced disasters in rural India through a systematic archival analysis of five community testimonies published by the People's Archive of Rural India (PARI). Drawing on stories from Odisha, Maharashtra, Assam, and Kerala, the study analyses how climate change manifesting as erratic monsoons, intensifying floods, accelerating riverbank erosion, and catastrophic landslides disproportionately impacts women in agrarian and indigenous communities. The article employs a qualitative methodology combining systematic archival analysis with a str

title: Paleoseasonality through serial stable isotope analysis of Pleistocene to recent Etheria elliptica shells from the middle Atbara River, eastern Sudan
abstract: Rainfall magnitude and seasonality are primary determinants of African savannas today, governing essential aspects of biomass production, such as primary productivity and the amount of tree cover. It remains unclear to what extent past seasonality differed from today, potentially accounting for differences in habitats and faunal diversity. Stable isotopes along with trace elements of the growth layers in bivalve shells provide valuable insights into paleoenvironmental conditions, including rainfall, river productivity, and water temperature. title: Renoprotective effects of dapagliflozin and montelukast for diclofenac induced acute kidney injury through network pharmacology and experimental validation
abstract: Abstract Diclofenac (DIC)-prompted acute kidney injury (AKI) is associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and dysregulated autophagy, all of which contribute to renal impairment. Using a network pharmacology approach followed by experimental validation, this study evaluated the reno-protecting actions of dapagliflozin (DAPA) and montelukast (MON) against DIC-induced AKI in rats, both alone and in combination. title: Gastropod Diversity at Azheekkal, Kollam, Kerala, India: A Historical Baseline from August–November 2017
abstract: Motivation: Historical biodiversity records provide useful reference points for coastal biodiversity monitoring, particularly in areas subject to continuing human use. Azheekkal, Kollam, Kerala, supports a diverse molluscan fauna, but historical records of its gastropod assemblage remain limited. Objectives: This study documents the gastropod assemblage recorded at Azheekkal during August–November 2017 and provides a historical reference dataset for future biodiversity assessments. title: CLIMATE-RELATED DISASTERS AND PROVINCIAL CONTINGENCY BUDGET ADAPTATION IN INDONESIA
abstract: This study examines whether Indonesian regional contingency budgets adapt to realised climate-related disaster experience, treating budget responsiveness as one dimension of fiscal resilience. A balanced province-year panel covering 32 provinces is estimated using fixed effects with standard errors clustered by province. The dependent variable is the budgeted share of contingency expenditure (Belanja Tidak Terduga/BTT) in total regional expenditure. journal: Proceeding of The International Seminar on Business Economics Social Science and Technology (ISBEST)

title: Historical biogeography of Middle-East mangroves: paleobotanical evidence
Flowing between worlds: Water onto-epistemologies and educational plurality
abstract: Educational philosophy has been landlocked—built on terrestrial metaphors of ground, foundation, and territory that reproduce a sovereign ontology separating knower from known. This paper develops water onto-epistemologies as an alternative orientation, drawing on Indigenous philosophies, decolonial theory, Japanese aesthetics, and oceanic thought to argue that water offers not merely a different metaphor but a different grammar for educational thinking—one rooted in relationality, opacity, and movement. title: Análisis bioarqueológico de restos humanos del Período Arcaico Tardío (3950-1550 cal AP) en Talcahuano-1, sur de Chile: avances en la identificación de patologías y reconstrucción de estilos de vida
abstract: The Talcahuano-1 archaeological site in Southern Chile provides a unique context for studying Late Archaic (3,950 – 1,550 cal BP) populations. This study revisits three human burials previously analyzed for funerary practices, paleopathology, and lifestyle. Using updated methods and stable isotope analyses, new insights into diet, chronology and health were gained. Results reveal evidence of a marine-based diet, marked musculoskeletal stress, and pathologies such as porotic hyperostosis and treponematosis. title: Bocachico (Ichthyoelephas humeralis) en Ecuador: revisión sistemática y análisis espacial de su distribución
abstract: Ichthyoelephas humeralis (bocachico) is a native fish species of high ecological and socioeconomic importance in Ecuador. This study integrates a systematic review and a spatial analysis to synthesize its distribution, biology, ecological requirements, economic importance, threats, and conservation strategies. Under the PRISMA 2020 protocol, 29 available studies on the species were analyzed, primarily addressing biological, ecological, and use aspects. title: Identifying counties with suitable habitat for host-seeking Borrelia burgdorferi sensu stricto-infected Ixodes pacificus nymphs across seven states in the western United States
abstract: Abstract Background Tick surveillance is used to monitor acarological risk for Lyme disease. Most human infections arise from the bite of a Borrelia burgdorferi sensu stricto (Bbss)-infected nymphal tick. Tick surveillance records documenting the densities of host-seeking Bbss-infected nymphs are limited in the western US, where Ixodes pacificus (Cooley and Kohls, 1943) is the primary vector. title: Leviathan: fast, memory-efficient, and scalable taxonomic and pathway profiling for (pan)genome-resolved metagenomics and metatranscriptomics
abstract: Functional profiling of meta-omics is essential for understanding microbial communities, yet support for custom genome-resolved reference databases is limited. We introduce Leviathan for integrated taxonomic and functional profiling at both genome and pangenome resolution. Leviathan combines Sylph for ultrafast alignment-free taxonomic profiling with Salmon for pseudo-alignment-based read quantification in DNA space against (pan)genome-resolved gene catalogs, producing dual metrics per (pan)genome: pathway abundance and graph-based pathway coverage. title: Penerapan Kepemimpinan Digital dalam Mendukung Keberlanjutan Koperasi Unit Desa Lawallu, Kabupaten Barru
abstract: Lawallu Village Unit Cooperative (KUD), located in Barru Regency, South Sulawesi, is a community-based economic institution with strong social capital, yet it still faces limited digital leadership capacity in managing services, administration, and data-based decision-making. Most service processes remain manual, archives are not yet digitized, and internal communication lacks standardization. This community service program aimed to strengthen the digital leadership capacity of the cooperative's management board and key members through flexible, self-paced web-based learning. title: Mediaciones, medialidades y testimonios: entre cinedocumental, arte y memoria. Un análisis de Lemebel, Cicatrices en la tierra y Este arte que abraza
abstract: This article examines how documentary cinema establishes relationships between art and memory in three documentaries: Lemebel, Cicatrices en la tierra, and Este arte que abraza. The analysis identifies three distinct forms of mediation, mediality, and testimonial practice. Lemebel is an authorial and didactic documentary centered on the recovery of the artist’s archive and the reconstruction of his life and work. title: A new Caribbean species of the giant isopod genus Bathynomus (Crustacea, Isopoda, Cirolanidae) with notes on its evolutionary history
abstract: Abstract The new species Bathynomus tuebingoborikensis sp. nov., discovered in an historic museum collection, is described. We provide preliminary phylogenetic analyses of the genus, including extant and fossil species, using morphological characters. We reconstruct the evolutionary origin of the genus in the Caribbean, and suggest ten different migration waves all over the world oceans, including multiple recolonizations of the Americas. title: From national to global: Mapping global center-pivot irrigated cropland with knowledge-guided data augmentation
abstract: Center-pivot irrigated cropland (CPIC) is a large-scale, intensive agricultural irrigation practice with high water-use efficiency. This characteristic enables CPIC to increase crop yields and promote agricultural development, while simultaneously causing groundwater overexploitation and subsequent environmental issues. Mapping the global distribution of CPIC is critical for enhancing water resource management, guiding agricultural policies, and assessing ecological impacts. institutions: State Key Laboratory of Information Engineering in Surveying Mapping and Remote Sensing

title: Review of Salmonid Alphavirus: Focus on Viral Survival, Shedding, Detection and Effects of Vaccination
abstract: This review of salmonid alphavirus provides a collection of the most recent knowledge on the factors relevant for the transmission and control of the virus including updates on SAV survival, viral shedding, detection, and effects of vaccination as reported in peer-reviewed literature, presentations, theses, and annual reports. SAV can survive in all water types, being the longest in colder marine waters without organic loading. The biophysical properties of SAV indicate a moderate to high robustness. title: Konten Media Sosial @PandawaraGroup sebagai Mekanisme Pembentuk Kesadaran Lingkungan: Analisis Netnografi dalam Perspektif Akuntansi Sosial dan Lingkungan
abstract: Environmental degradation requires broader forms of social accountability that extend beyond formal regulations. Although social media has become an influential platform for environmental campaigns, limited studies have examined its role in fostering environmental awareness from the perspective of Social and Environmental Accounting (SEA). This study aims to explore how the social media content of @PandawaraGroup contributes to the formation of environmental awareness and expands the concept of social accountability in the digital sphere. title: Villa Ögel: A Vanishing Example of Modern Heritage at Şaşkınbakkal
abstract: This study investigates Villa Ögel, a rare surviving example of Suadiye’s modernist garden-villa era (1940s–1950s), to illuminate its architectural, historical, and socio-cultural significance amid Istanbul’s rapid urban transformation. Suadiye is a coastal residential district on the Anatolian side of Istanbul, with Villa Ögel located in Şaşkınbakkal, a smaller micro-geographical area within the broader Suadiye neighborhood, representing a specific locality within its wider urban and historical context. title: An Energy Integration Free Kubo-Bastin Formula Decomposition
abstract: Kubo formulae play a central role in modern spintronics and condensed matter physics, serving as the foundational ground for studying transport responses in the linear regime. In this work, we propose a reformulation of the widely used Kubo-Bastin decompositions that eliminates the need for numerical energy integration. title: Indian MAHASAGAR and the Evolution of India's Maritime Diplomacy
abstract: India's maritime diplomacy has undergone a decisive transformation over the past decade, evolving from a continental-focused posture toward a proactive, maritime-centric vision for the Indo-Pacific. This article examines that evolution and assesses the operational relevance of minilateral architectures in advancing India's strategic objectives. title: Cytochalasins are a fascinating class of natural compounds: advances in the chemistry, biological activities, mode of action, and structure-activity relationships of novel cytochalasins isolated in the last decade are described
abstract: Cytochalasins are a very intriguing group of natural compounds. Since the first isolation of the well-known cytochalasins A and B in 1966, over 300 analogues have been described as metabolites, primarily produced by various fungal genera. Their bioactivities, targets, total syntheses, and biosyntheses had been also extensively investigated. After the review of Scherlach et al., 2010 several other cytochalasins, isolated from different fungal sources, their biological activities and potential applications, were extensively described. title: A life cycle assessment and multi-regional adaptation pathways for Sargassum-based concrete as a low-carbon building material
abstract: This study develops the Sargassum-Based Concrete Integrated Carbon Evaluation Framework (SBC-ICEF) to assess the environmental implications of incorporating processed Sargassum particles into concrete for potential non-load-bearing wall applications in coastal China. Laboratory measurements are linked to production-stage carbon inventories and supplementary carbon-retention scenarios, with potential operational-energy effects discussed qualitatively, using 1 m 3 of concrete and a reference building as complementary functional units. title: Macroevolutionary insights into the range limits of species and lineages
abstract: Understanding the intrinsic and extrinsic factors that determine the range limits of species is an important goal in biology. Much work has focused on understanding the range limits of populations and individual species, whereas the factors that determine the distributions of evolutionary lineages have received less attention in the range limits literature. In this review I highlight recent macroscale insights into the range limits of flowering plant lineages, and briefly compare these to findings from other taxa. title: EFFECTS OF INVASIVE FISH SPECIES ON NATIVE SPECIES AND AQUATIC ECOSYSTEMS
abstract: Biological invasions have emerged as one of the major drivers of global biodiversity loss, threatening native species, ecosystem functioning, and human well-being. This review examines the impacts of invasive species on native fish species and aquatic ecosystems, with emphasis on mechanisms of invasion, pathways of introduction, ecological consequences, and management strategies. Deliberate and accidental introductions facilitated by globalization, aquaculture, trade, and transportation have accelerated the spread of invasive organisms across freshwater and marine environments. title: Re-evaluating ecoinvent’s suitability for direct product material footprint calculation
abstract: Abstract Sustainable Development Goal 12.2 aims to achieve the sustainable management and efficient use of natural resources by 2030. Its target indicator, the material footprint, is a key macroeconomic indicator for impacts related to resource extraction. On the microeconomic scale, it is complemented by the product material footprint (PMF). title: NEUROPROTECTIVE AND MEMORY-ENHANCING EFFECTS OF SARGASSUM TENERRIMUM ETHANOLIC EXTRACT IN SCOPOLAMINE-INDUCED AMNESIA IN WISTAR RATS
abstract: Objectives: The present study aimed to assess the neuroprotective properties and memory enhancement of the ethanolic extract of Sargassum tenerrimum (ST) with regard to the scopolamine-induced amnesia model in Wistar rats and explore the underlying mechanism involved in cholinergic neurotransmission. Methods: The extract was administered orally once daily for 14 consecutive days at doses of 50, 100, and 200 mg/kg. title: Pedro Carrere. Un japonista español en el México finisecular: colección, mediación y práctica artística
abstract: Historiography of Japonisme in Latin America has logically prioritized the study of prominent figures such as José Juan Tablada, leaving the role of cultural mediators whose influence proved decisive yet to be examined. Among them, Pedro Carrere stands out; however, his diplomatic career and collecting activities have lacked a systematic reconstruction until now. title: Clinical and Radiological Evaluation of Foreign Body Injuries in Yellow-legged Gulls (Larus michahellis): A Retrospective Study (2023–2026)
abstract: Yellow-legged gulls (Larus michahellis), which exhibit opportunistic feeding behavior, face a high global risk of interacting with anthropogenic waste originating from urban and fishing activities. The aim of this retrospective study is to evaluate in detail the aetiology, clinical findings, and treatment processes associated with foreign body ingestion and/or entanglement in Yellow-legged gulls (n=12) presenting to the clinic for flightlessness between 2023 and 2026. title: ACANTHUS ILICIFOLIUS L: ETHNOBOTANY, PHYTOCHEMISTRY, PHARMACOLOGYAND SYNTHESIS OF SILVER NANOPARTICLES (AGNPS)
abstract: Acanthus ilicifoliusbelongs to the family Acanthaceaeis a medicinal plant widely distributed in the coastal areas of tropical and subtropical regions. It has been traditionally used in various systems of folk medicine for managing conditions such as wounds, fever, inflammation, and respiratory problems. Phytochemical investigations have revealed the presence of several biologically active constituents, including flavonoids, alkaloids, phenolic compounds, and terpenoids. title: Toponymy and Shifted Identity: A Study of the Language Change in Rejang-Language Village Names
abstract: This study examines the changes in village names from the Rejang language to Indonesian in Kepahiang Regency, Bengkulu, focusing on referential meanings, community perceptions, and the impact on local cultural identity. Using referential meaning analysis and thematic analysis based on interviews with both older and younger generations, the findings show that the language shift alters not only linguistic forms but also the cultural, historical, and spiritual values embedded in the original toponyms. journal: Theory and Practice in Language Studies

title: A record of emplacement conditions from trapped volatile gases within nuclear test debris
abstract: Nuclear melt glass provides a valuable archive of information about the nature of the nuclear detonation. Study of melt glasses provides information on the device materials and performance, the emplacement conditions, the venting conditions (if any), and future environmental and human health impacts. Despite extensive study, direct records of redox conditions and cooling histories of the post-detonation environment are sparse. title: No critical slowing down in the Atlantic Overturning Circulation in historical CMIP6 simulations
abstract: Abstract. The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a key component of the Earth’s climate system, and is theorized to have multiple stable states. Critical slowing down (CSD) can detect stability changes in Earth system components, and has been found in sea-surface temperature (SST) based fingerprints of the AMOC. We look for CSD in simulations from 27 models from the sixth Climate Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP6). title: Prevalence and multimorbidity patterns of thyroid dysfunction in Chinese adults
abstract: The risk of thyroid dysfunction (TD) persists in the Chinese population. However, large-scale epidemiological studies investigating TD prevalence and its geographic disparities are limited. Previous studies have mostly focused on associations between TD and individual organ systems or single medical conditions. This nationwide, large-scale study utilized data from the Meinian Health Check-up database across all 31 provinces of the Chinese mainland. title: Leveraging word knowledge from everyday language
abstract: Within the first few years of life, children go from nonverbal infants to fluent users of hundreds of words. This feat unfolds as children are immersed in a sea of words in conversations, stories, and other language contexts. In principle, word contexts might support word learning because words with similar meanings tend to occur in similar contexts. Thus, a child who knows some fruit words and has heard them in the context of "juicy" might learn that a "juicy mango" is also a fruit even without ever seeing a mango. title: Ecological considerations for reintroducing Chinook salmon upstream of Shasta Dam
abstract: Abstract In this assessment, we reviewed existing literature to assess the ecological risks, benefits, and uncertainties associated with reintroducing Chinook salmon ( Oncorhynchus tshawytcha ) into the McCloud River, a tributary of the Sacramento River, California. Two source populations are being considered for reintroduction by co‐managers in the basin (the Winnemem Wintu Tribe, California Department of Fish and Wildlife, and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration): existing winter‐run Chinook salmon (WRCS) from the mainstem Sacramento River, and Chinook salmon from New Zealand (NZ

title: Declines in the diversity of fish represented in British domestic recipes over the past 100 years
abstract: Abstract Fish and shellfish are nutritionally important foods, yet consumption in many high‐income countries remains low and concentrated on a narrow set of environmentally costly species. In the United Kingdom, fish consumption is dominated by a small group of fish, the ‘Big Five’, which is often treated as an inevitable outcome of supply, convenience and ingrained consumer preferences. However, little empirical evidence exists on how and when such preferences emerged, or whether present‐day patterns reflect historical continuity or cultural loss. title: Illusions of peace: eurocentrism, endemic violence and the burden of the Postcolony in the Central African Republic
abstract: This paper interrogates how Eurocentrism structures what counts as violence and, by extension, what counts as peace. Using the Central African Republic (CAR) as a site of analysis, it argues that violence cannot be understood through calamitous moments but through the endemic conditions embedded in la longue durée that shape life in the Postcolony. These conditions are relational, produced through the entangled histories of metropole and colony, and sustained by structural and cultural domination. title: Nutrient legacies from elephant megacarcasses create coldspots of biodiversity and hotspots of ecosystem processes
abstract: Terrestrial megafauna (animals >1,000 kg) have substantial impacts on ecosystems while alive; yet, we know little about the impacts of these ecosystem engineers after they die. Like whale carcasses in the ocean, terrestrial megacarcasses may leave ecological legacies via the nutrient pulses they create on the landscape. Here, we investigated the impact of elephant megacarcasses on savanna ecosystems in Kruger National Park, South Africa. title: Energy Efficiency Measures vs. Biofuels - Implications for Vessel Operational Performance
abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine the relative importance of energy saving measures (ESMs) and alternative biofuels for the improvement of ship efficiency and for compliance with new regulations imposed on the maritime transport sector. In light of the fact that ESMs have proven that they are capable of providing a significant fuel saving potential by enhancing the hull condition, propulsion, and internal combustion efficiency as well as through operational optimization, the aim of this study is to investigate the advantages and disadvantages of ESMs compared to biofuels. title: From Curaçao to Coro: A Reexamination of Transimperial Marronage in the Eighteenth Century
abstract: This article reassesses the transimperial flight of enslaved Afro-Curaçaoans from the Dutch island of Curaçao to the Spanish mainland of Tierra Firme, particularly Coro, during the eighteenth century. Owing to Spain's policy of royal asylum, enslaved Afro-Curaçaoans could obtain freedom upon entering Spanish territory. Drawing on a detailed 1775 runaway register and colonial correspondence, the article reconstructs who fled, how they escaped, and why they undertook the maritime crossing. title: Sacralisation and Monumentalisation of World War I in the Isonzo/Soča Region
abstract: This article examines the monumentalisation of World War I in the Isonzo/Soča region (today divided between Italy and Slovenia), promoted by the Italian government and local authorities during the interwar period. Following Italy’s victory in the war, the liberal state – and even more emphatically Mussolini’s regime – fostered a patriotic cult that supported the dictator’s efforts to present Fascism as the rightful heir to that victory. title: Establishment of Regional Action Plan for conservation of critically endangered crucian carp in Czechia
abstract: The crucian carp ( Carassius carassius ) has declined markedly in recent decades due to the ongoing invasion of its congeneric species complex, the gibel carp ( Carassius gibelio ) and widespread habitat degradation. In Europe, the crucian carp occurs in two highly divergent phylogenetic lineages: the northern lineage distributed across northern and central-eastern Europe and occurs in the Elbe (Labe) and Oder (Odra) River Basins and the Danubian lineage restricted to the Danube (Dunaj) River Basin. title: The Efraim Berkovici Collection: Poesiealbum and Diary Writing in "Ilaniah" Children's Village
abstract: In September 1947, a train traveling under the auspices of the Red Cross departed Romania carrying over 420 Jewish children, via Prague, to the Netherlands. The children, among them Holocaust survivors from Transnistria, had been gathered from different parts of Romania, including orphanages, and were taken to the “Ilaniah” children’s village, located on the grounds of a former Jewish psychiatric hospital in Apeldoorn. A smaller group of over thirty Jewish child survivors from Germany arrived a few weeks later. In October 1948, these children boarded a ship, the Negba, and departed for Israel.

abstract: Abstract The insidious collapse of a 38‐year‐old businessman’s hyper‐rational life into a midlife marital crisis compels his psyche to demand a terrifying return to its origins. This paper maps his psychological rebirth by tracing the explicit structural parallels between the stages of the analytical process and the ancient Egyptian solar myth of transformation, illustrating how dream imagery shapes the analytic process. title: The Clandestine Circulation in Fascist Italy of an Italian American Antifascist Newspaper: The Case of “Il Nuovo Mondo”
abstract: Abstract The present article examines the clandestine circulation in Italy of Il Nuovo Mondo (1925–1931) to reconstruct the transnational political networks that developed around an Italian American antifascist newspaper. The article analyzes how its editors, contributors, readers, and supporters connected Italian immigrant communities in the United States to their homeland. title: Coping with Life’s Challenges in Ottoman Sarajevo: Freed Slaves and Agency in an Early Modern Borderland Society
abstract: This paper aims to fill in the gaps in the social history of the Ottoman borderlands by exploring the social integration and agency of freed slaves in Early Modern Ottoman Sarajevo. Recent scholarship has made considerable advances in evaluating the agency of freed slaves in the Ottoman Empire by using the collective biography approach. However, with few exceptions, attention has mostly been paid to materials relating to the inner parts of the Ottoman world, particularly to the Sharia court protocols of the Istanbul Region. title: Latin religious poetry in Orthodox Kyiv, 1685–1736: mediating Europeanness at the Mohyla Academy
abstract: This article uncovers an overlooked archive of religious poetry embedded in five Kyiv-Mohylian poetics manuals from 1685 to 1736, demonstrating how these poems served as a crucial mechanism by which Orthodox Kyiv participated in the learned culture of early modern Europe. Far from being decorative examples or routine school exercises, the manuals’ 287 religious poems and fragments show the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy actively transforming Latin, Jesuit, humanist, medieval, Polish, and Church Slavonic materials into instruments of Orthodox literary and intellectual formation. title: Scholars and Literati at the Académie Philomathique of Paris (1788–1800)
abstract: This document offers a concise portrait of the scholars who belonged to the Académie Philomathique of Paris from its founding in 1788 to the turn of the nineteenth century, in 1800. title: Dissecting the urban anatomy: modernist layers, institutional landmarks, and the Heritage-City Synergy in Cartagena
abstract: Cartagena, Spain, is a unique Mediterranean coastal city defined by its transition from a rigid 18th-entury military stronghold to a dynamic modern center. While its ancient ruins are well-documented, the city’s later layers – specifically its modernist architecture and institutional landmarks – are often overlooked in urban discourse. This neglect creates a gap between heritage preservation and the living city, risking a “museumification” that disconnects historical sites from contemporary social life. abstract: Context: Age segregation limits reciprocal learning among children, adolescents, and older adults and their participation in community responses to social and socioenvironmental challenges. title: The Natural Tourism Riches of Manyu Division, Cameroon: An Inventory of An Exceptional but Underexploited Ecological Endowment
abstract: Manyu Division, in the South-West Region of Cameroon, possesses one of the richest natural tourism endowments in Central Africa, anchored by Korup National Park among the oldest and most bio-diverse rainforests on the continent. It extends across the Takamanda highlands, the Cross River and its tributaries, a landscape of waterfalls, wildlife corridors, and geological formations that together constitute a natural capital of world-class quality. title: Spatial and genetic dynamics of Plasmodium falciparum histidine-rich protein2 in sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: BACKGROUND: Malaria rapid diagnosis tests (mRDTs) detecting Plasmodium falciparum histidine-rich protein 2 (Pfhrp2) are the most widely adopted diagnostic tool in malaria-endemic areas. However, extensive polymorphisms in Pfhrp2 could modify Pfhrp2 epitopes, rendering it undetectable by Pfhrp2-based mRDTs. title: Promotion of land-based carbon sequestration: state of research, knowledge gaps and strategy in India
abstract: Land-based Carbon sequestration is projected to play a critical role in India’s long-term low-carbon development strategy. This study aims to (i) identify the data, monitoring and modeling needs for Carbon sequestration programs in forestry and agroforestry systems, (ii) review the research funding agencies and programs, (iii) identify the research priorities and (iv) suggest a strategy to promote research on Carbon sequestration in India. abstract: As environmental constraints tighten and urban green transformation continues, whether National Forest City Construction (NFCC) can improve urban green production efficiency (GPE) and generate cross-regional spillovers remains an important theoretical and policy question. Using panel data for 277 cities at the prefecture level or above in China from 2006 to 2024, this study applies a spatial Durbin difference-in-differences (SDM-DID) model to estimate the effect of NFCC on GPE. title: The Imprint of a Few: Editorial Authority and Epistemic Inequalities in Elite Biology Journals
abstract: As scholarly publishing becomes increasingly commodified, market-oriented definitions of excellence are reshaping the organization and hierarchization of scientific knowledge. Using a sociology of elites framework, this article examines how the social conditions under which knowledge is produced, evaluated, and circulated shape epistemic inequalities. abstract: Eucheuma spinosum is a promising marine resource for food, hydrocolloid, and bioactive compound applications, although its nutritional and safety characteristics may vary with geographical origin. This study characterized E. spinosum from Gerupuk Waters, Central Lombok, focusing on raw material quality, nutritional composition, mineral and heavy metal contents, phytochemical profile, and antioxidant activity. abstract: This paper presents the development of a three-dimensional model of a historic townhouse located at the Market Square (Rynek 11) in Przemyśl using data acquired by terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) and terrestrial and aerial photogrammetry. The study aimed to assess the usefulness of an integrated measurement approach for preparing detailed architectural documentation of a heritage building and to evaluate the quality of the final products, including the point cloud, mesh model, vector 3D model, and orthophotos. abstract: This article examines the participation of Justo Florian Lobeck in the Chilean typographic space in the mid-nineteenth century; in particular, it explores his forms of intervention in the configuration of a structured and functional bibliographic corpus to the requirements of Chilean secondary education for Latin studies. title: “A Vile Character”
abstract: Alfons Sutter was perhaps the most notorious German police agent in the Łódź ghetto. A native of Łódź, he and dozens of other Volksdeutsche (ethnic Germans) were hired by the criminal police (Kriminalpolizei, or Kripo) after Nazi Germany conquered and annexed the city. abstract: This study examines how communication technology shapes contemporary globalization and why the same technologies can simultaneously integrate and divide the world. Earlier scholarship has documented either the integrative or the exclusionary effects of digital media, but few studies explain the conditions under which each outcome prevails. title: Between Secrecy and Ostentation: Shrines and Rites for the Barbarous Relic
abstract: ABSTRACT Central bank gold vaults occupy a paradoxical position in contemporary monetary systems: They are among the most symbolically charged and institutionally significant spaces of modern finance, yet they have received almost no scholarly attention. This article argues that gold vaults cannot be understood solely as technical infrastructures for the safekeeping of bullion. abstract: This article examines the operations of exclusion that have shaped the Chilean poetry canon and the ways in which women's poetic production during the dictatorship (1973–1990) articulated a counter-archive that challenged those mechanisms. abstract: The redevelopment of the Byker Estate in Newcastle upon Tyne (1969–82), designed by Ralph Erskine, is widely recognised for its serpentine wall and its participatory planning process. abstract: This paper analyzes the demographic dynamics of the aging process and the implementation of social policy in the State of Mexico. abstract: Although urbanization has profound ecological consequences, quantitative evidence on how socio-economic factors in this process affect China’s urban wetland ecosystem services (UWES) remains limited. abstract: A comprehensive strategy for improving agricultural sustainability, resource use efficiency, and livelihood diversification, especially for smallholder farmers, is represented by Integrated Farming Systems (IFS). abstract: Introduction: Elasmobranchs are particularly susceptible to handling-related impacts, making careful management essential to avoid excessive physical trauma and stress. abstract: Smile Chicken MSME faces challenges such as manual transaction recording, raw material inventory tracking, report preparation, and purchasing decisions that still rely on estimation. abstract: Host and parasite body size frequently scale positively (often referred to as Harrison's rule), potentially as a result of fundamental constraints on large parasite species simply being morphologically incapable of infecting small host species, or through a variety of alternative proposed mechanisms. abstract: The part-whole relations of body-part lexemes, or “body partonymy,” might seem like a key source of evidence for shared conceptual systems in support of embodiment theories of cognition, but widespread variation in this lexical field across world languages calls this assumption into question. abstract: Abstract Higher-education campuses are well suited to staged decarbonization because they combine concentrated electrical demand, substantial rooftop area, diverse load flexibility, and long-term institutional ownership of energy assets. This study develops a Campus Microgrid Renewable Integration and Energy-Saving Assessment Framework (CMR-ESAF) for planning the transition of Shivaji University, India, from grid-dependent operation to an optimized hybrid renewable energy system (HRES) microgrid. abstract: Didecyldimethylammonium chloride (DDAC) is a broad-spectrum quaternary ammonium compound (QAC) extensively utilized as a disinfectant and biocide. Widespread use of DDAC, significantly amplified during COVID-19 pandemic, increased human and environmental exposures, indicating need for updated, quantitative risk assessments. abstract: Abstract This research presents a techno-economic and environmental life cycle assessment (LCA) comparison between diesel water pumps (DWP) and solar water pumps (SWP) for smallholder irrigation in Ethiopia. To evaluate long-term operational sustainability amid volatile fossil fuel markets, local hydrologic conditions, and rural decarbonization targets, the study uses an integrated three-stage simulation architecture of the CLIMWAT database, CROPWAT, and PVsyst. title: Safety and health of workers in post-disaster reconstruction: a scoping review and evidence map
abstract: Post-disaster reconstruction (PDR) is essential for restoring damaged communities, yet the occupational safety and health (OSH) of PDR workers remains poorly understood. Although PDR involves many familiar construction hazards, these risks arise under distinct conditions, including damaged infrastructure, compressed recovery timelines, environmental contamination, fragmented governance, and pressure for visible recovery. abstract: Introduction: Perinatal grief has been socially delegitimized; it is often unrecognized or borne in silence. Consequently, families experiencing this type of grief find it difficult to find support and turn to the internet to seek alternatives in the face of their loss. The objective of this study is to understand how users of JICfundación appropriate digital platforms and social networks in this grieving process. abstract: Peru is one of the countries with the greatest diversity of native chili peppers, which make a significant contribution to the highly valued gastronomy of this nation. However, the use of these chili peppers remains localized, resulting in a limited number of studies focused on these species, which restricts their industrial utilization and increases the risk of extinction. title: Environmental Management and Community Well-Being in African: Challenges and Sustainable Development Strategies
abstract: Environmental management has become increasingly important in Africa because environmental degradation directly affects livelihoods, public health, food security, and community resilience. This study examines the relationship between environmental management and community well-being in African countries by focusing on institutional capacity, major environmental challenges, socioeconomic and governance factors, and sustainable development strategies. title: ‘Stuck in a Time Warp’ or ‘Going Forward With Care’? Traversing the Environmental Politics of Genetic Modification in Aotearoa New Zealand
abstract: This article offers an environmental politics history of genetic modification (GM) in Aotearoa New Zealand. GM has been on political agendas for half a century. It has again come to the fore with proposals to enable the technology after decades of stringent regulations. To better contextualise the major changes now in motion, this article traverses the evolution of GM politics in Aotearoa. We identify five key eras of GM politics, drawing on a database of social science literature and media and policy documents spanning the 1970s to today. abstract: Infectious disease severity, shedding, and within-host kinetics can vary substantially with exposure dose, inoculation route, and host factors. abstract: The accurate diagnosis of dental eruption anomalies in pediatric patients represents a critical multidisciplinary challenge in pediatric dentistry and maxillofacial surgery. abstract: Introduction. Kazakh-Dzungar relations from the second half of the XVII century to the 1750s were one of the important processes in the history of Central Asia. abstract: Agrochemicals are a fundamental component of modern agriculture, although their intensive use raises concerns regarding human health, biodiversity, ecosystems and the sustainability of production systems. The aim of this study was to analyse the regulatory, environmental and socio-economic differences associated with the use of agrochemicals between Europe and Latin America. abstract: Introduction: This work contributes to the understanding of Social Appropriation of Knowledge (SAK), addressing the academic need to clarify its meaning, scope, and impacts.
